title: Eliminate tall pillars: Langmuir-Blodgett perovskite nanosheets give planar high-k capacitors
idea: Eliminate the 3D pillar: transfer 3-5 monolayers of exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr2Nb3O10 perovskite nanosheets from a water trough by Langmuir-Blodgett onto storage electrodes, giving a 5-10 nm dielectric with k~150-200 that stays high when thin because there is no dead layer; a 5 fF cell then needs only a short cup.
why: Meets the fact-1 k~70 target with ~2-3x the capacitance per area of ZAZ, cutting AR to ~25 (fact 4); room-temperature water processing uses no vacuum gases; risks are leakage at sheet edges and conformality.
note: Ca2Nb3O10 nanosheets keep high k when thin; LB is planar, so conformality in cups is the issue.

title: Eliminate linear-only dielectrics: built-in-biased antiferroelectric zirconia storage capacitor
idea: Eliminate the assumption that the capacitor dielectric must be linear: use antiferroelectric ZrO2 between asymmetric ALD electrodes (TiN from TiCl4/NH3 vs RuO2, all with N2 purge, not argon) whose work-function difference biases the film onto the steep part of its double loop, so field-induced polarization adds 2-3x charge inside a 0-1 V window without full domain reversal.
why: Effective k~70-100 meets the fact-1 target without AR 115, using an ALD-only, rare-gas-free stack; risks are endurance of partial AFE switching (>1e15 needed) and temperature drift.
note: Biasing AFE onto steep branch boosts charge; hysteresis loss and partial-switching endurance unknown.

title: Eliminate vacuum high-k deposition: hydrothermal conversion of titania shells to SrTiO3
idea: Eliminate ALD of exotic high-k: coat capacitor holes with a few nm of TiO2, then convert it in place in an aqueous Sr(OH)2/Ba(OH)2 bath at 150-200 C into crystalline SrTiO3 or (Ba,Sr)TiO3 (k~100-300), conformal because the ion exchange follows the TiO2 template.
why: k well above the fact-1 target of 70 lets AR fall to ~30-40; a water-based step with no plasma or rare gases cuts tool cost (fact 4); risks are leakage below 8 nm and crystallization defects.
note: Hydrothermal conversion conformal in holes; STO leakage at thin films killed past STO DRAM caps.

title: Eliminate permanent tail cells: in-field Joule self-heating anneal of traps
idea: Drive a short high-current pulse through each gate-all-around nanowire access device, or use its wordline as a resistive heater, to reach ~500-700 C locally for microseconds and re-passivate the defects that cause variable retention time. Repeat periodically in the field to heal aging-induced leakage.
why: Heals the tail cells that dictate refresh, shrinking tail leakage ~10x (fact 3); demonstrable on university-fab nanowires with a probe station.
note: Electrothermal annealing shown for logic devices; local heat endangers neighbor data and BEOL.

title: Eliminate lithography for the cell layer: self-ordered anodic alumina template
idea: Deposit aluminium over the array and anodize it in oxalic or sulfuric acid; hexagonal pores self-order at 25-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios above 1000:1. One coarse imprint of pit seeds pins pore registry to the periphery, the pores host capacitors or vertical channels, and the alumina stays as the dielectric.
why: Removes EUV/multipatterning and high-AR plasma etch for the cell layer, using abundant Al and dilute acid; makes AR>115 capacitors trivial (fact 1).
note: Registering self-ordered pores to storage-node contacts at ~40 nm pitch is the key doubt.

title: Eliminate dissipative bitline charging: stepwise adiabatic charge from idle-bitline tanks
idea: Charge the active bitlines in 8-16 small voltage steps, using idle neighbouring bitline groups as charge reservoirs (stepwise adiabatic charging), and return the charge in reverse steps at precharge so resistive CV2 loss drops by the step count.
why: Bitline sense/restore is the largest slice of activation energy; 8-16 steps cut it ~8-12x using the existing array as the tank, with no inductors or added capacitor material.
note: Step switches add sense latency; half-VDD precharge already recycles part of the charge.

title: Eliminate the half-VDD precharge: single-ended precharge-to-ground sensing
idea: Bitlines rest at 0 V and only cells storing 1 lift their bitline, which a current-mirror sense amp compares against a reference cell; restore drives only the 1s, with no VBLP generator or equalization, and data are bit-plane encoded to be mostly zeros.
why: Bitline energy scales with the count of 1 bits; bit-plane encoded AI data at ~90% zeros gives up to ~10x lower array energy per access.
note: Gain depends on sparse bit-plane data; single-ended margin is the doubt.

title: Cold capacitor: quantum paraelectric k~1000 at liquid-nitrogen temperature
idea: Reverse the operating environment: run the array at 77 K, where SrTiO3 or KTaO3 films reach k ~500-2000 and silicon leakage collapses, so the cell capacitor becomes planar or a shallow 5:1 cup, with the memory sharing the accelerator's liquid-nitrogen loop.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1,4): 5 fF without the high-AR etch, leakage down >1e6 so refresh effectively vanishes; LN2 cost offset by lower wire resistance.
note: Thin-film STO k and field tunability far below bulk; cryo overhead.

title: Image-sensor pixels as memory: pinned-photodiode storage cells
idea: Reverse the image sensor: in existing 55-90 nm CMOS image sensor fabs, use a light-shielded pinned photodiode as the storage well, the transfer gate as the access device, and the floating diffusion plus source follower as an in-cell gain readout, with write-back through a reset/inject path. Pinned photodiodes show dark currents of ~1-10 e-/s, so a few-thousand-electron packet holds for minutes.
why: Near refresh-free retention (fact 3) on idle trailing-node CIS capacity; density ~1-3 Mb/mm2 limits it to a retention tier, while charge transfer in tens of ns stays DRAM-class.
note: Same CIS pinned-well cell; density 1-3 Mb/mm2 limits to retention tier.

title: Glass-panel DRAM self-aligned by backside exposure
idea: Build oxide-semiconductor DRAM tiers on large glass panels and expose the photoresist through the glass from below, so the opaque buried wordlines act as the mask for the channel/source-drain pattern above them; the only added mask is the panel contact opening.
why: Capital and litho (fact 4): panel area is ~10x a 300 mm wafer, display fabs have spare capacity, and self-alignment removes a critical overlay step.
note: Backside exposure is standard TFT art; density on panels very low.

title: Size the capacitor for the median, the code for the tail
idea: Reverse the design target: cut capacitor aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~20:1 so median cells still sense, and let the ~1% low-Cs or leaky tail cells be corrected by page-level ECC instead of building a taller pillar for the worst cell.
why: HAR etch/deposition time, fluorocarbon gas and support-nitride steps fall ~3x; fixes the capacitor charge wall in materials and capital rather than physics.

title: Model-emitted page-out tokens let the model page its KV
idea: Reverse who manages the cache: fine-tune the model to emit special <page-out span> and <page-in topic> tokens, so it moves the KV of finished sub-tasks to host storage and recalls it itself, like a program managing its own overlays.
why: Long agentic sessions keep only their working set resident: 3-10x less KV in HBM with software on existing hardware, so no new neon- or helium-dependent fab output is needed.

title: Origami memory: fold a flex ribbon of dies over compute
idea: Rearrange a planar layout into a fold: bond thinned memory dies to a parylene or polyimide flex with litho-patterned 5 um copper traces, then fold it accordion-style so the dies stack above the compute die while their wiring runs around the folds instead of through the silicon.
why: TSV-free 3D stacking with <5 mm links (fact 6), each die keeping its own traces; flex fabrication is standard in university cleanrooms.

title: Antiferroelectric double-loop capacitor that buffers leakage with phase-transition charge
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric dielectric with the plate biased so writing a '1' crosses the field-induced AFE-to-FE transition and stores extra polarization charge (~10-20 uC/cm2). As the node leaks down to the backward-switching field, the polarization collapses and releases charge, clamping the node voltage like a reservoir; no remanence means no imprint or nonvolatility side-effects.
why: Fact 1: effective charge per area ~3-5x linear ZrO2 at the same voltage, and the built-in charge reservoir stretches retention 2-4x (fact 3).
note: AFE ZrO2 charge reservoir plausible; loss and endurance of field-induced transitions unproven.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall bit in ScAlN or lithium niobate nanomesa
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: in each single-crystal nanomesa, a ns voltage pulse creates or erases a charged domain wall that conducts ~10^4x better than the bulk; the bit is wall present/absent, read non-destructively by a small current. Switching is ferroelectric with no ion motion, and CMOS-friendly wurtzite ScAlN is the target host.
why: Fact 8: non-destructive read with no restore; fact 3: nonvolatile, no refresh; crosspoint 4F2 with one lithography level.
note: LiNbO3 domain-wall memory already demonstrated; ScAlN switching endurance far below DRAM needs.

title: Homogeneity: n-type-only oxide periphery built with the array masks
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: every periphery circuit uses the same n-type IGZO TFT as the array, with bootstrapped dynamic logic, pseudo-differential charge-transfer sense amps and capacitive level shifters, so the whole chip, array plus periphery, needs ~8-10 masks with no wells or implants and can be repeated tier after tier.
why: 100x path: ~8x fewer masks than 60-80-mask DRAM, no EUV, and periphery repeated in each stacked tier keeps tiers independent and testable; trade-offs: ~10x slower periphery (us-class) and higher dynamic power. Attacks Facts 4 and 7 and U.S. manufacturability.

title: Beforehand cushioning: NAND-grade LDPC lets sense amps run at 1e-3 errors
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: a 4 KB-codeword LDPC decoder with soft-read support in the base die absorbs raw bit error rates up to ~1e-3, so sense amps can be minimum-size latches with large offset, cells ~2x smaller, and 2-bit multilevel storage practical.
why: 100x path: ~2x periphery shrink, ~2x cell shrink and ~2x bits per cell compound with stacking; trade-offs: ~0.5-2 us decode latency, 4 KB access granularity and ~10% parity overhead. Attacks Facts 1 and 7.

title: Microsecond flash anneal crystallizes strontium titanate on bare TiN
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rushing through the harmful window): deposit amorphous SrTiO3 by ALD on TiN and crystallize it with a ~1 ms flash-lamp pulse. The film reaches perovskite crystallization temperature before the TiN has time to oxidize into a low-k TiOx interlayer, which removes the Ru electrode that SrTiO3 capacitors historically needed.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k ~100-150 vs ~40 for ZAZ allows ~2x Cs or a pillar aspect ratio cut from ~70:1 to ~35:1, with no Hf or Ru (Sr, Ti and O are abundant).

title: Conformal graphite-foil chuck membrane cools wafers without backside gas
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics (a rigid chuck becomes compliant): face the chuck with a thin compliant pyrolytic-graphite or CNT-forest membrane that electrostatic force flattens against the wafer backside. Heat then flows through solid contact instead of through He-filled grooves.
why: Removes backside helium, the largest fab He use, entirely without the safety work that H2 needs. Uses only C on an AlN/Al2O3 chuck body.
note: Particles, backside contamination and reaching gas-gap conductance in vacuum are the doubts.

title: Anodic alumina self-ordered pores as the capacitor mold
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of plasma-etching 70:1 holes, grow them - deposit ~1.5 um aluminium over the array, nano-indent or DUV-print a shallow pit lattice at the storage-node pitch, and anodize so pores self-propagate straight down at 100:1+; widen pores, open the barrier oxide, then ALD the electrode and dielectric.
why: Replaces the costliest HAR etch (high-power/cryo RIE, many chamber-hours) with a room-temperature electrochemical bath at <1% of the capex; aspect ratio becomes nearly free, so Cs can rise toward 8-10 fF (facts 1, 4).

title: Work-function-asymmetric electrodes make ZrO2 capacitors nonvolatile antiferroelectrics
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: keep the existing DRAM cylinder capacitor module but swap the top electrode for a conductor ~1 eV higher in work function (e.g., RuO2), creating a built-in field that shifts one antiferroelectric double loop to straddle zero bias, giving two remanent polarization states read through the same 1T1C sense path.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh, with AFE ZrO2 endurance ~1e11-1e12; converting an existing DRAM fab needs one electrode change and no new tool types, so capex is near zero vs a new fab (facts 3, 4).

title: Fuzzy cross-request KV merging with sparse residual patches
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: beyond exact prefix sharing, the serving engine clusters KV blocks from concurrent requests whose vectors differ by less than epsilon (same retrieved chunks at different offsets after RoPE de-rotation, templated prompts) and stores one canonical block plus a sparse INT4 residual per request. A radix tree keyed on locality-sensitive hashes finds merge candidates.
why: RAG and agent workloads re-ingest the same chunks at varying positions where exact prefix caching misses; 2-5x KV memory reduction in multi-tenant serving.

title: Alveolar bulb capacitors: narrow neck with stacked spherical sacs
idea: Like lung alveoli hiding huge area behind a narrow airway, etch a modest 25:1 hole through alternating doped/undoped Si layers, then use a dopant-selective isotropic etch to inflate spherical sacs at each sensitive layer before ALD electrode/dielectric lining, forming a necklace of alveoli on one neck.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 2-3x electrode area versus a straight pillar of the same AR, giving target Cs with a far easier etch.
note: Bottle-trench lineage; multiple bulbs per neck need ALD to pass the neck without pinch-off.

title: Sodium-potassium pump: a 2T cell whose own feedback stays charged
idea: Neurons hold resting potential with a continuous pump; add a second vertical transistor per cell whose gate is the storage node and which feeds a weak bias rail back into the node, sized so its subthreshold current at '1' exceeds the node's 125 C leakage while at '0' it stays below the leak to ground, making the cell quasi-static.
why: Refresh-free at 125 C with one extra transistor (far cheaper than 6T SRAM) and stackable in vertical tiers; removes refresh power and bank blocking for automotive/industrial memory.
note: Feedback-held gain cell; subthreshold ratio margins across billions of cells at 125 C are the doubt. Testable on MPW.

title: Osteoclast sealed-zone catalytic etching of capacitor holes
idea: Osteoclasts dissolve bone by sealing a tiny compartment and pumping acid into it. Form storage-node holes by metal-assisted chemical etching: a patterned Ag or Cu catalyst dot burrows straight down through a sacrificial silicon or SiGe mold in dilute HF/H2O2 on a wet bench, then the mold is oxidized or replaced, so no long C4F6/C4F8 plasma etch is needed.
why: The HAR capacitor etch is the biggest fluorocarbon-gas and etch-tool-time sink; catalytic etching reaches 100:1+ on cheap wet benches, cutting high-GWP perfluorocarbons and etch capital.

title: Morpho-wing interference lithography prints the periodic cell array maskless
idea: Morpho scales make color by multilayer interference; the DRAM array is a perfect lattice, so expose active, buried-wordline and storage-node layers with 3- or 6-beam 193 nm immersion interference (~70 nm pitch hexagonal lattice, near-zero roughness), then one spacer doubling to ~35 nm. Array edges are trimmed and periphery printed afterwards with a cheap ArF mask.
why: Moves 3-4 of the 5-7 EUV array exposures onto a laser-and-optics bench costing ~1/20 of an EUV scanner (fact 4); est. 15-20% lower wafer cost and a large capex cut.

title: Nacre-style perovskite nanosheet tiling gives room-temperature k~200 dielectrics
idea: Nacre is brick-and-mortar layering; tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr-niobate nanosheets (k 200+ at ~2 nm) by Langmuir-Blodgett or electrophoretic layer-by-layer deposition, with a one-molecule polycation 'mortar' between bricks, from water dispersions below 100 C in a dip tool.
why: k~200 vs ~40 for ZrO2 stacks roughly quadruples charge per area (fact 1, target k~70), cutting capacitor height ~3-4x; dip tools cost <1/10 of ALD clusters.

title: Magnetotactic self-registration aligns HBM dies without precision bonders
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria align magnetosome chains to a field; electroplate a coded pattern of CoFe nanomagnet dots on each die backside and a matching soft-magnetic pattern on the target, float dies on a thin fluid film in a uniform field so they snap into <200 nm registration, then bond the whole batch in one anneal.
why: Replaces serial thermo-compression and hybrid bonders (~$3-5M each, ~1k units/hour) with batch self-assembly for HBM stacks (fact 6); est. 10x stacking throughput and ~80% less bonding capex.
note: Self-alignment known; <200 nm registration for hybrid bond is the test.

title: Kanerva sparse distributed memory replaces per-token KV slots
idea: Instead of one slot per token, keys are written into a fixed set of hard locations activated within a Hamming radius and values are superposed into counters there (Kanerva's cerebellum-inspired SDM); retrieval reads the activated locations, so memory grows with information content, not sequence length.
why: Long-context KV: a fixed 64 MB memory serving million-token contexts approximately.

title: Wood-frog cryogenic gain cells: mature fabs at 77 K
idea: Wood frogs freeze solid and resume life on thawing. Capacitorless gain-cell memory runs at 77 K in LN2-immersed AI racks, where subthreshold leakage falls by orders of magnitude and retention reaches hours, so older-node fabs can make effectively refresh-free memory.
why: Removes refresh (16-33% of idle power) and lets 65-28 nm fabs compete; cooling cost is partly offset.
note: Cryo-DRAM studied; old-node gain cells at 77K testable cheaply; cooling overhead is the doubt.

title: Kinematic-coupling self-alignment for cheap fine-pitch die stacking
idea: Use precision-optics kinematic mounts (three balls in three V-grooves): etch inverted pyramids into the base die and tapered posts on each tier die so dies settle into sub-50 nm registration by geometry during fluid-assisted placement, letting fast coarse pick-and-place feed fine-pitch hybrid bonding.
why: Stacking capital and throughput (facts 4, 6): replaces $10M-class high-precision die-to-wafer bonders with fast placement plus self-alignment; claims 5-10x bonding throughput.
note: Geometric/fluidic self-alignment known; sub-50 nm registration with pyramids is the claim to prove.

title: E-paper bistability: antiferroelectric cell read nondestructively by capacitance
idea: Like e-paper holding an image unpowered, use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor with asymmetric electrodes whose built-in bias keeps it stable in either the AFE or field-induced FE phase, then read with a 50 mV AC probe of differential capacitance (the phases differ ~2x), disturbing neither state, so no restore and no refresh.
why: Destructive read and refresh (facts 3, 8): no full-swing restore, no refresh; claims >10x lower read energy (50 mV probe vs ~1 V restore).
note: Built-in-bias AFE NV memory exists; small-signal C contrast and ZrO2 endurance are key unknowns.

title: Low-E glass tin oxide templates high-k rutile capacitor dielectric
idea: Architectural low-E and solar glass is coated with fluorine-doped tin oxide, a conductive rutile-structure oxide. Use ALD F:SnO2 or Sb:SnO2 as the storage-node electrode liner so TiO2 nucleates directly in the rutile phase (k ~80-100) below 400 C, replacing ZrO2/HfO2 stacks (k ~40) and the Ru electrodes normally needed for rutile templating.
why: Fact 1 says more charge needs k ~70; doubling k gives ~2x Cs or ~40% shorter pillars (less HAR etch) using only Sn, Ti and O, with no hafnium or ruthenium.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor anodizing grows self-ordered 100:1 storage holes
idea: Borrowed from aluminum electrolytic capacitor foils and AAO filters, which self-organize hexagonal pores with AR >1000 just by anodizing aluminum in acid. Deposit thick Al over the cell array, seed pores on the landing-pad lattice by shallow pre-patterning, anodize straight down to any depth, then ALD electrode and dielectric into the alumina template.
why: Facts 1/4: the high-AR capacitor etch is the costliest array step; anodizing is a room-temperature wet bath with no plasma tool and no aspect-ratio-dependent etch slowdown. Pore ordering at <40 nm pitch is the risk.

title: Shingled zones for heaps: tenured objects append to zoned NV
idea: Like shingled-magnetic-recording drives writing bands sequentially, a generational garbage collector keeps the nursery in DRAM and promotes survivors by appending them to zoned persistent flash; reclaiming a zone copies live objects forward, matching NAND erase-block physics.
why: The tenured generation is most of a managed heap and rarely written; moves 60-80% of heap bytes from DRAM onto durable media.
note: Reading tenured objects from flash costs tens of us; NVM-aware GC has prior work.

title: Solera optimizer: staggered moment updates live in persistent flash
idea: Like a sherry solera where only a fraction of each barrel is drawn and topped up per cycle, keep Adam's first and second moments in persistent CXL flash and update only a rotating 1/k slice per step (the rest use slightly stale moments), bounding NV write rate and wear while weights stay in HBM.
why: Optimizer state is 2-3x weight size in training; moves it to durable cheap media and doubles as continuous checkpointing.
note: ZeRO-Infinity-like offload; staggered stale moments bound flash wear, convergence impact unknown.

title: Bell Labs 1952 ferroelectric matrix revived with square-loop HZO superlattices
idea: The first ferroelectric memories (BaTiO3 crystal matrices, 1952) were transistor-free passive crosspoints that died of half-select disturb because their loops were not square. Revive the passive matrix with nucleation-limited HfZrO/ZrO2 superlattices whose Al2O3 pinning planes make switching probability at V/3 <1e-12 per pulse while full V switches in 10 ns, stacking 8 passive decks in BEOL.
why: No access device and 8 decks give ~4F2/8 effective cell, ~5-10x bits per mask (Facts 2, 4); non-volatile so no refresh (Fact 3); still destructive read with write-back.
note: Square-loop superlattices vs half-select disturb is the key bet; destructive read and long-line sensing remain.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina as a litho-free capacitor template
idea: Revive Keller's 1950s porous-alumina work and Masuda's 1995 two-step anodization: aluminium e-beam evaporated over the bitline layer (no Ar sputtering) is anodized in oxalic or sulfuric acid into hexagonally ordered pores at 40-60 nm pitch and >100:1 AR, registered to landing pads by a shallow imprinted pit pattern. Pores are lined by N2-purged ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN to form capacitors.
why: Facts 1 and 4: removes the capacitor-hole SAQP/EUV patterning and the high-AR plasma etch (~2 critical layers, ~10 steps) with a room-temperature wet tool and no rare gas; AR >100 gives Cs >=8 fF. Risks are pore defects and pad registration.

title: Drum optimum-programming assembler that fills every opened DRAM row
idea: Port the IBM 650 SOAP idea (place each word where the drum will be when it is needed) to DRAM rows: a placement pass lays out embedding rows, sparse KV blocks and gather targets so bytes consumed together by one kernel share one 1-2 KB row, keeping re-transposed copies per consumer when reuse justifies it. The memory controller then replays a compile-time row schedule instead of reacting to random requests.
why: Fact 8 (128x overfetch, ~5.9 pJ per useful bit): raising useful bytes per activation from ~1/128 to ~1/4 cuts random-access energy 10-30x and frees channel bandwidth, so fewer DRAM devices meet the same throughput.
note: Compile-time co-location raises row hit rates; data-dependent gathers limit gains.

title: Bell Labs 1952 ferroelectric matrix read by small-signal capacitance
idea: Revive Anderson's transistor-less ferroelectric crossbar in sputtered HZO or sol-gel PZT, but read it without switching: a small AC probe senses the polarization-dependent capacitance (the C-V butterfly asymmetry, enhanced by an imprint layer), so reads are non-destructive and fatigue-free, and V/3 biasing limits half-select disturb on rare writes.
why: A transistor-free 4F^2 stackable crossbar with unlimited reads and no restore holds read-mostly AI data outside DRAM, built with ALD/sputter and two metal layers.

title: Goto's Parametron Revived as Resonant Charge-Recovery DRAM Wordline Drivers
idea: Revive Eiichi Goto's 1954 parametron (resonant LC circuits that ran Japan's PC-1 computer) as on-package inductor tanks that swing DRAM wordlines and bitline groups sinusoidally over a ~10 ns window and return their charge to the tank instead of dumping it to ground, recovering 80-90% of CV2.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): CV2 on ~3 V wordlines and ~1 V bitlines dominates array energy; adiabatic recovery gives ~5-10x lower array energy per access; a periphery-only change licensable to every existing DRAM fab.

title: Matsushita 1995 Charge-Recycling Bus Revived for Memory I/O
idea: Revive Matsushita's mid-1990s charge-recycling bus, which stacked N bus lanes in series voltage domains so charge drained from one lane powers the next: stack 8 DQ lanes between VDDQ and ground so each swings VDDQ/8 and the same charge is reused eight times.
why: I/O energy per bit drops ~8-10x on DDR/LPDDR interfaces (fact 5: 10-20 pJ/bit for DDR5); periphery-only change usable by every DRAM maker.
note: Stacked-domain signaling known; VDDQ/8 swings face noise on off-package channels.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor parked at its field-induced transition knee
idea: Invert 'the capacitor dielectric operates linearly around zero bias' -> park it on a phase transition. A ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is DC-biased by the plate line to the edge of its AFE-to-FE transition, where dP/dE (effective k) is 5-10x the linear value, and data is stored as a small +/- swing around that knee.
why: Recovers the k~70 regime fact 1 demands, so ~5 fF fits at AR ~20-30 instead of 60-75 using existing HfZrO ALD; risks are hysteresis loss, temperature drift of the knee and fatigue.
note: Same AFE bias-at-transition mechanism.

title: Anodized aluminum nanopore capacitors replace plasma-etched silicon pillars
idea: Invert 'HAR capacitors must be plasma-etched into a silicon wafer' -> let electrochemistry grow them on aluminum. Anodizing an aluminum plate self-organizes hexagonal pores (~40-60 nm pitch, AR 100+) in minutes; ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines each pore as a cup capacitor, the aluminum is the common plate and heat spreader, and oxide-TFT access and wiring are built on the planarized top.
why: Delivers AR >100, past fact 1's AR-115 regime, with no HAR plasma etch, no EUV and no quartz-crucible silicon, cutting capacitor-module capex >10x; pore-to-TFT registration is handled by pre-patterned anodization seeds or several pores per cell.
note: AAO-templated MIM capacitors known; pore-to-access-transistor registration at cell pitch is the doubt.

title: Anodized aluminum capacitor forest: 1000:1 aspect ratio for free
idea: Inverts 'high-aspect-ratio capacitors need costly etch': anodize thick aluminum to self-organize vertical pores at ~40-60 nm pitch and ~1000:1 aspect ratio, then ALD-line them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN, giving tens of fF per cell so that cheap, leaky TFT access devices still retain for seconds.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) without deep RIE or EUV and lets low-cost leaky access meet retention (fact 3); stacked with TFT tiers, claimed ~100x cost/GB; trade-off is larger pitch and slower bitline sensing.
note: AAO-templated MIM nanocapacitors known; extreme height and slow sensing limit density gains.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as a registration-free capacitor forest
idea: Inverts 'each capacitor must be etched and aligned 1:1 to its transistor.' Anodize an Al film into self-ordered nanopores (AR>100, ~25-40 nm pitch), line them with TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN by ALD, and bond the layer so each landing pad randomly contacts several pores; pad area, not alignment, sets Cs.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR>100 capacitors with no deep plasma etch and no EUV capacitor mask; only Al, O, Ti, N.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell with back-gate lockout
idea: Inverts 'oxide-semiconductor cells need indium and gallium': a 2T gain cell of amorphous Zn-Sn-O whose write transistor has a back gate held at about -2 V in standby, pushing off-current toward 1e-23 A so retention exceeds the data's useful life (target >1 year at 85 C) and refresh is removed.
why: Zero refresh; no indium (China ~60%) or gallium (China ~98%); sputtered and stackable at <400 C over logic.
note: Negative back-gate standby to suppress off-current is plausible; 1e-23 A and >1 year at 85 C is aggressive.

title: Short-loop CCD memory: charge shifts instead of transistors
idea: Inverts 'each bit needs its own access transistor and contact'. Store bits as charge packets in 64-stage recirculating CCD loops with spacer-defined overlapping poly gates; a loop is randomly addressed and streamed out in ~64 x 1 ns, and recirculation doubles as refresh.
why: No cell contacts, capacitor module or leakage-tail access transistors (facts 1, 3); ~2F2 per bit at spacer-defined gate pitch from 180 nm litho; latency is loop-length-bound.

title: Weight radio: one DRAM read broadcast to 32 accelerators
idea: Inverts 'every accelerator needs its own copy of the weights': many small inference cards march in lockstep through the same layer while one shared DDR4 pool streams each weight tile once over a multicast fabric built from existing 28 nm FPGAs and SerDes. Each card applies the tile to its own batch.
why: Weight DRAM drops N-fold (e.g., 32x) across a pod, using trailing-node accelerators and legacy DRAM.
note: Lockstep across cards hard; batching already amortizes weight reads.

title: Harvest LPDDR from recycled phones onto CXL cards
idea: Inverts 'consumer device memory dies with the device': e-waste recyclers desolder LPDDR4/4X packages from phones and laptops, reball and burn them in, and mount them on CXL cards with 28 nm controllers for slow capacity tiers.
why: Billions of retired devices hold 4-12 GB each, an exabyte-scale stranded bit supply that needs only existing OSAT lines and trailing-node controllers.
note: Real stranded supply but PoP desoldering, aging LPDDR4 reliability and recovery rates limit it.

title: Cloud noisy-RAM tier for inference weights at a discount
idea: Inverts 'all memory bits must be equal': clouds sell a cheaper memory tier for model weights and KV caches on 1%-raw-BER DRAM; models get noise-injection fine-tuning, and sign and exponent bits sit in a small ECC-protected region.
why: Supply allocation: puts the largest new demand (AI inference) on memory that would otherwise be scrapped, freeing perfect DRAM elsewhere; ~20-40% lower cost per bit for that tier.
note: Approximate-DRAM idea applied to LLM weights; easy to simulate with injected errors.

title: Self-dissolving silver nanocluster bit with designed one-second lifetime
idea: In an RT-sputtered SiOxNy:Ag diffusive layer, a write pulse nucleates a sub-2 nm Ag bridge that conducts ~uA. Gibbs-Thomson surface energy then dissolves it with tau set by cluster size and matrix diffusivity, designed at ~1 s, and refresh rewrites it.
why: Dissolution kinetics replace capacitor leakage as the retention clock, with a uA gain-like read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1). Avoids permanent oxygen-vacancy damage, targeting 1e10+ endurance versus ReRAM's ~1e6.
note: Diffusive Ag memristors exist; endurance and variability at 1e15 refresh-rewrite cycles is the doubt.

title: On-die microheaters re-anneal worn cells every few hours at 350 C
idea: Embed a TiN heater serpentine under each memory mat. After ~1e10 cycles, migrate the mat's data and pulse it to ~350 C for ~10 ms to anneal out generated traps, vacancy clusters, ferroelectric imprint and MTJ barrier defects; the temperature stays inside the BEOL budget, so it heals without damage.
why: Converts finite-endurance elements (ferroelectric, ReRAM, charge-trap at 1e8-1e11 cycles) into effectively unlimited endurance, making them DRAM-class. Heater-based self-healing has been shown for NAND.
note: Heater anneal known for NAND; whether it reverses FE/ReRAM fatigue is open.

title: Image-sensor foundry dark pixels as long-retention memory cells
idea: CMOS image sensors fight exactly DRAM's leakage physics (SRH generation) and win: pinned photodiodes reach dark currents of ~1-10 electrons/s (~1e-18 A), against DRAM's 13 fA tail. Tape out a $200-300k MPW in a CIS process with light-shielded 4T pixels repurposed as memory. The pinned diode stores ~5,000 electrons written by fill-and-spill through the transfer gate, the transfer gate is the access device, and the floating diffusion with source follower gives a gain readout.
why: ~1e4x lower leakage means minutes of retention at room temperature. The tapeout is a cheap testbed for pinned-storage-node physics in future DRAM cells and a refresh-free macro for U.S. CIS lines (fact 3, U.S. manufacturability).
note: Same CIS pinned-well cell with concrete MPW plan.

title: Dopant-selective porous silicon replaces SiGe sacrificial layers in 3D DRAM
idea: SiGe/Si superlattices are strain-limited (mismatch accumulates, capping ~60-100 tiers) and need germanium. Grow a zero-mismatch superlattice of p+ (1e19 B) and lightly doped Si below 600 C, then anodize in HF: holes concentrate in p+ layers, turning only them into mesoporous Si (>100:1 selectivity), which is oxidized into inter-tier isolation.
why: No strain ceiling, so 200+ crystalline-Si tiers come from one epi run and one wet step: >=10x density at roughly today's wafer cost, with no germanium (China ~60%+).
note: Strain-free superlattice; doubts are lateral anodization contact through deep slits and boron interdiffusion.

title: Lattice-coded analog charge stores ten bits across three gain cells
idea: Thermal noise on a gain-cell node is sqrt(kT/C) ~2 mV against a ~1 V window, so Shannon allows ~8 bits per cell; drift and variation eat most of it, but coding 10 bits as one point in a 3-cell lattice (vector quantization, decoded at read) averages variation, and non-destructive reads allow verify-and-trim writes.
why: 3.3 bits/cell x 3 stacked oxide decks = ~10x bits per area at the same wafer cost; scarce material per bit falls ~10x.
note: Retention drift on oxide gain-cell nodes is the key doubt for 3+ bits/cell.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as capacitor molds
idea: First principle: high-AR plasma etch fights ion angular spread and neutral transport, but anodic Al2O3 pores grow by field-assisted dissolution at a pitch set by voltage (~2.5 nm/V) and keep going to any depth. Deposit ~3 um of Al over the storage-node contacts, seed pits with one imprint aligned to the contacts, and anodize at low voltage so the pores self-propagate straight down to AR >150:1; then line them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN by ALD.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and etch capex: no capacitor-hole mask and no high-AR mold etch; AR 150:1 at the same pitch gives ~2x Cs.
note: AAO nanocapacitors known; low-voltage pore order and barrier removal are the risks.

title: Learned activation codecs inside the memory interface die
idea: Activations lie on low-dimensional manifolds, carrying far less information than 16 bits x width. Put a per-layer trained transform plus vector quantizer and entropy coder in the HBM/CXL base die so tensors are stored as 8-16x smaller codes and expanded on read, with error budgets set by training loss.
why: 10-30x effective capacity alone and ~100x when codes live on a NAND tier; trades accuracy and codec latency.
note: KV/activation VQ known in software; base-die placement is the twist; 10-30x optimistic.

title: Decoupled access chiplet runs the address stream microseconds ahead
idea: Latency hurts only when addresses are known late, and most programs compute addresses from a small slice of their code. Compile that address slice onto a tiny access-processor chiplet that runs ~10 us ahead of the main core, issuing loads to a slow SLC-NAND or far-memory tier so data lands in a queue just in time.
why: Hides microsecond latency for irregular but computable access (graphs, sparse), so media at ~1% of DRAM price acts as working memory; trades slip penalties on data-dependent branches.
note: Run-ahead to NAND fails on pointer-chasing dependencies; works for computable address streams.

title: Lottery drum: tier-randomized row placement re-keyed every refresh window
idea: A lottery drum reshuffles before every draw: in a 3D or stacked DRAM, a keyed permutation maps logically consecutive rows to physically non-adjacent rows in different tiers, and the key rotates every 32 ms window as refresh migrates rows through a small spare region. A hammer pattern cannot keep hitting the same physical neighbors, and the DDR5/HBM command set and timing are untouched.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): targeted multi-sided attacks lose physical adjacency; effective threshold up 10-100x with no controller change.
note: Twist on RRS/SRS row-swap defenses riding on refresh; full re-keying each window costs bandwidth.

title: Seashell: calcium titanate capacitor dielectric from two abundant elements
idea: Stimulus 'seashell' (calcium carbonate) -> make the capacitor dielectric from calcium, the 5th most abundant element: ALD CaTiO3 (k ~150-180) with Al-doped grain boundaries, crystallized at low temperature on a seed layer between TiN or MoN electrodes.
why: Reaches the k >= 70 needed to beat the capacitor charge wall without hafnium, zirconium, strontium or ruthenium; Ca and Ti are geologically unlimited.

title: Beach sand: MoO2 rutile template grows k-100 TiO2 without ruthenium
idea: Stimulus 'beach sand' (rutile and ilmenite grains) -> use conductive rutile-structured MoO2 from abundant U.S. molybdenum as the bottom electrode so ALD TiO2 grows epitaxially in the rutile phase (k ~100) at low temperature, as it does on RuO2, with Al doping to curb leakage.
why: Delivers the k >= 70 the capacitor wall demands while removing both ruthenium and hafnium; Ti and Mo are abundant and U.S.-sourced.
note: Rutile TiO2 leakage remains the core problem even if MoO2 templates the phase.

title: Toaster: millisecond flash-lamp anneals stack 32 ferroelectric tiers monolithically
idea: Random stimulus 'pop-up toaster' (brief surface heat) -> each newly deposited HZO tier is crystallized by a 1-20 ms xenon flash or laser that heats only the top ~100 nm to >600 C while buried tiers and CMOS stay <400 C. This enables monolithic 32-tier FeRAM/FeFET stacking in BEOL.
why: Non-volatile 3D memory without wafer bonding. Density per litho area scales with tier count, and wafer cost per bit falls ~5-10x at 32 tiers.

title: Interlibrary loan: one shared weight copy serving sixteen hosts
idea: Like libraries lending one rare book, place a single read-only copy of popular model weights behind a CXL 3 switch, mapped read-only into 8-16 inference hosts that each keep only a hot-layer cache; an epoch counter replaces coherence traffic because the data is immutable.
why: Inference farms replicate the same 100-800 GB of weights per host; sharing cuts weight DRAM 8-16x per pod at +100-200 ns access hidden by layer prefetch.

title: Antiferroelectric-knee capacitor biased onto ZrO2's steep switching branch
idea: Box = {medium: field-induced polarization in antiferroelectric ZrO2 | access: vertical-channel Si FET | sense: standard charge-share SA | integration: 1T1C with a short pillar | substrate: 300 mm Si | fab: ALD ZrO2/Al2O3 nanolaminate}. The cell plate is DC-biased just below the AFE-to-FE critical field so the +/-0.5 V node swing rides the steep double-hysteresis branch, where dQ/dV equals an effective k of ~100-150; the cell runs minor loops and never reaches full remanent switching, which limits fatigue.
why: Fact 1 capacitor charge wall: 3-5x charge per area lets pillar AR fall from ~70:1 to ~20:1, removing the hardest etch and allowing a tighter pitch.
note: Hysteresis loss and fatigue at 1e15 minor-loop cycles are open.

title: Proton-transfer organic ferroelectric (croconic acid) as low-voltage polar bit
idea: Box = {medium: polarization from collective proton hopping along hydrogen bonds in croconic acid | access: Si FET | sense: FeFET threshold shift | integration: vapor-deposited BEOL layer | substrate: Si | fab: low-temperature thermal evaporation}. Switching moves only protons by ~1 angstrom inside hydrogen bonds, with no heavy-ion motion, which gives coercive fields far below hafnia and lets the layer be deposited below 150 C over finished logic.
why: Voltage floor (Fact 10) and BEOL stacking: sub-1 V nonvolatile switching, and the tiny thermal budget lets many tiers stack.
note: Croconic acid film thermal stability and retention under later BEOL steps unproven.

title: Imprint-engineered HZO capacitor read nondestructively by small-signal capacitance
idea: Box = {medium: polarization in a deliberately imprinted HZO capacitor | access: Si FET | sense: ~100 mV small-signal capacitance read (butterfly asymmetry) | integration: 1T1C over periphery | substrate: Si | fab: asymmetric TiN/conductive-oxide electrodes set a built-in imprint}. The imprint shifts the C-V butterfly so the two polarization states differ by ~30% in capacitance at 0 V, and the read senses that difference without switching, so reads never wear the ferroelectric.
why: Fact 8 and endurance: no destructive read or restore; the ferroelectric cycles only on writes, so a write-buffering cache makes endurance a non-issue.

title: Mist-CVD gallium oxide access TFT over stacked capacitor
idea: Box: stacked MIM cap x beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) thin-film access transistor x conventional latch SA x BEOL-over-CMOS x Si wafer x atmospheric mist-CVD at <450C. The wide-bandgap channel suppresses thermal generation so off-current falls toward ~1e-20 A/um, and mist-CVD needs no vacuum tool and no indium.
why: Attacks refresh (fact 3): retention moves from 64 ms toward minutes, cutting refresh energy/bandwidth >100x; In-free, low-capex, US-buildable deposition.

title: Anodic alumina nanopore templates host ultra-high-aspect capacitor arrays
idea: Box [MIM cap in anodic alumina pores | Si access below | voltage SA | capacitor layer over storage contacts | e-beam-evaporated Al film (vacuum, no gas) | two-step oxalic-acid anodization guided by NIL dimples]: anodize a 3 um Al film into self-ordered 25-40 nm pores registered to imprinted dimples, wet-open the barrier oxide, and deposit TiN/dielectric/TiN inside.
why: Capacitor charge wall and etch intensity: AR 100-200 holes cost about as much as a plating bath, with no fluorocarbon etch and no rare gases; Al is abundant and US-made.
note: AAO capacitors known in labs; registration, sub-40nm pitch uniformity and ALD lining at AR>100 are the doubts.

title: Monolayer doping forms damage-free access-transistor junctions
idea: Box [standard cap | RCAT Si with molecular-monolayer-doped junctions | standard | standard | Si | allylboronic or allylphosphonate SAM + oxide cap + N2 spike anneal]: replace beamline implants at the storage-node junction with self-assembled dopant molecules driven in by RTP, giving abrupt sub-5 nm junctions with no implant point defects.
why: Implant damage seeds the trap-assisted leakage tail; damage-free junctions could cut tail GIDL ~3-10x, which means less refresh, and remove implanter plasma-flood gas use.

title: Green DPSS laser zone-melting builds single-crystal tiers for 3D DRAM
idea: Box [lateral cap | crystalline-Si transistor per tier | voltage SA | monolithic 3D tiers | deposited a-Si on SiO2 with Si seed vias | 532 nm diode-pumped laser lateral zone melt in vacuum]: melt each deposited a-Si tier in narrow scanning lines that carry crystal orientation laterally out of the seed vias, giving near-single-crystal islands with no excimer (XeCl) laser and no epi.
why: 3D DRAM needs 26+ crystalline tiers: this avoids SiGe/Ge epi superlattices and rare-gas excimer lasers, at a per-tier cost of one laser scan.
note: Thermal budget on lower tiers and grain control.

title: Memory-efficient device certification with per-GB-avoided credits
idea: Box: demand reallocation × consumer OS and procurement × device SKU × certification × zram + app freeze-to-flash + shared web engine. Phones and laptops that pass a responsiveness benchmark with less DRAM earn a label and a per-GB-avoided credit funded by datacenter buyers.
why: Consumer devices take roughly half of DRAM bits; a 25% trim there frees ~10% of world supply for servers without building anything, so no fluorinated chemistry.

title: Po: bitline capacitance is negative — active NIC cancellation
idea: Po: a bitline that pretends to be shorter. A small positive-feedback negative-impedance converter (cross-coupled Si MOS pair driving a coupling capacitor) at the bitline end synthesizes about -0.5 Cb during charge sharing, so the cell sees half the load and develops ~2x the voltage signal.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and periphery (#7): ~2x signal, or Cs ~50% lower, or twice the cells per bitline (half the SA strips), with plain Si CMOS and no exotic dielectric.

title: Retention-graded tiers where data expires before it decays
idea: Po: memory that forgets on purpose. Build a 3D stack whose tiers are designed for graded, guaranteed retention (e.g., 50 ms, 2 s, 60 s via channel material and capacitor size), expose each tier's expiry in the address map, and have the allocator tag every buffer with a lifetime so activations, KV pages and gradients land in a tier that outlives them; refresh circuitry is omitted.
why: Refresh (fact 3): removes the ~46 fJ/bit refresh, 16-33% of idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss, plus refresh logic area.
note: Echoes refresh-free eDRAM for short-lived DNN data (RANA); guaranteeing retention against the leakage tail is the crux.

title: Weight carousel: weights exist only in transit around an accelerator ring
idea: Po: the weights have no home. Model layers circulate continuously around an optical ring of accelerators; each node holds only a two-layer sliding window and applies it to its resident batch as the layer passes (data stays, weights move), so the cluster keeps one in-flight copy instead of one replica per data-parallel group.
why: Data-parallel inference replicates weights N times; the carousel cuts per-node weight memory roughly 20-60x for 80-layer models, trading DRAM for optical link bandwidth (fact 5).

title: Predictive line coding: memory stores only what it could not guess
idea: Po: memory that lies, then gets corrected. A tiny predictor in the memory controller guesses each 64 B line from address neighbors and a per-page learned context (strides, pointer bases, float exponents); DRAM stores only the residual, which is near-zero for most lines and packed into variable-size slots, like inter-frame video coding for RAM.
why: 2-4x effective capacity on heaps and tensors where generic LZ gets ~1.5x; attacks cost per bit with no new cell.

title: Nearest-neighbor KV residuals: store only how this prompt differs
idea: Po: every conversation is a rerun of another one. Incoming context is matched by embedding search to the closest cached context; its KV is stored as a low-bit quantized residual against that reference KV, extending prefix caching to near-duplicate, non-prefix content (templated documents, RAG chunks, code files).
why: Near-duplicate context is common in enterprise RAG/code workloads; residual coding could cut KV memory 3-8x beyond exact prefix sharing.
note: Non-prefix KV depends on preceding context and position; CacheBlend-style reuse is prior art.

title: Stretch refresh until the raw error rate reaches 1%
idea: Po: memory that never refreshes on time. With 1% BER tolerated, the refresh window is set at the 1% quantile of the retention distribution (typically seconds) instead of the 64 ms dictated by the 1e-9 tail, and every refresh passes through the decoder as a scrub.
why: Refresh (fact 3): ~10-30x fewer refreshes, recovering 10-20% bandwidth and 15-30% of idle power at 32-64 Gb densities.

title: Antiferroelectric charge-step capacitor that pins voltage against leakage
idea: Worsen: demand ever more charge from a linear dielectric, forcing AR 115:1 pillars. Flip: use an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich HZO film with the plate biased so a stored '1' sits just above the AFE-to-FE transition; the switching charge adds ~2-3x Q per area, and as leakage pulls the node down the film releases bound charge, creating a voltage plateau that stretches retention.
why: Fact 1 charge wall: the same Cs at AR ~25-30:1 instead of 60-75:1; the plateau effect could roughly double retention time (fact 3).
note: Leakage-induced AFE plateau extending retention is a fresh twist on AFE capacitor work.

title: NAND-resident KV cache with in-flash top-k selection
idea: Worsen: keep the whole multi-million-token KV cache in HBM. Flip: put KV on NAND and give each flash die a tiny dot-product engine that scores keys against the query in place, returning only the top 1% of KV pairs to the GPU for exact attention.
why: Cost: KV at about $0.05/GB in flash vs HBM at about $20/GB, so 100-400x; trades approximate (top-k) attention and higher latency.

title: Expert-major batching streams MoE experts from QLC
idea: Worsen: keep every expert of a trillion-parameter MoE resident in HBM. Flip: store experts on QLC flash and reorder the token queue expert-major, so each expert is read from flash once per large batch and applied to every waiting token before being discarded.
why: Cost: expert weights at $0.04/GB vs $20/GB HBM, 100x+ cheaper capacity; trades per-request latency for batch throughput.

title: Tuareg sealed jar: Ga2O3 gain cell patterned through stencil masks
idea: A Tuareg potter seals water in a jar so none seeps out. A 2-transistor gain cell uses sputtered amorphous Ga2O3 channels (4.8 eV gap) with off-currents of ~1e-22 A, so charge stays for days. Reusable silicon-nitride stencil masks pattern the BEOL array, so those layers need no resist, develop, strip or post-etch clean.
why: Days of retention all but switches off refresh (fact 3), with a wider gap than IGZO. Stencil patterning removes the litho-track and wet-strip water for the storage layers, cutting UPW by more than 10x.
note: Ga2O3 gain cell is an IGZO twist; stencil masks cannot resolve DRAM pitch.

title: Detector physicist's charge amplifier: virtual-ground bitlines grab all charge
idea: Silicon-strip detectors read femtocoulombs with a charge-sensitive amplifier that holds the electrode at virtual ground. A feedback amplifier (shared by 4-8 bitlines through a mux) holds the bitline fixed so the whole cell charge lands on a ~1 fF feedback capacitor instead of sharing with ~50 fF of bitline.
why: Transfer ratio rises from ~0.1 to ~0.9, a 5-10x larger signal: ~1 fF cells without tall pillars, or 4x longer bitlines (facts 1, 2, 7).
note: Virtual-ground CSA captures full cell charge; pitch area and settling speed of shared amplifier.

title: Alien without lithography grows pores: anodized-alumina capacitor forest
idea: An alien that never invented lithography would grow the array. Anodize a 3-5 um sputtered Al film over CMOS so hexagonal self-ordered pores form at 25-60 nm pitch and >100:1 aspect ratio. Imprinted dimples at landing sites pin each pore over its transistor, and the pores are lined by ALD to become coaxial capacitors.
why: Reaches the AR ~115 that Fact 1 calls for with a wet electrochemical step instead of high-AR plasma etch; the capacitor layer needs no critical masks.
note: AAO capacitors known; anodizing over CMOS and pore registration.

title: Home renovator's second storey: post-CMOS capacitor tier on foundry logic
idea: Like adding a storey to a finished house, buy MPW logic wafers laid out as 1T1C access arrays with exposed top-metal landing pads. In a university cleanroom, add 3 masks: 5 um oxide, holes, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN capacitors.
why: Puts eDRAM-class memory on any logic node without the foundry offering it, ~3-4x denser than SRAM. Capex fits a 10-person team (U.S. manufacturability).
note: Very demo-able with MPW plus cleanroom; logic-transistor leakage and coarse post-processing litho cap density.

title: Biologist's self-ordering pores: anodic alumina as capacitor molds
idea: Diatoms grow perfect hexagonal pores with no blueprint. Deposit thick aluminum over the array, pre-dimple it with a coarse imprint, and anodize: pores self-order into a hexagonal lattice at ~30-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios beyond 200:1, which become the mold for cylinder capacitors (ALD electrode/high-k/electrode inside), with the alumina stripped or kept as a mechanical support.
why: Replaces the capacitor-hole litho layer and the $10M+ high-AR plasma etch with a wet bath; AR >115 attacks the charge wall (fact 1) and capex at once. Risks: registering pores to landing pads, and opening the barrier at the pore bottom.

title: Termite's chemical tunneling: metal-assisted chemical etching of capacitor holes
idea: A biologist watching termites tunnel with saliva sees etching without bombardment. Pattern a Ru or Pt catalyst mesh over a sacrificial silicon mold layer and immerse it in HF/H2O2: the catalyst sinks straight down, digging vertical holes beyond 200:1 at room temperature with no plasma; the catalyst is removed and the holes are lined with electrode/high-k/electrode.
why: Replaces cryogenic/high-AR plasma etchers (~$10-15M each, the slowest step in the flow) with a wet bench, and reaches the AR ~115 needed for >6 fF (fact 1). Risks: catalyst wandering, metal contamination, and stopping exactly on landing pads.

title: Mapmaker's zoom levels: bit-plane tiering of tensors across memory tiers
idea: A mapmaker never prints every street at world scale. Weights and KV are stored transposed into bit-planes: the top 3-4 planes live in HBM and the low-order planes in CXL DRAM or flash. Matmuls run on the coarse planes first and fetch fine planes only for rows whose partial results sit near a decision boundary, such as attention top-k or softmax peaks.
why: Most scores are decided by the MSBs, so HBM capacity per model drops 2-4x and HBM traffic drops roughly in proportion.

title: Cartoon animator's keyframes: video-model activations as keyframes plus sparse deltas
idea: Animators draw keyframes and let assistants fill the in-betweens. In video-generation and world-model serving, full per-frame KV and activations are kept only for keyframes every 8 frames. Other frames store sparse top-k token deltas against the nearest keyframe, since consecutive latents differ in only a few percent of tokens.
why: Video-model memory scales with frames x tokens. A 4-8x reduction makes minute-long generation fit on a single node.

title: Watchmaker's jewel registration: kinematic self-aligned fine-pitch die stacking
idea: Watchmakers seat parts on jewels and pins: etch V-pyramids and pits into the mating die faces and drop in silica micro-spheres so dies self-register kinematically to <200 nm, which allows 1 um hybrid-bond pitch with cheap pick-and-place tools instead of $5M+ bonders.
why: Cuts the capital intensity of advanced stacking while raising bond density 10x, so more memory bandwidth and dies per stack come from cheaper U.S. OSAT lines.
note: Spheres must seat fully recessed for zero-gap hybrid bonding.

title: Pulsed-power antiferroelectric charge release triples DRAM read signal
idea: Pulsed-power capacitors use antiferroelectrics because field-induced polarization dumps large charge on discharge; a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor written to '1' sits in the field-induced polar state and, during charge sharing, back-switches to release ~3-5x the charge of a linear dielectric, while a '0' releases only linear charge. No remanence is used, so fatigue stays modest.
why: Effective k ~100+ during read (fact 1) lets the pillar drop from 70:1 to ~25:1; the '1' level must exceed the ~1.5 MV/cm forward switching field, partly fighting the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: Downhole-grade amorphous Ga2O3 BEOL access transistor
idea: Oil-well electronics survive 200 C with wide-bandgap channels; deposit an amorphous Ga2O3 channel (4.8 eV gap vs IGZO ~3.2 eV) below 400 C as a vertical BEOL access device over the capacitor array. Generation leakage scales roughly as exp(-Eg/2kT), so off-current at 85 C should sit orders of magnitude below IGZO and silicon.
why: Facts 2 and 3: retention of minutes even when hot, so refresh nearly disappears, and the access device moves to low-temperature deposition that stacks in 3D; risk is low mobility (~1-10 cm2/Vs) and contact resistance.

title: Solar-cell economics: metal-assisted wet etching drills AR-200 capacitor holes
idea: Solar wafer makers texture silicon for cents with metal-assisted chemical etching; for DRAM, imprint a silver or platinum catalyst mesh and etch in HF/H2O2 at room temperature, which drills straight silicon holes at AR 200:1 with no plasma, no argon and no helium-cooled chuck. Line the holes with ALD electrode and high-k to form deep trench capacitors in each array tier.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 200 vs 60-75 gives ~2.5x Cs or a 2.5x smaller footprint, and the most expensive plasma etch and its rare gases are removed.
note: Catalyst wander and uniformity at sub-50 nm pitch.

title: Black-silicon solar etch: catalyst-guided holes reach 100:1 without plasma
idea: Black-silicon solar texturing uses metal-assisted chemical etching (MACE): a patterned Ag film sinks into Si in HF/H2O2 and drills straight holes. Pattern a catalyst mesh by e-beam or nanoimprint in a university fab to drill registered 100:1+ trenches for capacitors or vertical channels, then remove the catalyst with iodide etch plus sacrificial oxidation and verify retention.
why: Plasma-free high-AR etch removes fluorocarbon gases, etch-tool capital and chamber parts and reaches the AR ~115 that fact 1 calls for; metal contamination is the key risk.

title: 77K-cooled AI racks let DRAM drop the high-aspect capacitor module
idea: Extreme user: liquid-nitrogen-immersed AI racks. At 77K junction and GIDL leakage fall ~10^4x, so a ~0.5 fF planar MIM (or the access transistor's own gate/junction capacitance) holds data for seconds; the 60-75:1 pillar etch, its support lattice and 2-3 EUV layers disappear and the cell is built on a 28 nm-class logic flow.
why: Capacitor charge wall + capital: removes ~25-30% of front-end steps and the costliest etch/deposition tools; system cost/bit ~-30% even after cooling overhead, and refresh energy nearly vanishes.
note: Retention not the limit at 77K; sense margin with 0.5 fF and cryo overhead are.

title: Memory-hard attacker's pebbling: compiler picks store versus recompute
idea: From attackers who evaluate memory-hard functions in tiny memory using pebbling strategies: a compiler pass solves a red-blue pebble game over any program's dataflow graph (databases, simulations, compilers, not only backprop) to choose per array whether to keep or recompute it, emitting a schedule that meets a declared memory cap.
why: Generalizes activation checkpointing to all software; typical 2-5x peak-memory cut for 10-30% extra compute.
note: Checkmate-style rematerialization generalized; general programs rarely recomputable enough for 2-5x.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 200:1 silicon trench capacitors plasma-free
idea: Scale jump: a few-nm noble-metal catalyst mesh, patterned once, sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2 like a nanoscale drill and opens holes with AR >200:1 without fluorocarbon plasma. This revives trench-capacitor DRAM with the capacitor dug into the substrate beneath a vertical access transistor. The catalyst is stripped in iodide before any thermal step.
why: Bypasses the 60-75:1 mold etch that consumes C4F6/C4F8 PFAS-class gases. Deeper trenches give >10 fF per cell. Metal contamination of the leakage tail is the main risk.
note: Catalyst metal contamination of leakage tail; straightness at 30 nm.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 200:1 capacitor holes in a bath
idea: Replace plasma etch with catalytic wet etch: a patterned Pt mesh sinks into a sacrificial silicon mold in HF/H2O2 over minutes, carving vertical holes >200:1 that are then lined with capacitor films and the mold removed with the catalyst.
why: Breaks the AR wall (Fact 1) with a wet bench costing ~1% of a high-AR etcher; domestic chemicals and tooling.
note: Cheap wet bench; wandering and catalyst contamination at sub-50 nm pitch.

title: Memory whose precision fades with page age
idea: Software tags pages as tolerant (caches, embeddings, KV, media buffers). A memory-controller engine re-quantizes each tolerant page as it ages through epochs of seconds, then minutes, then hours: 16, 8, 4 and finally 2 bits per value, with per-block scales. It releases the frames this frees. Re-access re-promotes the page but cannot restore lost bits, much like the fading of human memory.
why: Tolerant data is 30-60% of the footprint on inference and caching servers. Aging it in time gives 2-4x capacity on those classes.

title: Ramtron FeRAM read without destroying: second-harmonic polarization sensing
idea: Ramtron FeRAM was hobbled by destructive reads that forced a write-back on every access and drove fatigue. Read instead with a small sub-coercive AC tone (~0.2 Vc): the sign of the capacitor's second-harmonic current, from its asymmetric C-V curvature, flips with polarization direction, so a lock-in style sense amp reads the bit without switching it.
why: Non-destructive read removes write-back energy and read fatigue (Fact 8): ~2-5x lower read energy and effectively unlimited read endurance.
note: SNDM-style nonlinear read moved into a sense amp; signal at small cell area is the doubt.

title: FeFET depolarization failure becomes hours-long dynamic retention
idea: FeFETs, from Bell Labs to modern devices, failed as nonvolatile memory because the depolarization field and charge trapping erased their state within days. Store the bit instead in an antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitor whose field-induced polar state is weakly stabilized by electrodes with mismatched work functions (built-in imprint). The state decays over hours rather than milliseconds, and it is read nondestructively through its field-dependent capacitance.
why: A 'slow-leak DRAM' that refreshes every few hours instead of every 32-64 ms, ~1e5x fewer refreshes. The cell never fully switches polarization, so it avoids fatigue.
note: Work-function-engineered AFE bistability reported; endurance under constant read/write unclear.

title: Qimonda's trench DRAM revived by metal-assisted chemical etching at 200:1
idea: Trench-capacitor DRAM (IBM, Infineon, Qimonda, IBM eDRAM) died when plasma RIE could not push silicon trenches past ~60-70:1, and Qimonda went bankrupt. Metal-assisted chemical etching sinks a patterned catalyst mesh into silicon in HF/H2O2 vapor with straight walls beyond 200:1; use a sacrificial non-gold catalyst followed by a verified metals strip, then line trenches with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN.
why: Gives the AR ~115+ needed for >8 fF without high-power C4F8/SF6 plasma (high-GWP, PFAS-class gases); capacitor sits under the transistor so the array stays planar; ~2x capacitance or ~30% smaller cell at the same charge.

title: Rutile TiO2 capacitors templated on MoO2 instead of scarce ruthenium
idea: Rutile-TiO2 DRAM capacitors (k~80-100) died on Ru/RuO2 bottom electrodes, a South African PGM that is costly and hard to etch, plus leakage. Template rutile on MoO2, a conductive rutile-structure oxide formed by in-situ oxidation of a Mo electrode, and suppress leakage with Al doping and a sub-nm Al2O3 interlayer.
why: k~80 versus ~40 for ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 hits the 'k~70' route through the charge wall, letting pillars drop from 60-75:1 to ~35:1; removes Zr/Hf and Ru; Ti, Mo, Al are abundant; ~40% less deep etch and deposition gas.
note: Leakage and MoO2 oxidation stability.

title: Qimonda's trench DRAM resurrected by metal-assisted chemical etching
idea: Infineon/Qimonda's trench DRAM lost to stacked capacitors around 2009 because plasma etching of silicon trenches beyond ~AR 70 became impossible. Metal-assisted chemical etching (a catalyst mesh sinking into Si in HF/H2O2) reaches AR >100 in a room-temperature wet bench, so sink buried capacitors before the transistors using a self-aligned, non-gold catalyst grid stripped before gate oxidation.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): AR 115+ via wet chemistry instead of $10M+ etch tools; capacitor-module capex down ~10x.
note: MACE reaches AR>100; catalyst wander and CMOS contamination are the open problems.

title: Reversible computing, fixed: integer-exact reversible layers erase activation storage
idea: RevNets and reversible computing were abandoned because floating-point inversion drifts and reconstruction errors accumulate. Build transformer blocks from fixed-point additive couplings computed in modular integer arithmetic (y = x + f(x) mod 2^k), which are bit-exactly invertible, so backprop recomputes every activation from the output and stores none.
why: Training activation memory (often 50%+ of training memory) becomes O(1) in depth, with no storage of any kind.

title: Antiferroelectric biased at critical field gives giant differential capacitance
idea: Effect walk: field-induced antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric transition. A ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is held by a built-in work-function bias just below its forward switching field, where dP/dE is 5-10x the linear permittivity, so a +/-0.3 V signal swing moves 5-fF-equivalent charge from a shallow AR~15 cylinder.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1: needs k~70 or AR~115) by borrowing a phase transition's effective k of ~150-300, permitting AR 15-25 pillars with fewer deep-etch steps; sub-loop hysteresis and fatigue are the risks.
note: Work-function bias parks ZrO2 AFE at transition for effective k~150; MPB/AFE HZO capacitors already studied; hysteresis, fatigue, temperature drift.

title: Talbot self-imaging prints periodic memory arrays without EUV
idea: Effect: Talbot self-imaging. DRAM arrays are strictly periodic, so displacement Talbot lithography (a simple phase grating lit at 193 nm and integrated across the Talbot distance) prints pitch-halved lines and honeycomb hole arrays with no complex reticle. Self-aligned quadruple patterning then reaches array pitch, and only the periphery uses conventional litho.
why: EUV single-supplier chokepoint and 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4): the array layers move to tools at ~1/10 EUV capex with mask cost near zero.
note: Periodic arrays suit DTL; overlay, array-edge stitching and defectivity are the doubts.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as etch-free capacitor molds
idea: Effect: field-assisted ion migration during room-temperature aluminum anodization self-organizes hexagonal pores with aspect ratios >1000:1. A coarse nanoimprint pre-pattern registers them, and ALD TiN/dielectric/TiN at <=300 C fills them, so no high-AR plasma etch is needed. Every step stays below 400 C.
why: PFAS/fluorocarbon etch gases (C4F6, C4F8) and capital-heavy etchers; AR ~150:1 pushes Cs toward ~10 fF, breaking the capacitor wall (fact 1).

title: Silver-catalyzed chemical etching makes vertical channel pillars in a wet bench
idea: Effect: metal-assisted chemical etching. A Ag mesh templated by block copolymer sits on Si; in HF/H2O2 the catalyst sinks straight down by local oxidation and dissolution, carving 10-15 nm pillars at AR >50:1 at room temperature with no plasma damage. Ag is stripped in nitric acid and residues are gettered. $1M covers wet benches, TXRF/SIMS contamination checks and 4F2 vertical-transistor test arrays.
why: Fact 4: a ~$100k wet bench replaces $8-15M HAR Si plasma etchers for 4F2 DRAM, and damage-free sidewalls may also shrink the leakage tail.
note: Ag contamination is a DRAM retention risk.

title: Ti: SnO2-seeded rutile TiO2 reaches k≈100 without ruthenium
idea: Use a 1-2 nm rutile SnO2 seed (isostructural, made of abundant tin) so ALD TiO2 crystallizes as rutile (k~90-170) at <=400 C instead of anatase (k~40), with ~1% Al doping to pin leakage; this replaces scarce Ru/RuO2 templates.
why: Delivers the k~70 escape route of fact 1, letting pillar AR fall from ~70:1 toward ~35:1 at the same 5 fF; cuts etch time and a scarce metal.
note: Template-seeded rutile known path to k~100; leakage of narrow-gap TiO2 is the risk.

title: Sodium-calcium glass panels host display-style oxide DRAM tiers
idea: Fabricate stacked oxide-TFT 2T0C/1T1C arrays on SiN-barriered soda-lime (Na, Ca, Si, O) glass using i-line or proximity litho and sputtering, as the university prototype of a display-fab memory line where one Gen-8.5 panel (~5.5 m2) offers ~78x the area of a 300 mm wafer.
why: Attacks capital intensity (fact 4) by repurposing idle LCD fabs and cheap glass for bulk-capacity, refresh-light memory tiers built from the most abundant elements on the table.

title: Aluminum anodization pores template litho-free vertical 4F2 cells
idea: Anodize a 300 nm sputtered Al film on Si in oxalic acid (two-step, seeded by a sparse e-beam pre-pattern for long-range order) to form a hexagonal pore array at 40-60 nm pitch, then ALD a ZTO shell channel, Al2O3 dielectric and TiN core gate down each pore with the capacitor on top.
why: Defines a 4F2 vertical array by electrochemistry and ALD alone, with no EUV (fact 4) and minimal masks; a beaker, power supply and ALD tool suffice.

title: Ni: nickel-seeded lateral crystallization of cheap amorphous tier stacks
idea: Deposit fast PECVD amorphous-Si/oxide stacks, open one vertical seed slit, add Ni there so NiSi2 fronts sweep laterally through every a-Si layer at ~550 C converting it to needle-like single-grain Si; the Ni-rich front ends in a sacrificial region that is cut away.
why: Fact 2: amorphous deposition is ~10x faster and cheaper than epitaxy and tolerates 100+ tiers; MILC gives near-crystalline mobility. Residual Ni leakage is the risk.

title: Uranium enrichment cascade: concentrate hot lines into dense hot pages
idea: A centrifuge cascade separates U-235 in many small stages; the controller counts per-line accesses and, every epoch, swaps hot 64 B lines into enriched pages and cold lines into depleted pages through a line remap table, so whole depleted pages can be compressed or pushed to CXL/flash tiers.
why: Page-level tiering fails because most 4 KB pages hold a few hot lines; enrichment makes 50-70% of pages truly cold, letting local DRAM shrink ~2x with little slowdown (cost/bit).

title: Osmium density: KV entropy-coded against in-block predictions
idea: Osmium is the densest element; each KV block is stored as an rANS-coded residual where each key is predicted from the previous token's key in the same block and each value from a learned linear map of its own key, both available in streaming order, and a hardware rANS decoder in the memory controller expands the stream.
why: Sequence and K-to-V redundancy plus entropy coding push KV toward ~1.5-2 bits per element instead of 16, so ~8-10x fewer bits are fetched per token (about 10x lower energy per access) and KV capacity grows ~8x (energy, density).
note: Same predict-and-code-residual mechanism with rANS.

title: Silver-halide latents: training activations saved as compact neural latents
idea: Film stores a faint silver latent image that development amplifies; during training each checkpointed activation tile is encoded by a small learned encoder into a 16x smaller latent written to DRAM and decoded on chip in the backward pass, with the codec co-trained to keep gradient error bounded.
why: Activations dominate training memory; 16x smaller latents cut activation DRAM ~10x and DRAM bits written and read per activation >10x, with the codec costing far less energy than the traffic it removes (energy, density).

title: Anodized-cookware pores: AAO capacitor forests on 28 nm logic
idea: Anodize a thick aluminium BEOL layer on 28-40 nm logic wafers to self-organize 60-80 nm-pitch pores with AR >100:1, ALD TiN/high-k/TiN into them, and tie each pore cluster to a logic-node access transistor to make stand-alone 1T1C DRAM in foundries that never made DRAM.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): AAO reaches AR 100+ by electrochemistry, not etch, for Cs >10 fF per cell, and it enlists U.S. trailing logic fabs with only a plating-bath module added.

title: Photographic contact print: Talbot self-imaging for periodic cell arrays
idea: Use displacement Talbot lithography, a contact-print-like method exploiting self-imaging of periodic masks, to expose dense hexagonal capacitor or channel arrays below 100 nm pitch with mature UV sources, then spacer pitch-split to ~40 nm.
why: Array layers are perfectly periodic, exactly Talbot's sweet spot; replaces immersion/EUV array exposures (fact 4) with ~$1-3M tools.
note: Overlay to prior layers is the key doubt.

title: Glassblowing silicon: hydrogen reflow seals stacked buried cavities for tiers
idea: Use surface-tension shaping like a glassblower: etch deep hole arrays with depth-modulated scallops, then hydrogen-anneal near 1100 C so silicon migrates and pinches each scallop into a sealed planar void (multi-level silicon-on-nothing), leaving stacked single-crystal Si plates that later receive gate and capacitor dielectrics.
why: Fact 2: single-crystal multi-tier silicon without the Si/SiGe superlattice epi that warps and dislocates beyond ~30-60 periods; one etch plus one anneal replaces ~100 epi layers.

title: Anodized-cookware pores: self-ordered alumina holes beyond 100:1
idea: Deposit 2 um of aluminium over the landing pads, pre-dimple it with the single added mask (10 nm-deep dot pattern), anodize in oxalic acid so pores nucleate at the dimples and grow straight down, open the barrier layer, and ALD the MIM capacitor into the pores.
why: Fact 1: a wet bath produces AR>100 holes at 30-60 nm pitch with no HAR plasma etch, for ~1.5-2x Cs; step capex down ~10x.

title: Sourdough crumb: porous-silicon capacitors cut by one isolation mask
idea: Like dough fermenting gas pockets, electrochemically porosify a 1 um doped poly-Si layer over the landing pads into ~20 nm random pores, coat with high-k and TiN by ALD, and use the single added coarse mask to cut a cell-isolation grid, so each cell's capacitor is whatever ~15-25 pores fall in it.
why: Fact 1: 10-30x surface-area gain with no hole litho or HAR etch; Cs spread handled by pad sizing and sense-margin binning; bath tool ~1/20 the cost of HAR etch.
note: Random pore count gives ~20% Cs spread per cell.

title: Mine-tailings reprocessing: keep token IDs, recompute evicted KV on demand
idea: Mines reprocess old tailings when a new assay shows value. Evicted KV entries are discarded, but their 2-byte token IDs and a 16-bit key sketch (random-projection signs) are kept. When a new query's sketch dot product flags a tailings span as relevant, the KV for that span plus its neighbors is recomputed by a short prefill and spliced back.
why: For cold spans, KV memory goes from context x layers x dims down to about 4 bytes per token, a 100x+ cut for million-token contexts; the recompute cost is paid only when a span is relevant.
note: Span recompute without full prefix gives approximate KV.

title: Group-technology cells: batch requests by expert-routing fingerprint
idea: Group technology puts parts with similar routings into one manufacturing cell. A router-predictor computes each request's MoE expert fingerprint from its first layers, and the scheduler batches requests that share a fingerprint. Each GPU then stages only a small 'kit' of experts in HBM, while the rest stay in host DRAM or flash and are swapped per cell.
why: MoE models normally keep every expert resident; batching by fingerprint cuts resident expert memory 3-8x, with high reuse of each staged expert.

title: Rebar concrete: protected outlier rebar, bulk codes in 1%-BER cells
idea: Reinforced concrete puts steel only where strength is needed. Weights and KV are split into a sparse 'rebar' of outliers plus all scale factors, kept in a small strongly-ECC'd region (about 3% of bits), and a dense 'concrete' of 3-4-bit codes stored raw in 1%-BER cells. With outliers removed and codes clamped to a narrow range, any flip moves a value by at most one bounded code range, which is a tiny perturbation in a dot product.
why: About 97% of model bits move into cheap, unrefreshed or defect-tolerant cells while also being quantized 4x, so the high-grade DRAM needed for weights drops about 10x.
note: Most of the 10x comes from known quantization; 1% BER tolerance is optimistic.

title: Halftone screen: error-diffused 1-bit weights that shrug off flips
idea: Halftone printing renders gray with binary dots plus error diffusion. Weights are binarized with Floyd-Steinberg-style error diffusion along the input dimension, carrying each residual to neighboring weights, and per-block FP16 scales are kept in protected memory. Each output sums thousands of +/-1 weights, so 1% flips act as small additive noise, like a few misprinted dots.
why: At 1 bit per weight (16x smaller than FP16), stored in unprotected 1%-BER cells, the high-grade memory needed for weights falls more than 16x.
note: Post-training 1-bit quality loss is the main doubt, not flip tolerance.

title: Hafnium-, zirconium-, ruthenium-free CaTiO3 capacitors on MoO2 electrodes
idea: Ideal: a capacitor made from limestone and common metals. Closest: ALD perovskite CaTiO3 (bulk k~170) or Al-doped rutile TiO2 grown on a rutile-structured MoO2 bottom electrode that templates the high-k phase at <=400 C, replacing RuO2/Ru electrodes and ZrO2/HfO2 stacks.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: k>=80 could cut required capacitor AR from ~70 to ~40 while removing Zr/Hf (zircon byproducts) and Ru (South Africa ~90%); leakage is the open risk.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching grows vertical channel forests at room temperature
idea: Ideal: sculpting deep silicon with no plasma. Closest: dewet a thin Ag film (or deposit Ag through a self-assembled mask) on silicon; in HF/H2O2 at room temperature the silver sinks vertically, leaving 100:1 nanopillars at 30-60 nm pitch for vertical-channel transistors or capacitor cores, made on plastic wet benches instead of $20M+ C4F6-burning etchers.
why: 100x path: wet-bench cost per wafer-pass is ~1-5% of a HAR plasma etch and removes PFAS etch gases; with self-assembled masks, array formation cost per GB falls >=100x. Trades pillar wander, Ag contamination control and porosity.
note: MACE known; pillar wander, Ag contamination and pitch uniformity at 30-60 nm are the doubts.

title: Park the dielectric at its antiferroelectric transition for k above 100
