why: A bit with no stored charge and no filament defects (unlike ReRAM): attacks refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor wall (fact 1); huge on/off ratio allows ~4F^2 cells.
note: Bubble dissolution/recombination speed and electrode degradation make ns cycling doubtful.

title: Ice cube tray: nanopore fills or drains, 80x capacitance swing
idea: Stimulus 'ice cube tray' (each cell full or empty) -> each cell is a 10 nm hydrophobic nanopore connected to a sealed water reservoir; such pores are bistable (liquid-filled vs vapor-filled), and an electrowetting pulse fills one while a reverse pulse triggers capillary drying. Water (k~80) vs vapor (k~1) changes pore capacitance ~80x, a giant read signal.
why: Huge per-cell signal removes the 5 fF capacitor requirement (fact 1); the state is thermodynamic, not leaking charge, so no refresh (fact 3); planar cell with no deep etch (fact 4).
note: Fill/dry bistability gives huge k contrast; sealing water and cavitation speed at 10 nm are the doubts.

title: Hand warmer: undercooled liquid tin nanodot versus solid tin
idea: Stimulus 'click-disc hand warmer' (supercooled liquid that crystallizes on a click) -> tin nanodots embedded in SiO2 (formed by thermal dewetting, no etch) can stay liquid ~150 K below their 232 C melting point; a Joule pulse melts a dot (1) and a sharp field or acoustic 'click' nucleates crystallization (0). Liquid tin is ~3x more resistive than solid, read nondestructively.
why: A new phase-memory class with no amorphous drift and tiny nanoscale latent heat, nonvolatile within the undercooling window (fact 3); fluorine-free dewetting fabrication.
note: Room temp is ~200 K below Sn melt, beyond reliable undercooling; stochastic nucleation threatens retention.

title: Ratchet ferroelectric gate that locks Vt high after every access
idea: Random stimulus 'ratchet wrench': it turns freely one way, then locks. A thin HZO layer in the access gate stack is pulsed to low-Vt polarization at wordline rise, and a short negative tail pulse at wordline fall ratchets it back to a +0.5 V high-Vt state, so retention-state isolation needs no standing negative wordline bias.
why: Decouples on-current from off-leakage (fact 3) and removes negative-wordline pumps from the periphery (fact 7); leakage tail down ~1000x. Risk: needs ~1e15 minor-loop cycles versus HZO's ~1e11-1e12 today.
note: Ratcheted HZO gate needs ~1e15 minor-loop cycles vs ~1e12 today.

title: Ice-cube-tray GaP storage junction lattice-matched to silicon
idea: Random stimulus 'ice cube tray': each cube sits inside a wall of a different material. Grow the storage-node-side source/drain of the access transistor as epitaxial GaP (2.26 eV gap, within 0.4% of silicon's lattice constant), so the junction where charge leaks has ~1e10x fewer intrinsic carriers and far weaker band-to-band tunneling.
why: Junction generation current scales with n_i and GIDL is band-to-band tunneling at that edge; both collapse in a wide-gap pocket, targeting the 13 fA tail (fact 3) for 10-100x longer retention. Risk: antiphase domains and Ga/P cross-doping into the channel.
note: GaP/Si epitaxy known; Ga and P cross-doping and interface defects may add leakage.

title: Totem pole: four voltage-stacked subarrays reuse one charge packet
idea: Stack four subarrays' sense-amp domains in series like a totem pole (0.75-1.0 V, 0.5-0.75 V, 0.25-0.5 V, 0-0.25 V); charge drained from the top domain's bitlines becomes the supply current of the next, so one packet does four activations' work, with small push-pull regulators balancing the domains during wide simultaneous fetches.
why: Supply energy per activation drops ~4x from charge reuse and swing is 0.25 V instead of 1 V, ~10x combined, but only if offset-trimmed SAs can sense the smaller stored signal.
note: Stacked charge recycling cuts supply energy, but a 0.25 V swing leaves too little stored signal.

title: Coffee straw: partial-charge sip reads defer restore for many reads
idea: Sip through a straw instead of draining the cup: drive the wordline only into weak inversion for ~5 ns so ~10% of the cell's charge (~0.25 fC) flows into a clamped bitline and onto a 0.5 fF integrating sense node (~0.5 V signal); the cell stays readable and is restored only every ~5 sips or at refresh.
why: Removes per-read restore, full bitline swing and the 3 V wordline pulse: ~10x less energy per read for read-mostly data such as AI weights; risks are weak-inversion variability and tracking a sip count per row.
note: Weak-inversion sip variability and leakage make cumulative charge tracking fragile.

title: Trampoline: segmented plate-line bounce restores cells, bitlines swing 0.25 V
idea: Bounce the cell up from below like a trampoline: segment the normally common cell plate into per-row-segment plate lines; bitlines swing only ~0.25 V during sense, and restore happens by pulsing the segment's plate so the storage node is bootstrapped back to a full level through capacitive coupling, as in FeRAM plate-pulse schemes.
why: Bitline swing falls ~4x (energy ~4-8x) and restore charge moves through one plate segment rather than 8k bitlines; ~10x on array energy; risks are plate-to-plate coupling and disturb of unselected cells.

title: Accordion: origami-fold one thinned wafer into an 8-tier stack
idea: Random stimulus 'accordion' forced onto stacking: build a planar DRAM array on a wafer thinned to ~5 um on a polyimide carrier, leaving 200 um flexible RDL 'hinge' strips between array panels, then fold the strip like bellows so 8 panels stack face-to-back. Bitline and I/O buses run continuously through the hinges, so the stack needs no TSVs and no per-layer bonding.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6) and per-layer bond yield: no TSV keep-out and no die-to-die alignment; claim wafer area per stacked bit -30 to -50% versus HBM, and lower capital per stacked GB.

title: Pasta extruder: drawn nanochannel glass bonded as capacitor mold
idea: Random stimulus 'pasta extruder' -> a glass preform with ordered core rods is drawn, stacked and redrawn several times, as microchannel plates are made, down to ~30 nm channels. Wafer-thin slices are bonded onto the transistor wafer, and the cores are etched out to leave AR >100 capacitor molds.
why: Capacitor charge wall and capital (facts 1 and 4): ~10^11 channels/cm2 are made by fiber drawing with zero litho, and the mold step moves out of the fab into a glass plant.

title: Snow globe: core-shell magnetic nanoparticles settle into wells as bits
idea: Random stimulus 'snow globe' (particles settle where they belong) -> chemically synthesized FePt-core/MgO-shell nanoparticles (each one a high-anisotropy bit with its own tunnel barrier) are fluidically self-assembled into DUV-defined wells over fixed-layer electrodes, then top-contacted and written with thermally assisted spin torque.
why: Non-volatile MRAM-class bits made by beaker chemistry instead of MTJ sputter and etch tools. It could cut the magnetic-module capex >10x, with 10-year retention at 5 nm from FePt anisotropy.

title: Loom: woven glass-fiber and microwire fabric interposer
idea: From a 'loom': glass fibers and 10 um insulated Cu microwires are woven on a textile loom into a fabric, resin-impregnated, and laser-opened at the pad sites. The fabric gives thousands of chiplet-to-chiplet links with zero lithography.
why: Capital intensity and CoWoS scarcity; could cut interposer cost ~10x, and textile looms are a U.S.-buildable tool base.
note: Woven microwire placement accuracy is far coarser than chiplet pad pitch.

title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid in nanopores: a ferroelectric that cannot fatigue
idea: Box = {medium: polar ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734-class, P~6 uC/cm2) | access: Si FET | sense: polarization charge released on read | integration: 10-20 nm pores in a BEOL oxide sealed with ALD | substrate: Si | fab: vacuum capillary fill}. At 1 V across 10 nm the director rotates in ~20 ns (tau ~ viscosity/(P*E)), and because the medium is a fluid, defects and domain pinning anneal out instead of accumulating as fatigue.
why: Endurance: a self-healing liquid ferroelectric, unlike hafnia; gives a FeRAM-like cell with large switched charge in a shallow pore instead of a high-AR capacitor.

title: Overlay-free crossbar cells from bonding two orthogonal line wafers
idea: [Box: MIM charge | two-terminal threshold selector (OTS/NbO2) | pulsed charge-share sensing | face-to-face bond of two line-grating wafers | Si | ArF SAQP gratings on each wafer] Wafer A carries bitline gratings capped with capacitor films, wafer B carries orthogonal wordline gratings capped with selector film; bonding them makes every crossing a 1S1C cell, and any overlay error only shifts the whole grid.
why: No EUV (fact 4): lines are the easiest ArF pattern and cells need no alignment, giving 4F2 at F~20 nm; selector leakage limits retention.

title: Thickness-defined vertical IGZO 3D DRAM on Gen-8.5 display glass
idea: Box: oxide gain-cell node charge x vertical IGZO TFT whose channel length is a deposited film thickness x current sensing x 48-tier monolithic stack x Gen-8.5 glass panel x i-line display lithography plus ALD. Every critical dimension (gate length, dielectric, node) comes from film thickness or recess time rather than resolution, so 1.5 um display steppers suffice and bits/area come from tier count on a 5.5 m2 substrate (~75x a 300 mm wafer).
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: borrows the display-fab cost model ($/m2 processed ~10-30x below DRAM fabs); claims 5-10x lower capex per bit for a capacity tier; risk is panel-scale ALD uniformity and per-tier density.
note: At 1.5 um rules per-area density is ~200x worse than DRAM; 75x area and 48 tiers barely offset it.

title: Copy-exact university-toolset microfabs for low-capex capacity DRAM
idea: Box: business axis set to fab model. Build 5k-wafer/month 150-200 mm microfabs that copy a university nanofab toolset (used ALD, sputter, contact and imprint aligners, ICP, anodization) and run only university-buildable flows (anodic-pore capacitors, oxide TFTs, interference litho), sited by U.S. data centers to make CXL memory-expander tiers.
why: Capital: ~$50-100M per fab vs $15B and 1-2 years to build, diversifying supply; risk is the cost-per-bit gap to leading-edge DRAM (target within 2-3x for a capacity tier).

title: Po: memory is baked like pottery — co-fired ceramic ferroelectric crossbar
idea: Po: memory is baked like pottery. Extracted: use MLCC tape casting to stack ~1,000 sub-um BaTiO3 layers with printed Ni electrodes running X and Y on alternate layers; each crossing is a ferroelectric capacitor bit and the coercive field acts as the selector (V/3 half-select), so the block contains no transistors.
why: MLCC lines make 1,000-layer blocks for fractions of a cent: ~1e8 crossings/cm2/layer x 1,000 layers is ~12 GB per cm2 footprint for cents, well over 100x cheaper per GB. Trade-offs: us latency, destructive read, edge-wiring thousands of lines to a CMOS driver die.

title: Antiferroelectric gate with built-in bias trades retention for endurance
idea: Po: memory that forgets on purpose. Put a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric layer in the gate stack of a single transistor with asymmetric work-function electrodes that shift its loop so one polarized state is metastable for ~1 s; the field-induced phase relaxes back on its own, giving a refreshed volatile 1T bit with much less fatigue than full ferroelectric switching.
why: Facts 1 and 3: capacitorless bit with refresh ~15x rarer than DRAM, aiming at 1e14+ endurance; goes beyond the prior nonvolatile HZO work.
note: Controlling a ~1 s metastable decay across variation and temperature is hard.

title: Ovonic threshold switch recovery-time as a volatile crosspoint bit
idea: Po: the selector remembers that it just fired. After an ovonic threshold switch turns on, its threshold stays lowered for ms before recovering; write a 1 by firing the cell, then read with a pulse between the lowered and recovered thresholds so only recently fired cells conduct, giving a capacitorless, transistorless 4F^2 crosspoint DRAM where refresh means re-firing.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 4: stackable BEOL crosspoint tiers with no capacitor or access transistor; speculative on retention control and read disturb.

title: Po: one amplifier hears sixteen bitlines via CCD transfer
idea: Po: bitlines without sense amps. Borrow CCD readout: short bitlines end in a buried-channel charge-transfer register that clocks each cell's charge packet losslessly to a floating-diffusion amplifier shared by 16 bitlines, which senses it non-destructively and writes it back through the reverse transfer.
why: Periphery (#7) and capacitor wall (#1): 16:1 fewer sense circuits, and charge-domain readout is not divided by bitline capacitance, so the full Cs charge is sensed; transfer time (~0.5 ns/stage) is the price.

title: Holes drilled in a bulk dielectric block form inter-hole capacitors
idea: Po: the capacitor is a hole, not a pillar. Deposit a 3-5 um block of crystalline high-k (rutile TiO2 or doped ZrO2, k 40-80), drill a hexagonal hole array, and fill alternate holes with storage and plate electrodes so the dielectric is the solid wall between neighbouring holes instead of a 5 nm conformal ALD film.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): reaches the k~70 target in a matrix that cannot lean or collapse; wall thickness set by etch spacing rather than ALD conformality at extreme AR.
note: Crystalline thick rutile block leaks and is hard to etch at high AR.

title: Chemically coded tier metals replace staircase contacts
idea: Po: the stack has no staircase. Build each tier's wordline from a distinct tungsten-free metal/liner pair (Mo, Ru, Co, TiN with unique etch-stop liners) so a contact etch stops on the target tier by chemistry; combined with binary chop etches, 64 tiers are contacted with ~6 masks in a single small contact field.
why: Facts 2/4: staircase area (~5-10% of die) and trim steps scale with tiers; chemical coding makes contact cost logarithmic and avoids tungsten (China ~80%).
note: Etch selectivity among Mo/Ru/Co/TiN insufficient for clean tier stops.

title: Self-locking p-type cell with ground-idled bitlines
idea: Po: the stored bit locks its own door. Use a p-type oxide access transistor whose back-gate is the storage node itself, on an insulating substrate, and idle all bitlines at 0 V: a stored 0 sees no drain-source bias so it cannot leak, and a stored 1 raises its own back-gate and drives the channel deeper off.
why: Refresh: both states are self-protected by removing leakage drive instead of fighting the tail; retention limited by dielectric leakage (hours).

title: Defect charge-state memory in stacked silicon-carbide sheets
idea: Po: the memory cell is a single missing atom. Store bits as the charge state of implanted point defects (e.g., divacancies in 4H-SiC) arrayed in thin bonded SiC sheets; a gate pulse moves the local Fermi level to set the charge state, which persists for days at room temperature because the level sits ~1 eV deep in the gap.
why: Zero refresh with wear-free switching (no atoms move); sensing through a nearby channel's conductance. Speed and density are speculative.
note: Deep-defect charge-state bits; capture/emission speed and single-defect read variability are the key doubts.

title: Graphene-hBN barristor access with a tunnelling-barrier off state
idea: Po: the switch is a wall electrons cannot climb. Build a vertical access device of graphene, 3-5 layers of hBN and MoS2 where the wordline tunes the graphene Fermi level and thus the barrier height to the storage node; the off state needs emission over ~1 eV plus tunnelling through hBN (<1e-21 A), and devices stack as van der Waals tiers.
why: Refresh eliminated at ~4F2 vertical footprint; risks are wafer-scale vdW growth or transfer and on-current.

title: NAND-style capacitor string sharing one transistor via threshold selectors
idea: Worsen: give each tiny capacitor its own expensive access transistor. Flip: stack 8-16 storage capacitors in a vertical string behind one access transistor, each gated by an ovonic threshold switch with staggered thresholds so the bitline voltage selects which capacitor charges or dumps.
why: 3D density without a lateral transistor per tier (fact 2); transistor count falls 8-16x and tiers are deposition-defined rather than litho-defined (fact 4).
note: Staggered OTS thresholds share one transistor; threshold variability and disturb are major doubts.

title: Ferroelectric negative-capacitance liner shrinks effective bitline capacitance
idea: Worse: make bitline capacitance as large as possible so the transfer ratio collapses. Flip: place a thin, stabilized ferroelectric layer in series within the bitline-to-neighbor spacer dielectric so its negative capacitance cancels part of the parasitic, lowering effective C_BL and amplifying the charge-sharing signal.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): signal ~ Cs/(Cs+CBL); halving effective CBL nearly doubles signal, allowing lower-AR capacitors or 2x longer bitlines with half the sense amps.
note: Static NC in a passive series stack is unproven and hysteretic.

title: Sapphire miscut step-bunches template sub-10nm wordlines without lithography
idea: Worse: print every line with a photon. Flip: anneal vicinal c-plane sapphire until its atomic steps bunch into a periodic 8-20 nm terrace grating, then decorate the step edges by step-flow selective nucleation of metal or oxide semiconductor. Parallel wordlines then form across the whole substrate.
why: Litho (fact 4): a sub-EUV-pitch wordline layer at zero mask cost, on sapphire grown without quartz crucibles.

title: Drawn nanochannel glass gives billion-hole capacitor templates
idea: Worse: create capacitor holes one etch step at a time at AR 75:1. Flip: stack and redraw glass rods with etchable cores again and again (nanochannel glass has reached ~30 nm channels) into plates of uniform hexagonal channels beyond 100:1. Etch out the cores, ALD the electrodes and dielectric, and bond a thin-film transistor layer on top.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): AR above 100 comes free from drawing, with no plasma etch; glass is U.S.-made.
note: Drawn channel lattice has no registration to a litho transistor array.

title: Negative wordline shake pulses lock traps into low-leak state
idea: Worse: leave variable-retention-time traps free to jump between high- and low-leak states unpredictably. Flip: periodically apply a short, strongly negative wordline and positive body pulse that empties or fills the metastable gate-edge traps into their low-leakage configuration, shrinking VRT-driven tail jumps.
why: Fact 3: VRT is why retention profiling is unreliable; taming it would let row-level adaptive refresh work safely, cutting refresh 3-5x.
note: If VRT can be pinned electrically, adaptive refresh becomes safe; mechanism unproven.

title: Self-clearing aluminum electrodes isolate SrTiO3 capacitor breakdown spots
idea: Worse: build capacitors where one pinhole short kills the cell, and lean on Hf/Ru stacks to avoid it. Flip: borrow the metallized-film capacitor trick: a thin Al top electrode over a SrTiO3 (Sr, Ti, O) dielectric on TiN, so a local breakdown dumps current that oxidizes or vaporizes the Al around the spot, isolating it while the cell keeps ~99% of its area.
why: Fact 1: makes a very high-k (k~100+) but defect-prone abundant dielectric usable because breakdown is no longer fatal, meeting Cs at lower AR with no Hf, Ru or Ta.
note: Clearing event at nm cell scale kills the cell; STO crystallization temperature.

title: Child's marble-in-egg-carton: double-dot charge-position bit
idea: A child pictures a bit as 'which cup holds the marble', not 'how full is the cup'. Store ~50-200 electrons in one of two tunnel-coupled silicon quantum dots under a split gate: a write pulse tilts the double well, a raised inter-dot barrier holds the state, and a single-electron-transistor sensor reads which side is occupied without dumping charge onto a bitline.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3): total charge is conserved, so leakage to ground cannot erase the bit, only inter-dot tunneling can; ~100x less charge than a 5 fF cell and non-destructive read (fact 8).

title: Sculptor carves inside the block: 50 porous-silicon tiers in one wet step
idea: A sculptor carves inside the block instead of adding clay. Pulse the current while anodizing a bulk Si wafer in HF to form 50 alternating high- and low-porosity layers in one ~10-minute wet step. A hydrogen anneal reseals the low-porosity layers into single-crystal Si sheets over voids (silicon-on-nothing physics), giving a 50-tier channel stack without epitaxy.
why: Meets the 10x constraint: a wet electrochemical step costing under ~$50 per wafer replaces a $1,000+ epitaxial superlattice, so a 50-tier 3D DRAM (~10x/mm^2) keeps wafer cost flat. It needs only U.S. wet-bench suppliers and no scarce gases.
note: Pulsed anodization plus H2 reseal (ELTRAN/SON) for crystalline tiers; doubt: sheet quality and uniformity over 50 tiers.

title: Mixed-conductor volumetric capacitance storage node from wearable bioelectronics
idea: Wearable sensors use organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors such as PEDOT:PSS whose entire volume charges at ~40 F/cm3, so a 100 nm cube stores ~40 fF, ~8x a DRAM pillar. A sealed solid-electrolyte version (polymerized ionic liquid) aims for 10-100 ns charging because ion diffusion time shrinks with the square of size.
why: Destroys the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) with no high aspect ratio and leaves room for multi-level storage; ion speed and 1e15-cycle stability are unproven.

title: Self-healing ferroelectric nematic liquid in nano-wells, fatigue-free
idea: Thirty-year industrial controllers cannot tolerate ferroelectric fatigue, so polarization is held by a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (P ~4-6 uC/cm2) sealed in nano-wells; being a fluid, pinned domains and defects anneal away, removing wake-up and fatigue. Surface anchoring gives two stable polar orientations, read by displacement charge or a coupled FET.
why: Promises effectively unlimited polarization endurance with ~5x the charge per area of a DRAM capacitor; switching (us today) must reach ~100 ns through nanoscale confinement.
note: New ferroelectric-nematic phase; us switching and nanowell anchoring bistability are big unknowns.

title: Idle rows nap in a charge-trap shadow inside the access gate
idea: Two timescales in one cell: the access transistor gate stack gets a thin SiN charge-trap layer; when a row has idled >1 s the controller applies one program pulse that copies each bit (via the storage-node-dependent channel potential) into trapped charge and stops refreshing the row; on the next access a Vt-shift sense restores the DRAM charge, so trap endurance is spent only on idle transitions (~1e6 over life).
why: Idle refresh power (16-33% of idle, fact 3) goes to ~0 for cold data, the majority of server capacity, while hot rows keep ns DRAM access.
note: Programming via storage-node potential in a DRAM gate stack risks disturb and needs high voltages.

title: Ferroelectric back-gate deep-freezes idle rows' access transistors
idea: Time shift: one switching event per idle episode (minutes to hours) instead of a refresh every 64 ms. A ferroelectric back-gate under each row's access transistors is flipped when the row goes idle, raising Vt ~0.8 V so subthreshold leakage drops ~10^4-10^6 and retention reaches hours; the next access flips it back, and no refresh exists.
why: Kills the leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3) without a new storage element; ~1 FE cycle per idle episode makes ~10^10 endurance ample.
note: Nonvolatile Vt boost for idle rows; GIDL and junction leakage, not only subthreshold, set the tail.

title: Rack-shared scrub appliance replaces per-device heavy decoders
idea: Shift heavy correction to rack scale and hour timescale: long-retention memory devices carry only a light access-path decoder sized for 1% raw BER, while one rack-level appliance with powerful soft decoders sweeps every pool over CXL in low-load hours, rewriting rows before drift pushes errors past 1%. Refresh becomes an hourly network service.
why: Amortizes decoder silicon across hundreds of devices and replaces ms-scale refresh (fact 3) with hourly scrubbing for long-retention cells.
note: Needs hour-retention cells; DRAM cannot, so it depends on a new cell.

title: HP rotaxane crossbar fixed: molecular shuttles locked in a MOF lattice
idea: HP/UCLA rotaxane crossbars failed because evaporated top metal punched through the soft monolayer, so the 'switching' was really filaments. Grow a thin rigid metal-organic framework whose linkers are bistable [2]rotaxanes, so each ring shuttles between two stations inside a stiff pore, and laminate a transferred graphene top electrode so no metal atoms enter.
why: Molecular-scale bits (~100 shuttles per cell ensemble), nonvolatile with no refresh, low-temperature and stackable in BEOL.
note: Rotaxane MOFs exist; solid-state shuttling speed and electrical readout unclear.

title: Kilopass VLT thyristor fixed in GaN: standby current vanishes when hot
idea: T-RAM and Kilopass's VLT thyristor DRAM died because latch holding and leakage currents scale with the intrinsic carrier density ni, which explodes at high temperature in silicon. Grow the vertical p-n-p-n in GaN-on-Si (Eg 3.4 eV, ni ~1e-10 cm-3): off-state leakage and holding-current drift sit many orders of magnitude below silicon at 125 C while the cell stays a ~4F2 static latch.
why: Refresh-free static cell at Grade 1 temperature with negligible standby power; uses existing 300 mm GaN-on-Si lines.
note: Weak p-GaN and poor bipolar gain make vertical GaN thyristor latching at 4F2 doubtful.

title: STT barrier wear-out turned self-healing with spinel MgAl2O4
idea: STT-MRAM as DRAM failed partly because write currents build oxygen-vacancy traps in MgO until breakdown (~1e10-1e12 cycles). Use a lattice-matched spinel MgAl2O4 barrier, cation-disorder engineered so vacancy traps anneal out at 125 C or below within hours, so a hot ambient repairs the barrier faster than writes damage it.
why: Turns 125 C from a stressor into a continuous healing anneal, potentially lifting endurance toward 1e15 for DRAM-class duty.

title: Contactless NEMS relay: tunneling-gap mechanical access switch
idea: Nanomechanical relays died from contact wear and stiction after 1e9-1e12 cycles. Never let the beam touch: an electrostatically pulled beam moves its tip from a 4 nm gap to a 1 nm gap against the storage-node pad, which switches electron tunneling current by ~1e9 without contact. A self-assembled-monolayer stopper serves only as a fail-safe.
why: No semiconductor in the off path, so retention is limited only by the capacitor dielectric and refresh is effectively eliminated. Because the switch never makes contact, the wear that killed relays never occurs.
note: Contactless tunneling gap avoids wear; ns motion, beam fatigue at 1e15 cycles and stiction are doubts.

title: Single-electron memory variability averaged out by printed Au55 cluster arrays
idea: Single-electron memories died because random background charges shifted each Coulomb-blockade island's threshold. Print a dense monolayer of ligand-capped ~1.4 nm gold clusters between storage node and bitline. Thousands of junctions in series and parallel average out the offset charges, and the room-temperature blockade (~0.2-0.3 eV charging energy) blocks conduction below threshold.
why: A printable two-terminal access element with exponential sub-threshold suppression and no semiconductor generation current, a new leakage physics. Speculative.
note: Ensemble averaging of offset charges is a fresh fix for SET variability; on-current and junction uniformity unproven.

title: Zero-extra-mask lateral bipolar sense amps from BiCMOS DRAM's ashes
idea: Failure mined: Hitachi's 1990s BiCMOS DRAM had superb bipolar sensing but died on extra masks and cost. Fix: form lateral npn transistors in the SA stripe from the existing buried-wordline trench, LDD and contact implants, with no new masks. The bipolar input pairs match Vbe to ~0.5 mV, ~10x better than MOS (5-10 mV).
why: The required bitline signal drops ~5x, so the storage capacitor can shrink ~3-5x (aspect ratio from 70:1 toward 20:1, fact 1) or bitlines can be ~3x longer with fewer SAs.
note: Lateral npn matching from shared implants likely far worse than claimed.

title: Avalanche-gain bitline preamp borrowed from failed impact-ionization MOS
idea: Failure mined: I-MOS (the impact-ionization MOSFET) died as a logic switch from high voltage and hot-carrier damage over billions of cycles. Fix: make a gated p-i-n avalanche preamp the first sensing stage, firing once per activation for ~1 ns and multiplying the cell's charge-share signal 10-30x before a conventional latch. Its duty cycle is ~1e-4 of logic use.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): cell capacitance can drop 5-10x (to ~0.5-1 fF), allowing planar or short capacitors and easing 3D DRAM (fact 2).
note: Avalanche excess noise and gain spread vs mV signals; smaller Cs also worsens retention.

title: Hadamard-coded multiplexed reads solve vertical ReRAM's sneak network
idea: Failure mined: vertical ReRAM (VRRAM) from Samsung and SanDisk stalled because sneak paths and IR drop worsened with every added plane. Fix: read all 64 cells of a pillar together with 64 measurements under Hadamard-coded +/- bias patterns on the word planes, then invert the known resistor-network model in a small periphery ASIC to recover each conductance. As in Hadamard spectroscopy, this gains ~sqrt(64) in SNR over one-at-a-time reads.
why: 10x at the same cost: 64 deposited planes per pillar etch become usable (VRRAM's whole premise) with ~8x SNR to spare, ~15x bits/mm^2 vs DRAM at 3D-NAND-like cost per mm^2. Latency is amortized because a pillar's 64 cells are read together.
note: Network inversion across shared planes is ill-posed; ReRAM endurance is not DRAM-class.

title: Failed SrTiO3 DRAM capacitors revived with self-clearing electrodes
idea: SrTiO3 (k ~100+) DRAM capacitors were researched and abandoned because weak spots leaked and broke down. Use an ultra-thin top electrode that vaporizes locally around a breakdown site, as in self-healing metallized-film capacitors. Each defect is isolated, so the capacitor loses a tiny area instead of shorting.
why: Delivers the k ~70+ the charge wall calls for (fact 1), allowing lower-AR pillars (AR ~40) while preserving yield. Self-repair is built in.
note: STO leakage is distributed, not just weak spots; clearing in nanoscale holes would destroy cells.

title: Thyristor RAM fixed with delta-doped barriers that pin holding current
idea: T-RAM and Kilopass VLT died because the gated thyristor's holding current and standby leakage swung exponentially with temperature, forcing SOI and big guard-banding. Insert a planar-doped (delta-doped) triangular barrier in the p-base so a designed barrier height, not bulk diffusion, sets regeneration; this flattens holding current versus temperature and lets the vertical cell sit in plain bulk silicon with no germanium.
why: Capacitor- and nearly refresh-free 4F2 cell: no ZrO2/HfO2, no TiN pillars, no 60:1 capacitor etch gases; bulk instead of SOI halves crystal silicon per substrate; ~2x density and ~40% fewer high-AR etch steps per bit.
note: Barrier-set regeneration still thermionic, so holding current likely stays exponential in T.

title: Zettacore's redox molecules reused as DRAM storage nodes, not nonvolatile bits
idea: Zettacore's porphyrin memory died chasing nonvolatile retention through a 400 C back-end. Use the molecules where retention is cheap: graft a multi-redox monolayer (ferrocene-porphyrin triads, 2-4 electrons per molecule at ~1e14 molecules/cm2) as the last step onto a short ~10:1 TiN cup, so faradaic charge (~30 uC/cm2) supplies the 5 fF-equivalent storage that today needs a 60-75:1 pillar.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall: ~6x shorter storage node, no ZrO2/HfO2 high-k, fewer fluorocarbon deep-etch steps; molecules are C, H, N, Fe; refresh already exists so molecular retention limits do not matter. Electron-transfer speed is the risk.
note: Faradaic charge density fits, but SAM electron transfer is slow and solid-state counter-ions are needed.

title: ZettaCore redox molecules turn squat capacitors into full-charge cells
idea: ZettaCore's porphyrin molecular memory folded around 2008 because the molecules could not survive 400 C back-end steps and needed all-new circuits. Use them only as a charge multiplier: graft a redox monolayer (~1e14 molecules/cm2, ~160 fC/um2) onto the storage-node electrode after all hot steps, so an AR~8 cylinder stores the ~2.5 fC an AR~70 cylinder holds today.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and deletes the hardest high-AR mold etch and its tool fleet; capacitor-module tool hours fall ~5-10x.
note: Solid-state redox needs counter-ion compensation; switching speed unclear.

title: Plated-wire memory reborn as thermally drawn crossbar ribbons
idea: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s-70s) died because hand-made wires could not reach semiconductor density. Thermally draw a preform of parallel metal electrodes embedded in a phase-change chalcogenide glass cladding down ~1000x into ribbons with ~200 nm electrode pitch, then laminate ribbons at 90 degrees so every electrode crossing becomes a cell, 50 laminations deep.
why: Meets 100x: patterning by a ~$5M drawing tower producing km per hour instead of lithography; est. ~$0.05/GB. Trades: coarse pitch, ribbon-registration yield, PCM endurance and write energy.
note: Multi-lamination addressing, registration and PCM endurance are unsolved.

title: Core memory reborn as colloidally patterned magnetic vortex nanorings
idea: Ferrite core memory died because cores were hand-threaded and millimetre-sized, yet its coincident-current selection made a passive crossbar with no sneak paths. Pattern magnetic vortex nanorings with mask-free nanosphere lithography (a self-assembled bead monolayer) over a coarse X/Y/sense line grid, so only rings under full coincident field switch and several rings per crossing vote.
why: Meets 100x: no transistor per bit, litho-free ring formation, unlimited magnetic endurance and non-volatility; est. ~$0.1/GB at 8 decks. Trades: destructive read-and-restore like core, high write currents, small inductive read signal.
note: Inductive read from 100 nm rings is ~uV; switching-field spread breaks half-select.

title: Pyroelectric read: a nanoheater asks the domain which way it points
idea: Effect walk: pyroelectricity. A 10-nm resistive nanoheater under a ferroelectric bit warms a ~20-nm volume by ~10 K for 2 ns (~0.2 fJ); the polarization-dependent pyro-current, whose sign is the bit, charges the aF sense gate of a gain transistor, so the domain is read without being switched or rewritten.
why: Replaces switch-and-restore reads and full bitline swings (facts 8, 10) with ~0.2-1 fJ of heat, ~10x below DRAM read energy per bit; the signal is only a few electrons, so sensing noise is the risk.
note: Heat-pulse NDRO for ferroelectrics is fresh; few-electron signal versus noise is the doubt.

title: Ionic drift leaky-integrator per row counts activations for row hammer
idea: Effect: ion migration. Add a sub-50 nm Ag/SiO2 (or Cu/Ta2O5) ionic cell per row, fed by a small tap from the wordline driver; each ACT pulse pushes a fixed ion dose forward while back-diffusion relaxes it with a ~32-64 ms time constant. Conductance thus encodes activations within the refresh window, and crossing a threshold flags the row for neighbor refresh.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): one BEOL device per row replaces SRAM/CAM counter tables of tens of KB per bank, and the natural decay matches the refresh window at no cost.
note: Diffusive-memristor variability makes a ~1k-ACT threshold with a 64 ms decay hard to hit reliably.

title: Logic-heat-biased VO2 hysteresis latches in BEOL tiers
idea: Thermal hysteresis: VO2 nano-bridge cross-point tiers are placed on the logic die, whose steady ~60-65 C waste heat parks every bridge inside its doped, widened hysteresis window. A heat pulse sets a bridge metallic, and a small hold bias keeps it there by self-heating. Briefly removing a row's bias resets that row before selective re-set.
why: Turns stacking heat, normally a refresh penalty (fact 3), into the storage bias; claim a capacitor-free BEOL latch at ~4F2 per tier with no refresh.

title: Avalanche-gain segment amplifies charge at each vertical bitline
idea: Impact ionization: a short vertical p-i-n avalanche section at the foot of each vertical bitline multiplies the charge dumped by a tiny tier capacitor 50-100x before it reaches the sense amp. It works like an avalanche photodiode, but for stored electrons.
why: Lets 3D tiers use 10x smaller capacitors (facts 1 and 2) and shrinks sense-amp periphery (fact 7); claim 10x Cs relief, with excess noise the main risk.

title: Spinodal vertically-aligned nanocomposite pillars as EUV-free 4F2 channels
idea: Spinodal phase separation: a single co-deposited oxide nanocomposite, such as IGZO-matrix/MgO or a ZnO pillar system, self-separates into ~10 nm-pitch vertical semiconductor pillars. A coarse DUV prepattern pins the pillar lattice so the pillars register to wordlines and become vertical channel transistors.
why: Replaces EUV patterning for 4F2 vertical-channel arrays (fact 4); claim removes 3-5 EUV layers, cutting about a quarter of wafer cost.

title: Persistent-photoconductivity oxide tiers written by through-stack light
idea: Persistent photoconductivity: a UV pulse sent down a vertical light pipe ionizes oxygen vacancies in IGZO/ZnO channel tiers into metastable donors that keep the channel conductive with the power off. A gate bias selects which tier captures the charge, and a positive-gate pulse erases by re-neutralizing the vacancies.
why: Gives non-volatile tiers with no capacitor and no per-tier write drivers (facts 1 and 7); claim days-to-months retention from a single light pipe per column, with the speed-retention trade as the risk.

title: Sealed nano-vacuum field-emission switches replace gate-oxide access transistors
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission. Mo nanotips face TiN anodes across a ~5 nm vacuum gap sealed by PECVD SiO2 at 350 C, forming the cell access device. Off-current falls exponentially with no thermionic subthreshold tail and no gate dielectric; field-enhanced tips switch on at ~2-3 V.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) and dependence on Hf high-k and single-crystal silicon; all steps are below 400 C.
note: Exponential tip-sharpness variability and unidirectional emission make bipolar cell writes and uniform off-current doubtful.

title: Coulomb-blockade nanocrystal chains as a spin-coated ultra-low-leakage access switch
idea: Effect: Coulomb blockade. A vertical chain of 3-5 sub-2 nm Si nanocrystals with 1 nm SiO2 shells, spin-coated from colloid into a via, forms a multi-tunnel junction whose off state is held by a single-electron charging energy above 10 kT at room temperature; a gate lowers the blockade to write the capacitor.
why: Facts 3 and 4: leakage is set by charging energy rather than dopant precision, and the ~20-mask access-transistor FEOL is replaced by BEOL-stackable cells; claimed 100x smaller leakage tail if dot sizes stay uniform.
note: Cotunneling leakage and dot-size uniformity make fA off-state doubtful.

title: Pyroelectric domain masters print charge patterns like nanoscale xerography
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. A LiTaO3 master is written once by e-beam domain poling; a 10 K heat pulse then raises surface charge only on the patterned domains, which picks up charged 10 nm hardmask nanoparticles electrostatically and transfers them to the wafer. The master is reused millions of times.
why: Fact 4 and masks: an optics-free, contact-light patterning tool under ~$5M for periodic array hardmask layers, with the master written only once.
note: 10 nm particle transfer defectivity and overlay unproven.

title: Dielectrophoresis drops pre-made capacitor rods into transistor-wafer sockets
idea: Effect: dielectrophoresis. Coaxial TiN/ZrO2/TiN capacitor nanorods are batch-made off-wafer by template electroplating and ALD, released into a fluid, and trapped one per socket by an AC field between bitline-contact electrodes, then anneal-bonded in place.
why: Separates the most capital-heavy module (the HAR capacitor) from the FEOL fab, and batch rods cost cents per wafer-equivalent. Placement yield must exceed 99.9999%.

title: Swift heavy-ion latent tracks etch 200:1 capacitor holes in one wet step
idea: Effect: latent-track etching. A thick SiO2 or polymer mold is exposed to MeV-GeV heavy ions through a stencil with one aperture per cell; each ion leaves a damaged track that etches ~1000x faster than bulk in dilute HF, so every hole etches straight to AR 200:1 at once. Several tracks per aperture merge into one hole.
why: Fact 1: the AR ~115 needed for more charge is beyond plasma etch; a cyclotron beamline (already used roll-to-roll for track-etched membranes) replaces fleets of $10M+ cryo HAR etchers. A 40 nm-pitch stencil is the main risk.
note: 40 nm stencil for MeV-GeV ions is implausible; ions damage underlying transistors.

title: Joule self-heating crystallizes each tier's channel through its own wordline
idea: Effect: localized Joule heating. Deposit amorphous Si channels in every 3D DRAM tier, then send a microsecond current pulse through each lateral strip so only that strip melts and recrystallizes (self-aligned electrical annealing) while lower tiers and BEOL stay cold. A $1M program on 100 mm wafers with 4-tier stacks measures grain size and leakage in 24 months.
why: Fact 2: low-thermal-budget single-grain channels block 3D DRAM; pulse generators replace $10M+ excimer laser annealers.

title: LC resonance: adiabatic energy-recovery memory buses recycle interposer line charge
idea: Make interposer line groups part of resonant LC tanks with on-package thin-film inductors so charge sloshes between line and inductor instead of dumping to ground; data is encoded in the phase/polarity of the resonant swing, resonant clocking applied to data.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5) and CV^2 floor (fact 10): recovers 60-80% of line energy, HBM bus ~3.5 to ~1 pJ/bit; constrains encoding to near-periodic signaling.

title: Dielectric-absorption reservoir backs up charge in tiny capacitors
idea: Effect: dielectric absorption (Debye relaxation, 'soakage'). The storage capacitor is a bilayer of thin fast high-k plus a slow polar layer with tau ~ms; on write the slow layer partially polarizes, and as leakage drains the fast charge, its relaxation current flows back into the node, stretching retention of a 0.5 fF cap several-fold. A two-step read (fast charge, then soaked charge) gives a second vote for marginal cells.
why: 10x density: 0.5 fF planar caps with ~3x retention extension stack 24 tiers at ~0.4x per-tier density (~10x). Same cost: the AR-75 pillar etch and its EUV patterning are removed.
note: ns writes cannot charge a ms-tau layer; soaked old data would oppose new writes.

title: O: single oxide-trap occupancy in a tiny FinFET as bit
idea: Use the random-telegraph trap that ultra-scaled transistors carry: one oxide trap near the channel whose occupancy shifts Vt by ~20-50 mV; set it with a gate bias, read via drain current, map out devices without a usable trap at test, and accept ~1% thermal flips per refresh window.
why: Atomic-scale storage inside a minimal transistor with no capacitor (facts 1, 4), turning device noise into a bit; only viable because 1% stochastic capture errors are allowed.
note: Trap occupancy randomness and short capture/emission times make retention and yield very uncertain.

title: F: fluorinated ferroelectric-nematic liquid crystal fills each storage well
idea: Fill nanoscale wells with a fluorinated ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (DIO-type, polarization ~5 uC/cm2, coercive field ~1,000x below oxide ferroelectrics) so the bit is the polar director orientation switched at ~1 V; fluid order cannot fatigue like a crystal, and anchoring defects that randomize ~1% of wells are tolerated.
why: Non-volatile, low-voltage polar storage (fact 10) filled by inkjet instead of ALD; switching speed of liquid crystal confined in nanowells is the main physics risk.

title: Cesiated vacuum nano-channel access device: off state is literal vacuum
idea: Cs: form a ~20 nm sealed vacuum gap between a cesium/oxide-coated emitter (work function ~1.5 eV) on the storage node and a bitline collector, with the wordline as gate; field emission turns on exponentially at a few volts, and the off state conducts nothing through solid matter.
why: Removes semiconductor leakage paths entirely (fact 3), leaving retention set by capacitor dielectric; Cs stability, hermetic sealing and emitter variability are the risks.
note: Vacuum off-state is leak-free; Cs migration, sealing and emitter variability are doubts.

title: Magnesiothermic reduction turns oxide pillars into porous-silicon capacitor electrodes
idea: Pattern SiO2 storage-node pillars by e-beam or i-line litho, react them with Mg vapor at ~650 C (2Mg + SiO2 -> Si + 2MgO), strip MgO in dilute HCl, and keep the resulting doped mesoporous Si as an electrode with ~5-10x surface area, finished with ALD Al2O3/ZrO2 and TiN.
why: Multiplies capacitance per footprint at low aspect ratio (fact 1), so a 10:1 pillar could hold what a 60:1 pillar holds; needs only a furnace, wet bench and ALD.
note: Battery-anode magnesiothermic chemistry; mesopores likely too small to fit a full MIM stack at DRAM pillar dimensions.

title: Mg: magnesiothermic reduction turns stubby oxide posts into porous capacitors
idea: Pattern short SiO2 posts (AR ~15), expose them to Mg vapor at ~650 C so SiO2 + 2Mg -> Si + 2MgO forms a nanoporous Si sponge, strip the MgO, then coat with ALD dielectric and electrode; surface area rises ~10x without a high-aspect-ratio etch.
why: Fact 1: decouples capacitance from aspect ratio, so the 60-75:1 etch (the costliest capacitor step) shrinks to ~15:1 or Cs rises several-fold at the same height.
note: No room for porous Si plus ALD stack inside a ~25 nm post.

title: S: in-tunnel sulfurization converts Mo into lateral MoS2 access channels
idea: Inside the lateral tunnels of a 3D-DRAM stack, ALD a few-angstrom Mo or MoO3 film around a pre-formed gate, then flow H2S or sulfur vapor so it converts in place to MoS2, giving an atomically thin lateral access transistor exactly where 2D-material transfer is impossible.
why: Facts 2 and 3: gas-phase conversion reaches deep lateral cavities, and MoS2's wide gap shrinks the leakage tail to extend refresh intervals.

title: S: sulfide threshold switch adds a leakage dead zone per cell
idea: Insert a GeS-based ovonic threshold switch (sulfur chalcogenide, As- and Se-free) between the access transistor and the capacitor; small leakage-driven voltage drops sit inside its hold-voltage dead zone and cannot drain the node, while full read/write pulses exceed threshold.
why: Decouples retention and disturb immunity from the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3) and passing-gate disturb (fact 9); speculative but could remove most refresh.
note: OTS drop and snapback disturb charge-share read.

title: S: Sulfide self-selecting crosspoint memory without tellurium or arsenic
idea: Build selector-only memory from Ge-S or Si-Ge-S-N sulfide chalcogenides whose polarity-dependent threshold shift stores a bit, stacked as 4F2 crosspoint decks in BEOL; sulfur comes from refinery byproduct.
why: Te/Se/As-free non-volatile crosspoint at ~10-50 ns, density 4F2 divided by deck count.
note: Sulfide SSM avoids Te/As; endurance and threshold-shift retention far from DRAM-class are doubts.

title: Lost-wax gyroid: cast interpenetrating electrodes in block-copolymer molds
idea: Use investment casting. A block-copolymer double gyroid self-assembles in the capacitor trench as the 'wax'. ALD fills one network with TiN, the polymer is burned out, and ZrO2 plus a counter electrode fill the second network, leaving two interpenetrating 3D electrodes at ~10 nm periodicity.
why: Fact 1: a gyroid has 3-5x the area of a cylinder per footprint. It reaches 5 fF at much lower AR, so pillars no longer bend and kill yield.
note: Only a few gyroid cells fit; 5 nm channels cannot hold dielectric plus electrode.

title: Diatom-fermented silica sponge, magnesium-reduced into porous silicon electrodes
idea: Diatoms build nanoporous silica using silaffin peptides. Here those peptides precipitate biosilica conformally inside each cup at room temperature from silicic acid, and magnesiothermic reduction (2Mg + SiO2 -> Si + 2MgO, MgO washed out) turns it into doped porous silicon, which TiO2/Al2O3 then coats to form the capacitor.
why: Fact 1 and scarce resources: a high-area storage electrode (target 5-8x area) from water, silica chemistry and magnesium. No Ru or W precursors and no deep etch.
note: Magnesiothermic reduction ~650 C and Mg contamination in cups are concerns.

title: Thermite-foil flash anneal: reactive Al/Ni layers crystallize BaTiO3 in-cell
idea: Borrow the reactive multilayer foils used for soldering: cap the capacitor stack with a 20 nm Al/Ni nanolaminate and ignite it with a pulse. The self-propagating reaction delivers a ~1 ns, >1000 C local heat spike that crystallizes the BaTiO3/SrTiO3 dielectric into high-k perovskite while the transistors below stay under 400 C.
why: Fact 1: crystalline perovskite at k ~200+ becomes BEOL-compatible without a high-thermal-budget anneal, and the NiAl product becomes the top electrode. Only Al, Ni, Ba, Sr, Ti and O.
note: 1 ns local heat unlikely to crystallize perovskite; thin BaTiO3 dead layers cut k; a 20 nm foil may not self-propagate.

title: Nitinol-stent style ferroelastic twin variants store bits as strain
idea: Borrow shape-memory-alloy training: a nanoscale ferroelastic or martensitic island is trained to two twin variants (strain orientations). A gate-adjacent piezo or electrostatic pulse flips it, and a piezoresistive channel underneath reads it.
why: Zero refresh: crystallographic twin state is non-volatile without charge storage. It differs from ferroelectric and MRAM routes and avoids leakage physics entirely.

title: Slipform tier growth: channels rise through self-aligned tiers
idea: Like slipform concrete poured as the forms climb, grow the vertical channel and the tier stack together: area-selective deposition lays each tier's dielectric and wordline everywhere except on the oxide-semiconductor channel stubs (an inhibitor monolayer binds only there), then selective ALD extends the channels by one tier; no deep hole etch and no per-tier lithography.
why: Eliminates the 60-100:1 vertical etch that caps 3D tier count (fact 2) and removes per-tier masks (fact 4); every tier is self-aligned, so tier count is limited by deposition time rather than etch.
note: Bottom-up ASD avoids deep etch; selectivity defects compound over many tiers.

title: Roll-to-roll memory foil laminated onto logic dies
idea: Run 10 um Invar foil through a newspaper-style web line: roll-to-roll sputter the IGZO/high-k/metal stack, pattern every gain-cell level in one pass with a multi-height self-aligned imprint (SAIL) stamp whose step heights encode each mask level, then laser-cut sheets and laminate them onto logic or base-die BEOL.
why: Capital intensity: a web line costs ~1/50 per m2 of a 300 mm fab and the multi-level stamp collapses ~5 masks into one imprint with zero inter-level overlay; density is relaxed (F 50-100 nm), so it targets a cheap capacity tier.

title: Permanent-mold casting: reusable mold casts capacitor forests for transfer
idea: Instead of etching a fresh 60:1 mold on every wafer, make one ultra-precise AR>100 mold in single-crystal Si with an anti-stiction release liner, ALD-cast TiN/high-k/TiN shells in it, bond the filled mold to the transistor wafer's landing pads, release the capacitor forest, and reuse the mold ~100x like a die-casting die.
why: Facts 1 and 4: HAR etch and its masks amortize over ~100 wafers, so the mold can use slow, perfect processes; ~2x Cs from taller nodes without per-wafer HAR etch capex.

title: Slip-form pour: grow capacitor pillars upward by dual selective deposition
idea: Like slip-forming a concrete silo that climbs as it pours, grow the storage-node pillar and its mold together from the landing-pad pattern: alternate area-selective ALD of TiN-on-TiN and SiO2-on-SiO2 with inhibitors swapped each supercycle, plus periodic etch-back defect correction, so no deep hole is ever etched.
why: Facts 1 and 4: removes the 60-75:1 etch (the costliest etch fleet), with no bowing or twisting, allowing AR>100 and ~2x Cs.
note: AS-ALD selectivity fails after nm of growth; micron-tall co-grown mold needs many correction cycles.

title: Origami membrane: one hinge mask folds memory panels into tiers
idea: Fabricate a <=300 nm oxide-semiconductor memory membrane over a sacrificial film and use the one added mask to place SiN/Cr bilayer stress hinges between panels; on release, hinges fold the membrane accordion-style into 4-8 stacked panels over the periphery, with hinge traces as vertical interconnect.
why: Facts 2 and 6: multi-tier memory from one planar flow plus one mask and no TSVs; footprint density x4-8.

title: Pop-up book kirigami toast rack of edge-mounted DRAM dies
idea: Laser-cut kirigami flex tabs pop up into slots on the interposer so DRAM dies stand on edge around the GPU like toast in a rack, joined by 90-degree edge bonds. Coolant flows between the slices.
why: Fits ~10x more die area within short-reach distance of compute, raising capacity and bandwidth per package footprint.
note: 90-degree edge bonds at fine pitch are the hard part.

title: State-dependent in-cell charge pump fed by global keep-alive wave
idea: IFR: every bit refreshes itself at once, with no row activation. Each cell gets a gated diode whose gate is the storage node and whose plate ties to a chip-wide sinusoidal keep-alive plane; a stored '1' forms the diode channel so each AC cycle pumps a few hundred electrons back in, while a '0' forms no channel and nothing is pumped.
why: Fact 3: refresh commands, sense-amp toggling and refresh bandwidth loss vanish; restore costs only a small AC displacement current, an estimated 10-30x less energy than row-by-row refresh.

title: Threshold-graded tiers selected by voltage eliminate the staircase
idea: IFR: select a tier with no staircase contact. Within each 8-tier group, every tier's channel is deposited with a composition giving a Vt step of ~0.4 V; one vertical wordline selects tier k by amplitude, reads by differential sensing between steps k and k-1, and writes top-down in a cascade so lower-Vt tiers rewritten later are not disturbed.
why: Constraint: staircases and tier contacts are a major area and cost item in 3D memory; removing them makes added tiers nearly free, a key lever for 10x bits at constant wafer cost.
note: Amplitude-selected tiers remove staircase; Vt variation and write disturb across 8 levels are doubtful.

title: Frequency-addressed resonant access: 64 cells share one wire
idea: IFR: address a cell with no wire of its own. Each of 64 cells on a shared line gets a nanomechanical resonator switch with a unique resonant frequency (set by beam length in one patterning step); an RF burst at f_k makes only cell k's beam swing into contact and connect its capacitor, cutting wordline and decoder count 64x.
why: Constraint: wordlines, drivers and decoders are much of the area (fact 7, periphery ~49%); frequency multiplexing over a passive array targets ~10x density at similar cost, with zero off-leakage across open gaps.

title: Charge-coupled vertical pillar: bucket-brigade string instead of per-tier wordlines
idea: IFR: 'no tier needs its own decoder.' Backward: make each vertical pillar a 32-stage charge-coupled shift register with three clock-phase gate planes repeated up the stack; bits are clocked down to one regenerating sense amp at the pillar foot and recirculated, like a CCD image column.
why: 3D blocker and periphery (facts 2, 7): three clock planes replace 32 wordline drivers and the staircase; ~16 ns pillar latency at 2 GHz shift, and circulation doubles as refresh.

title: Draw-tower lithography: fiber-drawn coaxial capacitor faceplates
idea: IFR: 'features shrink without a scanner.' Backward: build a centimeter-scale glass preform of low-melting-metal/dielectric/metal coaxial rods, draw it ~1,000x on a fiber tower, bundle and redraw to ~50-100 nm coax, and slice the fused bundle into 20 um plates, each a dense array of 200:1 coaxial capacitors to bond onto a transistor layer.
why: Charge wall and EUV (facts 1, 4): high-AR capacitors with zero etch or litho; the draw ratio replaces optical reduction.
note: Thermal drawing replaces litho/etch for coax caps; doubts: glass low-k, nanoscale draw uniformity, registration.

title: One-shot epitaxy of stacked GaN electron-gas channel tiers
idea: IFR: 'all tiers grow in one furnace run.' Backward: on sapphire, grow an MOCVD superlattice of 16 AlGaN/GaN heterojunctions, each a 2DEG channel tier with very low off-leakage (3.4 eV gap), then etch gate and storage-node trenches through the stack to form lateral 2DEG gain cells per tier, reusing idle LED/microLED MOCVD fabs.
why: 3D blocker and refresh (facts 2, 3): single-crystal channel tiers with no per-tier deposition or bonding; leakage far below the 13 fA tail.
note: Contacting and isolating individual 2DEG tiers and Si CMOS integration are unsolved; low leakage plausible.

title: Spatial-ALD roll-to-roll steel foil deposits 64-tier stacks
idea: IFR: 'tiers deposit at newspaper speed.' Backward: run stainless-steel foil past spatial-ALD heads (precursor zones split by gas curtains, no pump-down cycles) to lay a 64-tier channel/dielectric superlattice continuously at meters per minute, then pattern vertical holes by roll nanoimprint and fill.
why: Capital (fact 4) and 3D deposition cost: ~10x lower deposition tool cost per tier than batch vacuum ALD/CVD on a cheap U.S.-available foil.
note: Device-grade 64-tier superlattice on rough steel foil plus nanoimprint holes is a big unknown.

title: Anodic-alumina self-ordered pores replace lithography for vertical-channel stacks
idea: Ideal: a memory array that grows itself in a beaker. Closest: atop a Mo/SiO2 tier stack, anodize a Masuda-pre-textured aluminum film into perfectly ordered hexagonal pores (~40 nm pitch) used as a litho-free, self-aligned mask for the vertical holes; ALD ZnSnO channels make strings of 64-128 volatile gain cells, with bitlines registered to the AAO lattice rows.
why: 100x: array cell definition costs one wet anodization (~$0.1/m2) instead of EUV multipatterning; ~7e10 sites/cm2 x 100 tiers ~ 0.9 TB/cm2 raw, so even 5% array efficiency reaches ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades pore-domain defects (spare mapping) and us-class string latency hidden by caching.
note: Litho-free AAO hole lattice over tier stacks is novel; still needs deep etch and registration to bitlines.

title: Second-harmonic phase sensing reads ferroelectric bits without switching them
idea: Constraint: bits must survive power loss and reads must not wear the cell. Store data as HZO polarization but never switch it to read: a 100 mV, ~1 GHz sinusoid on the plate yields a second-harmonic bitline current whose phase flips with polarization direction (dielectric nonlinearity is odd in P), and a per-column mixer clocked from the same plate tone integrates ~5 ns and latches the sign.
why: Non-volatile with a non-destructive read: no write-back (fact 8), no refresh (fact 3), and read endurance effectively unlimited, since wear happens only on writes.
note: Like SNDM, the odd-in-P second-order permittivity reads polarization without switching; signal from fF caps in 5 ns is tiny.

title: Charge-trap access transistor captures each cell's bit at shutdown
idea: Constraint: non-volatile with zero added cell area. The access transistor's gate stack includes a nitride trap layer; at power-fail, bitlines float and a high wordline pulse lets each storage node's own potential (0 or 1 V) set the drain-edge field, injecting charge asymmetrically; at power-up SAs sense the Vt shift by reverse-reading through a gate ramp, then rewrite the capacitors.
why: Per-cell NV backup in the existing footprint (no backup layer). Risk: write disturb and program margin from a 1 V difference.

title: Antiferroelectric avalanche preamp multiplies femtocoulomb ferroelectric signals
idea: Constraint: non-volatile ferroelectric cells too small to give usable charge. At each SA input, a tiny antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitor is biased just below its AFE-to-FE transition field; the cell's switching charge tips it over, releasing a large field-induced polarization step (~5-10x charge gain), and it relaxes back when the bias is removed.
why: Density: lets 3D-stacked FeRAM cells shrink to ~30 nm with ~1 fC signals, with charge gain built from the same HZO/ZrO2 toolset.
note: AFE-to-FE transition as charge amplifier for tiny FeRAM cells; variability and hysteresis unknown.

title: Mist-CVD gallium oxide write transistors, deposited without vacuum
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years and with no vacuum deposition tools: grow alpha-Ga2O3 (~4.9 eV bandgap) channels by ultrasonic mist CVD at atmospheric pressure and ~400 C over the CMOS periphery, giving a gain-cell write transistor whose projected leakage stays in the sub-aA range even hot.
why: Fact 3: refresh-free retention at 125 C; capital: mist-CVD tools cost ~1/10 of ALD/PVD clusters and are BEOL-compatible.

title: Backside-etched trench capacitors use the wafer itself as mold
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: after front-end transistors are bonded to a carrier, thin the wafer to ~3 um and etch capacitor trenches from the back into the silicon under each access transistor, using crystalline silicon as the mold (no carbon mold, no support mesh) for ~25 fF cells.
why: Facts 1 and 3: 4-5x Cs buys 125 C retention; front-side contact AR collapses and the capacitor mold and support-lattice deposition steps disappear.
note: Uniform 3 um thinning and storage-node contact through silicon are the doubts.

title: MicroLED mass-transfer stamps tile micro-chiplet DRAM in laminated layers
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Dice DRAM into 0.5 mm micro-chiplets and use microLED elastomer stamps to place 1e4 per stroke into a planarized polymer layer with printed RDL, repeating 10-20 layers like a PCB build-up.
why: Tiny chiplets yield ~99% and reclaim wafer-edge area, mass transfer cuts placement cost ~100x, and the layered build gives ~10x bits per footprint.
note: Footprint density only; bits still come from the same wafers, and 10-20 layer thermal/interconnect yield is unproven.

title: NbO2 Mott threshold switch as an in-stack local sense element
idea: A ~10-20 nm NbO2 device biased just below its threshold voltage sits on each local bitline segment. A '1' signal (~200 mV on a 64-cell segment) tips it over threshold; Joule heating drives the Mott transition (~1080 K locally) and the device snaps to a low-resistance state, producing a large current spike that a shared global sense line or latch detects. A '0' leaves it insulating. The device is a regenerative, abrupt, non-linear element only ~20 nm across, stackable in the cell tiers. Mott insulators cannot isolate a storage node (their off-state conductivity is many orders too high), so this card uses the transition only for sensing.
why: [SPECULATIVE] Enables 64-cell local bitlines inside a 3D/BEOL stack: Cs need drops 5.4 -> ~1.2 fF and VARY to ~0.4 V (array energy ~16x lower per A1), without 8x more silicon sense amps.

title: Solid-state proton double-layer nano-capacitor [SPECULATIVE]
idea: Replace the high-k film with a 3-5 nm PECVD phosphosilicate-glass (PSG) proton conductor between ion-blocking TiN or W electrodes, optionally with a 1-2 nm pseudocapacitive WO3 or MnO2 skin. Applying the bit voltage (<=~1 V) moves protons a fraction of a nm to form double layers at both interfaces: an all-solid-state nano-supercapacitor with ~10-20 uF/cm2 (EDL) or ~100 uF/cm2 (pseudocapacitive) vs 6.3 uF/cm2 for EOT 0.55 nm. The access transistor and sensing are unchanged. MIT showed nanosecond proton shuttling through PSG at room temperature under ~1 V/nm fields.
why: 5.4 fF from a 0.41 um stub (EDL, 20 uF/cm2) or 0.08 um (pseudocapacitive, 100 uF/cm2) at 21 nm diameter, vs 1.3 um today: 3-16x shorter, with all-abundant P/Si/O/H/W.
note: Ionic double-layer charge likely cannot be extracted at low field within ns.

title: Grow-the-hole: bottom-up dual area-selective deposition replaces the high-aspect-ratio etch [SPECULATIVE]
idea: 3D memory molds are normally deposited and then plasma-etched with holes at aspect ratios of 40-80, the hardest and most fluorocarbon-hungry step in 3D NAND. Instead, define the hole lattice once at the bottom as metal seed dots and grow the stack around them. For each tier, selective CVD tungsten grows ~30 nm only on the exposed W pillar tops (selectivity holds for ~100 nm per cycle), a dielectric (SiO2 or SiN, alternating by tier) grows only on dielectric with a short-lived inhibitor on the W, and an in-situ NF3/H2 etch-back removes stray W nuclei. After the last tier the W pillars are dissolved, leaving vertical holes through the whole stack, aligned by construction.
why: [SPECULATIVE] Eliminates the high-aspect-ratio mold etch: AR 38 (64 tiers) to 77 (128 tiers) with zero plasma etch and no bow or twist; hole CD set by the seed, not by depth.

title: Self-timed NEMS-selector crosspoint: a two-terminal hysteretic nanorelay that charges the capacitor and lets go by itself
idea: Each cell is a stub capacitor (~1 fF) plus a vertical or lateral 2D/ALD nanobeam relay (gap ~5 nm, stiffness ~1 N/m) at a 4F2 crosspoint. Relays have abrupt pull-in and release thresholds (effectively 0 mV/decade), so a half-select voltage below pull-in cannot close them. Write '1': the bitline at 2.2 V closes the relay; the capacitor charges until V_BL - V_cap drops below release (0.75 V); the relay opens and V_cap settles at ~1.45 V, set by mechanics rather than timing. Write '0': a slightly negative bitline leaves 0.45 V. Read: a bitline voltage between the two windows closes the relay only for '0' cells, producing a charge pulse (destructive, then restored). Hold: the gap is open vacuum, so leakage is through the capacitor dielectric only. Lines idle at mid-level and use V/3 biasing so unselected relays never see pull-in.
why: Retention of 6-58 s at 1 fF (against 64 ms); 2-4 decks of 4F2 give 1.3-2.7x 1-beta density at F = 20 nm; the stored level is set by mechanics.

title: Swap per-token old KV for a holographic superposition trace
idea: Substitute discrete per-token storage with superposition. Each distant token's key and value are bound by circular convolution (holographic reduced representations) and added into a fixed d-dimensional trace per head. Recent tokens stay exact, queries unbind the trace for approximate recall, and the model is fine-tuned to tolerate the noise.
why: Old-context memory drops from O(n*d) to O(d) per head, 100x or more at 1M tokens, which caps the KV size for very long contexts. Quality is the risk.

title: Cryogenic quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 capacitor at 77 K
idea: Combine liquid-nitrogen-cooled memory pools with SrTiO3 or KTaO3, quantum paraelectrics whose permittivity climbs from ~300 at room temperature to over 1000 near 77 K. A 5 nm STO film in a planar or AR-10 capacitor then delivers 5 fF without high-AR pillars.
why: Fact 1 and capital: k rises 15-50x over ZrO2, so the capacitor module drops from 60:1 etch to near-planar (~50% lower capacitor-module capex); thin-film k is below bulk, which is the risk.
note: Thin-film STO permittivity collapses below ~10 nm; quantum-paraelectric boost is strongest far below 77 K.

title: Magnify self-ordering: anodized-alumina pore forests replace array lithography
idea: Anodize aluminum films so they self-organize ~10^10 nanopores/cm2 in an electrochemical bath, register the pores to the wordline grid with a nanoimprinted dimple pattern, and ALD-fill each pore as a vertical capacitor plus oxide-semiconductor channel; repeat for 3-4 tiers.
why: Swaps 5-7 EUV array layers (and their depreciation burden) for a ~$10k bath at near-DRAM density per tier; stacking tiers in a small fab targets ~100x lower cost per GB.
note: AAO pore pitch (~100 nm at 1e10/cm2) is ~10x sparser than DRAM cells, undercutting the density claim.

title: Eliminate the stored KV cache: recompute K/V from residual checkpoints
idea: Instead of keeping K and V for every layer, store only the residual-stream vector every 8th layer per token and regenerate K/V for the intermediate layers on the fly during decode, using the FLOPs that sit idle in memory-bound decoding.
why: Attacks data movement and KV capacity: 4-8x less KV memory per session, turning a memory-bound phase into a compute-bound one on hardware with spare FLOPs.
note: Intermediate layers need attention over all tokens, so recompute is a prefill per step.

title: Percolation-edge metal-nanoisland dielectric with giant effective permittivity
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: disperse 1-2-nm Ru or TiN nanoislands in ZrO2 just below the percolation threshold, using ALD nucleation-delay cycles, so percolative/Maxwell-Wagner effects push effective k toward 150-1,000 while isolated islands leave no continuous leakage path.
why: Fact 1: even k~150 would let pillar AR drop to ~25:1; hopping leakage and ns-scale frequency dispersion are the risks.
note: Interfacial giant k relaxes well below GHz and rides on leakage; fundamental trade-off.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium sponge as the storage-node electrode
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: deposit a Ru-Al alloy into a shallow ~10:1 hole, then selectively dissolve the Al so spinodal dealloying leaves a 5-10 nm-ligament Ru sponge; conformal ALD ZrO2 and TiN then coat it, multiplying surface area 5-10x without a tall hole.
why: Trades aspect ratio for internal porosity: 5 fF in a hole ~1/4 as deep, deleting the HAR etch and support-mesh steps (facts 1, 4).
note: 5-10 nm pores cannot hold ~5 nm ZrO2 plus a TiN top electrode.

title: Layer-stride KV checkpoints recomputed by idle tensor cores
idea: TRIZ #8 Counterweight: balance scarce memory with abundant FLOPs by storing the residual-stream hidden state only every Nth layer (e.g., N=4) for cold tokens and recomputing the intermediate layers' K/V on demand during decode, using the tensor-core slack that memory-bound decode leaves idle.
why: Decode runs at 10-30% compute utilization; spending that slack cuts cold-context KV memory ~3-4x with modest added latency.
note: Recomputing intermediate layers for all cold tokens each step scales with context and exceeds idle FLOPs.

title: Thermophile S-layer protein crystals template sub-10 nm cell pitch
idea: Self-assemble an archaeal S-layer protein lattice (2D crystals with 10-13 nm unit cells) on the wafer inside coarse DUV guide frames, convert it to an inorganic AlOx hard mask by sequential infiltration synthesis, and etch vertical access pillars at that pitch: nature's own crystalline lithography.
why: Litho-bound scaling and EUV dependence: sub-EUV pitch with zero EUV exposures; 4F2 vertical cells at very small F could give several-x bits per area if defectivity is controlled.

title: Sea-urchin amorphous precursor infiltration crystallizes high-k inside pores
idea: Sea urchins fill spine molds with a liquid-like amorphous carbonate and crystallize it in place; flow a polymer-stabilized liquid amorphous titanate precursor into capacitor holes by capillarity, then crystallize it to rutile TiO2 or SrTiO3 (k 80-150) at low temperature on a thin seed liner that templates the phase.
why: Delivers k~100 (fact 1) with a spin-and-bake instead of slow ALD supercycles; est. 5x faster dielectric module and a shorter, easier-to-etch capacitor.
note: TiO2/STO leakage and sol-gel thickness control in 70:1 holes.

title: Developmental genome grows weights from seeds and growth rules
idea: Each weight matrix is stored as a compact 'genome' (PRNG seeds, a small hypernetwork and low-rank corrections) that is expanded tile-by-tile into SRAM at use time, the way a genome encodes a body plan instead of every cell's coordinates; DRAM holds only the genome.
why: Weight capacity: 10-50x smaller resident footprint for layers that tolerate generative parameterization, trading cheap compute for scarce DRAM bits.

title: Swiss-roll pastry: strain-released self-rolling capacitor stack
idea: Deposit a planar TiN/Al2O3-HfO2/TiN stack on a strained SiNx bilayer over a sacrificial layer; selective release lets the built-in strain roll it into a 3-5-turn microtube, multiplying capacitor area per footprint ~10x from planar deposition only, like rolling a Swiss roll.
why: Facts 1 and 2: 3D capacitance with no high-AR etch, a natural fit for lateral capacitors in horizontal 3D DRAM; demonstrated with sputter, ALD and wet release in university labs; shrinking roll diameters below ~1 um is the risk.
note: Rolled tubes are micron-scale; shrinking to a DRAM cell pitch is the doubt.

title: Perovskite-solar ink chemistry for k-70 capacitor dielectrics
idea: Borrowed from perovskite-solar labs, which make films by spin-coating inks and low-temperature anneals: infiltrate Ba-Sr-Ti alkoxide inks into storage holes with supercritical-CO2 assist, then crystallize the BST (k 70-150) by flash-lamp photonic curing, all in a glovebox-scale line a 10-person team can run.
why: Fact 1: a k jump allows AR ~50 instead of 115 without a $5M ALD tool; conformal infiltration into 20 nm holes and leakage at nm thickness are high risk.

title: Copper-oxide rectifier revival: diode-access capacitor crosspoint, stacked tiers
idea: Revive the 1920s cuprous-oxide rectifier as a BEOL p-Cu2O/n-ZnO heterojunction diode in series with a MIM capacitor at each crosspoint, selected coincident-current style like core planes (half-select stays below diode turn-on) and stacked in several DUV-patterned tiers.
why: No access transistor, no tungsten, no Hf and no EUV, using abundant Cu, Zn and O; claims 4F2 per tier over 4 tiers; the honest risk is diode reverse leakage limiting retention.
note: Oxide diode reverse leakage limits retention.

title: Colloidal sphere monolayers print the DRAM honeycomb
idea: Inverts 'patterns must be printed'. Langmuir-transfer a monolayer of 40 nm silica spheres; they self-pack into the same hexagonal lattice DRAM capacitors use, are shrunk by O2/CF4 RIE and serve as the etch mask, while 180 nm stepper fences force grain boundaries onto dummy rows.
why: Sub-50 nm honeycomb with no EUV (fact 4); remaining grain defects absorbed by spare rows.
note: Registration of self-packed sphere lattice to buried wordlines and landing pads is the core doubt.

title: Generative weight seeds expanded on the memory base die
idea: Invert 'needed bytes must be stored and moved verbatim': store weights as a PRNG seed plus a low-rank or quantized residual, and let a base-die engine regenerate the full tensor on demand as it streams to the GPU.
why: If 50-80% of weight information folds into seeds plus residual, DRAM capacity and link traffic for weights drop 2-5x, stretching scarce bits.

title: Negative-U oxygen-vacancy metastability as an electrically-written bit
idea: In RT-sputtered amorphous ZnSnO or InGaZnO, oxygen vacancies are negative-U: ionized VO2+ relaxes the lattice outward, and a configuration-coordinate barrier (~0.5-1 eV) blocks recapture. Hole injection writes (vacancies ionize and the channel conducts), electron injection with gate field erases, and the read senses channel conductance.
why: Turns the defect behind oxide-TFT persistent photoconductivity into the storage element, with no capacitor (fact 1). Retention is set by a lattice-relaxation barrier, not a junction leakage tail (fact 3).
note: Hole injection into n-type IGZO is hard; PPC decays over hours.

title: Catalytic metal-assisted etching drills 3D DRAM holes, no plasma
idea: First principle: plasma etch rate collapses with depth because ions and neutrals must reach the hole bottom (Knudsen transport), whereas metal-assisted chemical etching dissolves Si only at the catalyst/Si interface, so its rate does not depend on depth. Imprint Au or Pt nanodots on an epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice and let them sink through 100+ tiers in HF/H2O2 to form the vertical bitline and channel holes of a 3D DRAM.
why: 3D DRAM blocker (fact 2) and etch capex: a wet bench replaces cryo-etch tools (~$5-8M each) and reaches tier counts where plasma etch stalls.

title: Borax box: boron-aluminum nitride ferroelectric from U.S. boron, no scandium
idea: Stimulus 'borax laundry box' (mined in Boron, California) -> sputter wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric (remanent polarization ~100 uC/cm^2, ~5-10x HZO) from Al/B targets in N2/Ar and pattern it with Cl2/BCl3; use it as a planar storage capacitor or ferroelectric gate. No hafnium, scandium or fluorine.
why: ~10x charge per area enables a planar storage element (fact 1) built from abundant domestic boron and aluminum (scarce-resource and U.S. manufacturability axes).
note: Huge coercive fields and poor endurance in AlBN/AlScN conflict with DRAM-class cycling.

title: Self-organized anodic TiO2 nanotubes as both dielectric and 3D mold
idea: [Box: rutile TiO2 charge (k~80-100) | VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | Ti anodization + RuO2-templated rutile anneal] Anodize a sputtered Ti film over the landing pads into vertically aligned nanotubes nucleated on each pad, crystallize them to rutile on a RuO2 seed, and fill tube cores with the storage electrode, so the high-k dielectric grows itself in 3D with no hole lithography or plasma etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1, k~70 target) and no EUV (fact 4): mold, etch and dielectric deposition collapse into one electrochemical step.
note: Anodic TiO2 tubes are too wide, defective and leaky for DRAM pitch; self-ordering will not register to pads.

title: Colloidal BaTiO3 nanocube dielectric poured into capacitor wells
idea: Worsen: make a k ~70 dielectric only by atom-by-atom ALD. Flip: borrow the MLCC industry's BaTiO3 nanocube powders, spin-cast self-assembled 10-20 nm cubes into shallow capacitor wells and infiltrate them with ALD alumina, aiming at effective k of 100-300 in a $1M, 24-month bench program.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): AR could drop to ~20:1, with low capital and an existing MLCC supply chain.
note: Alumina infill in series and BTO size effect drop effective k sharply.

title: Baker's leavened bread: dealloyed nanoporous metal capacitor electrodes
idea: Bread rises because yeast leaves holes. Sputter a 300 nm Ag-Au or Cu-Mn alloy, dealloy it in acid to a nanoporous metal with 15-30 nm ligaments, then coat it with ALD high-k and an ALD TiN top electrode.
why: ~10-20x electrode area per footprint at 0.3 um height instead of 70:1 pillars (Fact 1). A sputter tool, an acid bath and ALD fit a small team.

title: Oyster's trick: hydrothermal perovskite capacitor dielectric grown at 150 C
idea: A marine biologist notes that shells grow ceramics in cold seawater. Line the capacitor holes with ALD TiO2, then convert it in place to crystalline SrTiO3 or BaTiO3 by hydrothermal reaction in Sr(OH)2/Ba(OH)2 solution at 120-200 C, skipping the 600-700 C crystallization anneal.
