idea: Invert 'dies stack flat on top of each other': thin DRAM dies are inserted vertically like books into a deep-etched silicon comb, I/O routed to one edge and joined by sidewall metallization to the comb floor; each die's full edge is its beachfront and heat flows in-plane to a top cold plate.
why: No TSVs, no 30 um thinning, no vertical thermal stacking penalty; aims at HBM-class density and bandwidth at near-DDR5 wafer area per bit (removing much of the ~3x HBM area tax).
note: Same edge-on die mounting.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory vault on U.S. industrial gas
idea: Invert 'memory runs at room temperature beside compute': put DRAM sleds in a liquid-nitrogen bath from domestic air-separation plants next to the racks, linked optically; at 77 K leakage falls orders of magnitude and wire resistance ~5-7x.
why: Refresh nearly vanishes (16-33% of idle power), retention rises, and cold copper allows longer passive links at the same pJ/bit.

title: Nanoimprint the periodic cell array, keep EUV for periphery
idea: Inverts 'every critical DRAM layer needs EUV': because the cell array is a near-perfect periodic lattice, pattern it with nanoimprint masters replicated from one e-beam write, and use EUV or 193i only for irregular periphery layers.
why: EUV single supplier and capex: removes 3-5 EUV exposures per wafer; litho capex per wafer start could fall 25-35%.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer bit with zero bond-breaking switching
idea: Use rhombohedral-stacked bilayer hBN or MoS2: its out-of-plane polarization flips when one layer slides by a/sqrt(3), so the barrier is only interlayer stacking energy (meV per cell, ~1 eV for a 10 nm domain) and no ion or bond moves. Read the polarization non-destructively through the field it imposes on an adjacent MoS2 channel.
why: Fatigue mechanisms (vacancy migration, domain pinning) need bond rearrangement; removing them targets >1e12 endurance at ~aJ switching energy in an atomically thin cell. Attacks the charge wall (1), destructive read (8) and voltage floor (10).
note: Sliding FE fatigue-free reports exist; wafer-scale stacking-order control is the gap.

title: Sub-damage-threshold direct-tunneling charge trap with volatile retention
idea: Store ~500 electrons in a nitride layer whose traps are engineered ~0.9 eV deep behind a 1.6 nm SiO2 tunnel oxide, written by direct tunneling at <2 V. Electrons never exceed the ~2-3 eV hot-carrier energy that generates oxide defects, and thermal emission gives ~0.5 s retention at 85 C (~100 s at 25 C), matched to refresh.
why: Flash wear-out is hot-carrier defect generation, so staying below that energy aims at >1e15 cycles. Gives a capacitorless ~4F2 1T cell with no pillar (facts 1, 4).
note: Echoes nanocrystal/dual-function DRAM-flash work; SILC under direct tunneling may still limit endurance.

title: Stray-field-free antiferromagnetic tunnel junction bits packed at pitch
idea: Build Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions, where cluster-octupole order gives TMR with no net moment, and write them by spin-orbit torque with ps-scale intrinsic dynamics. With zero stray field, neighbor cells sit at 1-2F spacing without dipolar disturb.
why: Ferromagnetic MRAM density is capped by stray-field coupling; antiferromagnetic order removes it. Aims at sub-ns write and near-4F2 density with no capacitor or refresh (facts 1, 3).

title: Magnetoelectric exchange-coupled write: attojoule polarization flips magnet
idea: Put a 20 nm La-doped BiFeO3 layer under a CoFe nanomagnet: a ~100-200 mV pulse rotates BFO's coupled ferroelectric/antiferromagnetic order, and interfacial exchange drags the magnet 180 degrees. An MTJ on top reads the state.
why: Write energy is ~2Pr*A*V ~ 1e-16 J for a 30 nm cell at 0.1 V, ~1000x below current-driven STT and well under the CV2 floor of fact 10.
note: MESO-style BFO exchange switching widely pursued; 100 mV switching and BFO fatigue remain open.

title: Adiabatic ramped write that recovers the cell's CV2 energy
idea: A step charge through any resistor dissipates CV2/2, but a ramp of duration T >> RC dissipates only ~(RC/T)*CV2. Drive wordlines, bitlines and precharge from a resonant LC tank clock so cell writes ride a slow sinusoid and their charge returns to the tank.
why: Cuts write and precharge energy 3-10x at the same 1 V / 3 V levels, getting under the voltage floor (fact 10) without lowering voltage.

title: Proton-intercalation channel bit using the lightest mobile ion
idea: Stack a BEOL (<=350 C) WO3 channel over a hydrogenated HfO2 or PSG proton reservoir. A ~10 ns gate pulse moves ~1e3 protons into the channel and shifts conductance ~10x, read non-destructively; protons are chosen because ionic mobility scales inversely with ion mass and size.
why: Ionic storage at near-electronic speed with a uA read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1). The risk is retention and endurance under ns pulses.

title: Bucket-brigade CCD columns feed one floating diffusion per column
idea: For a streaming tier, arrange each 512-cell column as a charge-coupled shift register that clocks charge packets to a single floating-diffusion readout at the column end, as 1970s CCD memories did, but with modern 0.5 fF sense nodes reading ~1k e- packets.
why: Periphery collapses to one sense node per column, no per-bitline SA (fact 7); very high density for sequential workloads.

title: Bipolar transistor sense amplifiers escape MOS mismatch and BTI
idea: BJT offset depends on emitter-area matching (sigma dVbe ~0.2-0.5 mV) rather than random channel dopants (MOS sigma Vt ~5-15 mV), and BJTs have no gate oxide to suffer BTI drift. Use vertical SiGe BJT latches in a BiCMOS periphery for sensing.
why: ~10x lower offset means ~5-10x less cell charge needed (fact 1); offset stays stable through 10 y at 125 C.

title: Green-laser melt crystallizes each silicon tier using nine joules per wafer
idea: Melting a 20 nm Si film over a 300 mm wafer needs ~3 mg x ~2.8 MJ/kg = ~9 J, and a nanosecond pulse's ~100 nm thermal diffusion length keeps lower tiers cold. Deposit a-Si by PECVD and crystallize it with a green solid-state laser through grain-filter seed holes so each transistor sits in one grain; repeat for 32 tiers.
why: Crystalline-quality tiers at ~$15 per tier with no epi, no germanium and no neon excimer lasers; 32 tiers x relaxed cell = ~10x density at equal cost.
note: Grain-filter laser crystallization is known; per-tier patterning keeps cost per bit from falling 10x.

title: Nanoimprint guides plus block-copolymer rectification replace EUV array layers
idea: First principle: imprint costs mechanical work, not photons (EUV turns ~0.02% of wall power into dose), but imprint suffers defects, while block copolymers anneal toward their free-energy minimum and heal defective guides. Imprint coarse 2x-pitch guides, then let a high-chi BCP (e.g., PS-b-PDMS) self-assemble to the final ~24 nm pitch, repairing imprint defects before pattern transfer.
why: EUV dependence (fact 4): tool ~$15M vs ~$200M and ~1/50 the power; removes the single-supplier EUV dependence for array layers.

title: Endurance-budget tiering: unlimited endurance only where writes demand it
idea: From first principles, DRAM's unlimited endurance matters only for frequently written pages, and most resident bytes are written less than once an hour. Per-page write-rate counters in the controller migrate write-cold pages to a cheaper byte-addressable tier with limited endurance (NOR-like or high-bandwidth flash), and the controller enforces wear budgets.
why: If 50-70% of resident bytes are write-cold, DRAM per server can roughly halve while reads stay byte-addressable.
note: Needs a cheap byte-addressable endurance-limited tier that does not exist post-Optane.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods with kT-scaled link swings
idea: Thermal noise and leakage both scale with temperature: at 77 K, kT drops 4x, copper resistivity ~7x and access-transistor leakage collapses. Immerse HBM-plus-accelerator modules in LN2 and redesign links for ~4x lower swing, longer unrepeated wires and lower threshold voltages, with refresh nearly eliminated.
why: ~2-4x link energy reduction plus refresh removal and a lower voltage floor (facts 3, 5, 10).

title: Time-share each DRAM gigabyte among a hundred tenants via optical swap
idea: A working set only needs DRAM while it runs. Give accelerators small DRAM plus a co-packaged-optics swap path (~10 TB/s) to a NAND pool and gang-schedule jobs so each job's working set swaps in for a 10-20 ms slot; one DRAM GB serves ~100 tenants in rotation.
why: Effective DRAM per tenant ~100x lower; trades latency, job slicing and swap energy.

title: Direct-tunneling germanium nanocrystal trap cell: volatile but wear-free
idea: Charge-trap flash wears out because FN/hot-carrier injection gives electrons enough energy to break oxide bonds. With a 1.5-2 nm tunnel layer, writes at <2 V happen by direct tunneling below the damage threshold. Discrete Ge nanocrystals mean one leaky path drains only one dot. Target ~1 s retention, >1e15 cycles, scrubbed like DRAM.
why: Capacitorless, low-voltage writes, ~15x rarer refresh. Endurance comes from energy-below-damage physics, not from margin.
note: Nanocrystal direct-tunnel memory explored in 1990s-2000s; speed vs retention tradeoff.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall cell with non-destructive read
idea: Charged domain walls in LiNbO3/BiFeO3 films conduct 1e3-1e6x more than the bulk. Write by creating or erasing a wall segment between two electrodes with a sub-ns lateral field pulse. Read the wall current without switching polarization, unlike FeRAM's destructive read. The state is polarization topology, so no charge leaks.
why: Destructive read (fact 8) and refresh (fact 3) both removed. Wall pinning, the residual failure mode, is handled by write-verify plus ECC.
note: LiNbO3 domain-wall NDRO memory is active research; scaling and wall pinning unresolved.

title: Buckled-nanobeam bistable bit stores data mechanically
idea: A pre-compressed SiN/SiC nanobeam has two buckled states separated by an elastic barrier of ~1e-18 J (>1e5 kT), so it can't leak or relax. An electrostatic snap-through pulse writes it, a capacitive or piezoresistive gauge reads it non-destructively, and with no contact the elastic cycling exceeds 1e12.
why: Refresh-free, no charge tail, built on a U.S.-native MEMS process. Speed and density still need proof.
note: Buckled-beam bistable memory known; speed and density unproven.

title: Cash-settled DRAM bit futures damp the cobweb shortage cycle
idea: The DRAM boom-bust behaves like a delay-line oscillator: a 3-5 year capacity lag chasing a ~1-year demand signal (cobweb model). A cash-settled Gb futures curve out to 4 years gives fabs a forward price to hedge expansions and buyers a way to lock supply, effectively shortening the control loop's delay.
why: Supply stability: lowers the peak-to-trough amplitude that produced the 4x price spike, and hedged revenue reduces risk premia on new capacity.

title: Nanoimprint array patterning sidesteps EUV's ruthenium and molybdenum optics
idea: EUV mirrors rely on Mo/Si multilayers with Ru caps, so a Ru-free DRAM cannot lean on EUV. Pattern the periodic array layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint from fused-silica (Si, O) replica templates cloned from one master, where pattern transfer costs mechanical contact rather than 92 eV photons.
why: EUV single-supplier and capital: NIL tools cost ~1/10 of EUV at ~1/10 the power, and array redundancy absorbs imprint defects.

title: Zipper: sliding bilayer registry flips polarization by one atom-step
idea: Stimulus 'zipper' (two rows of teeth interlock in one of two registries) -> bilayer hBN or MoS2 stacked AB or BA; a vertical field slides one layer by one bond length, flipping the interfacial polarization, read by tunnel current through the bilayer. Switching is a shear slide, not ion or defect motion, so fatigue is minimal.
why: Sub-nm nonvolatile storage element switching below 0.5 V breaks the CV^2 voltage floor (fact 10) and removes refresh (fact 3); transferable sheets stack as BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Apollo core rope: toroidal nanomagnet rings with coincident-current selection
idea: Stimulus 'Apollo core memory' -> revive ferrite-core memory at 100 nm: each bit is a closed-flux CoFeB nanoring whose clockwise/counterclockwise circulation flips only where two half-select currents in a crossbar coincide, so no access transistor is needed. Read uses a tunnel junction on one arc of the ring.
why: Removes the access transistor and its leakage tail (fact 3), turns the array into a pure BEOL crossbar stackable in tiers (fact 2), and flux closure gives zero stray field for tight packing.
note: Same as nanoring core revival; half-select currents heavy at 100 nm.

title: Abacus beads: successive-approximation sensing reads two bits per cell
idea: Read like sliding abacus beads one rank at a time: after charge sharing a 2-step SAR sense amp compares against a mid reference for the MSB, then switches in a binary-weighted half-step reference capacitor to resolve the LSB, and a 4-level write driver restores one of four voltages.
why: Density and cost per bit ~2x with the same capacitor, but it needs ~3-4x signal, so it must pair with a gain or low-C_BL idea; adds ~20% SA area.

title: Coin-counting machine: multi-row charge summation read by bitline ADC
idea: A coin counter weighs the pile instead of counting coins one at a time: activate up to 8 rows of a bit-plane at once so their cell charges sum on each bitline, then digitize the analog sum with a 3-bit SAR built from the SA's reference caps, returning popcounts or dot-product partial sums rather than raw bits.
why: One activation replaces 8 activations plus 8x data transfer for reductions and binary/ternary dot products; ~10-30x less energy per useful operation; risks are cell variation and destroyed data needing copy rows.

title: Bookshelf: dies stand on edge, bonded spine-down onto logic
idea: Books stand spine-out on a shelf: dice 30 um DRAM dies, polish one edge to expose bitline and I/O wires routed there, then stand 100+ dies upright and hybrid-bond their edges onto a logic base die. Each edge carries thousands of wires at ~2 um pitch, and no die needs a TSV.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6) and data movement (fact 5): no TSV area or yield loss, one base die hosts 100+ dies with short uniform wires; claim ~1 pJ/bit and TB-class stacks.

title: Coral reef: self-ordered anodic alumina pores as capacitor molds
idea: Coral builds its skeleton bottom-up: deposit ~1.5 um of Al over the transistor array, pre-dimple it at each storage-node landing pad, and anodize it. Self-organized pores grow straight down from the dimples at aspect ratios beyond 100:1, and lining them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN makes the capacitors with no high-AR plasma etch.
why: Capacitor wall and capital (facts 1, 4): AR >100:1 from wet electrochemistry; claim capacitor-module capex -50% and Cs ~8 fF.

title: Creme brulee torch: laser-grown single grains form monolithic cell tiers
idea: A torch caramelizes only the top: deposit amorphous Si over the finished periphery and lower array, then melt it with an excimer laser through a micro-Czochralski grain filter (a seed hole at each cell site), growing one single-crystal grain under each future access transistor at a BEOL thermal budget. Extra cell tiers stack above, and the die is still a standard DDR5 part at ~2x density.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2): near-single-crystal upper-tier transistors without wafer bonding; claim 2-4 tiers at <450 C for ~1.8x bits per die area.
note: Micro-Czochralski grain filter is known (TU Delft); DRAM-grade leakage in laser grains unproven.

title: Bamboo: grow vertical access transistors by in-situ-doped selective epitaxy
idea: Random stimulus 'bamboo' (grows in segments from a node) -> vertical channel transistors for 4F2 cells are grown, not etched: single-crystal silicon pillars are selectively epitaxied up through spacer-shrunk holes in an oxide template, switching dopant gas mid-growth to form n+/p/n+ junctions with abrupt profiles.
why: Removes the high-AR pillar etch and 2-3 implant/anneal steps. Grown sidewalls are damage-free, which narrows the leakage tail (fact 3), and the 4F2 layout gives 1.5x density over 6F2 without a node shrink.

title: Fingerprint: random self-assembled cells with a per-die learned address map
idea: Random stimulus 'fingerprint' (unique random pattern, identified after the fact) -> only coarse wordline/bitline grids are patterned with relaxed DUV, and storage elements form randomly at crossings from block-copolymer or nanoparticle self-assembly with no registration. A built-in self-test fingerprints each die and writes a remap table, so the controller addresses only crossings that captured a working cell.
why: Removes overlay and critical-litho requirements for the storage node (fact 4). The design accepts ~60-80% site occupancy in exchange for eliminating several EUV/ArFi layers; this trades 20-40% raw area for large capex savings.

title: Fridge magnet: define MTJ bits by ion irradiation, not etching
idea: Random stimulus 'fridge magnet' (stripes magnetized into a continuous sheet) -> the STT-MRAM stack stays continuous, and He+/N+ or oxygen ions implanted through a DUV-patterned mask destroy perpendicular anisotropy and tunnel magnetoresistance in the gaps, isolating bits magnetically without ion-beam etching the stack.
why: Non-volatile MRAM with endurance >1e12. It removes the MTJ etch (sidewall redeposition shorts, the yield killer) and IBE tools, and could cut MTJ pitch from ~90 nm to ~45 nm at DUV, about 4x density.

title: Conducting charged domain wall in thin-film lithium niobate as bit
idea: Box = {medium: presence or absence of a conducting head-to-head domain wall in LiNbO3-on-insulator | access: Si FET in the CMOS below | sense: nondestructive wall current (on/off ~1e4) | integration: hybrid-bonded LNOI film over logic | substrate: LNOI | fab: ion slicing + e-beam-defined electrode pairs}. A ~3 V pulse between two in-plane electrodes 30 nm apart nucleates or erases a charged wall bridging them; a read only measures conduction through the wall, so polarization never reverses on read.
why: Fact 8 destructive read and Fact 3 refresh: a nonvolatile cell with nondestructive read (NDRO) avoids restore energy (~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and refresh; wall motion needs no oxygen-vacancy drift, so endurance may exceed hafnia.
note: LiNbO3 domain-wall memory with NDRO already demonstrated (Jiang group); scaling and retention open.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn tunnel junction with zero stray field
idea: Box = {medium: magnetic octupole order in Mn3Sn | access: Si FinFET | sense: antiferromagnetic tunnel magnetoresistance | integration: BEOL above periphery | substrate: Si | fab: sputtered Mn3Sn on a Pt spin-orbit-torque line, 400 C anneal}. Spin-orbit torque rotates the octupole; with no net magnetization, cells at 15 nm pitch do not disturb neighbors and switch in tens of picoseconds.
why: Density and energy: removes the stray-field pitch limit of ferromagnetic MRAM, sub-100 ps writes at ~10 fJ, built from abundant Mn and Sn.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN gating a MoS2 channel
idea: Box = {medium: interlayer-sliding polarization of parallel-stacked bilayer hBN | access: MoS2 channel underneath acting as a FeFET | sense: nondestructive channel conductance | integration: BEOL 2D stack on logic | substrate: Si | fab: wafer-scale CVD + transfer}. Polarization flips by an interlayer slip of a fraction of a lattice constant, with no bond breaking or oxygen-vacancy motion, which early reports suggest gives fatigue-free switching past 1e11 cycles at sub-volt fields.
why: Endurance and the voltage floor (Fact 10): sub-volt switching with no ion motion, nonvolatile so no refresh, and an atomically thin storage layer for many-tier stacking.
note: Same sliding-FE mechanism.

title: Magnetoelectric Cr2O3 antiferromagnet written by voltage, read by Hall
idea: Box = {medium: Neel vector of boron-doped Cr2O3 | access: Si FET | sense: anomalous Hall voltage in an adjacent Pt film | integration: BEOL | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + boron doping to lift the Neel point above 400 K}. Because Cr2O3 is magnetoelectric, its Neel vector flips under a small voltage combined with a static bias field built into the stack, with no charge current through the bit.
why: Energy (Fact 10): aJ-to-fJ write energy, nonvolatile, no current-induced wear, and antiferromagnetic order immune to neighbor disturb.
note: Nebraska B:Cr2O3 work is prior art; needs bias field, small Hall readout signal.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch revived as refresh-free one-transistor SRAM
idea: Box = {medium: bistable node voltage between two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (negative differential resistance) | access: one Si FET | sense: standard bitline | integration: diodes stacked vertically on the drain | substrate: Si | fab: low-temperature epitaxy of delta-doped tunnel junctions}. The two NDR curves cross at two stable points held by valley current alone, so the cell is static like SRAM in a ~8F2 DRAM-like footprint.
why: Fact 3: no refresh and no capacitor, 3-4x denser than 6T SRAM; standby power is set by valley current, which must reach <1 pA per cell.
note: Tunneling SRAM proposed by TI in 1990s; pA valley current per cell is the hurdle.

title: JEDEC retention-map register and per-row refresh command
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sense x vendor-measured retention class per row group exposed in a readable register plus a targeted-row refresh command x controller multi-rate refresh x Si x zero masks. Policy: push the standard through JEDEC and require it in CHIPS-funded and federal procurement so every vendor ships it.
why: Most rows retain >1 s; multi-rate refresh cuts refresh 70%+ (fact 3) but has been blocked by missing vendor data, which a standard unlocks.
note: Multi-rate refresh (RAIDR) blocked by vendor data; JEDEC adoption slow and vendor-resisted.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM with cryo-tuned long-bitline sense amps
idea: Box: smaller cap x Si access x cryo-optimized SA x LN2-immersed module x bulk Si x standard fab. At 77 K the subthreshold slope falls to ~20 mV/dec and mismatch narrows, so SAs resolve smaller signals; bitlines grow 4x and retention reaches hours, removing most refresh logic.
why: SA count /4 (periphery ~-20%) and refresh ~0; energy per bit lower even after cooling overhead in large AI pods.

title: Dies stand edge-on on the base die, wired through cut edges
idea: [Box: standard 1T1C | Si FET | conventional SA | edge-mounted 'bookshelf' dies | thinned Si | dicing exposes top metal + edge micro-bump plating] Instead of stacking DRAM dies flat with TSVs, stand thinned dies vertically on the logic base die and bring thousands of fine wires out of the polished die edge, where top-metal lines exposed by dicing are plated into edge bumps.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSV keep-out area and no thinning/TSV yield loss (20-30%); capacity scales with dies per row rather than stack height.

title: Epitaxial vertical pnpn thyristor pillars as capacitorless 4F2 cells
idea: [Box: thyristor bistable conduction | gated self-latching pnpn | current sense | monolithic, repeatable by layer transfer | Si | in-situ doped blanket epitaxy then pillar etch] Grow a blanket p+/n/p/n+ epitaxial stack so junction positions are set by deposition, etch it into pillars and wrap a gate on the p-base; the latched/blocking state is dynamic storage with large read current and no capacitor.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and 3D (fact 2): no capacitor, junctions defined by epitaxy not lithography, and identical stacks can be transferred tier by tier.
note: Very close to Kilopass VLT / T-RAM; thermal sensitivity and standby current are known issues.

title: Mask-free interference lithography for perfectly periodic cell arrays
idea: [Box: 1T1C | VCT | standard SA | monolithic | Si | 193 nm two/three-beam immersion interference + one spacer step + low-res block mask] DRAM arrays are periodic, so expose them with mask-less two- and three-beam 193 nm immersion interference (~34 nm half-pitch per shot, ~17 nm after one spacer step) and trim array edges with a cheap low-resolution DUV block mask.
why: No EUV (fact 4): no reticle and much simpler optics; litho cost per array layer could drop to roughly a fifth of EUV.

title: Laser-grown location-controlled silicon grains for stacked single-crystal tiers
idea: [Box: 1T1C or 2T0C | grain-boundary-free Si FET | standard SA | monolithic sequential tiers | Si | excimer laser + DUV grain-filter holes (micro-Czochralski)] On each new tier, deposit a-Si over a small DUV-patterned grain-filter hole at every transistor site and melt it with an excimer laser, so one grain grows from each hole and a single-crystal island lands exactly where each transistor goes.
why: 3D (fact 2) without EUV: near-single-crystal, low-leakage transistors on every tier at relaxed DUV pitch, with density from tier count.
note: Dup of location-controlled laser grains.

title: Keep the SiGe layers: superlattice wells become floating-body storage
idea: [Box: holes in a SiGe quantum well | lateral Si nanosheet FET | current sense | monolithic Si/SiGe superlattice | Si | epitaxy-defined layers, ArF slits] Normally the SiGe in a 3D-DRAM superlattice is sacrificial; instead grade each sheet as Si channel / thin SiGe well / Si so the valence-band offset traps holes as a capacitorless storage node under each lateral gate.
why: 3D blockers (fact 2): no lateral capacitor, ~3x shorter cell; all critical dimensions set by epitaxy thickness.
note: SiGe QW 1T-DRAM published; floating-body retention poor.

title: Panel-scale DRAM: oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays on Gen-8.5 LCD glass
idea: Box [MIM cap | IGZO TFT | off-panel Si sense-amp chiplets | panel-level fan-out | 2.2x2.5 m glass | LCD-line photolithography]: fabricate relaxed-pitch (F~1 um) oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays on idle, depreciated LCD lines, dice into tiles and flip-chip Si sense/periphery chiplets at panel level for a capacity tier.
why: Capital/EUV and crucible intensity: F=1 um gives ~16 Mb/cm2, so one 5.5 m2 panel holds ~100 GB with no EUV and no crystalline-Si array; low density limits it to slow capacity tiers.
note: Same Gen-8.5 oxide-TFT memory as I-06624.

title: 2T1C cell with in-cell preamp shrinks capacitor to 1 fF stub
idea: Box [1 fF stub cap, AR ~12:1 | Si access + stacked vertical oxide-TFT read transistor | current sense | monolithic | CZ Si | standard]: the storage node both holds charge on a short capacitor and gates a stacked read transistor, so readout is non-destructive current rather than charge sharing.
why: Capacitor charge wall and materials: AR 70:1 drops to ~12:1, cutting mold-etch fluorocarbons and ALD precursor per bit ~5x and removing destructive-read write-back energy.
note: Small cap gating read FET is known gain-cell-with-cap art; leakage still sets retention.

title: Monolithic gain-cell memory in logic BEOL using dry steps only
idea: Box: 2T0C gain cell x ALD In2O3 channel transistors x current sensing in logic FEOL x monolithic BEOL integration x the logic wafer x ALD, plasma etch and vapor-HF cleans only. Memory layers are deposited above the compute inside its interconnect stack: no separate DRAM wafer, no dicing, no thinning, no package-level memory link.
why: Water: the separate DRAM fab and packaging water disappear and the added BEOL steps are dry, >10x less per GB; data movement drops to ~0.05 pJ/bit.
note: imec-style 2T0C BEOL is widely pursued.

title: Corrected-error-rate feedback drives each bank to its own Vmin
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard with per-bank VARY/VPP regulators | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. An on-die loop lowers each bank's VARY and VPP in 10 mV steps until the ECC-corrected error rate hits a target such as 1 per 1e9 bits, and raises them on temperature rise or error bursts, removing worst-silicon, worst-temperature and end-of-life guard bands.
why: Constraint: typical banks settle near 0.4-0.5 V versus the 1 V spec (~4-6x CV^2), and VPP scaling brings the wordline path to ~8-10x; reliability is a measured, regulated quantity.

title: Non-switching butterfly-capacitance read of ferroelectric cells
idea: Box [medium: HZO ferroelectric capacitor | access: planar | sense: small-signal capacitance at a fixed plate bias | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. Instead of switching polarization to read it, the sense circuit applies a 50 mV probe at a fixed bias and measures differential capacitance, which differs between the two polarization branches of the butterfly C-V curve; the weak signal is decoded with soft ECC.
why: Constraint: no 2Pr switching charge moves on reads, ~10-30x lower read energy; reliability: removes read fatigue and wake-up wear, so endurance becomes effectively unlimited.
note: FeCAP capacitive NDRO is known; the signal margin is tiny.

title: Nanoimprint-only DRAM capacitor and bitline patterning consortium
idea: Box[Fab=nanoimprint lithography for repetitive array layers x Owner=multi-maker consortium sharing master templates x Finance=template cost pooling]: pattern the highly periodic capacitor-hole and bitline layers by NIL instead of EUV, with a consortium sharing the master-template and defect-learning cost.
why: Capital intensity: cuts 2-4 EUV layers per wafer and ~30-40% of litho capex for array layers.

title: Po: the bit is a spinning top — on-chip parametron phase memory
idea: Po: the bit is a spinning top. Extracted: each bit is a nonlinear LC or NEMS resonator pumped at 2f by a shared clock; it rings at f locked to phase 0 or pi, the phase is the bit, and readout compares it against a reference, so nothing sits as static charge that can leak.
why: Removes leakage-driven refresh and destructive read (facts 3, 8); energy set by resonator Q rather than CV2 at 1 V (fact 10). Resonator area/density is the main risk.
note: Same parametron phase memory.

title: Po: a magnet with no magnetization — chiral antiferromagnet Mn3Sn bit
idea: Po: a magnet with no magnetization. Extracted: store the bit in the octupole order of a chiral antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn), switched by spin-orbit torque from a BiSb topological-insulator line (no Pt/W) and read by tunnelling magnetoresistance; zero stray field lets cells touch without crosstalk.
why: Non-volatile (no refresh, fact 3) with ps-scale dynamics and crosstalk-free packing; avoids tungsten/platinum chokepoints. Read signal is still small.

title: Po: memory that remembers by bending — bistable SiC nanobridge
idea: Po: memory that remembers by bending. Extracted: a compressively prestrained SiC nanobridge buckles up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it through, its position changes a capacitance read by the bitline, and stiff contact-free SiC (no stiction) targets >1e15 cycles.
why: Zero leakage and zero standby (fact 3) with aJ snap energy (fact 10). Fatigue at 1e15 cycles is unproven.

title: Series dual-wordline vertical access with stack-effect leakage and AND addressing
idea: Po: every lock needs two keys. Put two independently driven gate rings in series on one vertical pillar channel, one on a row wordline and one on a column-group wordline; the cell opens only when both are high, so off leakage falls by the stack effect and half-selected cells see only one gate on.
why: Facts 3 and 9: stack effect cuts subthreshold leakage 10-30x and splits the drain field to curb GIDL; AND-addressing also blunts row hammer because an aggressor wordline only half-opens its neighbors.

title: Erasable conductive ferroelectric domain walls as nondestructive bits
idea: Po: the wire appears and disappears. In a thin-film lithium niobate cell, a pulse between two side electrodes nucleates a charged domain wall that conducts ~1e4x better than the bulk, and an opposite pulse erases it; reading wall current is nondestructive, so the bit needs neither capacitor nor refresh.
why: Facts 1, 3 and 8: no capacitor, refresh or restore, with ns domain switching; risk is LiNbO3-on-Si integration and wall current at 20 nm.

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor alpha-In2Se3 channel as its own memory
idea: Po: the channel remembers which way it points. Make the transistor channel from the ferroelectric semiconductor alpha-In2Se3, whose out-of-plane polarization flips with a gate pulse and modulates channel conductance; there is no separate ferroelectric layer or capacitor, and read is nondestructive.
why: Facts 1, 3 and 8: capacitorless, refresh-free, nondestructive low-voltage bit beyond the HZO prior; risk is endurance and CMOS-compatible In2Se3 deposition.

title: Po: bitlines amplify themselves — oxide TFT segment preamps
idea: Po: a bitline with gain built into it. Cut each bitline into 32-cell local segments, each sensed by a BEOL IGZO thin-film gain transistor stacked above the capacitor array whose gate is the segment node; the tiny segment capacitance (~1/8 of a full bitline) gives ~6x larger swing that the TFT converts into current on a global bitline.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and 3D (#2): Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~1 fF at equal signal, enabling shallow capacitors that suit stacked tiers.

title: Po capacitor made of white paint: rutile TiO2 on MoO2 electrodes
idea: Po: 'the capacitor dielectric is the white pigment in house paint.' Extracted: grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~80-110) at low temperature by templating it on a rutile MoO2 bottom electrode, which is lattice-matched like RuO2 but made from U.S.-mined molybdenum, and Al-dope it to suppress leakage, replacing ZrO2/HfO2 stacks and ruthenium.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1 needs k ~70): k ~90 gives ~1.5-2x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or lets the AR fall from ~70 to ~40; titanium and molybdenum are abundant and U.S.-sourced (Climax, CO), removing hafnium and platinum-group dependence.
note: Same rutile-templated TiO2 mechanism as I-07553, MoO2 electrode.

title: Po memory never forgets because it is cold: 77 K planar cells
idea: Po: 'memory that never forgets.' Extracted: run 180 nm-built DRAM in liquid nitrogen, where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by many orders of magnitude, so a simple planar MOS capacitor of 3-5 fF holds data for hours and refresh nearly vanishes; LN2 comes from air, not helium.
why: Lets cheap planar 180 nm cells (no high-AR etch, no high-k) work; refresh energy ~0 and transistors get faster; the price is ~10 W of wall power per W removed at 77 K, best in already-cooled racks.
note: Same LN2 cryo-DRAM mechanism as I-02504, with planar 180 nm cells.

title: Mask-ROM foundation models: freeze the weights in vias
idea: Po: RAM is read-only. Frozen, widely deployed model weights are fabricated as via-programmed multi-level mask ROM (only one or two masks change per model) on cheap mature-node wafers stacked under the accelerator; DRAM holds only activations and KV.
why: Weights are 50-90% of inference memory; ROM needs no capacitor, no refresh and ~1-2 custom masks, cutting weight cost/bit several-fold and freeing DRAM for KV.

title: Hot-line consolidation: memory tiering at 64-byte granularity
idea: Po: the page is one byte. The memory/CXL controller tracks hotness per cache line and migrates hot lines out of mostly-cold pages into dense hot-line pages in DRAM through a line-remap table, leaving cold remainders in compressed or far memory.
why: Page-granular tiering keeps 4 KB resident for a few hot lines; line-level consolidation shrinks the DRAM tier 2-3x for sparse-access workloads (fact 8 overfetch).

title: Resonant charge-recovery drivers that recycle bus wire energy
idea: Po: wires give their energy back. Drive memory data lines through small on-die inductors so each line resonates; line capacitance swings adiabatically and most of the CV2 charge returns to the tank instead of being dumped to ground.
why: Breaks the CV2 voltage floor on interface wires; 2-4x lower link energy per bit at the same swing.
note: Adiabatic/resonant signaling known; aperiodic data and on-die inductor area limit recovery.

title: Capillary self-assembly places hundreds of DRAM dies at once
idea: Po: chips swim to their sockets. One mask defines hydrophilic bond sites on the target wafer; water droplets pull hundreds of DRAM dies into sub-micron alignment in parallel before hybrid bonding.
why: Die-to-wafer bonding throughput up ~10x versus pick-and-place, cutting stacking cost and tool count.

title: Multi-reference soft sensing lets a 2 fF capacitor work
idea: Po: the capacitor is too small to matter. Each sense amp compares the bitline against three staggered references in one sensing window (time-multiplexed offset injection), emitting a hard bit plus a confidence flag; low-confidence bits go to the decoder as erasures, so cells with half the signal still read correctly.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~2-2.5 fF, so pillar AR falls from ~70:1 toward ~35:1 and the hardest etch steps go away.

title: Strategic DRAM Reserve that buys gluts and sells spikes
idea: Po: DRAM is oil. A government reserve buys known-good DRAM dies and modules during price troughs, stores them in nitrogen dry cabinets, and auctions them when contract prices rise more than ~50% year-over-year.
why: Smooths the boom-bust cycle that makes fabs underinvest: trough buying keeps fabs near full utilization and spike releases cap 4x price surges; attacks supply stability and capital risk.

title: Block copolymer self-assembly prints hexagonal capacitor arrays
idea: Po: chips are grown, not made. A cylinder-forming high-chi block copolymer self-assembles into a hexagonal lattice matching the DRAM capacitor honeycomb; a coarse ArF guide pattern at 3x pitch registers it (density multiplication), and the cylinders become the hard mask for storage-node holes.
why: Defines the densest DRAM layer without EUV or quadruple patterning, saving ~3-4 litho/etch passes; attacks litho capital.

title: Flip leaky bucket into snap-through buckled nanobeam bit
idea: Worsen: store every bit in a leaky bucket that drains in milliseconds. Flip: store the bit in the shape of a pre-stressed buckled nanobeam (20 nm SiN or SiC) that snaps between two stable states under an electrostatic pulse and is read by the capacitance change to a sense electrode; a shape cannot leak.
why: Kills refresh (fact 3: 16-33% of idle power) and sidesteps the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); fJ-scale writes, unlimited retention, NEMS resonators already show >1e12 cycles.

title: Antiferromagnet Neel-vector bit with zero stray field
idea: Worsen: use bits that disturb their neighbours (row hammer, stray fields) so cells must sit far apart. Flip: store the bit in the Neel vector of a chiral antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn or CuMnAs) switched by ns spin-orbit current pulses and read by anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance; antiferromagnets have no stray field and THz dynamics, so cells pack at minimum pitch and ignore neighbour activity.
why: Row-hammer immunity (fact 9), no refresh (fact 3), ps-ns writes; avoids the stray-field pitch limit of ferromagnetic MRAM.
note: AFM Neel-vector memory widely pursued; tiny read signal.

title: Rutile TiO2 capacitor grown on lattice-matched MoO2 electrodes
idea: Worsen: make the capacitor dielectric depend on ever more Zr and Hf from zircon refining. Flip: grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~90-120) at low temperature by templating it on conductive rutile-structure MoO2 bottom electrodes, with a thin Al-doped TiO2 top layer to suppress leakage, using only abundant Ti, Mo and Al.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k ~70) and Hf/Zr dependence: ~1.5-2x Cs per pillar, or the same Cs at AR ~40 instead of 70, with no hafnium or zirconium.
note: Same rutile TiO2 on MoO2 as I-06628/I-07553.

title: DUV-guided block-copolymer honeycomb replaces EUV for capacitor array
idea: Worse: add more EUV layers to every shrink. Flip: print only a coarse DUV guide pattern, then let a cylinder-forming high-chi block copolymer self-assemble into the hexagonal lattice that the 6F2 honeycomb storage-node and landing-pad layers already use, tripling density per guide post.
why: Litho/capital (fact 4): removes 2-3 of the 5-7 EUV layers on the array (~8-12% wafer cost). Row/column redundancy absorbs DSA defectivity.

title: Wafer-scale MoS2 epitaxy on sapphire for stackable access transistors
idea: Worse: insist that the access transistor be bulk crystalline silicon. Flip: grow single-crystal monolayer MoS2 by MOCVD on step-engineered sapphire and stack transistor layers monolithically at <400 C. The 1.8 eV gap and 0.7 nm body give sub-fA off-current and atomically thin tiers.
why: 3D DRAM tier pitch shrinks ~5x versus Si/SiGe epi, and the leakage tail falls (fact 3).

title: Hardware forwarding enables low-headroom pauseless compaction
idea: Worsen: give garbage-collected runtimes 2-3x heap headroom so the GC rarely runs. Flip: the memory controller holds forwarding tables and a read barrier, so objects relocate concurrently with no pauses and heaps can run at 1.2x of live data.
why: Capacity: 40-60% less DRAM for Java, Go, .NET and JavaScript fleets, which hold a large share of server memory.
note: Azul Vega shipped hardware read barriers; managed-runtime headroom is a big share.

title: Nanoimprint for periodic array layers, EUV only for periphery
idea: Worse: expose every perfectly periodic cell layer on $200M EUV tools. Flip: pattern honeycomb capacitor and buried-wordline array layers with nanoimprint templates written once by e-beam, stitched by alignment marks to DUV- or EUV-patterned periphery.
why: Removes 3-5 of the 5-7 EUV layers; litho capital per wafer down ~40-60% and the single-supplier EUV chokepoint loosened.
note: Canon NIL for DRAM under evaluation; defectivity and overlay.

title: Bucket brigade: 64-cell charge-packet loops replace per-cell transistors
idea: A firefighter's bucket line delivers water without a pipe to every house. Store bits as charge packets marching around short CCD-style loops of 64 gate electrodes clocked at 4 GHz, with one sense/regenerate tap per loop. Worst-case access is ~16 ns, and every lap refreshes the charge for free.
why: Removes the per-bit access transistor and its leakage tail (fact 3) and shrinks the periphery (fact 7); a cell is just gates (~4F²) with no high-AR capacitor (fact 1).
note: Same CCD loop; 4 GHz clocking of all gates costs heavy power.

title: Luthier's arched top: bistable pre-stressed buckled nanobeam bit
idea: A violin maker knows that an arched, pre-stressed plate snaps between two stable shapes. A 200 nm compressively stressed SiN/TiN nanobeam is buckled either up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it over and a capacitive readout senses its shape, with zero standby power and no charge to leak.
why: A non-volatile mechanical state removes refresh (fact 3) and row hammer (fact 9: no charge coupling between rows); elastic snapping of amorphous films has no intrinsic wear-out mechanism, so the target is >1e15 cycles.

title: Siberian permafrost engineer: 77 K SrTiO3 quantum-paraelectric capacitor
idea: A Siberian engineer treats cold as a free resource. Run the memory immersed in liquid nitrogen, where SrTiO3's quantum-paraelectric permittivity climbs into the thousands and access-transistor leakage falls by more than 1e6. A flat planar capacitor then holds enough charge, and refresh happens hours apart.
why: Removes the high-AR capacitor (fact 1) and nearly all refresh (fact 3); the planar cell cuts EUV and etch steps (fact 4). The price is cryocooling at the rack.

title: Sailor's storm-proof compass: antiferromagnet Neel-vector bit
idea: A sailor wants a compass that no passing magnet can deflect. Store the bit in the Neel vector of an antiferromagnet (CuMnAs or Mn3Sn), switched by a picosecond current pulse through spin-orbit torque and read through anisotropic or anomalous Hall resistance.
why: Non-volatile, immune to stray fields, switching at THz rates, with no row-hammer coupling and no MTJ stack (facts 3, 9).

title: Transistor-less alien: tunnel-diode Goto-pair latch with picoamp standby
idea: An alien that never invented the transistor builds memory from negative resistance. Two series resonant tunneling diodes form a bistable 'Goto pair' latch whose standby current is set by the RTD valley current (~pA), giving an SRAM-like, refresh-free bit in about 4F².
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor (fact 1), in far less area than a 6T SRAM.
note: Duplicate tunneling-SRAM cell.

title: ISS astronaut: directly grown 3R-MoS2 sliding-ferroelectric bit
idea: On the space station every drop is recycled, so there is no wet transfer. 3R-stacked bilayer MoS2 shows sliding ferroelectricity: the layers shift by one atomic registry to reverse polarization. Grow it directly on the BEOL by ~400 C MOCVD as a FeFET gate, with no water-bath transfer, PMMA strip or rinse.
why: Atom-thin, sub-1 V non-volatile switching attacks the voltage floor (fact 10) and refresh (fact 3). The storage layer is made entirely in gas-phase steps, with more than 10x less water.
note: Sliding ferroelectric FeFETs widely studied; wafer-scale 3R growth at 400 C uncertain.

title: Desert traveler's sand-scrub: sacrificial carbon getter blanket, nitride trap cell
idea: Desert travelers scour pots with sand when water is precious. Before each critical step, a sacrificial amorphous-carbon blanket captures particles and metal ions and is then ashed away in O2 plasma. The storage element is a 3 nm direct-tunnel Si3N4 charge-trap gate (fast MNOS), written in ~10 ns at <3 V and retaining charge for ms to s.
why: A flash-like trap that writes at DRAM speed by direct tunneling cuts refresh ~100x (fact 3) with no capacitor (fact 1). Getter-and-ash dry cleaning replaces wet cleans, for more than 10x less water; endurance is the main risk.

title: 2050 engineer's hBN-sealed WSe2 access channel with vdW contacts
idea: A 2050 engineer would wonder why we ever used channels with dangling bonds. Transfer a monolayer WSe2 or MoS2 channel, fully encapsulated top and bottom in hBN, onto the capacitor tops and contact it with van der Waals-transferred metal, so there are no doped junctions or pinning defects; leakage is bounded by the 1.6-2 eV gap and atomically clean interfaces.
why: Removes the junction/trap-assisted-tunneling tail behind the 13 fA spec (fact 3); projected off-current <1e-19 A per cell gives seconds-to-minutes retention, and a 0.7 nm body suppresses DIBL so channels can shorten (density).
note: Same 2D channel with hBN encapsulation.

title: Glassblower's indium-free amorphous Ga2O3 ultra-wide-gap access channel
idea: A glassblower knows amorphous networks forgive disorder. Instead of indium-based IGZO, deposit ALD amorphous Ga2O3 or AlGaOx at <400 C as a back-end access channel; its ~4.8 eV gap pushes off-current toward 1e-22 A per cell and it avoids indium, a byproduct metal concentrated in China.
why: Retention of hours removes refresh and lets capacitors shrink, and frees oxide-semiconductor DRAM from indium supply risk (scarce-resource axis).

title: Building inspector's occupancy certificate: per-bank retention data in SPD
idea: An inspector certifies each room's safe occupancy. A JEDEC rule, seeded by CHIPS Act procurement, requires every module's SPD to store measured per-bank retention at three temperatures from final test, and DRAM to expose per-bank refresh-rate registers, so the OS and controller refresh each bank at its own rate instead of the global worst case.
why: Most banks retain 4-16x longer than the worst bank; standardized data unlocks ~2-4x refresh savings across the installed base with firmware, not fabs.
note: Same per-bank retention data standard.

title: Titan alien's 77 K memory pool with sub-volt wordlines
idea: An alien from 94 K Titan would run memory where its physics is happiest. Pooled DRAM is immersed in liquid nitrogen and the array redesigned for 77 K: subthreshold slope steepens to ~20 mV/dec, so the access threshold drops and the wordline swings 0.8 V instead of a pumped 3 V, VARY falls to ~0.5 V, and leakage-driven refresh disappears.
why: Wordline and array CV^2 plus pump losses fall ~10-20x per access and refresh energy goes to ~0; the cryocooler cost (~5-10 W per W removed) only pays off for large shared pools, so the device-level gain must be big.

title: Librarian fetches one book: row-and-column coincident access cell
idea: A librarian pulls one book, not the whole shelf. Each cell gets a second vertical access transistor in series, gated by a column-group select line, so a cell reaches its bitline only when both its row and its 64-bit group are selected; the other 127/128 of the row stay isolated, unread and unrestored.
why: Removes the 128x overfetch and the destructive restore of untouched cells (fact 8): activate energy per useful bit drops ~10-50x and row-hammer disturb shrinks; costs ~1.3-1.5x cell area unless the second device is stacked vertically.

title: Burrowing mole's shortcut: heterojunction tunnel-FET access at 0.5 V
idea: A mole tunnels through the hill instead of climbing it. The access device is a vertical Ge-source/Si-channel tunnel FET: band-to-band tunneling turns it on within ~0.3 V at sub-60 mV/dec, and when off the tunneling window closes, leaving no thermionic tail.
why: A ~0.5 V wordline instead of a pumped 3 V cuts wordline energy ~30x; the low on-current is acceptable on short local bitlines, giving >=10x lower access energy.

title: 2050 engineer's atom-thin tiers: 2D-semiconductor lateral access transistors
idea: From 2050, silicon tiers look too fat. Grow monolayer MoS2 or WSe2 by MOCVD at <=400C on each tier's dielectric to make the lateral access transistor, so a tier shrinks to ~15 nm versus ~60 nm for Si/SiGe.
why: The ~1.8-2 eV gap pushes the leakage tail well below 1 fA (Fact 3), and thin tiers allow 100+ tiers within today's etch depth (Fact 2).

title: Blacksmith nitrides manganese into a racetrack memory
idea: Persona: a blacksmith who case-hardens steel with nitrogen. Reactively sputter ferrimagnetic Mn4N, which has perpendicular anisotropy and low magnetization. Tune it near angular-momentum compensation with Ni substitution so that current drives domain walls at ~1 km/s along vertical racetracks.
why: Non-volatile, with many bits per access transistor, which cuts periphery and area per bit. No Co, Pt, Gd or Tb.

title: Leather tanner's chrome green: voltage-written chromia magnetoelectric memory
idea: Persona: a tanner who works with chromium oxide, the chrome green pigment. Boron-doped Cr2O3 is a room-temperature magnetoelectric antiferromagnet, so a voltage pulse with a small bias field reverses its boundary magnetization. An exchange-coupled Fe/MgO/Fe junction reads the state.
why: Non-volatile memory written by voltage instead of current, at fJ-class energy, with no Pt, Ir or Co.
note: B-doped Cr2O3 ME memory is active academic research; speed and density versus DRAM unproven.

title: Printmaker's mask-free interference lithography for crossed array gratings
idea: An etching artist makes plates by interfering beams, not by drawing. Expose array line and hole layers with 193 nm immersion two-beam interference lithography, a mask-free, lens-free tool that writes a ~70 nm-pitch grating across the whole wafer in one flash; two rotated exposures form a hole lattice, and one spacer doubling reaches DRAM pitch, aligned through the moire between the grating and a reference mark.
why: No reticles and no projection optics: a ~$5-10M laser-and-mirror tool replaces immersion or EUV passes on periodic layers, with throughput set by laser power rather than stage scanning. Claim ~50% less litho capex on array layers.

title: 2050 engineer: confined-nucleation MoS2 grown at 300 C as access transistors
idea: A 2050 engineer grows channels instead of etching them. Low-temperature MOCVD (<=350 C) of monolayer MoS2 or WSe2 inside litho-defined pockets that confine nucleation to one grain per pocket forms the access transistors of each stacked memory tier, grown tier by tier within the BEOL thermal budget.
why: A ~1.8-2 eV gap and an atomically thin channel could push leakage below 1 fA (fact 3), relaxing refresh, while tiers grow sequentially with no bonding. High risk: contact resistance, and low-temperature film quality.

title: Net weaver: aligned carbon nanotube periphery transistors above the array
idea: A net weaver lays parallel threads. Align solution-sorted semiconducting carbon nanotubes (>99.99% pure) into dense parallel arrays by dose-controlled floating evaporative self-assembly at room temperature, making CMOS periphery transistors (polarity set by contact work function) in tiers above the cell array at <=200 C.
why: Puts fast periphery above the array instead of beside it, reclaiming much of the 49% periphery area with no high-temperature step. High risk: residual metallic tubes, and alignment uniformity at 300 mm.
note: CNT BEOL CMOS exists (MIT/SkyWater); metallic-tube purity at Gb scale still open.

title: Plumber's two-way pipe: simultaneous bidirectional interposer wires
idea: A plumber's pipe carries flow both ways in a heat exchanger: drive each HBM data wire from both ends at once and cancel your own transmitted signal with a hybrid echo canceller at each receiver, so every wire carries read and write traffic at the same time.
why: Halves the bumps and interposer wires per unit of bandwidth (or doubles bandwidth), which eases the beachfront limit and interposer cost; ~0.4 pJ/bit.
note: Same SBD wires idea.

title: Central banker's Strategic DRAM Reserve of nitrogen-stored dies
idea: Treat DRAM like oil: a federal reserve buys known-good DRAM wafers and dies in gluts, when contract prices fall below cash cost, and stores them in dry-nitrogen cabinets where dies keep for over 10 years. It auctions them to U.S. module assemblers when prices pass 2x the trailing average.
why: Supply stability and capital: damps the boom-bust cycle that deters capex; a ~5 EB reserve could cap a 4x spike, keep fabs running full through downturns, and lower every producer's cost of capital.

title: Ham radio operator: 32-die stacks talk through inductive coils
idea: A ham operator talks without wires. Stack 32 thinned DRAM dies that pass data through on-die inductive coils (near-field links, ~1 pJ/bit) instead of TSVs, bonded with thin adhesive and powered by edge-plated rails. Any OSAT can assemble them on NAND-style die-stacking lines.
why: Meets the 10x constraint per package footprint: 32 dies is ~10x the bits of 2-4-high packages. Removing TSVs (HBM's ~3x area-per-bit tax and 20-30% yield loss) holds $/GB at commodity DDR level, so this is same cost per bit, not per package.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods shrink the capacitor to planar 1 fF
idea: Borrowing from 77 K cryo-computing users, DRAM dies run immersed in LN2 where trap-assisted and subthreshold leakage fall ~1e6x and sense-amp offsets shrink, so retention reaches minutes. The 60:1 pillar is replaced by a ~1-1.5 fF planar or shallow-cup MIM read on short 64-cell bitlines.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3): HAR etch/deposition steps disappear (~30-50% capacitor-module cost) and refresh power goes to ~0; the ~10 W/W cryocooler overhead must be amortized at rack scale.

title: Radiation-proof snap-through buckled nanobeam holds bit mechanically
idea: Satellite memory must ignore single-event upsets, so a 200 nm compressively pre-stressed SiN or TiN beam is buckled up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it between the two stable shapes in ~5-20 ns and a capacitive readout senses its position. There is no stored charge for a heavy ion to disturb and standby power is zero.
why: Non-volatile, rad-immune, BEOL-compatible bit with no capacitor wall (fact 1) and no refresh (fact 3); nanobeam endurance beyond 1e12 cycles and stiction are risks, density ~10-20F2 initially.

title: Tunnel-diode latched storage node for always-on phone sensor hubs
idea: Phones' always-on hubs burn standby power on refresh, so two series interband tunnel diodes (Si/SiGe Esaki) form a Goto pair on each storage node, creating two stable voltages held by picoamp valley currents. The access transistor reads and writes as usual; the node simply never decays.
why: Eliminates refresh (fact 3, 16-33% idle power) with ~pA/cell standby at near-1T1C area; requires tight peak/valley current control in BEOL-compatible tunnel diodes.
note: TI tunneling SRAM prior art; pA valley currents with tight PVCR control in BEOL is hard.

title: Fatigue-free sliding ferroelectric bilayer for fifty-year deep-space probes
idea: Voyager-class probes need 50-year memory; MOCVD-grown bilayer MoS2 or hBN shows 'sliding' ferroelectricity in which polarization flips by a lateral interlayer shift without breaking bonds and shows no measurable fatigue. One mask patterns the BEOL bilayer into capacitors or FeFET gates over existing vias.
why: Atomically thin polarization storage with potentially unlimited endurance and sub-1 V switching (fact 10); wafer-scale control of bilayer stacking order is the risk.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor heritage: self-ordered anodic alumina capacitor mold
idea: Thirty-year industrial power supplies rely on anodized aluminum's self-ordered pores; e-beam-evaporate aluminum (no argon sputter) over the array, pre-indent it by imprint to lock the pore sites to the ~40 nm cell pitch, and anodize it so straight nanopores at AR 300+ form in an electrolyte bath. ALD TiN/high-k/TiN into the pores to make one capacitor per landing pad.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 300 gives ~4x Cs or lets a lower-k dielectric work, using only wet anodization with no plasma etch or rare gas.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods: cold kills leakage, so capacitors shrink
idea: Cryo-CMOS users at 77 K see junction and subthreshold leakage fall by 6+ orders of magnitude, so a few tenths of a fF holds charge for hours. Immerse memory sleds in LN2 made from air on site (not helium), with tiny planar or capacitorless floating-body cells, and recover cold through the data center's air-separation unit.
why: Removes high-k capacitor materials and high-AR etch, and makes refresh energy (fact 3) near zero; wire resistance also drops, partly offsetting the cooling penalty.

title: Core-rope legacy: mask-ROM weight planes for frozen inference models
idea: From the Apollo Guidance Computer's woven core-rope ROM: store a frozen LLM's weights in via-programmed mask-ROM dies (one via present or absent per bit, no capacitor, no refresh) stacked beside the accelerator, so HBM/DRAM holds only activations and KV. A model update re-spins only one or two via/metal masks on a mature node.
why: Weights are often 50-80% of inference memory; a ROM bit needs no capacitor (fact 1) and no refresh (fact 3) and can be ~3-5x cheaper per bit on a mature node, cutting DRAM per served model 2-5x.
note: Mature-node ROM is less dense than leading DRAM; mask NRE per model version.

title: Thirty-year PLC discipline: static region memory for cloud services
idea: From industrial PLCs that run for decades with no heap: compile services with region inference and per-request arenas so peak memory is proven at build time, eliminating allocator fragmentation and garbage-collector headroom; the scheduler bin-packs services by proven peak instead of observed max plus margin.
why: Managed runtimes reserve 1.5-3x live heap for GC and fragmentation; static regions can cut server DRAM provisioning 30-60%.
note: Static peak-memory proofs for cloud services; same core as I-11334 and hard to prove at build time.

title: Hearing-aid LC resonant bus recycles line charge
idea: Hearing aids live on a 1-2 mW zinc-air budget. Pair each memory data line with an integrated on-package inductor so line plus inductor form a resonant tank; bits are sent as half-cycles of resonance, so the line's charge sloshes back instead of being dumped to ground each transition.
why: Recovering 80-90% of line CV2 cuts I/O energy ~5-10x; on short HBM-class wires this reaches ~10x lower interface energy per access (fact 5).
note: Same LC tank charge-recovery mechanism; 80-90% recovery overclaimed.

title: Genomics-grade sub-row activation with host column masks
idea: Genome aligners hammer memory with random 8-32-byte k-mer lookups. Add a column-mask field to ACT so segmented local wordline drivers fire only one 512 B segment of a row, and route only those bits to the I/O.
why: Attacks the 128x page overfetch (5.9 pJ per useful random bit): activating 1/16 of a row cuts random-access energy ~8-12x with a small periphery change.
note: Same sub-row/segmented activation mechanism.

title: Ga2O3 ultra-wide-bandgap access transistor for hour retention
idea: Time-shift retention from 64 ms to ~1 hour by replacing the silicon access device with a 4.8 eV beta-Ga2O3 thin-film transistor, whose off-state leakage can be below 1e-21 A, while keeping a conventional stacked capacitor.
why: Refresh and leakage tail: refresh energy cut >1000x; Cs can shrink 3-5x because only sense margin matters.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayers switch by 1.4 angstrom registry shift
idea: Scale down to van der Waals stacking: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or MoS2 the bit is the AB versus BA stacking order, flipped by a sub-angstrom interlayer slide under field, with reported low fatigue because no ions move.
why: Endurance and voltage: sub-1 V switching, 1e10+ cycles target, wafer-scale 2D growth enables BEOL stacking.

title: Power-grid thyristor shrunk to a 15 nm memory pillar
idea: Scale shift from grid-scale SCRs to a 15 nm vertical pnpn pillar: regenerative bipolar feedback latches the cell on or off, a gate pulse switches it, and a small holding bias keeps it, giving a 4F2 capacitor-free cell.
why: Density and process: 4F2 with no capacitor etch, fast read current 10x DRAM.
note: Vertical thyristor RAM pursued by T-RAM/Kilopass; holding current and variability are known blockers.

title: Magnetoelectric BiFeO3 flips nanomagnets with voltage alone
idea: Shift write energy to the atto-joule scale: a voltage across thin BiFeO3 rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which exchange-couples to a CoFe free layer, writing a magnet with no current and reading it by TMR.
why: Voltage floor and energy: ~100 mV, aJ writes break the CV2 wall; no capacitor and no refresh.
note: Known MESO/Heron-type BFO-CoFe coupling; reliable deterministic switching and endurance still unproven.

title: 77 K co-designed DRAM pool with refresh switched off
idea: Scale jump from device to rack plus a time jump in retention: a CXL memory rack immersed in liquid nitrogen with DRAM redesigned for 77 K, with access-transistor Vt lowered ~0.3 V (subthreshold slope ~20 mV/dec at 77 K), VARY dropped to ~0.6 V and wordline to ~1.8 V, so leakage collapses by >10 decades and refresh is replaced by an hourly scrub.
why: Eliminates refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) and breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): ~3-5x lower CV^2 array energy, with cryocooler overhead amortized across a rack-scale shared pool.

title: Microsecond laser seeded recrystallization makes single-grain stacked access transistors
idea: Time shift in thermal processing: deposit amorphous Si for each 3D-DRAM tier, then sweep a microsecond-pulse laser so melt fronts grow laterally from a seed opening, giving one grain per access transistor while the short melt keeps lower tiers below 450 C.
why: No manufacturable 3D cell (fact 2): grain-boundary-free silicon gives bulk-like low leakage for lateral access transistors across 26+ tiers using only Si, with no IGZO In/Ga.
note: Grain-filter laser crystallization known; repeated tiers stress lower-tier thermal budget.

title: Thin-film gated thyristor cells stacked in tiers
idea: Shrink the regenerative gain of kiloamp power thyristors to a cell: build gated thin-film p-n-p-n thyristors vertically in each poly-Si tier at 180-nm rules, each acting as both storage element and amplifier. Cells need no capacitor and drive uA read currents into long shared bitlines.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and periphery (fact 7): no capacitor, and high read current allows longer bitlines with fewer sense amps.
note: T-RAM tried and failed; poly-Si thyristor standby current and variability are the doubts.

title: Rutile TiO2 high-k grown on niobium-doped tin-oxide template electrodes
idea: Jump to the atomic lattice: rutile SnO2 matches rutile TiO2 within ~3%. A conductive Nb- or Ta-doped SnO2 bottom electrode therefore templates ALD TiO2 into its rutile phase (k ~80-100) at low temperature without Ru/RuO2, and Al doping of the TiO2 suppresses leakage.
why: Delivers the k ~70+ needed to break the capacitor charge wall using Ti, Sn and Nb instead of Hf/Zr and Ru. Holding 5 fF lets AR fall from ~70:1 to ~35:1.
note: Same rutile-templated TiO2 as I-07553 with Nb-SnO2 electrode.

title: Nanosecond laser crystallization builds silicon tiers atop finished arrays
idea: Time-shift the thermal budget from furnace hours to nanoseconds: deposit amorphous Si on each finished tier and melt-recrystallize it with a ~30 ns excimer pulse seeded through small vias, so it becomes near-single-crystal while layers below stay under 400 C; repeat per tier for monolithic 3D DRAM.
why: Enables monolithic tier stacking without wafer bonding (Fact 2); each extra tier costs a deposition plus a laser pass, not a new wafer.

title: Talbot self-imaging prints the cell lattice with U.S. lasers
idea: Displacement Talbot lithography: a 1:1 periodic phase mask from a U.S. mask shop and a U.S.-built 213/266 nm solid-state laser self-image the lattice across the whole wafer with near-unlimited depth of focus; no projection optics, so no imported scanner.
why: Removes EUV/ArF scanner dependence (single-supplier chokepoint) for array layers (Fact 4) with a ~$3-8M domestic tool.

title: Micro-LED imaging-fiber links move HBM a meter from the accelerator
idea: Scale HBM's parallelism into optics: a 2D array of hundreds of micro-LEDs and photodiodes couples into a coherent imaging fiber bundle, each pixel a 2-4 Gb/s lane, so a stack can sit a meter away at HBM-class width with no lasers or SerDes.
why: Frees accelerator beachfront (fact 6) and enables pooled HBM at ~1 pJ/bit (fact 5) with memory cooled separately from the GPU.

title: Memristor without filaments: conducting ferroelectric domain walls in LiNbO3
idea: HPE's TiO2 memristor died from random oxygen-vacancy filaments that caused variability, sneak paths and ~1e6-1e9 endurance. Replace the filament with a charged, conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa: writing nucleates or erases the wall deterministically at a lithographic edge, and a sub-coercive read senses wall conduction between side electrodes without moving it.
why: Deterministic, non-destructive read; endurance >1e12 because no ions migrate; ~1e3 on/off. Attacks destructive read (Fact 8) and refresh (Fact 3).
note: Same LiNbO3 charged-wall NDRO cell.

title: Dense MRAM's heat-and-crosstalk wall broken by antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
idea: Early dense-MRAM efforts lost thermal stability at small sizes and high temperature, and stray fields coupled neighbouring bits. Store the bit in the magnetic-octupole order of noncollinear antiferromagnetic Mn3Pt (TN ~475 K), read through an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction: exchange-enhanced anisotropy and zero net moment give Delta > 60 at 125 C in a 20 nm cell with no stray-field crosstalk.
why: Grade-1 retention at sub-20 nm pitch; ps-scale antiferromagnetic dynamics allow fast SOT writes; no inter-cell coupling raises density.
note: Mn3Pt AFM tunnel junctions are an active research front; TMR still small.

title: BeSang monolithic 3D fixed with seeded rapid-melt-growth tiers
idea: BeSang and other monolithic-3D ventures failed because low-temperature upper tiers had poor polysilicon transistors. Open seed windows to the single-crystal tier below and deposit amorphous Si over the oxide. Melt it with nanosecond laser pulses so it regrows laterally as single crystal from each seed (rapid-melt growth), while lower tiers stay under 450C.
why: Gives crystalline access transistors in every tier of 26+ tier 3D DRAM (fact 2) without a wafer bond per tier. Leakage approaches bulk Si (fact 3).
note: Seeded rapid-melt growth variant; lateral growth length from seeds is limited.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous splitting stops grinding away 96% of HBM wafers
idea: HBM core dies are ground from 775 um to ~30 um, wasting ~96% of each Cz wafer; Canon's ELTRAN (double porous-Si layer, water-jet split) died because SOI demand was small and Smart Cut won. Grow the DRAM device epi on sealed porous silicon, process and bond it into the stack, water-jet split, and re-polish the donor for 10-20 reuses.
why: Cuts Cz silicon, polysilicon and quartz-crucible use per HBM bit ~5-10x and eliminates grinding slurry and rinse water; softens the material side of the HBM 3x-area tax.

title: Graphene lacked a bandgap; MoS2 capacitorless gain cells grown on glass
idea: Graphene logic programs stalled because a zero bandgap gives no off-state. Monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV, 0.7 nm) shows off-currents below 1e-18 A/um: grow it by MOCVD at <=450 C directly on display glass and build 2T gain cells where the read transistor's gate is the storage node.
why: Retention of seconds or more cuts refresh energy >100x; no capacitor, so no Hf/Zr and no deep etch; a monolayer uses ~3 mg MoS2 per m2, from diversified Mo supply.
note: 2D-channel gain cells actively researched; low-temp MOCVD uniformity on glass is the doubt.

title: Cavendish Kinetics' stiction problem inverted into a refresh-free NEMS bit
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory fought stiction and pivoted away. Make stiction the storage: back-end nano-cantilevers latch by van der Waals force onto a contact (1) or rest open (0) and are released by a pull-off electrode, and the electromechanical hysteresis window rejects half-selected cells so a passive crossbar needs no transistor.
why: Refresh-free with zero standby leakage (fact 3); metal-and-dielectric-only BEOL process at ~3 masks per deck, stackable over periphery, no front-end area.
note: Essentially Nantero's original CNT vdW-latched crossbar concept.

title: 3D XPoint rebuilt vertically: one hole mask for 200 layers
idea: 3D XPoint died on cost: every deck needed its own critical patterning and tall double etch, so two decks never undercut DRAM enough. Use the 3D NAND recipe instead: stack 200 metal/oxide word planes, drill one hole array, line holes with a self-selecting chalcogenide film and fill with a metal bitline pillar, so every plane-pillar crossing is a cell made with the same single critical mask.
why: Meets 100x: litho amortized over 200 layers like NAND, est. ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades: ~1e8-1e9 endurance (wear-leveled behind a small DRAM cache), us-class writes, thermal disturb between planes.
note: Vertical RRAM/PCM proposed widely; endurance makes it storage-class, not DRAM-class.

title: Mask ROM's per-design killer fixed: imprinted ROM for frozen AI weights
idea: Mask ROM died because every code change needed new masks and weeks of lead time. Frozen AI model weights are read every token but almost never rewritten, so store them in 16-deck 3D diode-ROM where every layer is a common template except one via layer per model, imprinted from a template e-beam-cut in a day, with 2 bits/cell coded by via size.
why: Meets 100x: no capacitor, no refresh, a single custom layer; est. ~$0.01-0.05/GB with low read energy. Trade: immutable, so a new model needs new dies and KV-cache still uses DRAM.
note: 3D diode ROM echoes Matrix Semiconductor OTP.

title: Racetrack shift errors fixed with disk-style servo markers and self-clocking codes
idea: IBM's racetrack memory stalled because domain walls pin or overshoot, so one bad shift offsets every following bit. Fix: borrow hard-disk servo practice by interleaving fixed marker domains and writing data in a run-length-limited self-clocking code, so the read head detects any over- or under-shift and re-shifts before decoding.
why: Turns catastrophic positional errors into ordinary correctable symbols, enabling capacitor-free magnetic shift memory with many bits per access device (density, fact 1).
note: Position-error codes for racetrack already studied.

title: Cavendish NEMS memory's stiction killer turned into the latching mechanism
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' NEMS memory pivoted away because cantilevers stuck unpredictably (stiction). Fix: design for controlled stiction, using a self-assembled monolayer that sets adhesion energy inside a narrow window so a beam latched to the 'on' contact stays put unpowered, while a counter-electrode pulse plus the beam's spring force releases it reliably.
why: Mechanically bistable: zero refresh, no leakage tail, immune to radiation and row hammer, BEOL-buildable over CMOS with no capacitor.

title: IBM Josephson memory density fixed with NbN kinetic-inductance persistent loops
idea: IBM's 1980s Josephson computer was cancelled largely because superconducting loop memory cells were microns wide and Pb-alloy junctions failed on thermal cycling. Fix: store bits as persistent supercurrent in ~100 nm NbN nanowire loops whose kinetic inductance replaces bulky geometric inductance, with cycling-robust Nb/AlOx junctions and moats that trap stray flux away from cells.
why: Persistent currents need zero refresh and dissipate nothing while holding; dense cryogenic main memory for superconducting or cryo-CMOS AI accelerators.
note: Kinetic-inductance nanowire memory cells already researched; niche cryogenic market.

title: Flash-as-DRAM endurance killer fixed by triple-barrier resonant-tunneling storage
idea: Attempts to use floating-gate flash as working memory died on tunnel-oxide wear (~1e5 cycles) and high write voltage. Fix: replace the oxide with an InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunneling structure that is opaque at rest but passes electrons at a ~2.5 V resonance, so charge enters the floating gate without hot-carrier damage (UltraRAM-style).
why: Nonvolatile, zero refresh, low-voltage writes with reported >1e7 cycles; a capacitor-free 1T cell with a path toward DRAM-class endurance.

title: Qimonda lesson: counter-cyclical strategic DRAM wafer reserve
idea: Qimonda went bankrupt in the 2008-09 crash with buried-wordline technology in hand because no one would bridge a 12-month cash trough. Fix: a sovereign reserve buys finished DRAM wafers and known-good dies at a cost-based floor during busts, stores them in nitrogen cabinets (unpackaged wafers keep for years), and releases them at a ceiling price during shortages like 2026.
why: Keeps capacity alive through troughs and flattens spikes: a reserve of ~5% of annual bits could hold a 4x spike nearer 2x, and it prevents capacity destruction that takes $15B and 4 years to rebuild.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet bits pack tight with zero stray field
idea: Effect walk: spin Hall switching + anomalous Hall effect in a Weyl antiferromagnet. 10-nm Mn3Sn islands store the bit as the chirality of their triangular spin order, switched by spin-orbit torque from an adjacent line and read by the sign of the large anomalous Hall voltage they emit despite near-zero net moment.
why: Zero stray field removes inter-cell magnetic disturb so pitch can approach 2F, and dynamics reach 10-100 ps; Mn and Sn are abundant; aims at density and endurance beyond MRAM's dipolar limit.

title: Layer-counted h-BN tunnel barrier dials retention like a knob
idea: Effect walk: direct quantum tunneling through atomically defined barriers. A 2D semi-floating-gate cell (graphene or MoS2 storage layer) sits behind exactly N layers of h-BN; because direct-tunneling current drops ~10x per added 0.33-nm layer, N=4-6 sets retention near 1 s while 10-ns writes use direct (not Fowler-Nordheim) tunneling at 2-3 V that creates no oxide traps.
why: Replaces junction leakage statistics with a quantized, atomically uniform barrier, collapsing the retention tail (fact 3) and refresh energy, and needs no capacitor (fact 1); wafer-scale defect-free h-BN and the write/hold current ratio of ~10^8 are the risks.
note: Close to published hBN semi-floating-gate quasi-nonvolatile cells; write/hold ratio 1e8 via direct tunneling is the doubt.

title: Buried Ge quantum well holds holes behind a band-offset wall
idea: Effect walk: heterojunction band-offset confinement. A capacitorless cell stores holes in a 5-nm compressively strained Ge quantum well beneath a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset, not a leaky p-n junction, is the retention barrier, and stored holes shift channel threshold for a gain read.
why: Removes the capacitor (fact 1) and attacks the junction-generation leakage tail (fact 3), allowing a 4F2 vertical cell built with SiGe epitaxy already running in U.S. fabs.
note: SiGe/Ge quantum-well capacitorless DRAM studied since ~2010; retention gain modest.

title: Bulk photovoltaic read: polarization reports its sign as photocurrent
idea: Effect walk: bulk photovoltaic (shift-current) effect. Ferroelectric nano-capacitors (BaTiO3 or CuInP2S6) under a shared transparent electrode are flood-illuminated by a backside waveguide flash; each cell's photocurrent sign equals its polarization direction, integrated by a per-column gain stage without switching the domain.
why: Non-destructive ferroelectric read removes FeRAM's read-then-rewrite fatigue and restore energy (fact 8), letting polar cells act as working memory with unlimited reads; shift currents are small, so sensing gain is the risk.
note: Ferroelectric-photovoltaic NDRO already shown (2013); tiny shift currents.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayer flips by interlayer slip at 0.2 V
idea: Effect walk: sliding (stacking) ferroelectricity. In a parallel-stacked h-BN or 3R-MoS2 bilayer, the out-of-plane dipole reverses when one layer slides one bond length (AB to BA) under ~0.1-0.3 V, and a graphene-contacted tunnel junction reads the ~10x tunneling-resistance change non-destructively.
why: No ion displacement across the film and ~0.2 V on an atomically thin capacitor cut write energy ~25x versus 1-V CV2, and the non-destructive read removes restore energy (fact 8); reported fatigue-free switching suits the endurance target.

title: Van der Waals stiction latch: nanoflap stays stuck until kicked
idea: Effect walk: van der Waals/Casimir adhesion. A 50-nm graphene or SiC nanoflap is pulled into contact by a ~0.5 V electrostatic pulse and held at zero power by vdW adhesion; a second electrode releases it, and a 10-mV contact-resistance check reads the state.
why: Zero hold power (no refresh), ~aJ contact reads at 10 mV and ~0.1 fJ actuation of an aF-scale gap put access energy >10x below DRAM; contact wear over >10^15 cycles is the reliability risk.
note: Essentially the Nantero NRAM vdW-held contact mechanism.

title: Monolayer MoS2 channel tiers stacked at 20 nm pitch
idea: Quantum confinement: atomically thin MoS2 channels, MOCVD-grown at <450 C, have a ~2 eV confined bandgap that suppresses off-state tunneling and thermionic leakage about 1000x versus silicon. Because each channel is only 0.7 nm thick, tiers can stack at ~20 nm pitch, which makes 50+ tiers practical.
why: Shrinks tier pitch and leakage at once (facts 2 and 3); claim 3D break-even reached at lower stack height and 10x longer retention.
note: 2D-channel DRAM widely pursued; BEOL MOCVD quality.

title: Layer-transferred InAs/AlSb resonant-tunneling floating-gate tiers
