Replace the access transistor with an a-Si:H or chalcogenide photoconductor between bitline and storage node; the wordline is a silicon-nitride waveguide, and a light pulse makes the row conductive for nanoseconds, while in the dark leakage is bulk dark current (aA) with no gate, no GIDL and no wordline voltage.
why: Facts 3 and 10: no 3 V wordline and no GIDL, with dark-current-limited leakage allowing minute-scale refresh; risk is photoconductor speed and optical power per row.
note: Light-gated photoconductor removes GIDL and wordline voltage; doubts: ns photoconductor speed and micron waveguide pitch vs cell pitch.

title: Origami stack: one thinned die folded into eight layers
idea: Po: chips are folded, not stacked. Fabricate eight DRAM arrays on one reticle-stitched strip, thin it to ~15 um with polyimide-backed hinge zones carrying continuous metal, and fold it accordion-style so every inter-layer link is an ordinary on-die wire running through a fold.
why: No TSVs and no bonding steps, so stack yield loss from TSV/bond defects disappears; thousands of fold wires at 2 um pitch give HBM-class width.

title: Helical-channel vertical access transistor for long channels in 4F2
idea: Worse: shrink the channel until DIBL dominates leakage. Flip: wrap a screw-thread spiral channel around each pillar (tilted-ion spiral sidewall mask, then conformal channel deposition) so the effective gate length is 3-4x the pillar height in the same footprint.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 10-100x lower off-current without area penalty; enables longer refresh or smaller Cs (fact 1).
note: Helix fabrication in nm pillars and on-current are doubts.

title: Volumetric holographic exposure patterns thirty tiers at once
idea: Worse: expose, develop and etch each tier separately. Flip: spin a thick (3-5 um) photo-patternable hybrid dielectric, write a 3D holographic interference intensity pattern that cross-links the cavity layout of ~30 tiers in one exposure, develop it into a 3D scaffold, then fill the cavities with ALD channel, high-k and metal.
why: One exposure replaces dozens of patterning steps: three exposures for ~90 tiers give ~10x density at roughly today's lithography budget, with no EUV (fact 4).
note: 3D interference limited to ~100-200 nm periodic features; ALD into polymer scaffold yields poor channels.

title: Industry-wide open cell-array mask standard shared by all makers
idea: Worse: every maker pays for proprietary array masks, and entrants must reinvent the cell. Flip: a consortium standardizes one array lattice and pitch and the masks/OPC for its critical array layers, licensed royalty-free. Vendors differentiate only in periphery, materials and capacitors.
why: Capital/entry barrier: entrants skip ~$1-2B of array integration R&D, and mask and OPC learning is pooled, enabling U.S. second sources.

title: Double-sided wafers: native two-high stacks on both faces
idea: Worse: use only one face of every expensive crystal wafer. Flip: run FEOL on both faces in edge-gripped double-sided tools. Furnace anneals and blanket depositions treat both faces in one pass, while litho alternates sides. TSVs then link the faces into a native two-high die stack without any bonding step.
why: Bits per wafer start ~1.8x with shared thermal/deposition steps; crucible-limited substrate use per bit roughly halves; HBM gets one bond layer free.

title: MLCC tape-casting lines build high-k capacitor substrates
idea: Worse: fight the 5 fF wall with ever-deeper etched holes. Flip: use the multilayer-ceramic-capacitor industry's tape-cast, co-fired BaTiO3 (k>1000) as the substrate: hundreds of sub-um layers with one via electrode per cell, topped by thin-film access transistors. Charge comes from k, not aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1 needs k~70): k in the thousands, made on low-capex, high-volume MLCC lines.
note: BaTiO3 k collapses in thin layers; TFT-on-ceramic integration unproven.

title: Dieless memory: deposit arrays directly on the package substrate
idea: Worse: make a die on one substrate, dice it, and bond it onto another (the package). Flip: build low-temperature oxide-TFT memory arrays directly on the glass-core package panel that carries the processor. The result has no die, dicing, bonding or separate test insertion, with memory millimeters from compute.
why: Packaging capital plus data movement (fact 5): die and assembly costs vanish, and short wires cut pJ/bit.

title: Fiber-loop carousel broadcasts weights so no GPU stores them
idea: Worsen: give every GPU its own HBM copy of the full model. Flip: model weights circulate continuously in a WDM fiber delay loop with amplifiers; every accelerator taps the loop and runs each layer's batch as that layer's weights stream past, holding only activations locally.
why: Cost: one circulating copy serves hundreds of accelerators, so weight memory cost per accelerator drops 100x+; trades rigid layer-synchronous scheduling and optical engineering.
note: Fiber delay-line storage of 100 GB needs thousands of km of amplified fiber; noise and rigid scheduling dominate.

title: Vacuum-gap floating electrode written by Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, oxide-free
idea: For reactor and deep-space users whose oxides trap radiation charge and wear out, the storage node is a metal island over a sealed 2-3 nm vacuum gap; electrons are written and erased by field emission through vacuum and the island gates a read transistor. Vacuum has no bonds to break or traps to fill, so tunnel wear disappears.
why: A flash-like non-volatile, non-destructive-read cell with DRAM-class endurance: no refresh (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1), ~10-100 ns writes at 3-5 V; gap uniformity at the angstrom level is the risk.
note: Angstrom-uniform sealed 2-3 nm vacuum gaps and electrostatic collapse of the island are unsolved.

title: Global-shutter pinned storage node borrowed from image sensors
idea: Image sensors hold photo-charge in pinned memory nodes for hundreds of ms with dark current of a few electrons per second, by burying the n storage region under a p+ pinning layer that keeps it away from the Si/SiO2 interface. Build the DRAM storage-node junction as such a pinned structure so interface-state generation is screened off.
why: Fact 3: surface and junction generation leakage could drop >10x, leaving channel leakage, which Vt can fix; fitting the pinning layer into 6F^2 is the challenge.
note: Pinning layer conflicts with storage-node contact to the capacitor and 6F2 space; interface screening idea is fresh.

title: Reactor-robot vacuum-gap access transistors for near-zero off-current
idea: Robots inside reactors use vacuum electronics because vacuum has no lattice to damage; make each access device a vertical nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor, a ~10 nm emitter tip facing a collector inside a ring gate, sealed in its 4F2 pillar when the tier is capped. With no conducting medium, off-state current is only zero-bias field emission, essentially nothing.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3) eliminated, radiation-immune, and tiny capacitors become viable (fact 1); claim retention of hours.
note: Zero off-current, but field-emission on-current needs volts and varies exponentially with tip radius.

title: 77 K superconducting REBCO interposer frees HBM from beachfront
idea: Extreme user: MRI and fusion-magnet labs that run HTS tape at 77 K. Pattern REBCO thin-film transmission lines on a sapphire/MgO interposer held at 77 K by a closed-cycle cooler; lossless, near-dispersion-free lines let 16-32 HBM-class stacks sit 5-20 cm from the GPU instead of crowding its edge, with no retimers or equalizers.
why: Breaks the shoreline/beachfront limit (~8 stacks per GPU) and the interposer reticle limit; 2-4x memory capacity per accelerator at similar pJ/bit; generalizes to any cryo-cooled AI rack.
note: Holding only the interposer at 77 K next to warm GPU and HBM is a severe thermal problem.

title: Downhole micro-Dewar layer lets DRAM sit directly atop hot GPUs
idea: Downhole logging tools survive 200 C by putting electronics in vacuum flasks. Insert a vacuum-gap/silica-aerogel interlayer between logic and a DRAM stack, crossed only by sparse hybrid-bonded copper pillars for signals, and give the DRAM its own top-side cold plate, so memory stays below 70 C while logic runs at 105 C.
why: Enables memory-on-logic 3D stacking (no interposer, mm-to-um wires, ~5-10x lower I/O energy) without the refresh doubling and retention loss that hit DRAM above 85 C.
note: Thin vacuum/aerogel gap leaks heat via pillars; logic heat removal path unclear.

title: Fiber-drawn memory: thermally draw a cm-scale array preform 1000x smaller
idea: Shrink with a drawing tower instead of a stepper: assemble a cm-scale preform of chalcogenide-glass semiconductor, polymer dielectric and low-melting metal electrodes in a cell-array cross-section, and draw it down 1000-10000x to nm features. Slice and bundle the fiber cross-sections into tiles bonded to 180-nm CMOS periphery.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): patterning by deformation instead of litho; a fiber tower costs ~$1M against ~$200M for EUV, and features shrink with the draw ratio.

title: Cell-to-wire PAM: 2-bit analog cells drive the link undigitized
idea: Collapse two signaling scales into one: each cell holds four charge levels, and the sense path forwards its level directly as a PAM-4 symbol over the short hybrid-bonded link, where the host slicer makes the only decision. Cell and link noise merge into one 1% symbol-error budget decoded once.
why: ~2x bits per cell, sidestepping the charge wall (fact 1) by tolerating level errors, and half the wire transitions per bit (~40% less interface energy).
note: MLC DRAM failed on margin; forwarding analog charge without restore conflicts with destructive read.

title: TSRAM fixed: hBN monolayer barriers make tunnel-diode latches reproducible
idea: TI's tunneling SRAM and 1960s Esaki-diode memories died because peak current depends exponentially on barrier thickness, so a one-monolayer deposition error broke the latch. Build each resonant-tunneling diode from an hBN/graphene/hBN stack whose barrier thickness is an integer layer count. A Goto pair of two series RTDs then holds a static bit at nA holding current with no capacitor.
why: Refresh-free static cell of ~8-10F2 vs SRAM's ~120F2; removes refresh energy (Fact 3) and the capacitor (Fact 1); variability is set by quantized layer count, not deposition drift.
note: Quantized hBN barriers address TSRAM variability, but 2D stack yield and PVCR at scale are big unknowns.

title: 3D core memory: deposited magnetic rings threaded by vertical vias
idea: Core memory died because millimetre ferrite cores had to be threaded by hand. Deposit alternating CoFeB-ring/dielectric tiers as 3D NAND does and etch one vertical metal pillar through each ring stack: coincident currents in the pillar and a tier plate line flip one ring's vortex chirality, and a TMR sensor on each tier reads it.
why: 3D density from one etch with no lateral transistor per tier (Fact 2); nonvolatile, and closed-flux rings do not couple even at tight pitch.
note: 3D NAND-style ring tiers; coincident-current selectivity and per-tier TMR read hard.

title: Selectron-style binary-coded tier selection replaces the 3D DRAM staircase
idea: Failure mined: RCA's Selectron tube picked one of 256 storage spots with combinations of a few grid bars, a decoder built into the medium, and died on vacuum-tube complexity. Fix: in a 3D DRAM stack, each tier's cells sit behind log2(N) series select gates whose thresholds are set by log2(N) masked implants, so 6 shared vertical gate lines decode 64 tiers. Staircase contacts and per-tier wordline drivers disappear.
why: 10x at the same cost: periphery and staircase area stay nearly flat as tiers grow (log N, not N), which moves 3D DRAM break-even from ~26 tiers to ~8 (fact 2) and makes 64-128 tiers ~10x denser at near-3D-NAND cost per mm^2.
note: Vt-coded series select gates remove the 3D staircase; they cut read current, and the 3D cell itself stays unsolved.

title: Spansion MirrorBit idea for DRAM: one split pillar, two capacitors
idea: MirrorBit stored two bits at the two ends of one charge-trap cell and died with Spansion's NOR business. Split each vertical access pillar into two half-channels with independent front and back gates. Each half connects to its own capacitor, one stacked on top and one buried below, so one 4F2 footprint holds two bits.
why: Effective 2F2 per bit (fact 4) with no extra EUV layers, doubling density per litho step.

title: Uni-Solar steel coils plus HP SAIL imprint for kilometer memory coils
idea: United Solar Ovonic (bankrupt 2012) ran roll-to-roll deposition on 2.5 km stainless coils, and HP's self-aligned imprint lithography encoded every mask level as heights in one 3D stamp with no overlay; both died on solar and display economics. Combine them: planarized, glass-insulated steel coil, oxide-TFT gain-cell memory deposited roll-to-roll, all levels patterned by one SAIL imprint roller and sequential etch-back.
why: Substrate ~$5-10/m2 versus >$1,000/m2 for silicon wafers; no Cz, quartz, helium chucks or EUV; one stamp replaces 4-6 masks; ~4 GB/m2 at 2 um, so cost wins only if processing stays under ~$15/m2.
note: Combining R2R coil deposition with SAIL imprint is novel; processing cost and density at 2 um are doubtful.

title: Embedded-substrate failures fixed: memory tiers deposited inside glass package cores
idea: Embedded dies and passives in organic substrates failed because one bad buried part scrapped an expensive package. As processors move to glass-core substrates, deposit 2-4 oxide-TFT memory tiers on the glass core panel before build-up, test them with built-in self-test and redundancy repair at panel level, and bin packages by working capacity so a bad tier downgrades, never scraps.
why: Puts gigabytes of DRAM-class memory 1-3 mm under the processor, cutting data movement from 3-4 pJ/bit toward ~0.5 pJ/bit, with no silicon wafer, TSVs or HBM area tax; the glass core is already paid for.
note: Clever yield-binning combo, but TFT tiers at panel rules give low density; gigabytes per package doubtful.

title: Fairchild CCD memory, refit as transistor-free KV-cache shift banks
idea: 1970s CCD memories were denser than DRAM but lost on random-access latency. Attention reads every token's K and V in order each decode step, so build KV banks as CCD shift registers (no access transistor per bit, ~2-4F^2) that circulate continuously past a sense row synchronized to the decode loop.
why: Density/cost per bit for the KV cache (often >50% of inference memory): removes per-cell transistors and most row/column periphery.

title: Mercury delay line reborn: fiber-loop memory circulating AI weights at light speed
idea: Delay-line memory died because data was only available as it came round (sequential access) and the medium drifted with temperature. LLM inference reads every weight in the same order each token, so sequential access is fine: a ~10 km multicore-fiber loop (19 cores x C+L WDM, ~1 Pb/s) holds several GB in flight with all-optical amplifiers and a clock-recovering regenerator every few laps, and taps feed each accelerator as its layer's weights come round.
why: HBM capacity and data movement (facts 5, 6): weights delivered at ~100 TB/s with holding cost set by amplifier power (tens of W) rather than DRAM bits, freeing HBM for KV cache; claimed 2-5x less HBM for weight-streaming inference.
note: Pb/s transceivers and lap-synchronised taps cost more than the HBM saved.

title: Optical wordlines open dark-insulating photoconductive access pillars
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. Each storage capacitor reaches the bitline through a wide-gap photoconductor pillar (amorphous Se or ZnS, dark resistivity >10^13 ohm-cm, engineered short carrier lifetime for <10 ns turn-off); a row is opened by light from an on-die SiN waveguide grating, so the wordline is photons and the hold state is a dark insulator.
why: Leakage tail and periphery (facts 3, 7): attoamp dark current makes refresh near-zero; removes wordline drivers, row charge pumps and VPP from the ~49% periphery.
note: Per-row optical delivery at DRAM pitch and photoconductor on-current are doubts.

title: Field-ionized deep-dopant extensions stay semi-insulating while holding
idea: Effect: Poole-Frenkel field-assisted ionization. Dope the storage-node-side extension with a deep donor (e.g., S or Se in Si, ~0.3 eV, kept away from midgap to avoid SRH generation) so it is mostly un-ionized and semi-insulating at the low hold field, but the wordline-on field lowers the barrier and ionizes it within picoseconds so the extension conducts.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): removes the field-enhanced junction path that dominates the <=13 fA tail; claims ~10x tail reduction. Risk: deep levels as generation centres.
note: Deep levels act as generation centers; ps ionization questionable.

title: Hydrogen-terminated diamond access channel using surface transfer doping
idea: Effect: surface transfer doping. A bonded thin diamond film with an H-terminated surface and MoO3 acceptor cap forms a 2D hole gas that the wordline depletes; the 5.5 eV bulk band gap makes thermal generation essentially nil, and diamond's ~2000 W/mK conductivity spreads array heat.
why: Leakage tail and thermal (fact 3): retention hours and no high-temperature refresh doubling; bonded diamond layers are a route to cool 3D tiers (fact 2).

title: Field-drifted mobile-ion Vt trim repairs weak cells at sort
idea: Effect: thermally activated ion migration. A sub-nm Cs-doped sublayer sits in the access gate dielectric; at wafer sort the tester biases only retention-failing rows at ~200 C so ions drift from the channel side to the gate side, raising those transistors' Vt ~0.1-0.2 V; high activation energy (~1.5 eV) freezes them for life at operating temperature. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): ppm weak rows join the bulk distribution, so internal refresh can follow the median; claims 4x refresh interval.
note: Mobile ions are a classic reliability hazard; lifetime freeze unproven.

title: CCD bucket-brigade shifts bitline charges to one shared correlated-double-sampling amplifier
idea: Effect: charge-coupled transfer. Turn local bitlines into buried-channel CCD registers: on activation, cell charges are clocked across 64 columns into a single low-noise floating-diffusion amplifier with correlated double sampling (scientific CCDs reach <5 e- noise), and written back by a reverse shift. One amplifier serves 64 bitlines and resolves ~100-electron packets.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and capacitor wall (fact 1): ~64x fewer sense amps and Cs up to ~20x smaller; the cost is ~32 ns of serial shift latency, which suits burst page fetches.
note: Lateral CCD in DRAM array needs near-perfect transfer efficiency over 64 columns; serial latency.

title: Vertical BiSb spin-Hall pillar writes MTJs on eight tiers
idea: Spin Hall effect: a vertical bismuth-antimony topological-insulator pillar (no tungsten) threads eight BEOL tiers of perpendicular MTJs. Current in the pillar delivers spin-orbit torque to every MTJ along it, and a voltage-controlled-anisotropy bias on one tier's MTJ chooses which bit actually switches.
why: Gives non-volatile 3D SOT density with one write line per column (fact 2) and avoids the W chokepoint; claim 8x bits per footprint versus planar SOT-MRAM.
note: Sidewall perpendicular MTJs on a BiSb pillar are very hard to make; VCMA-gated selection is known.

title: Pyroelectric non-destructive readout of boron-aluminum-nitride ferroelectric cells
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. Store bits in wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric capacitors (no Hf, no Sc) and read them without switching: a ~5 K heat pulse from a wordline micro-heater makes a pyro-current whose sign gives the polarization. Because the signal is only hundreds of electrons, an in-cell gain transistor senses it.
why: Destructive read (fact 8) and Hf/Sc dependence: endurance is limited only by writes, and Al, B and N are abundant and U.S.-sourced.
note: Pyroelectric NDRO of nitride ferroelectrics is fresh; hundreds-of-electron signal and per-row heaters are severe doubts.

title: Electrochromic WO3 shutters hold model weights inside the photonic multiplier
idea: Each weight is a Li-intercalated WO3 attenuator on a silicon-nitride waveguide mesh. An ion-injection pulse sets its optical transmission once, and it holds without power. Activations ride on light and are multiplied as they pass through the colored film, so the weights live in the compute fabric and DRAM holds only activations and KV.
why: Weight-stationary optics takes both weight capacity and weight traffic out of DRAM (fact 5). That means 50-90% less DRAM for inference appliances whose models rarely change.
note: Doubt: photonic attenuators are ~100 um devices, so weight capacity per chip is tiny versus model sizes.

title: Spin-orbit domain-wall racetrack serves the append-only KV cache
idea: The KV cache is written only at its tail and read in full order every decode step, which is exactly a racetrack's access pattern. SOT current pulses shift magnetic domain walls along nanowires, appending each new token at the write head and streaming all tokens past a read head once per step. No random-access decoders or row activations are needed.
why: At ~1-2F^2 per bit with no refresh, the KV tier costs 3-5x less per bit than DRAM (facts 1, 3, 8).
note: Access pattern fits racetrack well, but racetrack remains unproven at density and speed.

title: H: bistable hydrogen site at Si/SiO2 interface as atomic bit
idea: Engineer a dense array of identical hydrogen defects that have two metastable configurations (bond-centred vs antibonding site, DX-like bistability); a field pulse moves the proton between sites, changing the local charge and a nearby nanowire's conductance.
why: The bit is one atom's position, giving density far beyond 6F² with no charge to leak (facts 1, 3, 4); reproducibility and room-temperature barrier height are speculative.
note: Reproducible identical defect arrays and RT barriers are speculative.

title: N: Idled 3D-NAND fabs build gain cells with charge-trap backup tiers
idea: In one 3D NAND staircase stack, form vertical-channel gain-cell tiers as working memory next to SiN charge-trap tiers; on power-loss detect an on-die capacitor bank streams the gain-cell contents into the charge-trap tiers.
why: Uses underutilized NAND capacity for non-volatile-backed DRAM-class memory; NAND endurance is spent only at shutdown.
note: Poly-Si channel leakage and on-die backup energy are doubts; novel pairing.

title: Lab-grown-gem CVD diamond access transistors with 5.5 eV channels
idea: Reuse the U.S. lab-grown diamond industry's CVD reactors to grow thin single-crystal diamond tiers. Build H-terminated surface-channel access FETs on them, using transfer-doping oxide such as MoO3 to switch the channel on.
why: Zero refresh: intrinsic generation in 5.5 eV diamond is effectively nil and junctionless surface channels remove GIDL, giving retention of years. This also creates a domestic, non-EUV memory supply chain.
note: Single-crystal diamond tiers over CMOS and unstable H-terminated channels are major hurdles.

title: Movable-type periphery: reusable pre-tested sense/decoder tiles across array generations
idea: Like Gutenberg's reusable type sorts, cast a library of periphery tiles (sense-amp strips, sub-wordline driver strips, pump and I/O tiles) on a depreciated logic wafer, test them, and hybrid-bond known-good tiles under each new array die. When the array shrinks, only a thin bitline-pitch adapter layer is re-cut; the tile library is reused for 3-4 array generations.
why: Periphery (~49% of die) is redesigned and re-fabbed on the expensive DRAM node every generation; reusable tiles cut DRAM-node wafer area per bit ~35-45% and periphery mask/NRE cost ~70%.
note: Reusing tiles across generations is new; a bitline-pitch adapter for hybrid bonding is the hard part.

title: Xerographic bitlines: light-switched photoconductive segments shorten bitlines on demand
idea: Borrow the photocopier drum: build each bitline from segments joined by amorphous-silicon photoconductor bridges that insulate in the dark. An on-chip SiN waveguide fed by an off-chip laser lights only the bridges between the accessed segment and the SA, so the SA sees a short, low-capacitance line and the rest is electrically absent.
why: Bitline capacitance per access falls 4-8x, multiplying the signal: Cs could drop from ~5 fF to ~1-2 fF (breaking the charge wall), with one SA serving very long bitlines.
note: a-Si photoconductor response is us-scale with persistent photoconductivity; laser and waveguide overhead.

title: Camcorder-CCD row buffer: charge packets shuffle to few amplifiers
idea: Borrow the 1990s CCD imager: on activate, every bitline's charge is dumped into a buried-channel CCD register under the SA strip, which holds the row in the charge domain. Only the requested columns are clocked a few stages to floating-diffusion amplifiers with correlated double sampling, then the packets are shifted back to restore.
why: One low-noise amplifier per 8-16 columns instead of one SA per column (SA area -80%); correlated double sampling resolves ~1,000-electron packets, so tiny planar capacitors made at 180 nm can be read.

title: Mortise-and-tenon bond pads enable per-cell split-wafer DRAM
idea: Joinery self-aligns parts; etch conical tenons on a transistor wafer and matching mortises on a separate capacitor wafer so mechanical engagement during hybrid bonding pulls overlay from ~100 nm to ~10 nm, allowing one bond per cell at ~200 nm pitch, with transistors from logic-like lines and deep capacitors from MEMS-like lines.
why: Splits the cell's two incompatible processes (capacitor thermal budget vs transistor leakage, facts 1 and 3) onto optimized wafers; per-cell bonding is ~10x too coarse today, and self-alignment is the enabler.
note: Mechanical self-alignment cannot correct wafer-scale distortion; per-cell bonding at ~200 nm pitch still far from DRAM pitch.

title: Gravure-cylinder nanoimprint rolls DRAM honeycomb arrays
idea: Gravure presses print magazines from an engraved rotating cylinder; build a nickel-sleeved cylinder carrying the capacitor and landing-pad honeycomb and roll it continuously across a UV-curable, fluorine-free resist on each wafer, phase-locked interferometrically so every rotation lands on the same array grid.
why: Replaces several ArF-immersion multipatterning or EUV exposures on the array's most repetitive layers with a tool costing ~1/20 of EUV, using no photomask blanks, no tin plasma and ~1/100 the electricity per layer.
note: Overlay and defectivity of a rotating cylinder over a rigid wafer at 30 nm pitch is the doubt.

title: Vacuum-gap floating electrodes in hermetic cavities hold charge for years
idea: Ideal: a capacitor with no leakage path at all. Closest achievable: each cell is a micro-electrode suspended in a wafer-level vacuum cavity with no dielectric to tunnel through, charged by a field-emission tip on write and sensed capacitively by an underlying transistor gate without contact, so stored charge persists for years without refresh.
why: Facts 1 and 3: removes both the dielectric and junction leakage paths that force refresh; hermetic vacuum packaging becomes the memory technology itself.
note: Field-emission write per cell needs high voltage and large area; density and speed unlikely to be DRAM-class.

title: Janus pillar: bitline at the waist, cells at both ends
idea: Limit: capacitor height capped at 300 nm per side. A 4F2 vertical pillar has a buried bitline contacting its middle. The upper half has its own gate and frontside capacitor. After wafer flip and bond, the lower half gets a second gate and a backside capacitor, so the pillar holds two independent cells.
why: Facts 1 and 4: 2F2 per bit with two short, low-AR capacitors instead of one 75:1 pillar, about 3x density at the same F.

title: Diamond via-layer lets DRAM sit directly atop hot GPU logic
idea: Scarcity: memory may not exceed 85 C yet must sit within 50 um of compute. A 20-50 um CVD-diamond interlayer (k~1,500 W/mK) with laser-drilled copper vias at 10 um pitch sits between GPU and hybrid-bonded DRAM, spreading hotspots sideways to edge cold plates before heat reaches the DRAM.
why: Data movement (fact 5): vertical DRAM-on-logic drops ~3-4 pJ/bit HBM traffic to ~0.2-0.5 pJ/bit by deleting the interposer trip; diamond makes the thermal stack survivable.

title: No silicon wafer: memory built inside glass-core package substrates
idea: Forced limit: no memory die. Substrate makers deposit oxide-TFT gain-cell tiers directly on the glass core of advanced package substrates (about 510x515 mm panels), so the substrate under the processor is itself a near-memory tier.
why: Supply and data movement: package-substrate makers become memory makers, and the wire to the processor is millimetres long, cutting I/O energy toward 1 pJ/bit.
note: Memory tiers in the package substrate itself is novel; coarse panel rules, thermal load under the processor and build-up process compatibility are doubts.

title: No silicon wafer: HDD media lines make MRAM crossbars on glass disks
idea: Forced limit: use another industry's substrate and tools. Hard-disk media lines, which sputter thousands of glass platters an hour and nanoimprint bit-patterned media, deposit MTJ plus threshold-selector crossbars on 95 mm glass disks.
why: Capital: reuses a shrinking HDD media industry with world-class sputter and nanoimprint tools, adding non-Si, endurance-unlimited memory capacity.

title: No silicon, no dicing: undiced panel-scale memory slab appliance
idea: Forced limit: the panel is never cut. A whole oxide-TFT memory panel with panel-level redundancy (spare tiles fused out by laser) is laminated into a rack-mounted CXL memory slab with dozens of edge controllers.
why: Removes dicing, packaging and yield loss per die; one slab supplies hundreds of GB of capacity tier at panel cost.
note: Undiced laser-repaired panel slab is novel; TFT density and speed make it a slow capacity tier at best.

title: Click-RAM: a snap-through 2D-nanoribbon mechanical floating gate over an oxide channel
idea: A ribbon of graphene, monolayer MoS2 or ~2 nm ALD Al2O3/TiN, 50-100 nm long and 10-20 nm wide, is clamped at both ends over a sealed 3.5-6 nm cavity with 0.1-0.3% built-in compressive strain, so it has two stable buckled shapes (+q and -q, q = 1.2-2.3 nm) that never touch the floor. An IGZO (or Si) channel under the cavity is the bottom electrode: a 1.9-2.8 V pulse between ribbon and channel snaps the ribbon down; a pulse on a top plate snaps it up. Read: hold the ribbon at ~0.8 V as a suspended gate; the up/down gap changes gate coupling ~1.5x, which gives a ~10^3 channel-current ratio while the read force is only 18% of the snap force (non-destructive). Cells sit in BEOL tiers above CMOS periphery. Because the state is mechanical, retention is set by a ~45-80 kT elastic barrier, not by leakage.
why: Refresh energy and standby power go to zero (non-volatile); intrinsic write energy is ~2-4 aJ, versus ~3 fJ stored on a 1-beta cell plus ~46 fJ per refresh; mechanical switching is sub-ns (f0 = 2-15 GHz). Density reaches 1-beta parity only with two BEOL tiers of 50 nm ribbons. The step change is on energy and volatility, not density.

title: Swap tall pillar for on-chip multilayer-ceramic nanolaminate capacitor
idea: Deposit ~100 alternating ALD layers of TiN (3 nm) and ZrO2 (4 nm) and cut each cell block with one DUV etch. Then recess and insulate the odd electrodes on one sidewall and the even ones on the other (like MLCC end terminations), so all plates connect in parallel.
why: ~100 stacked parallel plates give pillar-class Cs (fact 1) from a ~0.7 um low-AR block at DUV pitch, with no EUV and no 60:1 etch (fact 4).
note: Selectively recessing alternate identical TiN layers at cell pitch is not straightforward.

title: Swap ZrO2 for high-entropy relaxor perovskite with k near 500
idea: Deposit a lead-free high-entropy relaxor such as (Ba,Sr)(Ti,Zr,Hf,Sn)O3, whose polar nanoregions give a slim, nearly linear loop and k ~300-800 in 15-20 nm films. Crystallize it by flash-lamp anneal to keep the CMOS below within its thermal budget.
why: ~10x k gives 5 fF from a 10:1 cap at 30-40 nm DUV pitch (facts 1, 4); entropy stabilization targets the leakage and thickness-scaling failures that ended 2000-era BST.
note: BST-like thickness scaling failure is the doubt.

title: Swap smooth electrode for dealloyed nanoporous metal sponge electrode
idea: Deposit an AlTi or AgAu alloy as the storage-node electrode and selectively dissolve the less noble element, leaving a nanoporous sponge with 5-10 nm ligaments and 10-30x the surface area. ALD then coats the dielectric and top electrode conformally.
why: 10x or more effective area per footprint breaks the charge wall (fact 1) with a short, relaxed-pitch DUV cap and no high-AR etch or EUV (fact 4).
note: A 30 nm cell holds only a few ligaments; ALD dielectric plus top electrode clogs 5-10 nm pores.

title: Substitute litho-defined pillars with self-ordered anodic alumina templates
idea: Substitute lithography for the vertical-channel array with anodized aluminum: self-ordered hexagonal pores ~15-25 nm wide, guided by a shallow imprinted pre-pattern. Vertical channels are grown inside the pores by selective H2-carrier epitaxy or ALD, and the alumina stays as the host for the gate dielectric.
why: The wet electrochemistry needs no rare gas and no EUV/DUV, and pore diameter is fixed by anodization voltage, tightening channel width and leakage spread while slashing capex.
note: AAO domain disorder conflicts with addressable wordline/bitline grids.

title: Series negative-capacitance HZO capacitor as passive bitline amplifier
idea: Substitute part of the transistor gain with a passive voltage step-up: a doped-HZO capacitor biased in its negative-capacitance region sits in series between the bitline and the latch input, so the transient voltage at the latch is amplified ~2-5x. It is buildable with ALD and e-beam in a university fab.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): if verified, the same latch resolves with ~2x less cell charge, relaxing capacitor aspect ratio.

title: Smart-cut silicon carbide tier replaces silicon access transistors
idea: Substitute the silicon access-transistor layer with a ~200 nm 4H-SiC layer transferred from a reusable SiC donor (as SmartSiC does for power devices) and bonded over the capacitor array; 3.26 eV bandgap and ~1e-9 cm^-3 intrinsic carrier density (vs 1e10 in Si) suppress junction/GIDL leakage, while low mobility is irrelevant for an access device.
why: Leakage tail forces refresh (fact 3): retention 64 ms -> seconds-minutes, cutting refresh power (16-33% of idle) and the 10-20% bandwidth loss by ~95%.

title: Thermally drawn nanochannel glass slices replace etched capacitor holes
idea: Substitute etched holes with drawn glass: bundle acid-soluble core rods in an acid-resistant matrix glass, redraw 3-4 times to 30-50 nm channels (microchannel-plate style), fuse, saw into 10-20 um slices, leach cores in HCl, CMP with silica/KOH slurry, ALD electrodes, and oxide-bond the slice onto the transistor wafer using the channel-smaller-than-pad-gap landing rule.
why: Capacitor charge wall: AR set by slice thickness (300-500:1 possible) -> Cs >15 fF or smaller cells; capital shifts from EUV/HAR etch to glass draw towers, fully fluorine-free.

title: Substitute anodized aluminum pores for EUV-patterned capacitor holes
idea: Deposit a thick Al film over the cell array and anodize it in oxalic or phosphoric acid from an imprinted seed-pit pattern so self-ordered hexagonal pores grow straight down at 100-300:1 aspect ratio; line the pores with TiN/high-k/TiN and keep the alumina as a rigid mold that prevents leaning.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV exposures and the fluorocarbon high-AR etch with room-temperature electrochemistry; AR >115 becomes cheap, breaking the charge wall. Aluminum is abundant and US-smelted.
note: AAO pores lack registration to cell transistors; imprinted seeds reduce but do not solve alignment.

title: Substitute 3 V boosted wordlines with negative-capacitance steep-slope access transistors
idea: Add a thin HZO layer to the access-transistor gate stack, capacitance-matched for negative-capacitance amplification (sub-60 mV/dec), so the same off-leakage is reached with a ~1 V wordline; the VPP charge pumps and the thick-gate-oxide periphery module with its masks are deleted.
why: Constraint and fact 10: wordline CV2 falls ~9x and ~30%-efficient pump losses vanish, giving >=10x on the row path; facet: removes 3-5 masks for dual/triple oxides.
note: Steady-state NC sub-60 and hysteresis-free operation remain contested.

title: Substitute front-end silicon periphery with carbon-nanotube CMOS in BEOL
idea: Swap silicon periphery for complementary carbon-nanotube FETs deposited from purified solution at room temperature, so sense amps and decoders are built in BEOL tiers too and a whole memory can be made in a <=400 C fab.
why: Lets a front-end-free fab make complete memories, cutting the 49% periphery footprint off the expensive wafer and dropping fab capex by an estimated ~60%.
note: CNFET maturity and sense-amp matching doubtful; 60% capex claim unsupported.

title: Pseudocapacitive redox storage node borrowed from supercapacitors
idea: Coat the storage-node electrode with 1-2 nm of hydrous MnO2 (or another fast surface-redox oxide) behind a thin blocking oxide, so surface faradaic reactions store charge on top of the dielectric's electrostatic charge, as in supercapacitor electrodes (hundreds of uF/cm2). The cell becomes a nano-supercapacitor with 10-50x the areal charge of a plain MIM stack.
why: Fact 1: a planar or AR<10 capacitor could reach 5 fF, collapsing the high-AR etch and multi-step ALD module (cost per bit, capital); the open question is whether redox kinetics keep up at ns timescales.

title: NEMS air-gap relay as zero-leakage access switch for capacitor
idea: Replace the access transistor with a vertical nanoelectromechanical relay whose off state is a 5 nm vacuum gap: no channel and no junction, so off-current is essentially zero and the capacitor keeps its charge for days, limited only by dielectric leakage. Carbon or TiN contacts sit under a hermetic BEOL cap, and a negative-stiffness spring lets the relay close in a few ns below 1 V.
why: Fact 3: the 13 fA leakage tail vanishes, so refresh drops from ~46 fJ/bit to zero; low pull-in voltage also removes the 3 V wordline (fact 10).

title: Thermally locked ionic glass gating: ions frozen between writes
idea: Combine electric-double-layer ionic gating with a glass transition: the gate dielectric is an ionic glass whose ions move only above ~120 C, so a nanoscale heater line warms one cell for ~10 ns to drive ions and set the channel charge, and on cooling the ions freeze in place. The channel conductance stores the bit with no hold power.
why: Zero refresh; EDL gating gives ~1e14 cm-2 charge density for a large read signal; thermal write energy and speed are risks.
note: Ion freezing below Tg known; 10 ns thermal write and crosstalk doubtful.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric film as bitline signal amplifier
idea: Insert a thin doped-HfO2 negative-capacitance layer in series at the SA input gate (or at the bitline contact), capacitance-matched so the charge-sharing step has voltage gain above 1 and amplifies the cell signal before the latch fires.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): 2-3x signal gain would let Cs drop to ~2 fF and permit lower VARY (fact 10).

title: Antiferroelectric-ferroelectric bilayer capacitor parks idle rows nonvolatilely
idea: Stack antiferroelectric ZrO2 (linear-like, unlimited-endurance charge storage) with a thin ferroelectric HZO in one capacitor: active banks store bits as AFE charge, and when a bank idles the controller 'parks' each row into FE polarization, stopping refresh until the next access.
why: Refresh (fact 3): idle-bank refresh power (16-33% of idle) to ~0; FE layer switches only on park/unpark (~10^6 cycles per day budget).

title: Wolfspeed SiC access-transistor wafer bonded onto silicon periphery
idea: Fuse a power-electronics material into memory: build the access-transistor and capacitor array on 200 mm 4H-SiC in a US wide-bandgap fab (Wolfspeed, New York), then hybrid-bond it to a US silicon CMOS periphery wafer; SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap suppresses junction and GIDL leakage by orders of magnitude.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): refresh interval from 64 ms toward seconds-hours, removing 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss; adds an existing domestic fab to memory supply.
note: SiC DRAM retention shown at Purdue in 1990s; pitch and interface quality are the doubts.

title: Colloidal nanosphere lattice patterns transistors and capacitors in register
idea: Combine nanosphere lithography with a vertical-channel 4F2 cell. A monolayer of ~25 nm beads, guided by coarse immersion-printed trenches so rows stay straight, defines the pillar transistors, and the same lattice, shrunk by etch, defines the capacitors above. The ~1% bead vacancies and dislocations are simply bad cells.
why: Removes 3-5 critical array masks and all array overlay steps, so array patterning capex collapses to coaters plus one coarse layer (fact 4).

title: 2D-heterojunction tunnel-diode pair makes a self-holding capacitor cell
idea: Combine Esaki tunnel-diode bistability (the 1990s TSRAM concept) with van der Waals heterojunctions: two series BP/MoS2 or WSe2/SnSe2 negative-differential-resistance diodes latch the storage node at one of two stable points with picoamp standby current, so the cell needs no refresh. Buildable in a university nanofab: flake transfer plus e-beam patterning.
why: Eliminates refresh energy and retention tail (fact 3) in a DRAM-like cell; risks are peak-to-valley ratio and uniformity.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium sponge as the storage electrode
idea: Adapt tantalum-capacitor porous sintered anodes and catalyst dealloying: deposit a Ru-Al alloy plug in each storage hole, selectively leach the Al to leave a 3-5 nm-ligament Ru sponge, then ALD a 2 nm high-k and a conformal counter electrode through the pores.
why: Fact 1: internal surface is 5-8x the plain cylinder wall, so ~5 fF fits in AR ~20 holes instead of 60-75; shallower holes cut etch steps and pillar-collapse yield loss.
note: Pores must fit 2 nm high-k plus counter electrode twice; few pores fit in a sub-30 nm hole.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor borrowed from supercapacitors
idea: Replace the high-k dielectric with a 2-3 nm fast proton conductor (hydrated Ta2O5 or CsH2PO4-like film) between ion-blocking electrodes, so stored charge sits in Helmholtz double layers ~0.3 nm from each electrode, an effective k >200.
why: Fact 1: 10-20 uF/cm2 areal capacitance (vs ~4-6 for ZrO2 stacks) puts 5 fF in a planar or AR<15 node; the open question is whether sub-nm ion relaxation charges in ns at 2 nm.
note: EDL ~10-20 uF/cm2 is ~2-3x real high-k stacks, not 10x+; ns charging and self-discharge unproven.

title: Thermal-battery superionic gate freezes ions for perfect retention
idea: Adapt military thermal batteries whose electrolyte is solid (zero self-discharge) until heated: store the bit as Ag+ position in an Ag2S/AgI film that is superionic only above ~150 C; a ns Joule pulse unlocks the ion sublattice to write, and ions freeze in place on cooling.
why: 10x at same cost: a two-terminal element in a vertical 32-word-plane array sharing one hole litho, with no refresh; retention and write speed decoupled by the phase change.
note: AgI superionic transition is real; ns Joule-heating crosstalk and ion-migration wear are risks.

title: Column-parallel single-slope ADC reads two bits per cell
idea: Borrowed from image-sensor column ADCs: one global voltage ramp is broadcast to all 8k columns of a mat, and each column's tiny comparator latches a shared Gray-code counter when the ramp crosses its bitline. Each cell stores four charge levels and is digitized in one ~8 ns ramp.
why: Density and cost per bit: 2 bits/cell for ~15% extra periphery, because the per-column cost is one comparator plus two latches instead of three sense amps.

title: Nanotube-forest growth: grow vertical channels instead of etching holes
idea: Adapted from carbon-nanotube forest growth, where catalyst dots sprout aligned tubes millimeters tall: place catalyst at cell sites, grow vertical Si or oxide-semiconductor nanowires to ~5 um by VLS, then build the tier stack around them with low-temperature conformal fills, so no 70:1 hole etch is ever needed.
why: High-AR hole etch and its tools are among the costliest 3D steps (facts 2,4); 100-wafer growth batches cut this module ~50x; misaligned wires handled by redundancy.
note: Au-catalyzed VLS contaminates with deep traps; placement accuracy across wafer is the doubt.

title: MLCC core-shell titanate grains for an abundant high-k capacitor
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitor makers flatten BaTiO3 permittivity with core-shell grains (a ferroelectric core inside a doped paraelectric shell). Adapt this as an ALD nanolaminate of SrTiO3 cores with Ba/Mg-doped shells on a TiO2-templated TiN electrode to reach k ~70-100 in a 6 nm film.
why: Fact 1 says k ~70 is needed. Titanates use abundant Ba/Sr/Ti instead of Hf/Zr and let pillar aspect ratio fall from ~70:1 toward ~40:1, cutting deep-etch fluorocarbon gas and helium-cooled etch time.
note: k 70-100 in 6 nm ALD film with low leakage is unproven.

title: DNA nanotechnology: origami placement templates for cell contacts
idea: Borrow from biotech: DUV-pattern only coarse binding sites, let DNA origami tiles (C, H, N, O, P) dock into them by shape-selective placement, each carrying a designed 3-5 nm contact or landing-pad pattern, then transfer it into SiO2 by DNA-mediated vapor HF etching.
why: EUV dependence (fact 4): the finest array features come from molecular self-assembly on a DUV grid; DNA synthesis cost has fallen ~10^6x; zero banned elements.

title: Polar-vortex superlattice dielectric with stabilized negative capacitance
idea: MAGNIFY effective permittivity ~10x by building the cell dielectric from 1-2 nm alternating lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3 layers whose polar vortices contribute a stabilized negative capacitance; the series stack nets k ~250-400 without hysteresis because the vortex state never fully switches.
why: Clears the k~70 requirement (fact 1) with margin, so capacitor AR could fall from ~70:1 to ~15:1, cutting etch steps and freeing height budget for tiers.

title: Many-electron polyoxovanadate clusters as molecular storage nodes
idea: MAGNIFY electrons per site: a grafted monolayer of tungsten-free vanadium/molybdenum polyoxometalate clusters on the storage electrode accepts ~6-12 electrons each at discrete redox steps, so a 20-nm node holds ~10x the charge of a same-footprint dielectric capacitor and can encode several levels.
why: Faradaic pseudo-capacitance breaks the charge wall (fact 1) and avoids the tungsten chokepoint; the risk is electron-transfer kinetics slower than 100 ns.
note: POM cluster variant of molecular redox node; kinetics doubt.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous metal sponge multiplies capacitor surface tenfold
idea: MAGNIFY electrode area: deposit a Ru-Al or Ti-Al alloy liner in a shallow capacitor hole, selectively leach the Al to leave a metal sponge with 3-5 nm pores, then coat with ALD ZrO2 and a plate electrode, giving ~10x the internal surface of a smooth cylinder.
why: Same ~5 fF at AR ~10:1 instead of 70:1 (fact 1), removing the hardest etch and making capacitors stackable; conformal dielectric inside the pores is the risk.

title: Avalanche-multiplying read transistor amplifies sub-femtofarad nodes
idea: MAGNIFY read signal 50-100x: the gain-cell read device is an impact-ionization MOS (I-MOS) biased just below breakdown only during read, so ~0.05 fF of stored gate charge switches avalanche on or off with a sub-5 mV/decade slope.
why: Lets Cs shrink ~50x (fact 1) and cuts read energy; hot-carrier wear is bounded because the avalanche bias is applied ~1e-9 of the time.
note: Breakdown-voltage variability across cells makes a uniform near-breakdown bias hard.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate planar capacitor at 77 K
idea: MAGNIFY permittivity through quantum paraelectricity: SrTiO3 near 77 K has bulk k ~1000-1500; a strain-engineered 5-nm film on a SrRuO3 electrode that keeps k >= 300 makes a flat 20x20 nm capacitor of ~0.2-0.7 fF, enough with cryogenic retention.
why: Flat, etch-free capacitor replaces the AR 70:1 pillar (fact 1) and its litho/etch steps (fact 4); interfacial dead layer is the main risk.
note: Thin-film dead layer and DC-bias tuning likely collapse k; cryo niche.

title: Threshold-switch-gated crosspoint capacitor without access transistor
idea: MINIFY the cell to a 4F2 crosspoint: each capacitor is in series with a Mott threshold switch (NbO2 or doped VOx) that is insulating below ~0.8 V and conducting above, so only fully selected cells charge or discharge while half-selected ones stay sealed; decks stack 8+ high using only deposition and line patterning.
why: No transistor, monolithic 3D stacking (fact 2) on mature-litho lines (fact 4); threshold-switch off-leakage may limit retention to ms.
note: Threshold-switch off leakage is orders above the ~fA needed for usable retention.

title: Nanorelay-gated storage node with effectively infinite off-resistance
idea: MAGNIFY access-device off-resistance to infinity: replace the access transistor with a ~1 ns, 15-nm-gap NEMS contact switch (Ru or TiN cantilever) so the storage node is isolated by a gas gap when open and only the capacitor dielectric leaks.
why: Kills the leakage tail (fact 3) for hours-to-days retention and lowers wordline voltage via ~1 V pull-in (fact 10); contacts must survive ~1e14 cycles.
note: Relay contacts must survive ~1e14 cycles; best NEMS relays far short.

title: Magnify off-resistance to a vacuum gap: NEMS access relay
idea: Replace the access transistor with a 30 nm torsional nanoelectromechanical contact relay (Ru/RuO2 tip, 3-5 nm sealed vacuum gap) pulled in by the wordline; when open the gap passes essentially zero current, leaving only capacitor dielectric leakage. Hermetic BEOL sealing targets 1e15 contact cycles.
why: Deletes the access-device leakage tail entirely; retention limited by the dielectric (minutes-hours), refresh nearly eliminated; contact endurance is the risk.
note: Vacuum-gap relay kills access leakage; contact endurance of 1e15 is far beyond demonstrated NEMS.

title: Minify grain to one domain: wall-free ferroelectric nanodots for fatigue immunity
idea: Pattern HZO into <=8 nm epitaxial single-domain islands on a templated seed so each switches coherently without domain-wall nucleation or pinning, removing the defect-redistribution paths behind wake-up and fatigue; arrays of dots form each cell capacitor.
why: Targets FeRAM endurance from ~1e11 to >1e15 for a non-volatile DRAM replacement; tighter switching distribution also lowers voltage.
note: Fatigue stems largely from electrode vacancies, not only domain walls; epitaxial HZO not CMOS-ready.

title: Periphery evicted upstairs: oxide-tellurium CMOS sense amps over array
idea: Within a 400 C budget, build sense amps and decoders in BEOL tiers directly above the cell array using n-type IGZO (deposited ~300 C) and p-type tellurium TFTs (evaporated near room temperature), MINIFYING periphery footprint on silicon toward zero.
why: Fact 7: periphery share of die from ~49% to ~15%, ~1.6x bits per wafer; tellurium p-FET stability is the main risk.
note: TFT mismatch and Te p-FET instability are poor fits for offset-critical sense amps.

title: Ferroelectric HZO negative-capacitance shunt minifies effective bitline capacitance
idea: A thin HZO film (crystallized at 350-400 C) in a capacitor shunted to each bitline segment is biased in its negative-capacitance region during charge sharing, MINIFYING the net bitline capacitance by 50-70%.
why: Fact 1: signal 2-3x, enabling ~2x smaller Cs or VARY ~0.6 V; hysteresis-free transient NC at ns speed is unproven, hence high risk.
note: Stable transient NC shunt at ns speed is unproven; hysteresis risk high.

title: Magnify capacitor AR to 300:1 with wet metal-assisted chemical etching
idea: Form the storage capacitor as a deep trench in the substrate using metal-assisted chemical etching, where gold or silver catalyst dots sink into Si in an HF/H2O2 bath to give AR above 300:1 with no plasma etcher. A vertical access transistor sits on top, reviving trench-capacitor DRAM.
why: Charge wall: Cs could reach about 15-20 fF at the same footprint, with a cheap wet bench instead of $50M+ high-AR plasma etchers.

title: Dirty fab: class-1000 cleanroom plus massive remapping
idea: Minify cleanliness requirements 1000x and magnify redundancy: accept up to 30% bad bits per subarray and let a controller with an on-die defect map route around them like a Teramac crossbar.
why: Fab capital and yield: cleanroom spend and particle control capex fall sharply; dies that would be scrapped become sellable at derated capacity.
note: Killer particles short whole lines at 10 nm pitch; 30% bad bits is far past remap economics.

title: Kilometer-scale web: printed gain-cell memory sheets
idea: Magnify the substrate to a 1 m-wide polyimide web moving at 10 m/min, printing oxide 2T gain cells at 20 um2 per bit (~6 GB per m2), used as a capacity tier behind an SRAM/DRAM cache.
why: Capital intensity: a roll-to-roll line costs ~$20-50M; at ~$20/m2 this targets a few dollars per GB with zero EUV.

title: Laminated foil stack: 100 printed sheets per block
idea: Magnify tiers through lamination instead of deposition: print memory on 10 um foils, laminate 100 foils into a 1 mm block, and connect them through laser-drilled, printed-fill vertical edge vias.
why: 3D DRAM tier problem: 100 tiers with no tier-by-tier deposition yield compounding, because each foil is tested before lamination.

title: Minify the vacuum: atmospheric mist-CVD oxide memory fab
idea: Deposit IGZO/Ga2O3 channels and high-k capacitor oxides by atmospheric mist CVD and solution combustion synthesis, pattern with atmospheric-plasma etch, and eliminate vacuum chambers, load locks and turbopumps in a warehouse-grade fab.
why: Vacuum hardware is a large share of tool cost and energy; vacuum-free layers at ~$5-20/m2 each, stacked 16-32 high, target ~100x lower $/GB, accepting lower mobility and slower cells.
note: At ~1 um rules, 32 layers give ~$1-3/GB, not 100x cheaper.

title: Eliminate the solid storage medium: electrowetting nanodroplet position bits
idea: Eliminate solid-state storage: each cell is a sealed 30-nm pore holding a liquid-metal or ionic-liquid nanoplug that electrowetting moves between its top and bottom halves; capillary pinning holds it without power, and the plug position changes the cell capacitance 5-10x for readout.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free with no crystal-lattice wear-out (fact 3); viscous motion over ~10 nm might take 10-100 ns, which is the speculative part.
note: Capillary-pinned nanoplug is nonvolatile; 30 nm electrowetting speed and hysteresis are speculative.

title: Eliminate deep etching: self-rolling strained nanomembranes become swiss-roll capacitors
idea: Eliminate any deep etch: deposit a strained SiNx bilayer by SiH4/NH3/N2 PECVD (no helium or argon dilution) topped with electrode and dielectric layers, then dissolve a sacrificial layer so the stack curls into a multi-turn nano-roll; a 30x30 nm footprint could host a coil with 5-10x the area of a planar capacitor.
why: Multiplies area without HAR etch (facts 1, 4) using only nitrogen chemistry; risk is that controlled rolling below 100 nm is unproven.
note: Multi-layer stack rolls to hundreds of nm diameter; sub-30 nm multi-turn rolls unlikely.

title: Eliminate dopants: polarization-induced 2DEG GaN access transistor
idea: Replace the doped Si access device with an AlGaN/GaN heterostructure whose channel electrons come from spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization rather than dopants, turned off with a recessed p-GaN gate. No implant, no random dopant fluctuation and a 3.4 eV gap remove the junction and thermal-generation leakage tail.
why: Intrinsic carrier density ~1e-10 cm^-3 vs 1e10 in Si; leakage could fall >1000x, pushing retention to seconds and removing most refresh energy; GaN-on-Si is an existing U.S. power-electronics process. Array-density integration is unproven.

title: Eliminate the Boltzmann limit: feedback-FET access device
idea: Use a gated p-i-n feedback FET whose intrinsic region holds charge barriers that collapse abruptly under positive feedback, giving <1 mV/dec switching. The device is hard off at 0 V gate and fully on near 1 V, so the 3 V wordline and the negative-wordline pump are removed.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10) and the leakage-vs-on-current tradeoff: ~1e-18 A off current at equal on current, wordline energy ~9x lower (3 V to 1 V), pump periphery area removed (fact 7).
note: A p-i-n feedback FET conducts one way and is hysteretic; an access switch must write both states.

title: Eliminate the semiconductor: ALD MIIM tunnel-diode 1D1C cell
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a metal-insulator-insulator-metal diode (ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 between dissimilar work-function metals) whose step-tunneling barrier gives ~1e6 nonlinearity; cells are crosspoint-addressed by V/2 biasing, and at hold bias tunneling is exponentially suppressed. Every layer is a university ALD or sputter step.
why: No crystalline silicon or dopants, BEOL-stackable for many tiers (fact 2); retention hinges on reaching <1e-17 A at half-select.
note: Hold leakage at full storage voltage conflicts with write current.

title: Eliminate the channel: volatile Ag/Ag2S gap-type atomic switch access
idea: Use a gap-type atomic switch: a 1-2 nm vacuum gap between an Ag2S electrode and a Pt counter electrode, where a gate pulse grows a single-atom Ag bridge for access and the bridge dissolves spontaneously when bias is removed. The off state is a true vacuum gap with tunnel leakage below 1e-20 A.
why: Retention set only by capacitor dielectric, so refresh is eliminated; built with e-beam lithography and evaporation in any university fab; endurance and speed are open risks.

title: Eliminate the consumable wafer: foil arrays stacked like paper
idea: Build thin-film DRAM arrays on a reusable sapphire carrier, release each 2-5 um array foil by laser lift-off, and laminate dozens of foils into a stack with printed vertical vias; the carrier returns to the line hundreds of times.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: cuts Czochralski wafer (and Spruce Pine quartz crucible) consumption per bit by >10x and multiplies bits per footprint.
note: Printed vias cannot meet array pitch; thin-film cells on sapphire are leaky.

title: Eliminate pitch-defining lithography: rotated superlattice slices
idea: Grow a 1000-period Si/SiGe or Si/oxide multilayer whose film thicknesses set the 10-12 nm line pitch, slice it perpendicular to the layers, and bond the slab flat so the layers become parallel bitlines/channels; litho is needed only for coarse cuts.
why: Litho and capital: replaces 5-7 EUV layers with epitaxy thickness control (Angstrom precision), attacking the ~55% depreciation share of wafer cost.
note: Like SNAP superlattice transfer; tiling 12 um slabs across a wafer with alignment is the hurdle.

title: Eliminate regulator losses: series-stacked bank domains recycle bitline charge
idea: Stack four bank groups in series across 4x0.5 V rails so charge dumped from one bank's bitlines flows down to power the next domain instead of to ground, with a small switched-capacitor balancer absorbing load mismatch.
why: Charge is reused ~3-4 times and pump/LDO losses (~2.5x) vanish, together ~10x lower energy per activation.
note: Charge recycling via stacked domains is known; 10x claim ignores load imbalance and balancer losses.

title: Eliminate the 1 V array: 0.25 V storage with auto-zeroed sense amps
idea: Store and sense at 0.25 V from an efficient buck rail and run all long data wires at 50-100 mV, using offset-cancelling sense amps that sample their own offset onto a capacitor before each activate.
why: Bitline and data-line CV2 drop ~16x; the 4x lower field across the capacitor lets thin Al2O3/TiO2 stacks replace Hf/Zr high-k.
note: 0.25 V storage gives tiny signal vs noise/leakage; offset cancellation helps but retention margin is thin.

title: Retention-dial memory: one die is both DRAM and storage
idea: Eliminate the DRAM-to-SSD copy and the two-chip BOM: use a spin-torque or ferroelectric cell whose write pulse width/amplitude sets retention (short pulse: hours, ~1e15 endurance, ns writes; long pulse: 10 years), with the base die re-writing pages in long-retention mode as they cool.
why: Removes storage-to-memory transfers and duplicate copies across tiers; in phones and edge devices one package replaces LPDDR+UFS, saving ~30% memory BOM and all load-time traffic.
note: STT retention is set by thermal stability, not write pulse; mechanism questionable.

title: Eliminate the silicon wafer: memory tiles on idle display-glass lines
idea: Eliminate the 300mm wafer and the DRAM fab: retool overbuilt Gen-6/8 LCD/OLED backplane lines (oxide-TFT tools already installed) to build 8-16 stacked tiers of low-temperature oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on glass, diced into cheap capacity tiles for CXL far memory.
why: Panel area costs ~100x less per cm2 than 300mm silicon and lines are depreciated; with tier stacking, capacity-tier cost per bit could approach DRAM with almost no new capex and no EUV.
note: Micron-scale display rules give ~100x lower density; per-tier panel cost makes DRAM-like $/bit doubtful.

title: Access transistor turns avalanche amplifier during the read window
idea: Reverse the access device's job on read: for a 1 ns window its drain junction is biased just above breakdown, so the few hundred electrons released from a tiny 0.1 fF node trigger quenched impact-ionization gain of ~100 (SPAD-like) and produce a full-swing bitline signal; at idle it is a normal off transistor.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): Cs can shrink ~50x to a planar capacitor while keeping sense margin; risks are avalanche noise, dark counts and hot-carrier wear.

title: Grow, don't etch: VLS nanowire electrodes at 150:1 aspect ratio
idea: Reverse subtractive to additive: Al or Sn catalyst dots on each storage node grow vertical silicon nanowire electrodes by vapor-liquid-solid growth (150:1 is easy to grow and impossible to etch), then ALD high-k and a conformal top electrode wrap them.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): the AR ~115 needed for more charge is reached without aspect-ratio-dependent etch limits, ~8 fF per cell; risk is catalyst contamination and wire placement.
note: Catalyst contamination, placement at DRAM pitch, and conformal ALD fill in a dense 150:1 forest remain hard.

title: Cell refreshes itself: storage-gated keeper on a pulsed restore rail
idea: Reverse who refreshes: instead of the periphery sensing and rewriting row by row, add a tiny second transistor to each cell whose gate is the storage node and whose channel links the node to a shared restore rail. Pulsing the rail to a boosted level (about VARY+Vt) tops up only cells still holding a '1' (their keeper is on) while '0' cells stay off, so one array-wide pulse refreshes millions of cells with no sense amps, no bitline swing and no bank lockout.
why: Refresh energy and time (fact 3): ~46 fJ/bit refresh shrinks to the few-fJ CV top-up of decayed charge, and the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss goes to ~0; costs ~30-40% more cell area (2T1C).
note: As described the keeper's gate equals its source when the rail is high (Vgs=0), so it cannot top up; topology needs rework.

title: Split the cell across wafers: capacitors bonded onto transistors
idea: Fabricate storage capacitors on a separate wafer where perovskite (Ba,Sr)TiO3 can be crystallized at 650-750 C (k~100-300), then bond it face-to-face onto the transistor wafer through a self-aligning nano-pad lattice and strip the capacitor carrier. Transistor and capacitor never share a thermal budget.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): k>100 means AR <20 for 5 fF, removing the AR-115 requirement; the real risk is ~50 nm-pitch bonding versus today's ~400 nm.

title: Pillars first, tiers grown around them
idea: Invert stack-then-etch: start with short vertical Mo bitline pillar stubs on the base, then build each tier bottom-up around them (deposit and planarize dielectric and channel), extending each pillar by area-selective deposition per tier, so no 60+ tier high-aspect-ratio hole etch is ever needed.
why: 3D process wall (fact 2): removes the HAR etch and its hardmask cost; tier count is limited by deposition cycles rather than etch AR.
note: Area-selective deposition mushrooms laterally each tier; selectivity loss compounds over 60 tiers.

title: Let the pores place the cells: anodic alumina template
idea: Reverse 'cells define holes': anodize aluminum into a self-ordered hexagonal pore array (~40-60 nm pitch, AR >500), use the pores as capacitor molds, then self-align the access transistors to the pore lattice instead of drawing them by litho.
why: Capacitor charge wall: AR far above 75:1 without plasma etch or EUV; the main capacitor module litho goes away.
note: Pore lattice defects make transistor self-alignment hard.

title: Pattern once, select forever: permanent scaffold lattice
idea: Reverse 'one mask per layer': define one master dielectric grid by double spacer patterning at the very start and keep it as a permanent scaffold; every later layer only fills or opens grid cells, chosen with coarse i-line block masks.
why: Critical-mask count drops from ~20+ to ~2 DUV, the rest on i-line; overlay is set by the scaffold, not the scanner; no EUV.

title: Electron recapture pulse after aggressor activation bursts
idea: Reverse the hammer charge flow: after N activations of a row, the drivers apply a brief opposite-polarity pulse to the neighboring passing wordlines and local well contact to drift injected electrons back toward the aggressor's drain before they reach victim storage nodes.
why: Row hammer: if electron migration is the dominant path, the flip threshold could rise 5-10x with no refresh bandwidth spent.

title: Bistable buckled 2D-membrane nanodrum stores the bit as curvature
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution + #14 Spheroidality: a pre-compressed few-layer hBN or graphene membrane over a ~30-nm cavity buckles either up or down; an electrostatic pulse from the top or bottom electrode snaps it over, and its capacitance to the bottom electrode reads the state without disturbing it. No charge is stored, so nothing leaks.
why: Facts 3 and 8: zero refresh and non-destructive read; 2D membranes survive >10^12 flex cycles; back-end array over periphery at ~4F2.
note: Buckled-membrane bits studied; density and ns snap at 30 nm uncertain.

title: Self-rolled-up nanomembrane Swiss-roll capacitor in every cell
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #7 Nesting: deposit a strained TiN/ZrO2/TiN/SiN multilayer flat with no deep etch, then release a sacrificial layer so built-in strain rolls it into a 5-10-turn tube; each turn adds electrode area, and lateral rolls suit horizontal 3D DRAM tiers.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 4: ~10x area per footprint from planar deposition and release, replacing 70:1 etching; scaling roll diameter to tens of nm is the risk.

title: Self-ordered anodic-alumina pores host lithography-free coaxial access transistors
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: anodise an aluminium foil or Al-coated glass panel so it self-organises into hexagonal nanopores at 30-60 nm pitch (~1e10-1e11 per cm2). ALD lines each pore coaxially with bottom electrode, wide-gap oxide channel, gate dielectric and a wrap gate at the top, with the lower pore volume forming the storage capacitor: gate-all-around access at near-4F2 density without EUV.
why: Attacks capital intensity (Fact 4: 5-7 EUV layers) while GAA electrostatics plus wide-gap channels cut leakage (Fact 3); aluminium is abundant and U.S.-produced. Wordline/bitline addressing at pore pitch is the hard part.

title: Hermetic NEMS relay access switch: an air gap is the perfect off-state
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution, inverted: replace the field-effect switch with an electrostatically actuated nano-cantilever relay built on glass and sealed in a vacuum/inert micro-cavity. Open, the gap gives zero channel leakage so retention is set only by capacitor dielectric leakage (minutes to hours); closed, a metal contact gives near-ideal write/read with abrupt switching at low actuation voltage.
why: Eliminates the access-transistor leakage tail entirely (Fact 3) and the 3 V wordline (Fact 10) via abrupt actuation; key risks are contact endurance at 1e12-1e15 cycles and ns-scale switching.

title: Vacuum-nanogap field-emission access transistor on sapphire
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): a <50 nm vacuum channel, operable near atmospheric pressure because it is shorter than the mean free path of air, separates a sharp emitter from the storage electrode on a sapphire substrate, with a surrounding gate modulating field emission. With no semiconductor in the channel there is no thermal generation or band-to-band leakage in the off state.
why: Off-state leakage effectively zero (Fact 3), radiation-hard and heat-tolerant, so no high-temperature refresh derating; risks are emitter stability and turn-on voltage (Fact 10).
note: Writing a 0 needs emission from a blunt storage electrode; bidirectional low-voltage FN access is the doubt.

title: Thermal expansion: latching bimorph nano-relays as zero-leakage wordline decoders
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: wordline decoders are built from bistable electrothermal bimorph nano-relays patterned in BEOL metal and oxide layers above the array, with no transistors; a heat pulse flexes a relay into contact where it latches mechanically, routing ~3 V wordline drive with zero off-state leakage.
why: 100x path: decoders move out of front-end silicon into ~4 cheap metal masks at 90 nm-class pitch, enabling transistor-free periphery over stacked arrays; trade-offs: ~0.1-1 us switching and relay wear (~1e9-1e12 cycles) limits activations per row. Attacks Facts 7 and 10.
note: Decoder relays switch on every activation; 1e9-1e12 cycles falls far short.

title: Feedback: shared sigma-delta loops read three bits per cell
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: after charge sharing each bitline holds its voltage on its own capacitance while one 1-bit sigma-delta modulator per 128 bitlines visits them in turn, feeding back charge packets until balanced, resolving 8 charge levels (3 bits) per planar cell in ~2 us instead of a binary latch per bitline.
why: 100x path: 3x bits per cell and 128x fewer sensing circuits, compounded with stacked mature-node tiers; trade-offs: microsecond reads, cells must hold ~8x finer charge levels so leakage must be very low (oxide TFTs), and refresh must rewrite multilevel values. Attacks Facts 1 and 7.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials, resolving 'taller capacitor vs. costlier etch': sputter ~3 um Al over the storage-node landing pads and let the pad topography seed pore nucleation. Anodizing then grows self-ordered 20-25 nm pores straight down at AR >150:1 in minutes; thin the barrier at the pore bottoms and ALD TiN / high-k / TiN into the pores, keeping the alumina as the mechanical support lattice.
why: Fact 1 and 4: AR ~115-150 without high-AR plasma etch or a capacitor-hole litho layer; ~1.5-2x Cs (or same Cs at ~30% smaller footprint) and removes one of the costliest etch modules.

title: Antiferroelectric gate held between its double loops as volatile bistable
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2 antiferroelectric layer in each cell transistor's gate and park the wordline plane at a hold bias between the two hysteresis loops, where both the nonpolar and the field-induced polar phase are stable. A short over- or under-pulse toggles the phase and the channel Vt reads it.
why: Fact 1 and 3: capacitorless 1T cell, minor-loop AFE switching aims at >10^12 cycles, no refresh while the hold bias is on, and whole 3D tiers share one gate plane.
note: AFE minor-loop endurance at ns speeds and hold-bias disturb are unproven.

title: Negative-capacitance gate stack amplifies tiny gain-cell storage charge
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight: counter the 'weight' of a tiny stored charge with an internal uplift: add a thin ferroelectric layer to the read transistor's gate, matched to operate in its negative-capacitance regime, so the storage node's voltage is amplified at the channel surface. The storage node can then be just the bare gate (~0.1 fF) with an unchanged read margin.
why: Fact 1 and 10: ~2-3x read current per stored electron, storage swing down to ~0.5 V (CV2 -75%) and smaller capacitorless cells.
note: Static negative capacitance remains contested; hysteresis-free gain at storage node unproven.

title: Anodized mesoporous silicon electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: anodize heavily doped silicon electrode arms in HF to form 3-5 nm mesopores, line the pores with ALD Al2O3/TiO2 nanolaminate, and fill them with TiN, so each electrode becomes a sponge with ~3-10x the surface area.
why: Reaches the needed Cs at an aspect ratio of ~20:1 instead of ~70:1, or makes lateral 3D-DRAM capacitors ~3x shorter, with no exotic high-k (Si, Al, Ti, N, O, F only).
note: 3-5 nm pores cannot hold a ~5 nm dielectric plus TiN fill at DRAM electrode widths.

title: Undercritical ferroelectric zinc-magnesium oxide adds negative-capacitance boost
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial action: place a thin wurtzite Zn1-xMgxO ferroelectric (a 2021 discovery made only of abundant elements) in series with Al2O3 and deliberately keep it just short of switching. It then operates in its negative-capacitance region and raises total stack capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.
why: Could boost Cs ~1.5-3x at the same geometry with only Zn, Mg, Al and O. The risks are negative-capacitance stability and leakage at ns timescales.

title: Matryoshka multi-shell capacitor contacted by etch-selective recesses
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting resolves 'more charge but no taller hole': ALD alternating TiN and Ru electrode shells separated by ZrO2 inside one hole, then a TiN-selective top recess and a Ru-selective bottom recess tie odd shells to the storage node and even shells to the plate, giving 3-4 parallel capacitor walls per hole.
why: Cs ~2-2.5x per hole at constant AR, so today's ~5 fF needs only ~30:1 instead of 60-75:1; removes 1-2 support-mesh masks and the slowest HAR etch tool-hours (facts 1, 4).
note: Multiple electrode/dielectric shells do not fit in a ~30-40 nm hole.

title: Stiction-latched nanopillar relay built with the capacitor-hole etch
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: use the existing 70:1 mold etch to free-stand a ~20 nm TiN pillar between two side electrodes; a pull-in pulse snaps its tip onto one electrode where van der Waals adhesion (stiction, normally a yield killer) holds it at zero power, and the read senses which side conducts.
why: Zero refresh and zero standby; a ~1 um pillar resonates at ~20-50 MHz, giving ~10 ns switching; reuses DRAM's own HAR etch and ALD tools so conversion capex is small, with no dielectric-leakage spec at all (facts 3, 10).

title: Twin tunnel-diode latch grown where the capacitor used to be
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging joins storage and restoring in one element: epitaxially stack two Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes in a short ~5:1 hole above the access transistor; their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages, and with sub-pA peak current the node self-latches (TSRAM-style).
why: Zero refresh power, with hold power ~0.05 pW/bit vs ~0.7 pW/bit for refresh today; the 60-75:1 capacitor module and its masks are replaced by low-AR epitaxy (facts 1, 3, 4).
note: Sub-pA peak current with tight ITD variation at cell scale is the doubt.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric 3R-MoS2 channel as a refresh-free 1T cell
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: store the bit as the stacking order (AB vs BA) of a wafer-scale CVD-grown bilayer 3R-MoS2 channel; a gate pulse slides the layers by one bond length, flipping out-of-plane polarization and shifting threshold voltage, which persists without power and without mobile ionic defects to fatigue.
why: Zero refresh in a 1T cell (~4F2 possible) with no capacitor module; sliding switching breaks no bonds, so endurance could exceed HZO FeFETs, and growth below ~500 C fits any BEOL (facts 2, 3, 4).

title: Elapsed-time-aware sensing reads decayed charge without refresh
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: instead of holding charge constant, make the read reference follow it - each row stores a few-bit write-epoch tag, and the sense reference is stepped down along the measured decay of matched reference cells written at the same time, keeping cells readable ~10x longer; paired with a page time-to-live, refresh is never issued.
why: Zero refresh; ~10x usable retention lets the fab cut Cs or accept a leakier, cheaper access transistor (drop a halo/channel implant mask, shallower buried gate) (facts 3, 4).
note: Reference cells track median decay; tail/VRT cells still fail.

title: Nacre brick-and-mortar perovskite nanosheet capacitor dielectric
idea: Copy nacre, where staggered aragonite bricks sit in a thin organic mortar. Tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10-type perovskite nanosheets (k ~200 at 2-3 nm) in staggered, overlapping layers bonded by a 0.3 nm Al2O3 mortar, deposited by flow-coating into the capacitor. The staggered seams force leakage paths to wander, the way shell deflects cracks.
why: Hits the k~70 target for the charge wall (fact 1): k_eff ~100-150 gives ~3x Cs per area, so AR can drop from ~70 to ~25. It also removes the Zr/Hf ALD dependence.

title: Photosynthetic cascade trap: stepped wells carry electrons out of reach
idea: Reaction centres prevent charge recombination by hopping the electron down a chain of acceptors, each step further away. Build the storage node as a graded staircase of 3-4 oxide-semiconductor quantum wells (e.g. IGZO/Ga2O3/ZnMgO with stepped conduction-band offsets) beside a transistor channel. A write pulse cascades electrons into the far well, where back-tunneling is exponentially suppressed by distance, shifting Vt non-volatilely; an opposite low-field pulse reverses the cascade.
why: Non-volatile charge storage at low write field (~0.3 V steps instead of ~10 MV/cm Fowler-Nordheim tunneling), aiming at 10^9-10^12 endurance and ~50 ns writes. BEOL oxide process, no EUV.
note: Stepped barriers echo crested/VARIOT tunnel stacks; retention-vs-write-speed tradeoff persists.

title: Calcium-transient diffusive selector as a volatile two-terminal access switch
idea: Synaptic Ca2+ floods in and is cleared within ms; use an Ag-nanocluster diffusive threshold switch in sputtered SiO2 (room temperature) as the access device: a bitline-wordline pulse forms a filament that spontaneously dissolves within ~1 us, leaving a high-resistance off-state with ~1e10 on/off.
why: Two-terminal access lets 4F2 crosspoint DRAM tiers stack in BEOL without a transistor or EUV gate layers; the open problems are fA-level off-current and 1e15 endurance.
note: fA off-current and 1e15 endurance both orders beyond diffusive selectors today.
