why: Gives monocrystalline access transistors on every tier without the 400-500 C split anneal of Smart Cut, and donor reuse cuts wafer use. High risk: spall roughness, thinning uniformity, low-temperature gate-dielectric quality.

title: Sticker-book kid: micro-transfer-print periphery chiplets onto low-T arrays
idea: A kid peels finished stickers onto a page. Make sense-amp and decoder chiplets (~100x100 um) in a cheap mature CMOS fab, release them by undercut, pick thousands at once with an elastomer stamp using kinetic adhesion, and print them onto the <=400 C memory-array wafer or panel, wired by one BEOL redistribution layer; the memory fab itself never exceeds 400 C.
why: Splits the high-temperature periphery (49% of die) from the low-temperature arrays so each runs on its cheapest line; one stamp moves ~10k chiplets per cycle. Risk: ~1 um placement accuracy limits connection density.
note: ~1 um placement cannot meet bitline-pitch sense-amp connections.

title: Temporary-tattoo decal: freestanding perovskite membranes as capacitor dielectric
idea: A child applies a temporary tattoo. A materials supplier grows single-crystal SrTiO3 or BaTiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer; dissolving that layer frees the membrane, which the memory fab laminates like a decal onto planar stacked-tier capacitors and bonds at <=300 C.
why: Bulk-like k >100-300 gives ~5 fF in ~0.03 um2 planar footprints in stacked-tier cells, skipping high-AR pillars (fact 1) while the memory fab stays <=400 C. High risk: wafer-scale membrane handling, cracking, patterning.

title: Gutenberg's press: one 3D imprint stamps all 128 staircase steps
idea: Gutenberg replaced hand copying with a press. A 3D multi-level nanoimprint template, written once by e-beam, stamps all 128 staircase steps and tier contacts of a 3D DRAM stack in a single imprint, replacing ~30 litho/trim cycles. U.S. template shops and NIL tool vendors form the supply chain.
why: Meets the 10x constraint as a cost enabler: staircase and contacts are ~30-40% of a 3D memory wafer's cost, and collapsing them to one imprint lets a 128-tier 3D DRAM (~10x/mm^2) be built at about today's DRAM wafer cost.

title: Astronomer's CCD loops: charge-packet memory made in image-sensor fabs
idea: An astronomer knows CCDs move charge packets almost losslessly. 'CCD-loop memory' circulates rows of 64 contactless charge buckets in short loops past one sense amp, each bucket holding a 3-bit packet, with no access transistor per bit. It is built in U.S. CMOS image-sensor fabs on a mature process.
why: Meets the 10x constraint: ~2F^2 per bucket vs 6F^2 (3x) times 3 bits per packet (3x) is ~9-10x bits/mm^2 at mature-node wafer cost. Average access is ~32 shifts x 2 ns, about 70 ns, and dark current sets the refresh rate.
note: 3-bit packets at small bucket sizes face CTE loss and dark current.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate capacitor with k near ten thousand
idea: Cryogenic quantum-computer controllers can use SrTiO3, whose permittivity climbs to ~1e4 near 4 K because quantum fluctuations suppress ferroelectric order, giving tens of fF in a planar 0.01 um2 cell. The generalizable version strain-tunes SrTiO3/KTaO3 superlattices on scandate-like buffers so the incipient-ferroelectric permittivity peak sits at 300-350 K, targeting k~300-1000.
why: Beats the k~70 requirement of fact 1 by 5-100x so the 60-75:1 pillar collapses to a planar stack; dead-layer and leakage control in sub-10 nm films is the hard part.
note: Room-temperature k peak via strain is plausible, but thin-film dead layers and leakage cut k sharply.

title: FD-SOI back-plane island stores bit beneath buried oxide
idea: Space-grade FD-SOI already sits on a thin buried oxide; one implant mask forms isolated doped islands in the handle wafer under each transistor, and charge injected into an island shifts the front channel threshold through the 20 nm BOX like a back gate. The BOX shields the island from front-side transient strikes and front junction leakage.
why: Capacitorless gain-type cell at ~4-6F2 with ~10x the retention of floating-body cells (facts 1, 3), on existing FD-SOI lines including U.S. capacity, for one mask.

title: Venus-lander vacuum nanogap field-emission access switch
idea: Vacuum electronics are the switches that survive Venus' 460 C surface; build each access device as a vertical ~10 nm sealed vacuum gap with a sharp emitter on the storage-node side and a gate ring, so electrons cross by field emission only when the wordline raises the tip field. Off, there is no channel, junction or trap to leak through.
why: Fact 3: junction and subthreshold leakage are gone (only exponentially suppressed Fowler-Nordheim tunneling remains), giving near-static, temperature-immune retention; hermetic nanogap sealing and emitter wear are the risks.

title: RFID-cheap transistorless crosspoint capacitors with MIIM tunnel selectors
idea: Penny RFID tags use two-terminal tunnel structures. Replace the access transistor with a back-to-back metal-insulator-insulator-metal tunnel selector (~1e6-1e8 I-V nonlinearity) in a 4F^2 crosspoint of stacked capacitors; half-selected cells leak and disturb, giving ~1% raw BER that page coding absorbs.
why: Facts 2 and 4: no transistor means no lateral-transistor blocker for 3D and no EUV access layer, with 4F^2 stacked tiers for 2-4x density per mask; refresh is frequent, so it fits streaming and ephemeral data.

title: SPAD-style avalanche first stage turns electrons into digital pulses
idea: LIDAR single-photon detectors get enormous gain from impact ionization; the SA first stage is an impact-ionization MOSFET biased just below breakdown, so a stored '1' (~1000 electrons) triggers a self-sustaining avalanche that is quenched and reset like a SPAD, while a '0' does not.
why: Gain ~1000x lets ~0.2 fF cells be sensed (fact 1); risks are dark-count false triggers and hot-carrier wear.

title: Downhole-200C Ga2O3 vertical gain-cell tiers become refresh-free at room temperature
idea: Design the cell for a 200 C oil-well logging tool: a capacitor-less 2T gain cell whose write and read transistors are vertical beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV bandgap) pillars at 4F2, stacked 8-16 tiers over CMOS by low-temperature ALD. A cell qualified to hold charge 10 ms at 200 C holds it for many minutes at 85 C, so the same array ships to datacenters with refresh essentially gone.
why: Attacks the leakage tail and refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor wall (fact 1); recovers 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth, and 4F2 vertical stacking gives ~3-8x bits per mm2.
note: Low-temp ALD Ga2O3 is amorphous, poor mobility; IGZO already gives long retention.

title: Two-mask-per-tier self-aligned crosspoint gain cell for $1 IoT
idea: A $1 IoT chip cannot afford 30 masks, so define every memory tier with exactly two orthogonal line masks, as in crosspoint memory: line set A forms the write wordline plus storage gate, line set B forms the bitline plus vertical channel, and a 2T gain cell self-aligns at every crossing. All tiers reuse the same two masks.
why: Mask count and capital (fact 4): 2 masks per tier instead of 5-7 EUV layers, 4F2 per crossing, ~2-3x lower cost per bit at mature nodes, and memory buildable in the BEOL over a cheap MCU.
note: Self-aligning write, read and storage of a 2T cell with only two line masks is very constrained.

title: MLCC-style nanolaminate storage capacitor with interdigitated ALD electrodes
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitors get high capacitance cheaply from hundreds of interleaved electrodes; build each DRAM storage node as an ALD nanolaminate of 6-10 alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers (nitrogen purge, no sputtering) in a lateral cavity, contacting odd electrodes on one side and even electrodes on the other by selective wet recess. Capacitance scales with layer count instead of aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~3-5x Cs per footprint without AR 115 or k 70, sized for lateral 3D DRAM tiers (fact 2).

title: Radiation-detector diamond: carbon access transistors with near-zero leakage
idea: Particle-physics and implant users rely on CVD diamond because its 5.5 eV bandgap gives essentially no leakage. Build hydrogen-terminated diamond surface-channel FETs with ALD Al2O3 passivation as DRAM access devices, on polycrystalline diamond grown in a university microwave-plasma CVD reactor.
why: Carbon from methane is unlimited; diamond access devices could cut the 13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) by >1000x and end refresh. Mobility, stability and integration are high risk.
note: H-terminated diamond stability and Si integration are miracles.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium electrode inside every storage pillar
idea: Scale shift from battery-electrode science to the cell: deposit a Ru-Al alloy liner in the hole, selectively etch the Al to leave a 3-5 nm ligament nanosponge, then coat with ALD high-k and top electrode so one pillar has 3-5x internal surface area.
why: Capacitor wall: 3-5x Cs at the same footprint or same Cs at AR ~20:1, removing the hardest etch step.
note: No room to coat 3-5 nm ligaments with dielectric plus electrode inside a ~20 nm hole.

title: 2D tunnel-diode bistable latch stacked in BEOL
idea: Shift the Goto-pair latch from III-V wafers to atomic layers: two WSe2/SnSe2 band-to-band tunnel diodes in series form a bistable node with negative differential resistance, plus one oxide access transistor, all in BEOL tiers.
why: 3D density: no capacitor, standby current in the pA range, stackable 10+ tiers over logic.

title: Global pulse self-restore: whole-die refresh in one nanosecond broadcast
idea: Time shift from serial row-by-row refresh (8k REF commands per 64 ms) to one die-wide pulse: each cell adds a tiny gain transistor gated by its own storage node, with its drain on a shared 'restore' mesh; pulsing the mesh to VARY for ~2 ns tops up every node still reading '1' (gain device on) and leaves '0' nodes untouched, with no wordline, bitline or sense-amp activity.
why: Refresh bandwidth loss (10-20%, fact 3) goes to ~0 and refresh energy falls ~20-50x because only cell charge moves, not bitlines; the 2T cell costs ~40% area, offset if it relaxes capacitor targets (fact 1).
note: As described, a node-gated device sourcing into its own node cannot restore above Vnode-Vt; needs a boosted gate.

title: Silicon NEMS relay as access switch: an air gap never leaks
idea: Scale jump from the telephone relay to a 60 nm silicon beam: each cell's access device is a doubly clamped Si beam pulled onto a TiN contact by the wordline's electrostatic force; when released, a ~5 nm gap gives effectively zero off-current, so retention is limited only by the capacitor dielectric.
why: Leakage/refresh (fact 3): channel leakage vanishes and refresh intervals stretch to seconds-minutes; switching ~1-5 ns at this scale; the risk is stiction and >1e15-cycle contact endurance; materials Si, Ti, N only.
note: Needs ~1e15 contact cycles; relays demonstrated far below that.

title: NEMS contact-switch access device with true zero off-current
idea: Scale jump from MEMS relays to ~20 nm: the access transistor is replaced by a nano-electromechanical contact switch with a vacuum gap when off, so the storage node leaks only through the capacitor dielectric and surfaces, giving hours of retention; refresh is omitted and data idle longer moves to NV.
why: Removes the subthreshold/GIDL leakage tail (fact 3) entirely -> zero refresh; contact wear and ~ns pull-in are the risks.

title: Anodic alumina nanopores template 40-nm-pitch vertical transistors
idea: Let self-ordering electrochemistry pattern below the litho scale: anodize an aluminum film so hexagonally ordered pores form at ~40-60 nm pitch, set by the anodizing voltage. Coat the pores by atomic-layer epitaxy with gate dielectric and a semiconductor channel to make vertical surrounding-gate transistors; 180-nm litho only defines mat boundaries and straps.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4): 4F2-like density at an effective F of ~25 nm without any stepper below 180 nm.
note: Gate electrode placement inside alumina and addressing an unregistered hex lattice are unsolved.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers from dopant-contrast silicon superlattices
idea: Instead of Si/SiGe stacks (germanium is ~60%+ China-controlled), grow alternating p++ boron-doped and intrinsic Si tiers in one low-temperature epi run. Anodization porosifies only the p++ layers, which are then oxidized into tier isolation. Scale shift: atom-level dopant contrast replaces alloy contrast to define 26+ tiers.
why: Removes germanium supply risk and the Si/SiGe critical-thickness strain limit on tier count, potentially allowing 50+ lattice-matched tiers for 3D DRAM.
note: Dopant-contrast superlattice avoids Ge; dopant diffusion over 26+ tiers and porous-Si control are doubts.

title: Atom-precise probe master cloned through a template family tree
idea: Time shift: spend weeks writing one perfect master array by parallel scanning-probe hydrogen-depassivation lithography on U.S.-built tools, then clone it through generations of imprint templates (1 -> 100 -> 10,000) so the slow atomic write is amortized over millions of wafers.
why: Sub-10 nm array templates without EUV; master cost falls below ~$0.01 per wafer.
note: Hydrogen-depassivation litho writes um2 areas slowly; a full-reticle master looks impractical.

title: Bioreactor-grown protein crystals as nanoscale etch masks
idea: Jump from fermentation tank to wafer: bacterial S-layer proteins grown in U.S. biomanufacturing plants recrystallize on the wafer as 2D lattices with 10-25 nm periodicity, and metal infiltration hardens them into a mask for the capacitor or contact lattice.
why: A litho-free 10-25 nm periodic template at ag-biotech cost (cents per wafer) removes EUV from 1-2 array layers.

title: Charge-pump-free single-rail stack frees power TSVs and periphery
idea: Collapse the die's multi-rail scheme into one package-level ~0.7 V rail: the ~3 V wordline boost and 1 V array rail go away, and the resulting ~1% sensing and leakage errors from weaker access transistors are absorbed by the code. Without VPP pumps and extra regulators the stack needs far fewer power TSVs.
why: Attacks the voltage floor (fact 10, ~2x CV2), periphery (fact 7, pumps and regulators) and TSV area (fact 6, power TSVs are often the majority).
note: Without VPP boost cells cannot write full level; 1% raw errors too heavy.

title: Bubble memory without the shift register: one garnet bubble per cell
idea: Magnetic bubble memory died from serial millisecond access and external rotating-field coils. Pattern ~40 nm insulating TmIG garnet dots under a Pt strip: a spin-orbit-torque pulse nucleates or annihilates one bubble domain in place, and spin-Hall magnetoresistance in the same Pt reads it, so nothing moves and no tunnel barrier exists to wear out.
why: Random access in ~10 ns, nonvolatile (zero refresh), no barrier breakdown so endurance is not oxide-limited; insulating magnet means no electromigration. Risk: small SMR read signal.
note: Spin-Hall magnetoresistance read signal (~1e-4) is far too small for fast sensing.

title: ZettaCore molecules as built-in tunnel barrier and capacitor
idea: ZettaCore's porphyrin charge-storage molecules died on electrolyte integration and temperature limits. Covalently anchor ferrocene or porphyrin redox molecules to a TiN nanopillar through a rigid alkyl tether of chosen length, inside a solid polymer electrolyte. The tether's tunneling distance sets the self-discharge time, each CH2 unit multiplying it ~3x, so the molecular layer is both a multi-electron capacitor and its own leak-limiting access barrier.
why: Redox monolayers hold ~1e14 e/cm2, beating the MIM capacitor charge wall, and retention can be tuned from seconds to minutes by tether length. Speculative mainly because of write speed.
note: ZettaCore failed on this; ns writes with ionic counter-charge unlikely.

title: Second-harmonic polarization read makes FeRAM non-destructive
idea: Failure mined: Ramtron FeRAM's read switched the ferroelectric, causing fatigue and imprint and forcing a write-back on every read. Fix: apply a sub-coercive sine (~0.2 Vc) and detect the phase of the second harmonic of the displacement current with a phase-sensitive sense amp. The nonlinear permittivity is asymmetric, so the harmonic's sign follows the polarization direction without switching it.
why: Removes destructive read and restore energy (fact 8, ~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and read-induced fatigue, pushing ferroelectric cells toward unlimited read endurance.
note: Nonlinear-dielectric (SNDM) read is known; harmonic signal at cell scale and ns is tiny.

title: Transient negative capacitance cancels bitline load only during sensing
idea: Failure mined: negative-capacitance FETs flopped because NC turned out to be hysteretic and stable only transiently. Fix: transient is all sensing needs. A thin HZO NC capacitor is switched in series with the bitline only for the ~3 ns charge-share window to partly cancel bitline capacitance, then disconnected before hysteresis matters.
why: The charge-share signal dV = Q/(Cs+Cbl,eff) grows ~2-4x, allowing ~2-3x smaller cell capacitors or 2x longer bitlines (half the SAs).

title: DSA arrays made defect-tolerant by sense-amp-level remapping
idea: Failure mined: directed self-assembly lithography died in high-volume manufacturing because it could not pattern irregular periphery or hit the ~0.01/cm^2 defect target. Fix: once periphery moves to a bonded logic wafer, the array wafer is purely periodic, which is what block copolymers do well. Each sense-amp group carries a remap table filled at test, so DSA defects (~1/cm^2) are mapped out like bad columns.
why: 10x at the same cost: block copolymers at ~7 nm half-pitch with no EUV give (12/7)^2 = ~3x density, x1.9 from an all-array wafer, x1.5 from regular 4F^2 vertical-channel cells, ~9-10x at lower capital.
note: Capacitor, not litho, limits cell scaling; DSA defectivity far above 1/cm^2.

title: Hitachi PLEDM revived: h-BN barrier write transistor stacked on read gate
idea: Hitachi's 1990s PLEDM gain cell stacked a vertical multi-tunnel-barrier write transistor on the read transistor's gate, but died on leakage variability in its Si/SiN barriers. Rebuild the stacked write device with atomically uniform h-BN tunnel barriers so the storage node (the read gate) leaks below 1 aA. The result is a two-transistor gain cell in a one-transistor footprint.
why: No capacitor (fact 1), non-destructive read (fact 8), and retention long enough to cut refresh ~100x (fact 3), at ~4F2.

title: Optane rebuilt from abundant elements: one-film sulfide self-selecting crosspoint
idea: 3D XPoint died on cost: roughly a dozen distinct films per deck (As-Ge-Se OTS selector, GST phase-change layer, carbon electrodes, W lines) made at tiny volume. Fix exactly that by collapsing selector plus storage into one As-free, Te-free sulfur-rich Sn-Al-S chalcogenide glass whose polarity-dependent threshold voltage is the bit (self-selecting memory, no melt-quench), between Mo lines, so a deck is three films.
why: Removes arsenic, germanium (China ~60%) and tellurium (copper-refining by-product) plus ~9 depositions per deck; no melting lifts endurance toward 1e10+ and cuts write energy; est. 40-50% lower cost per bit than Optane on cost and scarce-resource axes.
note: Self-selecting memory known (Micron); new sulfide composition's threshold window and endurance unknown.

title: Cavendish MEMS memory fixed: contactless bistable buckled nanobeams on glass
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory pivoted to RF because contacting cantilevers stuck and wore out. Make the bit the buckling direction of a pre-stressed, doubly clamped SiN or amorphous-carbon nanobeam that never touches anything: a coincident row/column electrostatic pulse snaps it through, and a sense electrode ~50 nm away reads it capacitively.
why: No transistor, no Hf/Zr dielectric and zero leakage in the cell, so no refresh; non-contact flexures survive >1e15 cycles; ~10-100 ns snap-through for ~1 um beams; built from sputtered films on glass.

title: IBM racetrack fixed with grain-free amorphous iron-boron wires on glass
idea: IBM's racetrack memory stalled because domain walls pinned on edge roughness and grain boundaries, and stacks needed Pt/Co/Ni multilayers. Sputter amorphous Fe80B20 (metglas chemistry, no grains) nanowires on fusion-drawn display glass with sub-0.3 nm roughness, shift in-plane walls by spin-transfer current pulses, and read at one end of each wire.
why: Stores 10-100 bits per access device, cutting transistors and periphery per bit; no Co, Pt, Ir or Ru; Fe and B are abundant; nonvolatile, so no refresh; shift latency suits streaming tiers.

title: Bubble memory without garnet: field-driven skyrmion loops on glass
idea: Magnetic bubble memory (Intel Magnetics, TI) died on costly gadolinium gallium garnet substrates, bias magnets and slow propagation. Sputter Pt/Co/Ta skyrmion multilayers on glass or Si, keep bubble memory's global rotating in-plane field from a package coil to move every bit at once with no per-track drivers, and define tracks with one coarse imprint and one shared magnetoresistive sensor per major loop.
why: Meets 100x: no garnet and no per-bit transistor, just a film plus one pattern; est. ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades: us-level serial access, coil power.

title: Proton-doped nickelate bit: electron filling flips resistance a millionfold
idea: Effect walk: ion migration driving a Mott transition. A 10-nm SmNiO3 channel exchanges H+ with an adjacent nanometre proton reservoir; each inserted proton donates an electron that localizes on Ni (Ni3+ to Ni2+), turning the metal into a strongly correlated insulator with up to ~10^6 resistance change, read at ~50 mV.
why: Holds state without refresh (fact 3) and the enormous read margin removes full sense-amp restore (fact 8); a vertical 4F2 BEOL stack with no capacitor; proton endurance (>10^12 cycles needed) and ns kinetics are the open risks.

title: Chiral molecules write magnets with mere capacitor charging current
idea: Effect walk: chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS). A monolayer of helical peptides or chiral perovskite between a gate and a 1-nm Co free layer injects spin-polarized displacement current while the capacitor charges, transferring enough angular momentum to flip magnetization with no DC current; TMR reads it.
why: Write energy is only the charging energy of an aF capacitor (~aJ), 10-1000x below fJ-class DRAM or STT writes; speculative because CISS magnitudes and timescales are disputed.
note: CISS magnetization switching reported but magnitude disputed.

title: Vacuum-nanogap field-emission access device with gated emitter pair
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission into vacuum. A sealed 10 nm vacuum gap sits between the bitline contact and the storage node with sharp emitter tips on both sides (for both write polarities) and a ring wordline gate around the gap; the gate raises tip fields above ~3 V/nm only during access, while at rest a ~4 eV work-function barrier conducts nothing measurable.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): no semiconductor channel means no GIDL, junction or trap-assisted tails; retention bounded by capacitor dielectric; radiation-hard bonus.

title: Graphene-silicon barristor access with gate-tuned Schottky barrier height
idea: Effect: thermionic emission over a gate-tunable Schottky barrier. The storage node contacts silicon through a graphene electrode whose low density of states lets the wordline shift its work function ~0.5 eV: barrier ~0.9 eV in hold (thermionic current ~aA), ~0.4 eV during access.
why: Leakage and 3D (facts 2, 3, 4): leakage set by barrier height exponentially, not by a 12 nm channel's slope; vertical junction is litho-light and stackable.

title: Diffusive silver-filament selector blocks access transistor subthreshold leakage
idea: Effect: electrochemical ion migration with spontaneous filament dissolution. A 3 nm SiOxNy:Ag layer in the storage-node contact forms a filament within ns when the open access transistor applies 0.5-1 V across it, then self-dissolves within ~1 us after the wordline closes, leaving an insulating gap (<1 aA) in series with the transistor's leakage tail.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): series ion gap claims 100x retention. Risk: 1e15 endurance and post-write dissolution window.
note: Diffusive Ag selectors fall far short of 1e15 endurance.

title: Crested tunnel barrier serves as two-terminal field-switched access
idea: Effect: field-sensitive tunneling through a crested (peaked) barrier. A Si3N4/AlN/Si3N4-type trilayer replaces the access channel; high bias pulls the central peak down (current rises ~10^12 over a 3x voltage change) so the node writes in ns at +/-3 V but leaks <1 aA at the +/-0.5 V hold and half-select bias.
why: 3D and leakage (facts 2, 3): two-terminal vertical stack layers into tiers without a lateral transistor; claims >=10 s retention. Risk: barrier wear and disturb.
note: Crested barriers (Likharev) as DRAM access; half-select disturb and barrier wear unproven.

title: Image-sensor floating-diffusion readout replaces charge sharing with full transfer
idea: Effect: complete charge transfer onto a tiny node (the CMOS image-sensor 4T pixel principle). Every 16 cells share a ~0.3 fF floating diffusion behind a transfer gate and a one-transistor source follower; the cell charge is dumped fully onto the tiny node instead of being shared with a ~50 fF bitline. The follower drives the bitline as a voltage, and correlated double sampling removes kTC reset noise.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): signal per electron rises ~30x, so Cs could drop to ~1 fF (AR ~15:1), removing high-AR capacitor steps.
note: 16 transfer gates load the FD well above 0.3 fF.

title: NbO2 Mott-selector over BEOL capacitor for 4F2 cross-point DRAM
idea: Mott insulator-metal transition: a doped NbO2 threshold-switch film is stacked directly on a BEOL MIM capacitor at each wordline/bitline crossing. Only the fully selected cell exceeds the ~1 V Mott threshold and charges; half-selected cells stay insulating. This gives a transistor-free 1S1C cell that can be repeated in 4-8 BEOL tiers over CMOS periphery.
why: Gives 4F2 per tier with no crystalline access transistor (facts 2 and 4); claim 4-8x bits per wafer area. The risk is off-state leakage, which needs a doping-engineered Mott gap.
note: NbO2 off-current is ~5 orders too high for capacitor retention.

title: Air-gap NEMS contact switch as zero-leakage 3D access device
idea: Electrostatic pull-in: in each tier, a laterally actuated Ru/TiN nanobeam, released from a sacrificial layer, replaces the lateral access transistor. In the off state a vacuum gap sits in series with the capacitor, so there is no subthreshold leakage tail at all.
why: Removes the ≤13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3); claim retention set only by dielectric leakage (minutes), so refresh energy falls ~90%. Contact endurance near 1e15 cycles is the big risk.

title: Dielectrophoretic placement of single-crystal nanowires as tier access transistors
idea: Dielectrophoresis: single-crystal Si nanowires are grown off-wafer, suspended in fluid, and pulled by an AC field into electrode gaps in every BEOL tier. Each tier gets crystalline lateral access transistors at <400 C without per-tier epitaxy.
why: Solves the missing lateral transistor in 3D DRAM (fact 2); claim crystalline mobility and low leakage in every tier with a cheap, low-temperature process.
note: DEP placement cannot reach DRAM pitch and yield over billions of sites per tier.

title: Straintronic nanomagnets switched by a shared piezo wordline film
idea: Magnetostriction: each non-volatile bit is a FeGa or Co nanomagnet sitting on an AlScN piezo film that forms the wordline. A voltage pulse on the film strains the row's magnets past their anisotropy barrier, a bitline bias picks which magnets flip, and an MTJ reads the state. No write current flows.
why: Attacks energy per bit and the voltage floor (fact 10) for non-volatile tiers; claim ~1-10 aJ writes, 100x below STT-MRAM, and stackable BEOL tiers.
note: Strain gives 90-degree rotation; deterministic low-error 180-degree switching remains unsolved.

title: Snap-through bistable buckled nanobeams in released tier cavities
idea: Euler buckling bistability: compressively stressed SiN/TiN nanobeams, released in cavities in each tier, rest bowed up or down. Electrostatic electrodes snap a beam between its two states without any contact, and capacitive sensing reads the position. Zero standby power, and no stiction or contact wear.
why: Gives non-volatile, leakage-free stacked bits with no refresh (fact 3) and no exotic materials; claim fJ-scale snap energy and high endurance because there is no contact.

title: Alpha-In2Se3 ferroelectric-semiconductor channel tiers stacked by the dozen
idea: Interlocked in-plane and out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization: atomically thin α-In2Se3 is both the channel and the ferroelectric. Gate pulses flip its polarization, which non-volatilely shifts channel conduction, and its ~1 nm thickness allows dozens of vdW tiers in vertical strings.
why: Gives a thin non-volatile 3D cell with no capacitor (facts 1 and 2); claim tier pitch <15 nm and 30+ tiers.
note: alpha-In2Se3 FeS-FETs are widely studied; endurance far from DRAM-class.

title: Strain-switched iron-aluminum nanomagnets on AlN, magnetoelectric memory
idea: Effect: inverse magnetostriction. A voltage across a sputtered AlN piezo layer strains an Fe-Al (Alfenol) nanomagnet and rotates its easy axis to toggle the bit for ~1 fJ, read through MgO tunnel magnetoresistance. Avoids Ga (Galfenol), Sc (ScAlN), Co, and the Pt/Ir/Ru of SOT and pinning stacks.
why: Energy per bit (voltage floor, fact 10) and scarce-element intensity: ~100x lower write energy than STT-MRAM, using abundant Fe, Al and N.
note: AlN d31 is small; reaching ~1e-3 strain at low voltage under substrate clamping is doubtful.

title: Euler-buckled silicon-nitride nanobeams store bits as snap-through states
idea: Effect: Euler buckling bistability. A PECVD SiN beam deposited at 300 C with built-in compressive stress buckles up or down, two states separated by a barrier much larger than kT. Electrostatic electrodes snap it through in ~10 ns (GHz-class stiffness at sub-um length), and capacitive sensing reads its position; tiers stack in BEOL.
why: Refresh and capacitor walls (no stored charge to leak), using only Si, N and Al; density comes from stacking tiers rather than from EUV.

title: Piezoelectric AlN nano-relays give zero-leakage access and end refresh
idea: Effect: the converse piezoelectric effect. A c-axis AlN bimorph sputtered at 300 C bends to close a Mo/TiN nano-contact, so the access device is a mechanical switch with an air-gap off-state and exactly zero subthreshold leakage. Retention is limited only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours).
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) largely gone; AlN needs no scandium, no Si channel and no thermal budget above 400 C.

title: Cu2O and SnO p-channel oxides put full CMOS periphery above arrays
idea: Effect: dispersive hole bands, from Cu 3d-O 2p hybridization in Cu2O and Sn 5s lone-pair mixing in SnO, give 1-5 cm2/Vs hole mobility. Sputtered at <=300 C and paired with n-type ZTO, they make complementary oxide decoders and drivers stacked over the array instead of beside it.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): die area ~-35% and bits per wafer ~+50%, so less single-crystal Si (quartz, poly) per bit; Cu and Sn are abundant.

title: Electrophoretic BaTiO3 nanocube monolayers form high-k capacitors cold
idea: Effect: electrophoresis plus size-dependent permittivity. 15 nm BaTiO3 nanocubes, already crystallized by hydrothermal synthesis at ~200 C, drift under DC bias into trenches or pores and pack face to face. An ALD AlOx infill at 250 C seals pinholes, giving k ~100-300 with no 700 C perovskite anneal.
why: Hf/Zr-free route to the k~70 the capacitor wall needs (fact 1); Ba and Ti are widely sourced; nothing exceeds 250 C.
note: 15 nm BaTiO3 loses permittivity and low-k AlOx infill in series dominates; cubes barely fit DRAM-scale pores.

title: Mott-selector stacked capacitor arrays built on idle 200 mm lines
idea: NbO2 threshold switches (Joule-triggered insulator-metal transition) serve as access devices in a 1S1C crosspoint of MIM capacitors stacked 8-16 tiers with blanket depositions and spacer pitch-quadrupling. That lets 200 mm fabs with 130 nm tools build CXL-expansion memory where cost per bit beats raw density.
why: Pulls mothballed 200 mm capacity into the memory supply with no single-crystal transistor per tier.
note: NbO2 off-state leakage far too high for capacitor retention.

title: Si: anodized mesoporous-silicon storage node multiplies capacitor area
idea: Electrochemically anodize a 1-2 um silicon layer under the array into 5-10 nm mesopores, then ALD-coat TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each storage node is a sponge instead of one etched pillar; a 30x30 nm footprint captures ~10-30 pores and ~20-50x its planar area.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): reaches 5+ fF without a 60-75:1 plasma etch, removing the hardest etch/deposition steps; per-cell pore-count variation is the main risk.
note: 5-10 nm pores cannot fit a TiN/ZrO2/TiN stack; pore-count variance per cell.

title: Sn: SnS in-plane ferroelectric sheet stores bit as rectification direction
idea: Use few-layer SnS (abundant Sn and S), whose ferroelectric polarization lies in the sheet plane, between two lateral electrodes; the polarization direction makes one Schottky contact lower than the other so the junction rectifies left or right, read non-destructively with a small bias.
why: Non-volatile, capacitor-free bit in a 2D sheet that can be laminated into many 3D tiers (fact 2) without vertical capacitors; switching speed and SnS air stability are open.

title: Ti: adhesion-latched TiN nanorelay holds bit by van der Waals
idea: A 10 nm TiN cantilever is pulled into contact with the storage pad and held by surface adhesion with no power, then released by a reverse-polarity pull-off pulse; the ~1% of cells that stay stuck or fail to latch per scrub interval are treated as erasures by the code.
why: Zero-leakage, refresh-free bit (fact 3) from CMOS-standard TiN, where stiction, the classic NEMS killer, is used as the latch and its failures are budgeted instead of engineered out.

title: C: ten-fullerene cluster charge bit sensed through a silicon nanowire
idea: Self-assemble ~10 C60 molecules per cell on a thin tunnel oxide over a silicon nanowire; each fullerene accepts one electron at a sharp LUMO level and the bit is the collective threshold shift; with only ~10 electrons per bit, shot noise and molecular dropouts give ~1% errors that the code absorbs.
why: The storage node shrinks to ~5 nm with molecule-defined, identical charge levels, far below a 6F² capacitor (facts 1, 4); carbon comes from soot-derived fullerenes.
note: ~10-electron bits over tunnel oxide: retention and 1% raw error are severe.

title: Antimony delta-doped tunnel diodes make a bistable, refresh-free storage node
idea: Sb: grow series pairs of Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (Sb and B delta-doped layers) epitaxially on each storage node; their negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages held by a ~pA sustain current, so the node self-restores, and every critical dimension is an epitaxial thickness.
why: Replaces periodic refresh (fact 3) with a static hold of ~4 mW/GB at 1 pA/cell; device dimensions come from epitaxy, so no EUV is needed (fact 4).

title: B: boron-doped avalanche junction as Geiger-mode bitline gain stage
idea: Place a tiny B/P-implanted p+n junction on each sense node, biased just below breakdown; the cell's few-thousand-electron surplus tips it into a self-sustaining avalanche (SPAD-style) that produces a rail-to-rail pulse, and an active quench transistor resets it in ~1 ns.
why: Gives digital-level output from a ~5 fF cell without a matched cross-coupled latch, potentially allowing Cs of 1-2 fF (fact 1) and smaller SAs (fact 7); risks are dark-count false triggers and breakdown drift with temperature.

title: Calcium fluoride and silicon epitaxial superlattice yields insulated crystalline tiers
idea: Exploit CaF2's 0.6% lattice match to Si to grow Si/CaF2 epitaxial superlattices by MBE or low-temperature CVD, so every Si layer is a single-crystal device tier and every CaF2 layer (12 eV gap) is a built-in insulator that can also be recessed selectively to open capacitor cavities.
why: One-pass growth of crystalline SOI-like tiers with no bonding and no germanium (fact 2), from abundant Ca and F; CaF2 doubles as isolation and sacrificial layer.

title: Strontium-calcium titanate superlattice gives k near 200 inside tiers
idea: Grow ALD SrTiO3/CaTiO3 nanolaminates with 1-2 nm periods whose interfacial strain stabilizes a high-k paraelectric state at ~8 nm thickness (k ~150-250) on TiN, crystallized by millisecond flash anneal; a lateral cylinder ~150 nm long inside a 40 nm tier then stores ~5 fF.
why: Meets the charge wall (fact 1) with a short lateral capacitor that fits one tier, making lateral 3D cells viable (fact 2) without Ru electrodes; Ca is abundant and Sr moderately available.
note: STO-type dielectrics lose k sharply below ~10 nm (dead layer); k~200 at 8 nm on TiN is doubtful.

title: N: silicon-nitride linear-drive optics extend DDR5 slots off-board
idea: Insert a linear, non-retimed optical extender at each DDR5 socket: Si3N4/SiP modulators driven directly by the DQ/DQS analog waveforms and photodiodes at a remote liquid-cooled DIMM tray 0.3-1 m away, with the host's existing read/write leveling absorbing the extra ~3-5 ns flight time.
why: Capacity per socket and data movement with interface unchanged: DIMMs leave the crowded board, allowing 2-4x more DIMMs per CPU and better cooling, at ~2-4 pJ/bit added.
note: Bidirectional multi-drop DDR5 signalling is hard to carry linearly over optics.

title: Si: DLP micromirror fabs build bistable nano-cantilever memory
idea: Scale the digital-micromirror MEMS process (Al hinges proven beyond 10^12 cycles) down to sub-100 nm Si/Al cantilevers that latch against contacts by adhesion and are read capacitively.
why: Reuses existing U.S. MEMS fabs with no new materials; zero standby power, no leakage tail, radiation hard.
note: Stiction latching reliability and >1e15 cycles at sub-100 nm are unproven.

title: Cr: Chromia magnetoelectric memory written by voltage, not current
idea: Boron-doped Cr2O3 films (Neel temperature raised above 400 K) flip their boundary magnetization with an electric field plus small bias field, read by anomalous Hall in an adjacent Fe layer.
why: Voltage writes cost ~100x less energy than STT; chromium is abundant and recyclable from stainless steel.

title: Ni: Electroplated permalloy racetrack memory from HDD write-pole plating lines
idea: Electroplate NiFe nanowires into deep trenches like HDD write poles to form vertical racetrack shift registers holding 10-100 domain-wall bits read by one sensor at the top.
why: Electroplating costs ~1/10 the capex of vacuum deposition and gives many non-volatile bits per footprint.

title: Seed-pulled single-crystal SrTiO3 capacitor via lateral epitaxial overgrowth
idea: Borrow Czochralski seeding. Open a window to a single-crystal SrRuO3 seed and grow SrTiO3 laterally over the bottom electrode as one crystal, the way GaN is overgrown laterally, instead of as a fine-grained film. Removing grain boundaries removes leakage paths and suppresses the dead layer that holds polycrystalline STO to k~100.
why: Fact 1: k of ~250-300 in 8 nm films is 5-6x today's ZrO2. Capacitor AR could drop from ~70:1 to ~15:1.
note: Epitaxy temperatures and 3D geometry clash with the DRAM flow.

title: Bead-strung vortex cores: nanoring magnets threaded on vertical wires
idea: Revive hand-strung core memory: deposit ~40 nm permalloy nanorings as 'beads' around vertical metal pillar 'strings'. Pillar current writes clockwise or counterclockwise vortex chirality by Oersted field, and the flux-closed rings have no stray field, so 4-8 can stack on one pillar and be read through a ring-segment MTJ.
why: Fact 2: multi-bit vertical stacking on a single pillar with no per-bit transistor. Zero stray field packs bits densely, with unlimited endurance.
note: One pillar current writes all rings alike; selective write and per-ring read contacts unsolved.

title: MLCC-in-a-pillar: tape-cast style Ni/BaTiO3 multilayer cell capacitor
idea: Shrink multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) manufacturing into each cell. A pillar holds 20 alternating Ni/BaTiO3 5 nm layers, like co-fired MLCC sheets, with odd layers recessed on one sidewall and even layers on the other, so a storage-node contact and a plate contact each reach every other electrode.
why: Fact 1: 6 fF from a pillar of AR ~7 instead of 70, using only Ni, Ba, Ti and O. MLCC makers already co-process Ni/BaTiO3 at enormous volume.
note: Echoes 1988 fin-stacked capacitors; 5 nm BaTiO3 dead layer and alternate-layer contacts are hard.

title: Preform-drawn coax capacitor wafers: draw, bundle, redraw, then slice
idea: Borrow optical-fiber drawing. Build a macroscopic preform (Zn-Sn alloy core, BaTiO3-loaded glass dielectric, metal outer shell), then thermally draw, stack and redraw it down to ~30 nm cores. Wafer-thin slices of the bundle carry billions of parallel coax capacitors, which are hybrid-bonded onto the transistor wafer.
why: Fact 1 and capital intensity: capacitor length equals slice thickness (um), not an etched hole, so each coax exceeds 5 fF with no litho or etch. A draw tower replaces a fab for the capacitor wafer.

title: Bimetallic-strip negative-capacitance capacitor: ferroelectric AlBN fights linear Al2O3
idea: A thermostat's bimetallic strip pairs two opposing layers to get a new behavior. Here a wurtzite ferroelectric Al(1-x)B(x)N layer sits in series with Al2O3 dielectric, matched so the ferroelectric's negative-capacitance region is stabilized and never switches, lifting total capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.
why: Facts 1 and 10: capacitance rises 2-3x, and the charge gain lets VARY fall toward 0.6 V. Only Al, B, N and O, with no Hf or Zr.
note: NC capacitance boost widely studied in HZO; AlBN's huge coercive field makes stabilization harder.

title: Thermochromic-ink spin-crossover bit: Fe-triazole molecules hold spin state
idea: Borrow thermochromic ink printing: a film of [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)](BF4) spin-crossover complex (Fe, C, H, N, B, F) sits inside its room-temperature thermal hysteresis loop. A ns heat or field pulse flips molecules between high and low spin, and the ~10% volume and dielectric change is read capacitively or through a strain-gated channel.
why: Bistable molecular storage needing no refresh (fact 3), solution-printable from cents of iron and organics. Write energy is the latent heat of a 20 nm dot, ~fJ.
note: Kahn-era SCO memory idea; weak readout and ns thermal switching at 20 nm are unproven.

title: Fermented bacterial S-layer protein crystals as access-pillar etch masks
idea: Ferment bacteria whose surface-layer proteins self-crystallize into 2D lattices with ~10-13 nm period. Harvest and transfer these sheets onto the wafer as hard-mask templates for the vertical access-pillar array.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): replaces 1-2 EUV or multi-patterning steps with a bioreactor. Atomically identical protein pores tighten pillar diameter, so VT and leakage spread narrow and the tail shrinks.
note: S-layer defectivity, 300 mm transfer and registration to wordlines are the doubts.

title: Plumbing check-valve pair: ultra-high-barrier Schottky diodes guard the node
idea: Isolate each metal storage node with two back-to-back high-barrier Schottky rectifiers (e.g., Pt/Ga2O3, ~1.8 eV) to separate write-high and write-low lines, like check valves cast into a pipe tee. Pulsing the line past the barrier fills or drains the node.
why: Zero refresh: thermionic reverse leakage over a 1.8 eV barrier is ~1e-30 A per cell, so retention exceeds the product's life. A two-terminal access device also removes the transistor and simplifies the wordline.
note: Read path undefined; real reverse leakage is defect/tunnel dominated, not ideal thermionic.

title: Laminated-glass hBN floating-graphene bit with sub-ns super-injection
idea: Like safety glass laminated around a PVB interlayer, stack a graphene charge layer between hBN tunnel barriers over a 2D MoS2 channel. Writes use the 2D-enhanced hot-carrier super-injection that reaches sub-ns programming, so the cell is read like a gain cell.
why: Zero refresh: charge behind 6 eV hBN stays for years. The open question is DRAM-class endurance, so the risk is honestly high.
note: Sub-ns 2D flash shown, but tunneling-oxide endurance far short of DRAM-class.

title: Coin-cell nanobattery bit holds voltage as state of charge
idea: Shrink coin-cell battery manufacturing to a solid-state Li-free nanobattery per cell (e.g., proton or Ag+ intercalation electrodes). The bit is its open-circuit voltage, read non-destructively through a gain transistor and written by a short current pulse.
why: Zero refresh: a battery holds its voltage for years by electrochemistry, not by isolating charge. Speed and endurance are the speculative risks.
note: Nanobattery self-discharge, ns writes and 1e15 endurance all unproven.

title: Ink-jet drop-on-demand cells: double-gated access opens one cell only
idea: Like a drop-on-demand print head that fires only the nozzles needed, give each access transistor two gates: a row gate (wordline) and an orthogonal column gate (column-select line). A cell conducts only at the row-AND-column intersection, so a 64-bit burst opens 64 cells and fires 64 SAs instead of 8,192.
why: Removes the 128x overfetch and the restore of untouched cells: ~50-100x less activate energy per useful bit, and row hammer weakens because full rows are never activated.
note: Half-selected dual-gate cells leak; a second gate is hard to fit in 4F2/6F2.

title: Lost-wax gyroid: block-copolymer network cast into capacitor electrodes
idea: Investment-casting analogy: fill each capacitor hole with a gyroid-forming block copolymer, remove one block to leave a ~10 nm-strut 3D network (the wax pattern), ALD-coat TiN over it, burn out the polymer, then coat dielectric and top plate, giving a bicontinuous sponge electrode inside the same hole.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 3-5x surface area at equal aspect ratio, so ~5 fF is reachable at AR ~20:1 instead of 60-75:1, relaxing etch and support-lattice steps (fact 4).
note: Same gyroid-electrode core; even harder inside a sub-40 nm hole.

title: Fermented S-layer protein crystals as sub-10 nm cell masks
idea: Grow bacterial surface-layer (S-layer) proteins by fermentation; they self-crystallize on wafers into 2D lattices of 10-20 nm period, which are metallized or infiltrated into a hard mask that defines vertical-channel or capacitor arrays without EUV.
why: Replaces 5-7 EUV array layers (fact 4) with a bioreactor product costing cents per wafer; defects handled by redundancy mapping; long-range order and registration to periphery are the risk.

title: Intaglio acid-etching: catalytic metal etch carves 115:1 silicon trenches
idea: Printmakers bite intaglio plates with acid only where the ground is scratched away; metal-assisted chemical etching does the same in silicon: a patterned silver mesh sinks straight down in HF/H2O2, carving capacitor holes in a sacrificial silicon mold at >150:1, after which the silver is recovered electrochemically and the mold is oxidized or replaced.
why: Reaches the AR ~115 needed for more Cs without C4F6/C4F8 plasma (PFAS, high GWP) or high-power RF etchers, near room temperature; silver is recycled in a closed loop.

title: Mirror-silvering bath grows rutile capacitor dielectric at 80 C
idea: Tollens' silver-mirror chemistry coats any shape from solution; adapt chemical bath deposition of Al/Nb-co-doped rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) from aqueous titanium peroxo complexes onto a rutile-templating MoO2 electrode, filling 70:1 holes by diffusion instead of vacuum ALD.
why: Reaching k ~70+ breaks the capacitor charge wall without raising aspect ratio, using abundant titanium and molybdenum instead of hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium, in an atmospheric bath with far less energy and precursor waste.
note: Bath-grown rutile with low leakage in 70:1 holes is a big stretch; rutile TiO2 leakage is the known problem.

title: MLCC co-firing on a carrier, then transfer the capacitor layer
idea: MLCC makers fire barium titanate layers at ~1100 C on carriers; fire a sub-100 nm relaxor (Ba,Sr)(Ti,Zr)O3 dielectric between conductive-oxide electrodes on a sacrificial carrier wafer, pattern a shallow 5:1 relief, then hybrid-bond and layer-transfer it onto the cold access-transistor wafer.
why: Decouples perovskite crystallization (k 300-1000) from the CMOS thermal budget, so a shallow capacitor reaches ~5 fF without 70:1 holes or hafnium/zirconium ALD; barium and titanium are abundant.

title: Deli-slicer nanoskiving: film thickness, not lithography, sets line pitch
idea: Deposit a 2,000-pair laminate of alternating Mo/Ru and oxide, each exactly F thick, on a carrier block, then slice perpendicular to the layers into thin sheets whose cross-sections are atomically uniform line/space gratings ~48 um wide (one mat), and transfer the strips as wordline or bitline arrays.
why: Fact 4: replaces SAQP/EUV line patterning (3-4 litho/spacer loops) with deposition-thickness control at about +/-0.2 nm and near-zero line-edge roughness; one block yields thousands of mat strips, tungsten-free.
note: Placing sliced strips with nm overlay across a wafer is the doubt.

title: Jelly-roll winding: strained membranes self-roll into multi-turn capacitors
idea: Borrow Li-ion jelly-roll winding: deposit a planar TiN/high-k/TiN/high-k ribbon on a strained bilayer over a sacrificial film, open one release edge, and let built-in strain roll each ribbon into a 4-6-turn Swiss-roll capacitor lying in a shallow trench.
why: Fact 1: plate area comes from planar ribbon length that cheap litho defines, giving ~4-6x one cylinder's area with no HAR etch.

title: Sewing-needle stack-then-drill one via through all sixteen dies
idea: Bond the thinned dies first, then deep-etch or laser-drill one via through the whole stack, like a needle through layered cloth, and plate it in one pass. Each die only needs a landing ring, not its own TSV module.
why: Removes per-die TSV processing and compound yield loss; claims ~50% lower HBM stacking cost.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous electrode multiplies capacitor area tenfold
idea: IFR: infinite capacitor area in zero footprint. Closest achievable: deposit a binary alloy liner (e.g. Ag-Au or Al-Ti) in the pillar, selectively dissolve one metal to leave a nanoporous sponge electrode with ~5 nm ligaments, then ALD-coat dielectric and top electrode for 5-10x surface area.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF at AR ~20 instead of 60-75; shorter deep etches cut tool time and capital (fact 4).
note: No room for dielectric and top electrode inside 5 nm pores.

title: Roll-to-roll anodized aluminium foil gives 150:1 capacitor pores free
idea: IFR: high-aspect holes that etch themselves. Closest achievable: anodize aluminium foil on a reel so self-ordered alumina pores grow ~20 nm wide and ~3 um deep (AR ~150) with no lithography, then spatial-ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside to form capacitor arrays laminated onto access-device layers.
why: Facts 1 and 4: passes AR 115 with zero EUV and zero plasma etch, on abundant aluminium.
note: AAO pores self-ordered but cannot register to transistor array.

title: Redox molecules as both selector and storage in crossbars
idea: IFR: the bit's own chemistry is the switch. Self-assemble a monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (ferrocene/porphyrin triads with ~0.5 V spaced oxidation potentials) between crossbar electrodes; oxidation stores charge, the discrete redox potentials give built-in threshold selectivity, and an insulating alkyl tether sets retention.
why: Constraint: each layer is a sub-5 nm monolayer between two lines, so 2 bits per site across several stacked crossbar layers targets ~10x density with only deposition and DUV lines.

title: Anodized aluminum foil grows its own capacitor template
idea: IFR: 'the substrate is the capacitor.' Backward: anodize high-purity aluminum foil into self-ordered porous alumina with 200-500:1 pores at ~50-60 nm pitch, remove the pore-bottom barrier so the remaining aluminum base contacts an ALD TiN plate liner, add high-k and a storage-node fill, and build oxide TFT access transistors on top roll-to-roll.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1, 4): capacitor AR >200:1 with no etch tool or lithography on a ~$5/m2 non-chokepoint substrate; cell pitch is ~3x coarser, so multi-level charge must close the density gap.
note: AAO MIM nanocapacitors known; roll-to-roll TFT access density far below DRAM, multi-level not credible.

title: Nanosheet-seeded glass grows high-k oriented perovskite capacitors
idea: IFR: 'k is so high the capacitor can be flat.' Backward: coat alkali-free glass with a Langmuir-Blodgett monolayer of Ca2Nb3O10 nanosheets that template (001)-oriented SrTiO3 or (Ba,Sr)TiO3 growth at <=600 C, giving k~200-300 films that a silicon BEOL cannot host, then stack oxide TFT cells over planar or shallow-trench capacitors.
why: Charge wall (fact 1 needs k~70): ~3-4x that target, so 5 fF fits in a <=10:1 structure and the 60-75:1 etch disappears.

title: Substrate-free van der Waals stack with nanometer-thin memory tiers
idea: IFR: 'each tier is a few molecules thick.' Backward: grow wafer-scale MoS2 channels and hBN dielectrics on reusable sapphire and dry-transfer them tier by tier, so each cell layer (2D channel, hBN, metal gate) is ~5 nm and 100 tiers fit in 0.5 um while the sapphire is reused.
why: 3D tiers and leakage (facts 2, 3): MoS2's ~1.8 eV gap gives very low off-current, and a ~20x thinner tier pitch keeps vertical etches shallow.

title: Remote-epitaxy peel-and-stack single-crystal oxide channel films
idea: IFR: 'every tier has a single-crystal channel and the substrate lasts forever.' Backward: grow single-crystal beta-Ga2O3 or In2O3 channel films by remote epitaxy through a graphene layer on a reusable seed crystal, exfoliate each film, and transfer it as the channel of each 3D tier.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): single-crystal ultra-wide-gap channels remove the grain-boundary leakage tail of deposited oxides; seed reuse removes substrate cost.
note: Remote epi of Ga2O3/In2O3 plus nm-film peel and per-tier transfer at wafer scale is unproven; seed reuse is attractive.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane capacitors replace high-aspect-ratio etching
idea: Ideal: a capacitor that builds its own height. Closest: deposit a strained SiN bilayer carrying a TiN/Al2O3/TiN stack, release a sacrificial layer, and let built-in strain roll it into a 5-10-turn micro-scroll that multiplies electrode area per footprint 20-50x with no 70:1 hole etch.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (Fact 1) without HAR etch (fluorocarbon gases, etch capex) or a k~70 material.
note: Scroll diameter of a ~15 nm MIM stack far exceeds 20-40 nm cell pitch.

title: Catalyst-grown vertical nanowire forests replace etched capacitor pillars
idea: Ideal: capacitor pillars that build themselves upward. Closest: DSA-placed catalyst dots on each storage contact seed vertical vapor-liquid-solid growth of doped-Si nanowires to 1-1.5 um; TiN, high-k and top plate are ALD-wrapped around them, so there is no mold, HAR etch or wet dip-out.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR set by growth time, not etch physics; removes mold deposition, HAR etch and collapse-prone drying; capacitor module step count roughly halved.

title: Nanosecond protonic gain cell stores bits as ions, BEOL-only
idea: Ideal: memory where nothing leaks because the state is atoms, not electrons. Closest: a BEOL transistor whose MoO3 or TiO2 channel conductance is set by nanosecond proton insertion from a thin solid electrolyte (PSG) gate, giving a volatile-to-hours state with non-destructive read; three DUV masks at <400 C, no capacitor.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no capacitor and slow refresh, stackable in BEOL tiers on any logic wafer; tungsten-free channel avoids the W chokepoint.

title: TiO2 crossbars hold recommendation embedding tables with in-array gather
idea: IFR: terabyte embedding tables cost nothing. Closest with abundant elements: Ti/TiO2-x/Ti resistive crossbars (no Hf or Ta oxide) store read-mostly embedding rows rewritten monthly (endurance need ~100 cycles), and an in-array gather-sum pools the looked-up rows before anything crosses to DRAM.
why: Embedding tables dominate recommender DRAM at TB scale; displaces 80-90% of it.

title: Optical weight carousel: one circulating copy feeds sixty-four GPUs
idea: Ideal: model weights exist exactly once in the whole cluster. Closest achievable: stream frozen weights continuously around a WDM fiber loop at ~10 Tb/s so each GPU taps its current layer as it passes, holding only a small double buffer instead of a full weight replica in HBM.
why: Usable supply: 64 data-parallel replicas of a 400 GB model collapse toward one, freeing tens of TB of HBM for KV cache and trading scarce DRAM for cheap fiber and optics.
note: 10 Tb/s loop is far below per-GPU weight bandwidth; 400 GB circulation takes minutes.

title: Volume-holographic weight crystals read by light into compute
idea: Ideal: weights held in a passive crystal and read by a flash of light. Closest achievable: record each layer's weight pages as angle-multiplexed holograms in a photopolymer or LiNbO3 block; a steered laser reconstructs one ~1 Mb page per pulse onto a photodiode array bonded to the accelerator, with no refresh and no electrical storage.
why: Zero refresh and page-parallel Tb/s reads of frozen weights at low pJ/bit; TB-per-cm3 class capacity offloads weights from DRAM entirely, though random access is microseconds, so it suits streaming.
note: Holographic storage failed repeatedly on media and optics cost.

title: Page-wide LDPC computed in the sense-amp stripe
idea: Ideal: error correction with zero overhead bits. Closest: since every activate already senses an ~8 kb row, add a long-block LDPC code over the whole row (~3% parity versus 12.5% for per-word SECDED) decoded bit-serially in the sense-amp stripe during tRAS, so dozens of marginal cells per row are fixed before any column read.
why: Facts 1, 3, 8: turns the 128x overfetch into an asset; tolerates ~100x higher raw BER at lower parity cost, letting Cs drop ~30% or refresh slow 4-8x.

title: Charge-density-wave electron-crystal bit in 1T-TaS2 nanoflakes
idea: Scarcity rule: no atom may move during a write. Store the bit as the electronic order of a 1T-TaS2 (or strain-stabilized analog) island: a ~ps current pulse switches the insulating commensurate CDW into a metallic hidden CDW state, a longer weak pulse restores it, and read uses the ~10x resistance contrast. Only the electron lattice rearranges, so there is no ionic fatigue.
why: Targets unlimited endurance with ps, fJ-class writes in a 2-terminal crosspoint element, sidestepping the CV2 floor (fact 10); room-temperature stability of the hidden state is the open physics question.
note: Hidden-state metastability at room temperature and 85 C is the open question.

title: Avalanche-gain readout lets a 50-electron node hold a bit
idea: Scarcity rule: storage charge is cut 300x. Each storage node sits on a junction biased just below breakdown, and during read a stored packet of ~50 electrons triggers a quenched SPAD-style avalanche with ~1e5 charge gain while an empty node stays silent, so a 0.01 fF planar node suffices.
why: Deletes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) entirely with fJ-scale reads; dark counts and afterpulsing set the raw BER that ECC must absorb.
note: SPAD dark counts and afterpulsing per cell; same avalanche-gain idea.

title: Wordlines capped at VARY: negative-capacitance HZO gate amplifies switching
idea: Limit: no wordline may exceed the array voltage. Add a 5 nm Zr-rich HZO negative-capacitance layer to the access transistor gate stack, capacitance-matched to the channel so internal voltage amplification gives ~40 mV/dec hysteresis-free switching. The same Ion/Ioff then needs ~1 V less swing, or the same swing gives ~25x lower leakage.
why: Facts 3, 7 and 10: retires the boosted 3 V wordline and its charge pumps (periphery area), or lengthens retention ~10x. Unlike prior HZO memory work, the ferroelectric is a gain element inside the switch, not the storage.
note: Stable hysteresis-free NC remains contested.

title: No carriers in the off-state: vacuum-channel field-emission access device
idea: Limit: the off-state medium must contain no carriers. Build a sealed 20 nm vacuum nanogap between a sharp emitter tip on the storage node and a bitline collector, with a surrounding gate as the wordline. The device turns on only by field emission above a threshold field; below it, Fowler-Nordheim current falls super-exponentially.
why: Fact 3: near-zero off-current makes refresh rare. Field emission is temperature-insensitive, which also removes the hot-temperature doubling of refresh. Speculative because of vacuum sealing and emitter wear.

title: Bookshelf memory: upright thin dies edge-bonded onto logic
idea: Limit: fixed footprint, no TSVs, and more than 32 dies. Stand 20 um thin DRAM dies on edge like books across the logic die, and hybrid-bond their polished edge pads directly to the logic surface. About 50 dies per mm of row.
why: Facts 5 and 6: far more dies per footprint than horizontal HBM stacks, a TSV-free signal path, and each die cools through its faces.
note: Echoes Irvine Sensors edge-connected cubes; edge hybrid bonding is unproven.

title: Ga2O3-channel tiers with planar 0.5 fF capacitors
idea: Under 400 C, ALD amorphous Ga2O3 (4.8 eV gap) access transistors leak orders of magnitude less than Si. Each tier then needs only a flat 0.5 fF MIM capacitor beside the transistor, with no pillar at all, and tiers become simple planar layers.
why: Facts 1 and 3: retention long enough for a 0.5 fF node removes the high-AR capacitor and nearly eliminates refresh energy.

title: Oxide-CMOS sense amplifiers distributed inside every tier
idea: Under 400 C, each tier carries its own tiny sense-amp strip of n-IGZO and p-SnO transistors deposited at 250 C, sensing short local bitlines. The bonded base logic only handles global I/O.
why: Fact 7 and 3D scaling: periphery stops growing with tier count; local sensing tolerates small Cs.
note: p-SnO is weak and hysteretic; same core as IGZO in-tier sense amps.

title: Redox-molecule pseudocapacitor storage node on nanoporous electrode
idea: Under 400 C, a nanoporous Ru storage node (about 50x surface area) is coated at 200 C with a monolayer of thermally robust porphyrin redox molecules. Bits are stored as molecular oxidation state, so many electrons are packed per nm2 at low voltage.
why: Facts 1 and 10: about 10x charge per footprint versus dielectric capacitors at about 0.5 V reads; planar storage nodes.

title: MLCC-in-a-cell: forty-plate interdigitated capacitor per bit
idea: Under 400 C, ALD forty alternating Ru and TiN plates separated by 4 nm ZrO2 (crystalline as deposited at about 275 C). Selectively recess Ru on one hole sidewall and TiN on the other so each cell's two contacts tie to alternating plates, like an MLCC termination.
why: Fact 1: about 5 fF in a 40x40 nm footprint at about 9:1 AR instead of 75:1; the capacitor scales by plate count, not etch depth.
note: Resembles fin capacitors; per-cell alternating plate contact at 40 nm is hard.

title: Antiferroelectric zirconia capacitors store more charge using existing tools
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: tune the ZrO2 already used in DRAM capacitors into a dopant-stabilized antiferroelectric phase with asymmetric electrodes, so the built-in bias parks the cell on the steep field-induced transition and the effective k in the sensing window exceeds ~100 from -40 to 125 C.
why: Facts 1 and 4: same ALD and etch tools, but ~2x charge per area lets capacitor AR fall from ~70 to ~40, cutting etch time and hardmask steps.

title: Resonant LC tank bus recycles signal charge between complementary wires
idea: Scarcity: the whole link gets 1 pJ/bit. Pair each data wire with its complement through an on-package thin-film inductor so a transition sloshes charge from one line to the other at LC resonance (adiabatic signaling) instead of dumping CV2 to ground; drivers only top up resistive loss.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5): recovering ~70-80% of line charge targets <1 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM and 10-20 pJ/bit DDR5.
note: Random data transitions do not suit resonant recovery; per-wire inductors cost area.

title: Infrared light shines straight through silicon to wire 100 tiers
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so a vertical beam from a VCSEL array under the stack passes through every thinned tier; each tier reads with a thin Ge photodiode and writes with a free-carrier-absorption modulator on the same spot, making optical vias with no drilling.
why: Deletes TSV process cost (fact 6) so tier count is limited only by thinning: 100 tiers of 10 um in 1 mm targets 10x bits per footprint at HBM-like package cost.
note: Same through-silicon IR vertical link mechanism; 100 tiers adds shared-beam crosstalk.

title: Die-level erasure coding admits cheap downbinned dies into 48-high stacks
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Spread every cache line Reed-Solomon coded across 40 data dies plus 8 parity dies, with the base die mapping out dead banks, so dies with failed banks or weak cells (today scrapped or sold at 40-60% off) become first-class stack members.
why: Stack yield stops multiplying and discounted partial-good dies pay for the extra tiers: ~10x bits per package at the same package price.

title: Alignment-free nanopillar film gives tenfold interconnect density
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. A directed-self-assembly block-copolymer membrane filled with 30 nm vertical copper pillars at 60 nm pitch joins any pad to the facing pad with no precision alignment, because every pad lands on hundreds of pillars.
why: Interconnect density: pads shrink from 9 um to ~1 um pitch without $5-10M hybrid-bond aligners, ~10-80x more vertical wires per mm2 at the same tool cost.
note: Pad-to-pad die alignment still required at 1 um pitch; film removes only bump alignment.

title: 64-activation cap: hot rows migrate into on-die SRAM
idea: Imposed limit: no row may be activated more than 64 times per refresh window. When a row hits the cap, its contents are copied into a small on-die hot-row SRAM (or a latched spare sense-amp stripe) and served from there for the rest of the window. The DRAM row is never re-opened.
why: Fact 9: row hammer becomes impossible at any threshold above 64, independent of cell weakness, and hot rows also get faster access.
note: At a 64-activation cap, ~20k rows/bank per window could qualify; SRAM size explodes.

title: Twice the bits, same capacitor: trellis-coded four-level cells
idea: Imposed limit: double the bits without a bigger capacitor. Each cell stores 4 charge levels and raw BER of ~1e-3 is accepted. Trellis-coded modulation across 8 cells (as in modems) adds structured redundancy, and the set is decoded by a Viterbi block in the sense-amp periphery.
why: Fact 1 charge wall: ~1.7x net bits per cell after coding overhead with no new capacitor geometry.

title: NEMS relay access switch: zero-GIDL DRAM cell
idea: A vertical TiN/W cantilever or clamped beam over each storage node is pulled in by the wordline electrode, closing a contact between bitline and capacitor; open, an air or vacuum gap isolates the node. Leakage then is only the capacitor dielectric's own (~1e-8-1e-7 A/cm2). Switching is abrupt (effectively 0 mV/dec), so the wordline needs only the pull-in voltage (~1 V) with no charge pump. A 100-200 nm beam resonates at 0.4-1.2 GHz, giving ~0.5-1.5 ns mechanical switching. Contacts switch only fC of charge at uA levels, far gentler than RF-MEMS hot switching.
why: Refresh 150-1,500x less frequent (10-100 s retention with today's capacitor); wordline energy ~0.06x (1 V unpumped vs 2.9 V pumped); hammer-immune by construction.

title: Flat AlBN ferroelectric capacitor with non-destructive capacitive read
idea: Sputter 5-10 nm wurtzite Al1-xBxN (x 0.02-0.15) at <=400 C on a planar landing pad: 2Pr*A for a 40x40 nm pad is ~4 fC (~26,000 e-), more than today's 1.3 um pillar delivers. Reads must not switch the film, so the state is read capacitively: the imprinted polarization gives different small-signal C (or a piezo/flexo-induced charge) for up and down states, sensed through a 2T gain cell on an oxide channel, so only writes wear the ferroelectric. Data are non-volatile: no refresh. A gain-cell or SRAM write buffer in front absorbs write traffic.
why: Zero capacitor height and zero refresh energy; 1-4 fC per bit from a planar 20-40 nm pad; Sc- and Hf-free. Gated by an endurance gap of ~1e5-1e9x.

title: Crystalline crested-barrier selector: transistor-less 1S1C crosspoint DRAM in stacked decks
idea: Each cell is a stub capacitor (~14 nm x 300 nm, k ~40, ~0.9 fF) in series with a layered tunnel barrier at a 4F2 crosspoint. Likharev's crested profile (a thin high-barrier centre with lower flanks), or VARIOT's low-k/high-k/low-k stack, makes current extremely field-sensitive. At hold and half-select (V/2 or less) the barrier is effectively thick and leakage is limited by direct tunnelling. At write voltage the bands bend below the crest and Fowler-Nordheim current flows. The barrier must be crystalline (hBN/graphene stacks, AlN/GaN epitaxy or epitaxial oxides), not amorphous ALD, because the full write charge passes through it on every cycle. Bitlines are 64 cells long with sense amps under the array, and decks stack like 3D XPoint.
why: Two decks at F = 20 nm give 1.34x 1-beta cell density; four decks give 2.7x, or 1.6x at F = 26 nm, which is reachable with SAQP and no EUV. No access-transistor GIDL tail.

title: DNA-brick nanotrench templates for an EUV-free cell lattice
idea: On a wafer with coarse lithographic landing pads (ArF, ~80-100 nm), DNA-brick crystals assemble into nanotrench arrays whose pitch is programmable (10-40 nm) and whose registry is set by the pads. The DNA is mineralised (silicification or metal infiltration, as in sequential infiltration synthesis) or used directly as an etch mask, and the pattern transfers into a hardmask for the capacitor or channel holes, or for the bitline and wordline lines. Only the array layers use DNA; the periphery uses conventional lithography or sits on a bonded wafer. Because DNA is molecularly addressable, a single template can also carry non-periodic features such as pads and cuts.
why: Replace up to 5-7 EUV exposures ($825-1,155 per wafer at 1c, per A1) with ~$0.5-25 of DNA per wafer and room-temperature aqueous assembly; pitch headroom is 3.4x finer than today's 35 nm capacitor pitch.

title: Swap single dielectric for negative-capacitance ferroelectric/dielectric series stack
idea: Put a 2-3 nm ferroelectric HZO layer in series with the ZrO2 dielectric, with thicknesses tuned so the ferroelectric's negative-slope region partly cancels the series 1/C term. The stack's capacitance then exceeds the dielectric alone, as transient negative-capacitance experiments showed with 2-3x boosts.
why: Facts 1 and 10 (charge wall, voltage floor): the same charge at ~60% of the voltage, or ~2x Cs in the same pillar.
note: Steady-state NC boost is contested and widely pursued; hysteresis at ns speeds.

title: Swap hafnia for wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric with 5x remanent charge
idea: Use sputtered Al0.7Sc0.3N (Pr ~100-120 uC/cm2, about 5x HZO), deposited at <=400 C, as the switching layer of a 1T1C cell. The larger switched charge lets a planar or AR-10:1 capacitor give a full DRAM-class signal.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~5x charge per area removes high-AR pillars, and nitride sputtering is cheap and available in the U.S. Scandium supply and endurance are the risks.
note: AlScN FeRAM actively pursued; high coercive field and ~1e7 endurance far from DRAM duty.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores replace fluorocarbon-etched capacitor molds
idea: Substitute fluorocarbon-etched oxide molds with anodic aluminum oxide: sputter 3-5 um Al over storage pads, two-step anodize in oxalic/phosphoric acid to grow 25-35 nm hexagonal pores at AR >100:1, open the barrier by phosphoric-acid widening, fill with TiCl4-based ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN; pore diameter < inter-pad gap so no pore bridges two cells and each pad statistically lands several pores in parallel.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): AR 100-150 at bath-tool cost gives Cs ~8-12 fF with zero C4F6/C4F8 etch, no mold litho, abundant aluminum.
note: Pore spacing ~50-100 nm exceeds cell pitch; random pore registration causes opens/bridges.

title: Solar-cell silicon nitride charge layers become a dynamic trap bit
idea: PERC solar cells rely on stable fixed charge stored in silicon nitride passivation. Write that charge on purpose: a 1T cell with a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide under a SiN trap layer, programmed by direct tunneling (not Fowler-Nordheim) for 10-100 ns writes, retention of seconds to minutes, and low-field cycling.
why: No capacitor, no Zr/Hf high-k and no deep etch, only Si/SiO2/SiN. Refresh is ~1000x rarer than DRAM's; trap-cycling endurance is the open risk.
note: Trap-cycling endurance far below DRAM-class.

title: In-situ leach mining: copper-catalyzed wet etching of deep holes
idea: As in-situ leaching dissolves ore where it lies, use metal-assisted chemical etching: copper catalyst dots (instead of Au/Ag) defined by imprint or self-assembly on silicon sink vertically in HF/H2O2, digging capacitor holes or vertical channels beyond 100:1 at room temperature in a wet bench.
why: Deep-etch capex and EUV (facts 1, 4): ~10x cheaper tools, unlimited AR, no plasma damage, no W-doped or thick carbon hardmask. Risks: catalyst wander and Cu contamination control.
note: Cu-catalyzed MACE tends toward porous, poorly directional etch.

title: Half-voltage arrays: trade sense margin for quartered energy
idea: Reverse the margin budget: drop VARY from ~1 V to ~0.5 V and wordline boost proportionally, let ~1% of cells fall below sense margin, and correct them with ECC.
why: Breaks the voltage floor on energy, a facet input: CV^2 array energy falls ~4x, cutting memory power and the fab-to-datacenter energy footprint.
note: Halving VARY halves sense signal; far more than 1% cells fail.

title: Copper-nanodot catalyzed chemical etching drills capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: self-assembled Cu nanodots sink into silicon in HF/H2O2, each locally catalyzing dissolution beneath itself, so they drill holes of 100:1 or deeper at room temperature without plasma. The silicon mold is then oxidized or lined to form the capacitor template.
why: Replaces the most capital-heavy, fluorocarbon-hungry step (high-aspect-ratio mold etch) with a wet bath: ~10x lower tool capital and no C4F8/CF4. Uses only Cu, Si, H, O and F.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching drills capacitor holes at wet-bench cost
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution replaces the ion field with a catalytic chemical one: pattern a noble-metal catalyst dot lattice, immerse in HF/H2O2, and each dot sinks vertically into silicon carving 100:1 holes for buried capacitors or vertical-channel transistors, 50 wafers per batch.
why: Wet bench ~$1-3M vs ~$5-10M+ per HAR etch chamber plus chillers; batch processing raises deep-etch throughput ~10x (fact 4, capital).

title: Protonic three-terminal transistor holds state as pumped ions
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics treats ions as a working fluid: a gate pulse pumps protons from a hydrogenated reservoir through a solid electrolyte into a WO3 channel, changing its conductance; removing the field freezes the ions, so the state is nonvolatile and read non-destructively through a separate channel path.
why: Zero refresh and non-destructive read (fact 8); BEOL-compatible below ~300 C with sputter/ALD only, so it is capital-light with no EUV; ns-scale protonic switching has been reported, but endurance and hot retention are the risks (facts 3, 4).

title: Shipworm catalytic drilling replaces plasma etch for 200-tier holes
idea: Shipworms bore by chemistry rather than force; place Au or Pt catalyst discs, defined by the single hole lithography, on top of a 200-tier Si/SiGe stack and run metal-assisted chemical etching in HF/H2O2 so each disc sinks straight down, drilling ~30 nm holes at >500:1 aspect in a wet bench.
why: High-AR hole etch is the most capital-intensive 3D step and caps tier count; a MACE bench costs ~1/20 of a cryogenic etcher and goes deeper, so 150-200 tiers (~10x+ bits/mm2) arrive at about flat wafer cost (fact 2).

title: Architectural anodizing grows capacitor templates without plasma etch
idea: Window-frame anodizing grows self-ordered hexagonal nanopores in aluminum. Deposit an aluminum mold layer over the array, nano-indent pore seeds aligned to the storage-node landing pads, and anodize to grow straight pores of 1000:1 aspect ratio at ~40 nm pitch, then line them with ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN; nothing changes at the DDR/HBM pins.
why: Replaces the hardest high-aspect-ratio plasma etch (fluorocarbon gas, helium chuck cooling, carbon hard masks, hole patterning) with a bench-top electrochemical step; AR >100 at near-zero tool capital for ~2x Cs.

title: Wurtzite AlBN ferroelectric cell: hafnium-free, nonvolatile DRAM
idea: Inverts 'ferroelectric memory needs hafnia or lead': sputter wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N from abundant Al and B in N2 as the cell capacitor's ferroelectric in a 1T1C array whose sense amps read polarization-switching charge (remanent polarization >100 uC/cm2, ~5x HZO).
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; the huge polarization lets a planar or shallow capacitor replace 70:1 pillars, cutting etch gas and mold; no Hf, Zr or Pb, and AlN is already a US-made MEMS material.
note: AlBN coercive field and endurance (~1e5-1e7) far short of DRAM-class.

title: Seesaw: negative-capacitance layer amplifies the storage capacitor
idea: Stimulus 'seesaw' (push one end down, the other rises) -> place a 3 nm ZrO2-based ferroelectric, biased in its negative-capacitance region, in series with an Al2O3/ZrO2 storage dielectric, all ALD from ZrCl4 and TMA/H2O; the dielectric stabilizes the stack so it shows no hysteresis while net capacitance exceeds the dielectric alone.
why: Raises Cs ~1.5-2x at the same AR (fact 1) or lets the array voltage drop for the same charge (fact 10); chloride/organometallic ALD only, no fluorine.

title: Washing machine: metal-assisted wet etching drills AR>100 capacitor holes
idea: Random stimulus 'washing machine' (a wet bath does the work) -> a patterned noble-metal mesh on silicon catalyzes local oxidation and dissolution in HF/H2O2, so the mesh sinks straight down and leaves a hole array with AR >100. Room-temperature wet tanks replace the plasma high-AR etch.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and capital: high-AR dielectric etch tools are among the costliest in the fab. MacEtch reaches very high aspect ratios with no plasma, so Cs could grow ~1.5x and etch capex fall >5x.

title: Catalyst nanodots burrow into silicon to drill capacitor holes
