why: Hours of retention at 125 C remove refresh energy (fact 3) for automotive and industrial memory, and avoid the HPQ and CZ chokepoints; SiC substrate lines already run in North Carolina and New York.
note: SiC DRAM cells shown decades ago; poor MOS interface and wafer cost.

title: CVD diamond heat spreaders keep hot-ambient DRAM twenty degrees cooler
idea: Magnify thermal conductivity ~5x over copper: bond a polycrystalline CVD diamond lid (grown from methane and hydrogen) to the memory die, so a 125 C ambient gives a ~105 C junction.
why: Every 10 C halves the needed refresh rate, so refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall ~4x (fact 3). Carbon is abundant and the lid is stable at 125 C indefinitely.
note: A passive spreader cannot hold junction below ambient; 125 C ambient to 105 C junction claim is unphysical.

title: Page-wide 100,000-nozzle printhead deposits only where needed
idea: Magnify nozzle count to a page-wide MEMS printhead array firing sub-femtoliter drops across the full web, depositing dielectric and electrode only where cells exist instead of blanket coating plus etch.
why: Material and step count: about 95% less material waste, and no litho-etch loop for coarse layers.

title: Gallium liquid-metal microbumps in micro-wells
idea: MINIFY the melting point to ~30 C: microbumps are galinstan-filled wells capped by a dielectric frame, so a die lifts off with gentle heat and reseats with the wells reformed.
why: Rework and recycling of stacked memory; dies come out clean with no solder residue, cutting scrap and tin use.

title: Infrared optical vertical links through bondless stacks
idea: MINIFY metal in the vertical path to zero: 1.3 um infrared emitters and photodiodes send light straight through the silicon dies (silicon is transparent there), so stacked dies need no TSVs and can be separated.
why: Removes the TSV tax and makes stacks separable for repair or recycling; claims ~0.5 pJ/bit vertical links.

title: Eliminate the VPP charge pump with a shared bootstrap boost plate
idea: Run a common boost plate under all wordlines of a sub-array. The decoder drives the selected wordline to VDD (1.1 V) and floats it, while all unselected wordlines stay actively clamped low. A 1.1 V step on the boost plate then couples only the floating wordline up to ~2.8 V for the restore window, as in a bootstrapped driver.
why: Removes the VPP pumps (~3-5% of die, 30-40% efficient) and roughly halves wordline energy, because the boost charge comes from a single 1.1 V swing (facts 7 and 10).

title: Eliminate transistor leakage: bistable SiC nano-relay memory cells
idea: Each cell is a ~100 nm electrostatically actuated SiC or TiN beam that snaps between two buckled stable states and closes a contact for a zero-leakage read; switching costs aJ of mechanical energy plus wiring.
why: Zero off-current removes refresh and the leakage tail, and the tiny switched charge makes access energy wire-limited, >10x below DRAM; contact endurance is the open risk.
note: Same bistable buckled-beam mechanism as I-06198, with contact readout.

title: Strain-held Mott latch: VO2 parked inside its hysteresis window
idea: Reverse the bias logic: a static strain from a piezoelectric underlayer holds a W-doped VO2 nanobar at the middle of its metal-insulator hysteresis, and ns current or voltage pulses flip it metallic or insulating; the electronic phase, not stored charge, holds the bit and reads as ~100x resistance contrast.
why: Refresh and endurance (fact 3): nothing leaks because the state is a thermodynamic phase, and Mott switching moves no atoms (target >1e12 cycles); risks are room-temperature hysteresis width and thermal crosstalk.

title: Leakage becomes the latch: tunnel-diode Goto pair on storage node
idea: Reverse leakage from enemy to keeper: stack two nanoscale Esaki (interband tunnel) diodes in series between VDD and ground with the storage node at their midpoint. Their negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages held by valley-current tunneling, so the node never drifts and the access transistor is only used to read and write.
why: Refresh disappears (fact 3) if diode valley current is <1 pA (otherwise static power rivals refresh); diodes stack vertically on the node, reviving the old TSRAM idea with modern Ge/Si tunnel junctions.

title: CCD bitline marches charge packets to one edge charge amplifier
idea: Move the charge to the sensor instead of the sensor to the charge: the bitline becomes a buried CCD channel with 3-phase clock gates, cells dump their charge into it, and packets are shifted (image-sensor style) to one low-noise floating-diffusion charge amplifier at the array edge, then shifted back for restore.
why: Facts 7 and 1: one amplifier per ~512 cells instead of per bitline; CCD charge amps resolve tens of electrons, so Cs could drop from ~5 fF to <1 fF with no 60:1 pillars. Shift speed is the main risk.

title: Lower-purity specialty gases, defects absorbed downstream
idea: Reverse the spec flow: qualify 5N instead of 6N-7N grades of NF3, silane, WF6 and ammonia from a wider supplier base, and let the trace-contaminant cell defects sit inside the 1% BER budget.
why: Specialty gas purification is energy- and supplier-concentrated; widening grades cuts cost ~30% and sole-source risk.
note: Trace contaminants hit yield broadly, not just tolerable cell bit errors.

title: VO2 hysteresis latch held bistable by the chip's own waste heat
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #36 Phase transition: dope VO2 (W/Ge) so its 5-10 K insulator-metal hysteresis loop sits at the stack's operating temperature, so each nano-VO2 cell stays insulating or metallic indefinitely while warm. Write '1' with a ns Joule pulse, reset with a piezo-strain gate pulse that shifts the loop, and read resistance non-destructively.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no refresh, non-destructive read; idle cost is heat the accelerator already makes; data are volatile at power-off like DRAM.

title: Pre-implanted cleave plane lets storage substrates be reclaimed repeatedly
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: build the storage array in a thin single-crystal layer transferred by hydrogen-implant ion cut onto a handle wafer that carries a second pre-implanted weak plane; at end of life or after test failure, the handle is split there, re-polished and reused 5-10 times.
why: Scarce resources: cuts Spruce Pine quartz-crucible and polysilicon demand per GB ~5x through handle reuse.

title: Dynamics: sense amps switch to two-bit multilevel mode when cool
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: each sense amp adds a second time-staggered latch and a mid-reference so a mat can run either 1-bit robust mode or 2-bit-per-cell multilevel mode; the controller enables multilevel on mats whose thermal sensor and retention telemetry show margin (cool, cold data) and migrates data out when temperature rises.
why: Density: ~1.6-2x bits per cell on cool, cold data, with capacity that flexes with conditions; Fact 1's small charge sets the risk.

title: Thin films: porous-silicon release layer enables 10x substrate reuse
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells/thin films: one added mask defines anodization windows that form a buried porous-Si cleave plane; after array processing the thin device layer is bonded to a cheap carrier and lifted off, and the CZ wafer is re-polished and reused ~10 times.
why: Scarce resources: cuts prime-wafer and HPQ crucible demand per bit sharply.

title: Statolith shuttle: nanoparticle moves between two ends of a sealed cavity
idea: Plant-root statoliths are dense starch grains that settle inside cells to record orientation. Seal a 10 nm conductive nanoparticle (Ru or a carbon onion) in a 30 nm vacuum nanocavity with an electrode at each end. An electrostatic pulse moves it to one end, where van der Waals adhesion holds it, and the bit is read by capacitance or tunnel current at that end.
why: Non-volatile with no bond breaking and so no material wear; ~1 ns transit over 20 nm and unlimited endurance in principle. Uses CMOS-compatible sealed air-gap processes.
note: Bucky-shuttle memory precedent; nanocavity fabrication and stiction reliability uncertain.

title: Proton-relay croconic acid: fluorine-free printed ferroelectric charge booster
idea: Enzymes and bacteriorhodopsin move charge along hydrogen-bonded proton wires. Croconic acid crystals switch polarization by the same proton tautomerism (~20 uC/cm2, no fluorine); inkjet-print them as the cell capacitor and run them in a volatile minor-loop mode that adds displacement charge without full switching, to protect endurance.
why: Replaces fluorinated P(VDF-TrFE) (a PFAS) and Hf-based ferroelectrics in printed memory, with ~5x more stored charge than linear printed dielectrics at a 150 C process.
note: Same croconic-acid printed ferroelectric as I-08950.

title: Fresnel capacitor: nested shallow shells replace one tall pillar
idea: As a Fresnel lens collapses a thick lens into concentric rings, collapse a 75:1 pillar into 3-4 concentric electrode shells nested in one cell footprint: alternate ALD of TiN, high-k and a sacrificial spacer inside a single ~20:1 hole, then selectively strip the spacers so both faces of every shell become capacitor area.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): roughly the area of a 75:1 pillar at AR ~20, cutting the hardest etch depth 3-4x and pillar leaning; claims 5 fF at a fraction of the high-AR etch cost.
note: Multi-crown capacitors are 1990s art; 3-4 TiN/high-k shells cannot fit in a ~30 nm hole.

title: Pendulum wordline planes: resonant LC drive recycles plate charge
idea: Like a pendulum clock trading kinetic for potential energy, make the large horizontal wordline plates of a 3D array the capacitor of an LC tank with an interposer spiral inductor, swinging the selected plate sinusoidally to VPP and back so ~85% of its charge returns to the inductor instead of ground.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): ~3 V wordline CV2 dominates plate-wordline 3D DRAM; claims 5-10x lower wordline energy per activation.
note: Dup of LC wordline tank; 85% recovery for aperiodic activations is optimistic.

title: Phone BAW-filter acoustic data links through the stack
idea: Phones filter RF with sputtered AlN bulk-acoustic-wave resonators deposited at ≤350 C. Put ScAlN transducer pairs on each thinned DRAM die so GHz ultrasound carries data straight up through the silicon. Channels are frequency-multiplexed, and each tier picks off its own.
why: Removes signal TSVs, their keep-out zones and their yield loss. Even 10-20 acoustic channels per mm² at 5-10 Gb/s would replace a large share of HBM signal TSVs.

title: Qi wireless-charging coils powering each stacked die
idea: Phones charge on a pad. Pattern thin planar Cu coils in each die's back-end RDL (≤250 C) and a driver coil in the base die, so power crosses the stack inductively at tens of MHz. Signals cross on capacitive coupling pads.
why: Removes power TSVs, about half of all TSVs, easing HBM's TSV tax and yield loss. Feasibility depends on reaching ~70% link efficiency.
note: Inductive power at ~70% efficiency adds heat to thermally limited stacks.

title: Persistent spectral hole burning: a thousand frequency bits per spot
idea: IBM's 1978 PHB patent stored bits as narrow holes burned at chosen frequencies in an inhomogeneously broadened absorption line. Use room-temperature PHB films (Sm2+ in BaFCl-type hosts) where each diffraction-limited spot holds ~1000 frequency channels, written and read by a fast chirped laser and photodiode.
why: Frequency becomes a third storage dimension (~1000x bits per spot) without lithography (Fact 4); erase endurance and speed unproven, so a speculative capacity tier.
note: Optical capacity tier; speed and erase endurance unproven; not DRAM-class.

title: One-mask NEMS relays for leakage-free row decoders
idea: Revive the relay computer (Zuse's Z3) at nanoscale. Lateral electrostatic relays are patterned in an existing upper metal layer and released by a single added air-gap etch mask, giving zero-leakage, abrupt-switching pass gates for row decoders and bank power switches.
why: Zero off-state leakage in decoders and power gates cuts standby power, and moving decoding into BEOL shrinks the silicon periphery (fact 7).
note: Relay endurance for decoder switching rates is the doubt.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode Goto-pair latches at bitline pitch
idea: The 1959 Goto pair used two series tunnel diodes as a bistable logic element. One added pocket-implant mask forms p++/n++ Esaki junctions at each sense node, and two in series make a negative-resistance latch that resolves a bitline differential in tens of picoseconds with 2 devices instead of a 4-6 transistor cross-coupled pair.
why: The sense amp fits at 1x bitline pitch in open-bitline arrays, roughly halving the sense stripe (fact 7) and cutting latch energy.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode bistable cells as stackable two-terminal static RAM
idea: Revive 1960s tunnel-diode memories: a BEOL-grown interband tunnel diode (oxide or 2D heterojunction) in series with a thin-film load has two stable operating points held by a shared standby-bias line, and 4-8 such decks stack as crosspoint static memory read by small current pulses.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no capacitor and no refresh; two-terminal decks dodge the 3D transistor blocker, viable if peak-to-valley ratio >10 keeps standby below DRAM refresh power.
note: Valley-current standby power per cell too high at Gb scale.

title: Plated-wire NDRO cells on copper bitlines, read without destroying data
idea: Revive 1960s aerospace plated-wire memory: electroplate a 20 nm NiFeCo sheath with circumferential anisotropy around damascene copper bitlines in BEOL, with aluminum word straps crossing over. A word pulse tilts the sheath magnetization without flipping it, so the sign of the induced bitline voltage gives the bit non-destructively. Aqueous plating at <80 C needs no W, no high-k and no fluorinated etch.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): only addressed bits are sensed and nothing is restored; avoids W, Hf and PFAS etch gases; nonvolatile, so no refresh; claims ~3x lower read energy per useful bit.

title: Protonic shuttle cell stores protons, not electrons
idea: Invert 'the stored carrier is an electron' -> store protons. A 5 nm phosphorus-doped SiO2 solid acid lets protons shuttle under ~1 V/nm pulses into or out of an Nb2O5 or WO3 nano-channel in nanoseconds, setting a non-volatile conductance; protons intercalate without breaking host bonds, the hoped route to near-unlimited endurance.
why: Refresh-free, non-destructive read, ~fJ writes (facts 3, 8, 10); Nb2O5 option avoids the tungsten chokepoint; risk is proving >1e15-cycle endurance.
note: 1e15-cycle ionic endurance is the doubt.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN grown roll-to-roll on copper foil
idea: Invert 'polarization switching moves ions inside a unit cell and fatigues' -> slide whole atomic layers by one bond length. Parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 grown by roll-to-roll CVD on copper foil and laminated onto glass or polyimide flips out-of-plane polarization as layers glide between AB and BA registry, a bond-preserving motion reported to resist fatigue; a 2D channel below reads it non-destructively.
why: Atom-thin, non-volatile, potentially fatigue-free sub-1 V storage (facts 3, 8, 10) on a non-silicon substrate; domain pinning and large-area stacking control are the risks.

title: Spin-crossover molecular films switching high and low spin states
idea: Invert 'the bit is a charge, polarization or magnetic direction' -> store it as a molecule's spin state. Room-temperature-hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover complexes vacuum-sublimed onto glass or polymer flip between low and high spin (with ~10% volume and large conductance change) under a gate-induced charge or strain pulse inside their hysteresis loop, read by tunneling current.
why: Non-volatile inside the hysteresis window, ~2 nm molecular cells, no scarce elements and low-temperature processing on any substrate; field-driven switching speed and room-temperature margins are speculative.

title: Redox-molecule monolayers store quantized electrons on ITO glass
idea: Invert 'a capacitor holds a continuous amount of charge' -> store discrete electrons in molecules. A self-assembled monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin or ferrocene triads) on ITO-coated glass holds 2-4 discrete oxidation states per site, giving up to 2 bits per cell at ~1e14 e/cm^2, read by redox current peaks at characteristic voltages.
why: ~10-20x the charge per area of a planar dielectric (fact 1), so no HAR capacitor, plus chemistry-defined multilevel cells; solid-state contacts, nanosecond kinetics and 1e15-cycle molecular stability are the risks.
note: Same multilevel redox-molecule monolayer.

title: Bistable buckled-nanobeam cell read by a single pull-up
idea: Inverting 'the bit is an electrical state': each bit is the up/down position of a buckled nanobeam that touches a contact only when down; reading is an ohmic open-or-short, so a weak pull-up and an inverter replace the sense amp, with zero leakage and no refresh.
why: Near-infinite on/off ratio removes sense-margin problems and all refresh energy; periphery becomes trivial. Contact wear and stiction limit endurance (~1e10-1e12).

title: Vanadium-dioxide hysteretic latch held inside its Mott window
idea: Inverting 'volatile memory must leak and be refreshed': each cell is a tiny VO2 element biased inside its metal-insulator hysteresis window, so it stays metallic or insulating as long as the hold bias is on, and a current comparator reads the ~100x resistance ratio.
why: One-element static cell with no refresh controller, no capacitor and a large read signal; hold power and thermal crosstalk are the risks.
note: VO2 Tc ~68 C is below DRAM operating temperature; hold power is high.

title: Buckled silicon-carbide nanobeam holds the bit mechanically
idea: Inverts 'bits are electric charge': each cell is a doubly clamped amorphous-SiC nanobeam deposited with built-in compressive stress so it rests buckled up or down; electrostatic pull electrodes snap it over in ~1-10 ns and capacitive sensing reads its position, with nothing to leak.
why: Zero refresh and zero standby; only Si, C and N, no high-k, Hf, Ru or W; SiC fatigue resistance targets >1e15 cycles.
note: Density, stiction and 1e15-cycle fatigue doubtful.

title: Wordlines as on-die heaters that anneal retention traps
idea: Inverts 'a leaky cell is permanently leaky': during idle, a driver mode passes current end-to-end through segmented wordline metal to Joule-heat one mat to ~200-300 C for milliseconds, annealing the interface and bulk traps behind VRT and GIDL tail cells.
why: Periodic self-healing of the leakage tail (fact 3) could recover 2-4x retention on aged parts and may reset hammer-induced trap damage.
note: Same wordline-heater anneal.

title: Pre-buckled 2D membrane snap-through as a leak-free mechanical bit
idea: Clamp a 20 nm MoS2 or graphene drum under compressive prestrain so it has two buckled states separated by an elastic barrier of ~1 eV (~40 kT). A ~1 V electrostatic pulse snaps it through in ~1/f0 ~ 1 ns, and a local sense transistor reads up/down as a ~10 aF capacitance change.
why: A mechanical position has no leakage path, so retention is set by the elastic barrier, not a 13 fA tail, and refresh (fact 3) disappears. There is no storage capacitor (fact 1), and write energy is ~CV2 ~ 10 aJ.
note: 2D drum snap-through; prestrain control and aF readout uncertain.

title: Spin-crossover molecular film switched electrically between spin states
idea: Sublime a ~10 nm Fe(II) spin-crossover film (triazole or bispyrazolylborate family) at <=200 C. Cooperative lattice strain gives a ~20 K-wide room-temperature hysteresis between low-spin and high-spin; field or charge-injection pulses switch it, and a vertical junction reads the 10-100x conductance or dielectric contrast.
why: A molecular-scale bistability set by lattice elasticity, with no charge to leak (fact 3). Uses abundant iron and organics and is compatible with top tiers.
note: Electrical spin-crossover switching is weak and slow; film work long studied.

title: Electrometer-style active guard bootstraps away bitline capacitance
idea: Parasitic capacitance only steals signal if its far plate moves differently from the bitline. Run a shield conductor between/under bitlines driven by a unity-gain bootstrap buffer that follows the bitline pair's common node (the electrometer guard trick), cutting effective Cbl ~5x.
why: Signal = Q/(Cs+Cbl_eff): ~4-5x more signal or ~4x smaller Cs at equal margin (fact 1); allows 2-4x longer bitlines, halving SA count (fact 7).

title: Molten-salt electro-deoxidation turns quartz sand into silicon near thermodynamic minimum
idea: Reducing SiO2 to Si needs a minimum of ~9 kWh/kg while the Siemens chlorosilane route uses 50-100. Press SiO2 into cathodes, electro-deoxidize in molten CaCl2 at 850 C (FFC route), then reach 11N with a float-zone pass, skipping trichlorosilane, HCl and H2.
why: Polysilicon energy down ~4-5x and the chlorosilane chemical chain removed; reaching electronic-grade purity is the risk.
note: FFC silicon well studied; electronic-grade purity is the blocker.

title: Conveyor-belt sushi: bits ride recirculating gigahertz phonon loops
idea: Stimulus 'sushi conveyor' -> store data as acoustic pulses circulating in short on-chip AlN acoustic loops (64 bits per ~1.3 ns, ~10 um loop), regenerated by a tiny amplifier each lap, like a mercury delay line made micro. Sound is ~10^5x slower than light, so a micron-scale loop holds a cache line with no capacitor or access transistor.
why: Capacitor-free, transistor-light storage with no leakage tail (fact 3) built on mature-node, EUV-free lines (fact 4); periphery shrinks to one amplifier per 64 bits (fact 7); density is lower, so it targets capital-light capacity tiers.

title: Chameleon: spin-crossover molecules toggle high-spin and low-spin states
idea: Stimulus 'chameleon' (changes color on cue) -> a 10 nm film of an Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover complex with room-temperature thermal hysteresis; a local ns heat or field pulse switches molecules between low-spin and high-spin, changing film permittivity and conductance by ~10-30%, read by a thin-film transistor gated through the film.
why: Intrinsically bistable molecular bit (no refresh, fact 3), solution-processed with no EUV (fact 4), built from earth-abundant iron.
note: Same spin-crossover film bit.

title: Toaster-pulse anneals heal retention-tail traps in the field
idea: Random stimulus 'toaster': short hot bursts restore crispness. Embed resistive heater lines in each mat under a deuterium-loaded nitride cap; during maintenance windows a microsecond-scale pulse heats the array locally to ~350 C, releasing deuterium that re-passivates the interface traps behind variable-retention-time cells and aged GIDL tails.
why: Turns the retention tail from a fixed guardband into something repairable; healing aged traps could hold refresh at fresh-die rates and reclaim 2-4x retention margin over life (fact 3).

title: Gecko-feet dry transfer of 2D access channel sheets
idea: Random stimulus 'gecko feet': stick and release by van der Waals forces, no glue. Grow wafer-scale WSe2/MoS2 on a sapphire donor, pick it up with a dry thermal-release stamp and laminate it onto the BEOL storage-capacitor array, forming the access transistors with ALD gates above the capacitors so the array needs no FEOL silicon access module.
why: Atomically thin, ~2 eV-gap channels give sub-fA off current (fact 3); replacing ~20 FEOL wet loops with one dry transfer plus ALD cuts access-module water >10x, and the sapphire donor is reusable.
note: Wafer-scale defect-free dry transfer and contacts over capacitors remain unsolved.

title: Bunk bed: oxide thin-film decoders stacked above the cell array
idea: Put the decoders upstairs like a bunk bed: build row predecoders, wordline-driver pull-ups and column-select logic from BEOL W-doped In2O3 or IGZO thin-film transistors (as in LCD gate-on-array drivers) directly over the array at <=400 C, connected down by vias, leaving only sense amps in silicon.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): decoders and drivers are ~15-20% of die; stacking them gives ~15% more bits per wafer with no EUV, and oxide TFTs tolerate the 3 V wordline swing.

title: Crystal radio: tunnel-diode Goto-pair sense amp biased at 0.2 V
idea: A crystal radio works with almost no power. Build each sense amp as a Goto pair, two series Esaki tunnel diodes (e.g., Si/SiGe or III-V on the periphery wafer) biased in their negative-resistance region at ~0.2 V; the bitline signal tips the pair into one of two stable states within picoseconds, with no high-voltage cross-coupled latch.
why: SA latch energy scales with V2: 0.2 V instead of ~1 V is ~25x less latch energy and allows a low-swing bitline; 10x on sensing energy even after diode peak-current overhead; risk is diode uniformity and integration.

title: Salt shaker: molten-salt electrolysis turns sand into domestic polysilicon
idea: Stimulus 'salt' -> reduce high-purity SiO2 pellets directly to silicon as the cathode in molten CaCl2 at ~850 C (FFC-Cambridge style), skipping carbothermic smelting and the trichlorosilane Siemens process, then zone-refine to electronic grade.
why: Polysilicon is >80% China-concentrated and Siemens costs ~50-60 kWh/kg; electrolysis could roughly halve energy and allow small modular U.S. plants.

title: Velcro: reworkable copper-nanowire hook-and-loop die stacking
idea: Forced 'velcro': dense Cu nanowire forests on both bonding faces interlock mechanically and cold-weld at room temperature at about 5 um pitch. A die that fails final test can be peeled off the HBM stack and replaced, which permanent hybrid bonds cannot allow.
why: HBM stack yield loss of 20-30%; reworkable stacks could recover most of the scrapped good dies, and room-temperature bonding avoids retention damage from heat.

title: Rubber stamp: R2R-replicated nanoimprint daughter stamps for EUV-free micro-fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'rubber stamp' -> one master carves millions of impressions. One e-beam master per layer is replicated roll-to-roll into thousands of flexible UV-imprint daughter stamps, mailed by subscription to micro-fabs that print DRAM array line/space and contact layers by jet-and-flash imprint.
why: Replaces 5-7 EUV layers with imprint for array levels; litho capex per layer down ~5-10x, and the single EUV supplier stops being a gate.

title: Low-barrier VCMA nanomagnet: deliberately volatile, refreshed-every-second MRAM
idea: Box = {medium: perpendicular CoFeB nanomagnet with a thermal barrier of only ~25 kT | access: vertical Si diode | sense: TMR | integration: BEOL crosspoint at 12 nm | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + ion-beam etch}. Writes use sub-ns voltage-controlled-anisotropy precessional pulses with almost no current, so the MgO barrier is never stressed; the low barrier makes the cell tiny and cheap to write, and a 1 s refresh replaces 10-year retention.
why: Energy (Fact 10) and endurance: ~10 fJ writes, effectively unlimited endurance because no breakdown current flows, and 15x less refresh than DRAM.

title: Hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2 as resistive bit
idea: Box = {medium: metastable hidden CDW domain state in 1T-TaS2 | access: Si FET | sense: ~10x resistance ratio | integration: BEOL film | substrate: Si | fab: MBE or CVD TaS2 + hBN encapsulation}. A ps-to-ns current pulse quenches the electron lattice into the hidden metallic CDW state, and a longer, weaker pulse restores the insulating commensurate state; switching is electronic ordering, not atom migration, so energy is fJ-scale.
why: Energy and endurance via purely electronic order switching: fJ writes and no refresh, but the hidden state has only been shown stable at low temperature.

title: Grown carbon-nanotube forest capacitors replacing etched pillars
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD dielectric coating a 30 nm vertically aligned CNT bundle | access: vertical Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: DSA-patterned Fe catalyst dots (Minnesota iron) + CVD growth from U.S. natural-gas methane}. Each cell's electrode grows 3 um tall from its catalyst dot instead of being etched, giving surface area beyond AR 100:1 without any high-AR plasma etch.
why: Fact 1 and capital (Fact 4): growth replaces the most expensive etch module, using domestic carbon and iron.

title: Test-floor laser anneal heals individual leaky-tail cells
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x retention test map x post-test die-level repair x Si x picosecond green laser through a BEOL window, like laser fuse repair. Retention test locates the ~0.01% tail cells and a localized pulse anneals trap clusters in that cell's junction, moving it into the main distribution instead of swapping it with redundancy.
why: Tail cells set the 64 ms interval; healing them extends refresh 2-4x (50-75% less refresh energy, fact 3) and frees redundancy area. Reaching the junction through the metal stack is the risk.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay row decoders and wordline drivers above the array
idea: Box: stacked cap x vertical Si access x conventional SA x BEOL-over-array decoders x Si x MEMS sacrificial release. Row decode trees and 3 V wordline drivers are built as electrostatic NEM relays (TiN beams, air-gap release) in the upper metal levels; relays have zero off-leakage and tolerate 3-5 V, so thick-oxide HV transistors leave the silicon.
why: Row decoder/driver area moves off Si (periphery -10-15% of die); HV driver standby leakage ~0. Relay endurance (needs ~1e15 cycles) is the open risk.

title: Resonant-tunneling-diode MOBILE latch replaces cross-coupled sense amp
idea: Box: stacked cap x Si access x NDR bistable sensing x heteroepitaxial devices under the bitline x Si x Si/SiGe RTD epitaxy. Two series resonant tunneling diodes clocked by a rising bias (monostable-bistable logic element) fall into one of two states set by a tiny bitline current imbalance, giving a 3-device latch with picosecond decisions.
why: SA area -60% and faster sensing; NDR supplies gain without large matched transistor pairs.

title: Photo-electrochemical macropore etching for 150:1 silicon capacitor trenches
idea: [Box: Si trench charge | VCT | charge-share SA | capacitor-first in substrate | n-type Si | backside-illuminated anodization in HF] Seed pits with a coarse ArF or DSA pattern, then grow capacitor holes into n-Si by backside-illuminated electrochemical etching that propagates straight at AR 150+ with no plasma; line with ALD high-k and fill with TiN.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR beyond 115 without plasma etchers or EUV; wet tooling is cheap and U.S.-buildable. Sub-100 nm pore pitch is the key risk.

title: Bistable buckled silicon-nitride nanobeams as non-volatile DRAM cells
idea: Box [mechanical state of a pre-buckled 300 nm SiN beam | electrostatic pull-in hysteresis, self-selecting with no transistor | capacitive sense of up/down state | BEOL cavity array | Si | LPCVD SiN from DCS+NH3 + vapor-HF/ethanol release in N2]: snap a compressively stressed nanobeam between two stable states with a 10 ns pulse; GHz beam frequencies allow 5-20 ns switching and non-contact snapping avoids wear.
why: Materials: a cell built only from Si and N, with no high-k, W, Hf or oxide semiconductor, and no refresh; endurance and density are the open risks.

title: Dry-grown carbon nanotube forests as compliant memory interconnects
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x standard x CNT-forest bumps densified and metal-capped x Si x dry thermal CVD growth plus ALD metal cap. Compliant CNT pillars absorb +/-1 um topography, so dies stack without CMP flattening, plating or solder flux.
why: Water: removes CMP, plating and flux wash (>10x); compliance tolerates thin-die warpage; contact resistance is the risk.
note: CNT bump contact resistance long unsolved.

title: Compress-then-protect: freed bits buy strong ECC at 0.4 V
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: low-swing | integration: codec on HBM/CXL logic base die | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. Each 64 B line is compressed (base-delta or zero-run) to at most 40 B, and the freed 24 B hold strong BCH/LDPC parity so that region runs at 0.4 V; incompressible lines (~25%) go to a 1 V region.
why: Constraint: ~1.6x fewer bits moved times ~6x lower array CV^2 gives ~10x per useful bit; parity costs no capacity.

title: Po: the transistor is empty — vacuum-channel access switch per cell
idea: Po: the transistor is empty. Extracted: isolate each storage node with a sealed ~5 nm vacuum nano-gap field-emission switch; below the Fowler-Nordheim threshold the gap has no carriers at all, so off-current falls exponentially below the 13 fA tail, and a gate-assisted emission pulse opens it for read/write.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): retention from 64 ms to minutes or hours, removing most of the 16-33% idle refresh power and 10-20% bandwidth loss. Emission voltage and emitter stability are the risks.
note: Same field-emission access switch.

title: Po: the bit is a traffic jam — charge-density-wave domain switching
idea: Po: the bit is a traffic jam of electrons. Extracted: thin 1T-TaS2 (or strain-stabilised variants) switches between commensurate and nearly-commensurate charge-density-wave states with ps electrical pulses; the bit is which electronic crystal is frozen in, read as a ~10x resistance difference.
why: Ps-scale, aJ writes with no capacitor at all (facts 1, 10). Room-temperature retention and BEOL integration of layered sulfides are open questions.
note: Same CDW bit; room-temperature retention unproven.

title: Po: the bit is a chemical reaction — polyoxometalate quantized-charge node
idea: Po: the bit is a chemical reaction. Extracted: a monolayer of polyoxometalate clusters on the storage electrode accepts 1, 2, 3 or 4 electrons at discrete, well-separated redox potentials, so each node stores 2 bits as quantized molecular charge states instead of a fragile analog voltage.
why: 2 bits per cell with built-in level separation and redox capacitance instead of tall pillars (facts 1, 4). Thermal stability of the molecules through BEOL is the risk.
note: Polyoxometalate variant of quantized redox storage.

title: Parametric phase bits in high-Q nanomechanical resonators
idea: Po: the bit is a rhythm, not a charge. Revive Goto's parametron: each cell is a nanomechanical resonator pumped at twice its natural frequency, which settles into oscillation at phase 0 or pi; the phase is the bit, held while the shared pump runs, written by a seed pulse and read by a phase detector.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no capacitor and no leakage decay; the shared pump replaces refresh; speculative on density and pump power per bit.
note: NEMS parametron memory demonstrated by NTT; density and pump power unsolved.

title: Buckled nanobeam bistable cells stacked in mechanical tiers
idea: Po: the bit is a shape, not a charge. Each cell is a pre-compressed 200 nm single-crystal Si nanobeam in a sealed cavity that buckles up or down; electrodes above and below snap it in ~10 ns and readout senses the capacitance difference, holding state with zero energy, and cavity tiers stack as bonded MEMS layers.
why: Zero refresh and standby; wear-free if strain stays elastic (<0.5% in single-crystal Si). Modest density aimed at a warm-data tier.
note: Bistable buckled-beam NEMS memory studied; stiction and fatigue at DRAM cycle counts doubtful.

title: Po wordlines drawn in pencil: intercalated graphene buried wordlines
idea: Po: 'wordlines are drawn with a pencil.' Extracted: form buried wordlines from multilayer graphene precipitated at <500 C from a sacrificial nickel liner, then intercalate with FeCl3 or bromine to drop sheet resistance; graphene's resistivity does not rise at sub-10 nm widths the way tungsten's does from surface scattering.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry removed from wordlines; at ~10 nm widths intercalated graphene could match or beat tungsten's effective resistivity, keeping wordline RC flat as cells shrink.
note: Intercalated graphene interconnects are published; buried wordline also acts as gate, adding work-function issues.

title: Acoustic bus: GHz sound waves through stacked silicon
idea: Po: memory talks by sound. Thin-film AlScN transducers on every die launch and detect 3-10 GHz bulk acoustic pulses that propagate vertically through the bonded silicon stack, carrying command, address and refresh-sync broadcasts with no TSV at all.
why: Frees all command/address TSVs for data and broadcasts to every die in one shot; trims TSV count and periphery.

title: Double-length 1024-cell bitlines halve the sense-amp count
idea: Po: everyone shares one bitline. Bitlines grow from 512 to 1024 cells, halving the number of sense-amp stripes; the halved Cs/Cb transfer ratio raises sense errors to ~1%, which the code absorbs.
why: Periphery (fact 7): ~10-15% die area recovered.
note: Halving transfer ratio drives ~1% raw BER; ECC for that erases area savings.

title: Two-bit-per-cell DRAM using relaxed-pitch fat capacitors
idea: Po: bigger cells hold more bits. With EUV forbidden, cells stay at ~20 nm-class pitch but capacitors grow to ~15-20 fF; that charge budget supports four-level storage read by a two-step sense amplifier against a reference ladder, giving 2 bits per cell.
why: Doubling bits per cell offsets the ~1.5-2x area penalty of skipping EUV; attacks density and cost per bit with no new litho, but sense margin and refresh risk are high.
note: 15-20 fF at 20 nm pitch is not achievable; MLC DRAM sense margins poor.

title: Charge-density-wave hidden state as an electrons-only phase bit
idea: Worsen: store bits by moving atoms or ions, which wear out. Flip: store the bit in the electronic order of a charge-density-wave material (1T-TaS2) whose metastable 'hidden' metallic state is set by a ps current pulse and erased by a longer pulse; only electrons reorder, so there is no atomic wear, and resistance contrast is 10-100x.
why: Endurance and speed (ps writes, fJ energy) with non-volatility; attacks refresh and the voltage floor (facts 3, 10). Room-temperature stability is the open question.

title: Leakage-twinned differential cell where drain currents cancel
idea: Worsen: let each capacitor leak through its own random tail transistor. Flip: store the bit as the charge difference between two half-size capacitors sharing one split-fin access device and one junction, so the dominant leakage (GIDL, junction trap-assisted tunneling) drains both equally and the differential signal survives ~10x longer.
why: Attacks the retention tail (fact 3): refresh interval 5-10x longer; half-size caps offset the 2C area penalty.
note: Tail leakage comes from random single traps, so it does not cancel common-mode; twin-cell DRAM known.

title: FeCl3-intercalated multilayer graphene bitlines replace ruthenium
idea: Worsen: move narrow bitlines and contacts to ruthenium mined almost entirely in South Africa and Russia. Flip: grow multilayer graphene at low temperature on sacrificial Co/Ni catalyst lines, then intercalate it with FeCl3 to raise carrier density, so its resistivity at <20 nm width beats Cu and rivals Ru.
why: PGM chokepoint and bitline RC: carbon is unlimited, with ~2x lower line RC than Cu at narrow widths claimed.
note: Same intercalated multilayer graphene lines as I-06627.

title: Through-silicon optical vias link stacked dies with infrared light
idea: Worsen: punch copper TSVs through every die. Flip: silicon is transparent above ~1.1 um, so bond micro-VCSEL and photodetector pairs on each die and send data vertically through the bulk silicon at 1.3 um through thinned windows, with no holes drilled at all.
why: TSV tax and yield (fact 6): no TSV keep-out area or via yield loss; short vertical optical hops at ~0.3 pJ/bit.

title: MEMS-fab nano-relay bistable memory on underused 200 mm lines
idea: Worse: leave U.S. MEMS and 200 mm fabs underused. Flip: build bistable nano-electromechanical relays, beams latched by adhesion with electrostatic set and reset, as memory cells that hold state mechanically with zero leakage.
why: Zero refresh and zero standby power, made on existing U.S. tools; contact wear limits endurance.

title: Pastry chef's caramel: spin-crossover film with room-temperature hysteresis
idea: A chef knows sugar sets differently depending on whether it was heated or cooled. Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover nanofilms have a ~30 K wide thermal hysteresis loop that straddles room temperature; a local ns heat or field pulse toggles high-spin and low-spin states, and the bit is read as a 10-20% change in dielectric constant.
why: A bistable molecular state holds without refresh (fact 3), and the molecules use cheap, earth-abundant iron instead of chokepoint materials.

title: Swiss banker's safe-deposit boxes: polyoxometalate multi-electron cell
idea: A banker keeps many items in one vault. Polyoxometalate clusters (e.g., [PW12O40]3-) accept 2-6 extra electrons in discrete, well-separated redox steps. A grafted monolayer of them forms the storage node and holds 2-3 bits per cell, read as distinct voltage plateaus.
why: 2-3 bits per cell multiplies density 2-3x at the same lithography (fact 4); discrete redox levels give better noise margins than analog multi-level charge.

title: Glassblower: glass-transition-gated lithium-ion latch, plasma-only cleans
idea: A glassblower can shape glass only while it is hot; once cooled, it is frozen. Li+ ions in a thin phosphate-glass gate drift to shift a transistor's threshold only while a microheater holds the glass above its transition temperature, and at room temperature they stay frozen for years. Remote H2/N2 plasmas do all the cleaning, with no sulfuric-peroxide or SC1 baths.
why: Retention comes from kinetic freezing instead of a leaky capacitor (fact 3). A sputter-plus-plasma flow cuts the module's water by more than 10x.

title: Judo master's leverage: negative-capacitance HZO gate on access transistor
idea: Judo turns the opponent's force against him. A matched ferroelectric HZO layer in the access transistor's gate stack uses its negative-capacitance region to amplify surface potential, reaching ~35 mV/dec over the critical decades, so the same off-current needs a ~0.5 V lower threshold and the wordline swings ~1.2 V straight from the supply.
why: A pumped 3 V swing becoming a direct 1.2 V swing is ~15x less wordline energy per toggle; HZO serves as a gate amplifier, not as the memory element covered in prior work.

title: Muralist's overpaint: oxide-TFT wordline drivers on top of the array
idea: An artist paints a second layer over the finished canvas. Build sub-wordline drivers and bitline-isolation switches as BEOL oxide-semiconductor (IGZO or IWO) TFTs above the cell array, which tolerate 3-4 V wordline levels with near-zero off-leakage, and delete the silicon SWD strips.
why: Removes ~10% of die area in high-voltage silicon periphery plus its leakage; oxide TFT breakdown suits the 3 V wordline (facts 7, 10).

title: Soviet core-memory veteran shrinks ferrite cores into nanorings
idea: Persona: a Soviet engineer who ran ferrite-core computers, now working at 40 nm. Permalloy (Ni80Fe20) nanorings threaded by a vertical copper via store a bit as a clockwise or counterclockwise flux-closure vortex. Current pulses through the via write the bit, and a small TMR sensor on a notch in the ring reads it.
why: Non-volatile with core-memory endurance. Flux closure has no stray field, so rings pack densely. Uses only abundant Ni, Fe and Cu, with no Pt, Co or Ir.

title: Historian revives Sandia's protonic memory in plain silicon dioxide
idea: Persona: a historian of forgotten technology recalling Sandia's 1990s work. A hydrogen anneal puts mobile protons into an ultrathin buried SiO2 layer. A gate field parks them at the top or bottom interface, which shifts the transistor threshold and holds it without power.
why: Non-volatile 1T memory from Si, O and H only, entirely native to a CMOS fab. Risk: write speed.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric layer boosts storage capacitance for 0.5-V hearing aids
idea: Hearing aids run from ~1 V cells and want sub-0.5 V arrays; a stabilized negative-capacitance HZO layer in series with a ZrO2 positive capacitor makes the stack's effective capacitance exceed either layer alone, behaving like k~100-200. The extra charge keeps the same sense signal at half the array voltage.
why: Attacks the charge wall (fact 1) and CV2 voltage floor (fact 10): ~2-4x lower energy per bit if NC stays hysteresis-free at ns speed, a contested claim.

title: Multi-electron redox molecules as pseudocapacitive storage for printed sensors
idea: Disposable printed sensors need cheap memory, so the storage electrode carries a self-assembled monolayer of porphyrin/ferrocene multi-redox molecules that each hold 2-4 electrons at distinct potentials, giving 5-10x the charge per area of a dielectric capacitor. Charging through short molecular tethers takes tens of ns and the distinct redox levels allow 2 bits per cell.
why: Faradaic pseudocapacitance beats the dielectric charge wall (fact 1) without high aspect ratio and adds multi-level storage; molecular stability over 1e15 cycles is the risk.
note: ZettaCore pursued porphyrin multi-redox memory; stability over 1e15 cycles unproven.

title: Self-clearing segmented electrode capacitor from subsea repeater film capacitors
idea: Subsea repeaters rely on metallized-film capacitors that vaporize their thin electrode around a breakdown spot and keep working; one mask patterns a 3-5 nm top-electrode film into fusible micro-segments so a dielectric breakdown burns out only its local segment. Tolerating breakdown lets the dielectric thin by ~30%.
why: ~1.3-1.4x capacitance with no new material (fact 1) and higher yield because breakdown no longer kills a cell; nanoscale fuse energetics are the risk.

title: Maskless direct-write lithography for small-lot DRAM
idea: Implant and defense users need 100-1,000 wafers, where a $5-15M mask set kills the economics. A 10-person micro-fab writes every layer with multi-beam e-beam or DLP maskless writers, so a design change takes hours.
why: Removes mask and EUV capital for niche supply; mask cost per product drops to about zero.
note: Multi-beam throughput too low and DLP too coarse for DRAM-density layers.

title: Dual-mode cell parks its charge in a trap layer
idea: Jump timescales inside one cell: in active mode the bit lives on the capacitor (ns access); before idle or power-down, a high-voltage pulse pushes the state into an adjacent charge-trap nitride (years retention), and on wake it is restored to the capacitor.
why: Refresh power: idle refresh (16-33% of idle power) disappears; also gives instant-on persistence.
note: Same trap-layer shadow copy; high-voltage stress on the thin capacitor dielectric.

title: MLCC-style interdigitated nanolaminate capacitor at cell scale
idea: Scale down the multilayer ceramic capacitor from mm to nm: conformally deposit 4-6 alternating electrode/dielectric layers in each hole, with odd and even electrodes tied at opposite ends, so capacitance multiplies by layer count instead of by aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall: ~3x Cs at the same AR, or a 25:1 AR cell matching today's Cs.
note: 4-6 electrode/dielectric layers cannot fit inside a ~30 nm storage hole.

title: Nanobattery bit holds voltage as chemical potential
idea: Scale an EV battery down to a 20 nm solid-state stack (Li-ion cathode/LiPON/anode): the bit is the open-circuit voltage set by tiny shallow charge swings and sensed by a gate, which holds without dielectric leakage.
why: Refresh: self-discharge is far slower than capacitor leakage, so refresh can be rare.
note: Same ionic open-circuit-voltage storage; ns speed and self-discharge at 20 nm doubtful.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric gate on sense-amp input pair
idea: Scale molecule-level dipole switching up into the sense path: a thin doped-HfO2 negative-capacitance layer in the gate stack of the SA input transistors gives ~2-3x internal voltage gain on the 50-100 mV charge-shared bitline signal before the latch fires.
why: More effective signal per femtocoulomb lets Cs drop ~2x or bitlines lengthen ~2x (facts 1, 7) and relaxes SA offset sizing.
note: NC-FET gain widely pursued and unproven.

title: Hot-aisle/cold-aisle tier zoning with embedded heat-spreader planes
idea: Scale datacenter airflow zoning down to a 3D die: insert a 50-nm AlN or diamond-like-carbon heat-spreader plane every 16 tiers, tie the planes to sidewall thermal vias, and put logic-heavy tiers at the hot end and cell tiers at the cold end. Leakage halves for every ~10 C, so a 20 C cooler cell tier needs a quarter of the refresh.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) and the thermal wall of tall stacks: ~4x less refresh, and more tiers can sit over hot logic.
note: A few-micron stack is nearly isothermal; 50 nm spreaders cannot create 20 C tier-to-tier differences.

title: A million zone plates steered by Texas micromirrors write maskless
idea: Zone-plate array lithography: a plate of ~10^6 diffractive micro-lenses, each switched by a U.S.-made DLP micromirror, focuses its own spot so the whole field is written in parallel without a mask or projection lens.
why: Maskless domestic patterning at ~30-40 nm with a ~$10M tool; pitch splitting finishes the array.

title: Large DUV cells store two bits each under Gray-coded LDPC
idea: No EUV: a 38 nm DUV-patterned cell can hold ~2-3x the charge of a 12 nm cell, so use four charge levels per cell (MLC DRAM) with Gray mapping and a row-level LDPC to absorb the level-tail errors. The retention budget is rescaled to 16 ms for the level spacing.
why: Recovers ~2x bits per cell to offset the coarser DUV pitch; a density step without EUV capex.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly of capacitor-hole arrays guided by UV-LED prepattern
idea: Scale jump from optics to molecules: polymer chains self-organize into a hexagonal array at 20-30 nm pitch, guided by a coarse prepattern exposed with 365 nm LED arrays rather than mercury-argon lamps or excimer lasers.
why: Patterns the densest DRAM layer without neon, argon or krypton light sources. Saves 2-4 EUV or multi-patterning steps per wafer.

title: TAS-MRAM without Joule heating: all-optical GdFeCo writes
idea: Crocus's thermally assisted MRAM died from the energy and time spent Joule-heating cells past the antiferromagnet blocking temperature. Write a GdFeCo ferrimagnetic free layer by helicity-independent all-optical toggle switching instead: a ~100 fs pulse, delivered by a shared on-chip waveguide and a plasmonic antenna per row, flips it, and an MTJ reads it.
why: Writes in <10 ps at ~10-100 fJ with no current through the barrier (no breakdown); one laser is amortized across thousands of cells.
note: AOS-MTJ demonstrated; on-chip fs sources and per-row plasmonics impractical.

title: Thinfilm PVDF fixed: vapor-deposited aromatic polyurea ferroelectric
idea: Printed PVDF-TrFE FeRAM (Thinfilm, Opticom) died partly because its ~100-130 C Curie point and slow switching ruled out hot or fast use. Vapor-deposition-polymerize an aromatic polyurea whose urea dipoles lock into H-bonded sheets that stay polar above ~200 C, coating 3D trenches conformally at room temperature.
why: An organic nonvolatile layer stable at 125 C/10 y, deposited at room temperature for monolithic many-tier stacks, with no ALD or EUV for the storage layer.

title: Goto's parametron stores bits as phase in NEMS resonators
idea: The parametron, which stored bits as the oscillation phase of parametrically pumped resonators, lost to transistors on speed. Store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at 2f from a shared line, and read it by phase-sensitive detection. There is no leakage to fight, only pump power of roughly stored energy times omega/Q.
why: Refresh is replaced by continuous pump power, estimated at ~0.5 pW/bit for Q~1e4. That is comparable to today's refresh power but has no access-transistor tail, so retention rests on different physics. Density is speculative.

title: Graphene's roll-to-roll CVD line repurposed for MoS2 access channels
idea: Graphene transistors failed as switches because graphene has no bandgap, yet roll-to-roll CVD growth and transfer of graphene worked. Reuse those R2R furnaces and transfer lines to grow monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV gap) on metal foil and laminate it onto capacitor foils as the access channel.
why: An atomically thin, wide-gap access channel: off-current approaches 1e-18 A/um with good electrostatics at short channels. R2R processing cuts capital per square meter.
note: R2R MoS2 quality far below wafer MOCVD; foil lamination onto capacitors unclear.

title: Solexel's porous-silicon lift-off foils as crucible-free low-leakage substrates
idea: Solexel's kerfless epitaxial silicon foils died against cheap Chinese wafers. Grow 20-40 um of epitaxial silicon on a porous-silicon release layer, lift it off, and handle the foils roll-to-roll on carrier tape, reusing each template ~50x. Epi silicon carries little oxygen and metal, so access-transistor junction leakage is lower than on Cz.
why: Fewer Cz ingots mean less demand for Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucibles, and epi material tightens the retention tail. Gives a U.S.-manufacturable foil supply.

title: IBM Millipede's tip-wear killer removed by non-contact charge-writing probes
idea: IBM's Millipede thermomechanical probe storage died on tip wear, slow thermal writes and cheap flash. Hover a million-tip MEMS array ~5 nm above an unpatterned ferroelectric film, write bits by polarization-switching voltage pulses with no contact or heat, and read each bit by piezoresponse through per-tip front-ends.
why: Meets 100x: medium cost ~0 and MEMS made at ~1 um litho; est. ~$0.05/GB. Trades: us-ms seek, mechanical scanner and shock sensitivity, so it serves as a bulk tier behind DRAM.
note: Probe storage is known and not DRAM-class (us-ms seek).

title: Printed-memory failures fixed: oxide-TFT DRAM on retired LCD lines
idea: Printed and plastic memories (Thin Film Electronics, Kovio) died without a dense, fast product. Fix: use retired Gen-2 to Gen-4 LCD lines (1990s tools, 1.5-3 um lithography, sputter tools reused for oxide channels) to make 1T1C DRAM in oxide TFTs on glass, where very low off-current gives minutes of retention, over square meters instead of wafers.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: ~2 GB per m^2 on fully depreciated panel tools, so cost per bit rests on cheap area rather than litho; a refresh-light bulk tier at ~100 ns-1 us.

title: One skyrmion per nanodisk: topological winding number as the bit
idea: Effect walk: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya chiral magnetism. A 20-nm Ta/CoFeB/MgO disk holds zero or one skyrmion; a current pulse nucleates or annihilates it at an engineered notch, and the bit is read through noncollinear magnetoresistance in a vertical tunnel stack.
why: Topological winding adds an energy barrier that does not scale with volume, so retention holds at smaller volumes than an MTJ free layer, pushing density past MRAM's thermal-stability limit.
note: Skyrmion stability at 20 nm room temperature and read signal remain hard.

title: Park VO2 inside its hysteresis loop; nudge bits with heat or strain
idea: Effect walk: thermal hysteresis of the VO2 metal-insulator transition. A strain- and dopant-engineered VO2 array (Tc ~90 C, ~15 K loop) is held at a regulated mid-loop temperature so metal and insulator are both stable; a 1-ns Joule nudge of a few kelvin writes 'metal', a piezo strain pulse that lifts the loop writes 'insulator', and the ~10^3 resistance ratio is read at 50 mV.
why: Write only supplies the latent heat of a ~10-nm volume (~0.2 fJ) plus a strain nudge, and read uses tiny bias on huge contrast: ~10x below DRAM cell+bitline energy with zero refresh, using the chip's waste heat to hold state.
note: Same mid-loop VO2 scheme; loop variation across nanoscale cells and die temperature control.

title: Clocked resonant-tunneling-diode pair as monostable-bistable bitline sense element
idea: Effect: resonant tunneling and negative differential resistance. Two series RTDs (Si/SiGe interband or InGaAs/AlAs) form a MOBILE: ramping the clock bias moves the pair from monostable to bistable, and the bitline current imbalance on the middle node decides which RTD drops into its valley. NDR gives regenerative gain with 2 devices at ~0.3 V.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10) and SA area (fact 7): sensing at 0.3-0.5 V cuts SA-stripe CV^2 ~4x, using 2 devices instead of ~8.

title: Vacuum nanogap field-emission triodes as BEOL wordline drivers
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission in vacuum. Etch sealed ~50 nm vacuum cavities in BEOL with sharp Mo or TiN emitters (no tungsten); grid-gated emission switches ~3 V wordlines with no channel leakage and no thick-oxide HV transistors, stacking the driver bank above the array.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): HV sub-wordline driver strips are ~10% of die; moving them into BEOL could shrink the die ~8%.

title: Electrostatic NEMS relays build zero-leakage row decoders above the array
idea: Effect: electrostatic pull-in hysteresis. Build BEOL TiN or poly-SiGe nano-relays (pull-in ~1-2 V) arranged as a relay-tree row decoder; hysteresis holds the selected path with no static current, and the metal contacts pass the 3 V wordline level directly, so no level shifters are needed.
why: Periphery area/leakage (fact 7): decoder and level-shifter area moves to BEOL and off-state leakage is zero in standby.

title: Spin-crossover iron complexes store bits inside thermal hysteresis loops
idea: Effect: Fe(II)-triazole coordination polymers switch between low-spin and high-spin states with a 20-40 K wide thermal hysteresis loop near room temperature. Nano-cells held at the loop center are flipped by a local Joule pulse and read through their 10-30% change in permittivity or conductance; there is no stored charge to leak.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and Hf/W/capacitor-etch dependence; uses only Fe, C, N, H, so no scarce element is involved.

title: Molten-salt electro-deoxidation turns ordinary sand into domestic silicon feedstock
idea: Effect: field-driven oxide-ion migration. In the FFC-Cambridge process O2- ions leave a SiO2 cathode into molten CaCl2 at ~850 C, leaving porous silicon with no carbothermic arc furnace or chlorosilane Siemens reactor; directional solidification and segregation refining then push purity toward CZ feedstock grade.
why: Polysilicon concentration (China ~90%) and Siemens energy (~50-60 kWh/kg): targets <20 kWh/kg from any sand at U.S. sites.
note: FFC route known; Ca/Cl/metal contamination makes electronic-grade feedstock a long reach.

title: Intercalated multilayer graphene wordlines grown by nickel-mediated precipitation
idea: Effect: charge-transfer intercalation doping. Carbon diffuses through a Ni film at ~350 C and precipitates as multilayer graphene in trenches (layer exchange). FeCl3 intercalation then shifts the Fermi level and cuts resistivity toward Cu, giving barrier-free, electromigration-proof wordlines made of carbon.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6; no liner volume at 10-15 nm and abundant feedstock, all below 400 C.
note: Same Ni-mediated intercalated graphene wordlines as I-06627.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous electrodes multiply capacitor area inside shallow holes
idea: Effect: dealloying (selective dissolution plus surface-diffusion coarsening). Deposit a Ru-Al or Ti-Al alloy liner in a low-AR (~15:1) hole and dissolve the Al to leave a bicontinuous porous electrode with 10-20 nm ligaments; then ALD a thin high-k and a top TiN. Surface area per footprint rises 4-6x.
why: Fact 1: reaching 5 fF without AR 60-75 removes HAR mold etch and pattern-collapse controls, which are among the costliest capacitor-module tools.

title: Electroluminescence: printed perovskite LED arrays drive thousands of slow parallel lanes
idea: Print perovskite micro-LED and photodiode arrays with ~10 um pixels on interposer film and image one onto the other through a fiber bundle; 10,000 lanes at 200 Mb/s give 2 Tb/s with plain NRZ and no SerDes.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5): wide-and-slow optical lanes avoid SerDes power (sub-pJ/bit); perovskite stability at 80 C and speed are the risks.
note: Avicena does this with GaN microLEDs; perovskite worsens stability and speed.

title: C: pre-buckled amorphous-carbon nanobeam snaps between two stable shapes
idea: Deposit a 5 nm x 80 nm a-C:H (diamond-like carbon) bridge under built-in compressive stress so it buckles up or down; an electrostatic pulse from an under- or over-electrode snaps it across (GHz-class resonance gives ~1 ns transit) and the gap capacitance or tunneling current reads it.
why: Elastic bistability holds the bit with zero leakage: no refresh (fact 3), no charge wall (fact 1), carbon from methane PECVD; stiction and fatigue over 1e15 cycles are the risks.

title: Deuterium micro-heater self-anneal heals variable-retention trap cells in field
idea: H (as deuterium): package the die in a sealed D2-loaded cavity and embed polysilicon micro-heaters under each bank; when retention telemetry shows a bank's weak-cell count rising, its data is migrated out and the bank is held at ~300 C for seconds so deuterium re-passivates Si/SiO2 interface and GIDL traps (Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier breaking far better than Si-H).
why: Attacks the aging-driven growth of the trap-assisted leakage tail (fact 3); keeping tail cells healed over life could hold refresh at 2-4x longer intervals, cutting refresh energy ~50%.

title: Epitaxial CaF2 gate insulator removes the traps behind VRT
idea: Ca: grow crystalline CaF2 (12 eV gap, within 0.6% lattice match to Si(111)) as the access-transistor gate insulator by fluoride epitaxy; its ionic, dangling-bond-free interface removes the border and interface traps whose capture/emission causes variable retention time and random-telegraph leakage.
why: VRT cells force pessimistic refresh guard-bands (fact 3); a trap-free insulator could shrink the VRT population ~10x and allow ~2x longer refresh.
note: Same epitaxial CaF2 insulator.

title: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 gate gives hysteresis-free negative-capacitance access device
idea: Zr: stack a thin antiferroelectric ZrO2 layer on the access-transistor gate dielectric and shift it, via work-function offset, into the negative-slope branch of its double loop, so capacitance matching gives sub-60 mV/dec swing without the memory window of ferroelectric NC-FETs.
why: Steeper slope lets a higher Vt keep on-current, cutting off-leakage ~10x or wordline voltage ~20-30% (facts 3, 10).

title: C: amorphous-carbon nanorelay row decoders with zero leakage
idea: Replace local decoder and sub-wordline-driver transistors with electrostatic diamond-like-carbon cantilever relays built in BEOL; carbon-on-carbon contacts resist stiction and wear, and a relay's infinite off-resistance and abrupt pull-in pass the full 3 V VPP with no gate-oxide stress.
why: Sub-wordline drivers are a large, leaky slice of periphery (fact 7, fact 10); stacked relays could halve decoder footprint and drop driver standby leakage to ~0; ns-scale nanorelay switching fits a ~30 ns row cycle.

title: Hf: hafnium-zirconia negative-capacitance gate boosts sense-amp gain
idea: Insert a thin HZO ferroelectric in the gate stack of the SA pull-down pair, matched for stabilized negative capacitance so the internal gate swing exceeds the bitline swing (~1.5-2x step-up) during sensing.
why: Pre-amplifies the ~100 mV signal, letting VARY drop below 1 V (fact 10) and SA transistors shrink; claims ~30% lower sensing energy.

title: V: vanadium dioxide insulator-metal switch as two-terminal comparator
idea: Bias a doped VO2 nanogap just below its insulator-metal threshold on each sense node; the cell's extra charge tips it metallic and hysteresis latches the result, replacing a 4-6 transistor latch with one two-terminal device. Doping shifts the 68 C transition above operating temperature.
why: SA area could fall ~3x (fact 7); the transition temperature and switching energy are open risks.

title: p-type tin-monoxide CMOS periphery stacked over the array
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sn (50): pair n-type ZTO with p-type SnO (hole mobility 1-5 cm2/Vs) to build complementary sense-amp drivers and decoders at <=400 C directly above the cell array, moving part of the 49% periphery off silicon wafer area.
why: ~25-35% less silicon wafer area per bit, hence fewer wafers, crucibles and EUV passes; Sn is abundant and already an EUV-source consumable.

title: Si: vicinal-wafer atomic step bunches as maskless wordline template
idea: Cut Si(111) wafers at a precise miscut so a UHV/H2 anneal bunches atomic steps into a self-ordered array whose pitch is set by the miscut angle (e.g. 24 nm); selectively nucleate an oxide or metal along the step edges to form the dense wordline hardmask with no exposure at all for that array layer.
why: Litho/capital (fact 4): the crystal lattice becomes the ruler, deleting one EUV or SAQP line layer (~4-8 steps) in the array; ~3-5% wafer-cost cut if edge-roughness is controllable.

title: Fermented magnetosome bits: bacteria grow uniform magnetite memory crystals
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria grow 35 nm single-domain Fe3O4 crystals with <10% size spread, uniformity that sputter-and-etch cannot match. The crystals are harvested, given DNA linkers and docked into lithographic sites on Pt or W spin-orbit-torque lines. Each bit is held as magnetization and read through magnetite's half-metallic tunneling.
why: Spin storage with unlimited endurance and no MTJ etch damage. The fab tool is a fermenter, which cuts capital intensity, and pitch is ~50 nm for nonvolatile working memory.
note: Same magnetosome bits; low magnetite anisotropy and docking registry are risks.

title: Splat-quenched charge-density-wave bit in 1T-TaS2 nanoflakes
idea: Use the splat quenching that makes metallic glass. A 30 ps current pulse melts the charge-density-wave order of a 1T-TaS2 flake and refreezes it into a metastable 'hidden' metallic state, and a longer gentle pulse restores the insulating state. The bit is the electronic phase, read as a 10-100x resistance ratio.
why: A purely electronic phase change: no atoms move, so endurance is unlimited (unlike PCM), and switching is ps at fJ energy. The risk is keeping the state stable near room temperature through strain and thickness.

title: Coin-stamped snap-dome bit: bistable buckled SiC membrane holds data
idea: Borrow keyboard snap-dome stamping: nanoimprint-coin a 40 nm SiC (or diamond-like-carbon) dome with built-in compressive stress over a vacuum cavity, so it is stable bowed up or bowed down. Electrostatic electrodes snap it in ~1-5 ns, and dome position shifts a capacitance on the sense line.
why: Facts 3 and 9: mechanical storage has zero leakage, so no refresh, and there is no stored charge to row-hammer. Si and C only, and SiC membranes are rated beyond 1e12 cycles.

title: Shape-memory 'training' bit: Ni-Mn-Sn martensite twin variant stores data
idea: Copy how shape-memory-alloy wire is trained: train a Ni-Mn-Sn Heusler nanodot so its martensite settles in one of two twin variants. Gate-applied strain or field flips the variant diffusionlessly, with no atomic migration, and magnetic or resistive anisotropy reads it.
why: Ferroelastic storage from Ni, Mn and Sn with no charge leakage (fact 3). Diffusionless switching aims at >1e12 cycles.

title: Furnace refractory lining: thermal break shields HBM from hot logic
idea: Like a refractory firebrick lining, insert a low-k porous thermal-break layer between the logic base die and the DRAM stack. Logic heat is routed around the DRAM through peripheral copper thermal columns to the lid.
why: Leakage roughly doubles every ~10 C. Keeping HBM 20 C cooler cuts refresh rate ~4x and lifts bandwidth.

title: Photographic-development tunnel-diode latch amplifies latent bitline charge
idea: Borrow film development, which amplifies a latent image of a few silver atoms by ~10^9: place a Goto pair of Esaki tunnel diodes on each bitline pair, biased near the peak of its N-shaped I-V. A few millivolts of cell signal tips it into one valley state in picoseconds, and a CMOS restore stage follows.
why: NDR latch offset is set by junction doping, not gate litho, and it switches at ~0.3-0.5 V: ~3x smaller usable bitline signal and lower array voltage, attacking both the charge wall and the CV^2 voltage floor.

title: Hall-Heroult for silicon: molten-salt electrowinning from sand
idea: Aluminum is won by electrolysis in molten salt; reduce silica pellets electrochemically in molten CaCl2 at ~850 C (FFC-style) or electrodeposit silicon from silica dissolved in chloride melts onto silicon cathodes, then zone-refine the product to electronic grade.
why: Bypasses carbothermic metallurgical silicon (coke electrodes, 11-13 kWh/kg) and the Siemens trichlorosilane process (~50-60 kWh/kg) and its chlorosilane chemistry, cutting feedstock energy by ~50% or more.

title: Printed redox-molecule monolayer storing quantized charge per molecule
idea: IFR: every molecule is an identical, perfect capacitor. Closest achievable: print a self-assembled monolayer of porphyrin or ferrocene molecules on printed electrodes; each molecule holds 1-2 electrons at sharp redox potentials, giving ~10 uC/cm^2 and natural multilevel states with seconds-to-minutes retention.
why: Fact 1: areal charge 10-100x an oxide capacitor, solution-printable; multilevel raises bits per cell.
note: Printed variant of porphyrin redox monolayer storage.

title: Printed ionogel double-layer capacitor shrinking the charge wall
idea: IFR: a dielectric one molecule thick. Closest achievable: print an ion gel (ionic liquid in polymer) between blocking electrodes; the electric double layer acts as a ~1 nm dielectric giving ~10 uF/cm^2 (hundreds of times a 5 nm high-k film), with nano-thin gels pushing charging toward sub-us.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF fits a planar ~0.05 um^2 pad with no high-AR etch; R2R printable.
note: Printed ionogel EDL with sub-us charging is too slow for DRAM.

title: Printed spin-crossover film held inside its room-temperature hysteresis
idea: IFR: a molecule that remembers its spin state at no cost. Closest achievable: print [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)]-class nanoparticles with a ~40 K wide hysteresis loop, hold the array at mid-loop temperature, set high-spin with a ns local heat pulse and low-spin with a piezo strain pulse, and read the ~10% volume/dielectric change.
why: Nonvolatile within the operating window, molecular switching with no wear, all-printed; write energy is the risk.

title: Light-through-glass optical buses replace vias between stacked dies
idea: IFR: 'tiers talk with no wire between them.' Backward: in a stack of thin transparent glass memory dies, put transfer-printed micro-LED emitters and oxide photodiodes in aligned columns with metal-free windows, so each die sends and receives its data bus optically straight through the dies above and below.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSVs or bonds in the data path and dies are swappable; ~0.5 pJ/bit at 1-10 Gb/s per channel, thousands of channels per die.

title: Compiler region inference sizes heaps to the exact peak live set
idea: IFR: programs allocate exactly what they use at each instant. The constraint pushes to zero new hardware: a whole-program region-inference compiler (lifetime analysis in the style of Rust/MLKit) assigns every allocation to a stack-like region freed in bulk, removing allocator slack, fragmentation and GC headroom.
why: Cuts footprint 25-50% for allocation-heavy services with zero materials of any kind.
note: MLKit-style region inference leaks for general programs.

title: Frequency-division memory bus: every bank owns a carrier
idea: Ideal: all banks talk at once on one wire. Closest achievable: each bank's I/O modulates its own RF carrier slot (2-40 GHz) onto a single shared interposer transmission line, and the controller demodulates all channels at once with a wideband ADC plus FFT, replacing hundreds of parallel traces.
why: Fact 6 and interposer cost: cuts trace and bump count ~16x, reducing interposer layers and area while enabling full bank-parallel access without wide buses.
note: Wideband ADC plus FFT energy likely exceeds wire savings.

title: Tail removal allowed only after packaging: wordline Joule self-anneal
idea: Limit: the leakage tail must be fixed in the field, not in the fab. In maintenance windows, drive a controlled current through segmented wordline straps to Joule-heat a few-um2 region to ~300 C for microseconds. This anneals variable-retention-time trap configurations and redistributes hydrogen at the access transistor's Si/SiO2 interface; the weak rows are then re-profiled.
why: Fact 3: VRT traps drive the 13 fA tail and its unpredictability. Periodic in-situ annealing could shrink the tail ~3-10x over life and allow longer refresh. Risk: thermal stress on neighboring cells.

title: Transistor-free predecoders: threshold-switch diode matrix in BEOL
idea: Limit: decoders may use zero front-end transistors. Build predecoders as a BEOL crossbar of ovonic threshold switches and resistors above the array; the address bits applied to its columns make only one row's series OTS chain exceed threshold and snap on, firing that local wordline driver.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): ~6-9% of decoder silicon moves into stacked BEOL, with no extra EUV layers.

title: Rutile TiO2 on RuO2 doubles k and halves capacitor etch
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: grow Al-doped rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100), templated below 400 C by RuO2 electrodes whose high work function plus Al doping suppress hot Schottky leakage, so capacitor aspect ratio drops from ~70 to ~35.
why: Facts 1 and 4: single-step capacitor etch, thinner carbon hardmask, fewer support layers; capacitor module cost ~-30%.

title: No silicon, no vacuum: EHD-jet printed oxide memory micro-fabs
idea: Forced limit: no wafer, no vacuum fab. Electrohydrodynamic jet printers write solution-processed ZTO/IGZO and metal lines at about 1 um on glass sheets in $5M micro-fabs distributed near users.
why: Distributed manufacturing: capital per site drops by about 1000x, giving local supply for defense and edge niches; density is low.

title: Oil infill drilling: recover wafer-edge DRAM die with partial fields
idea: Adapted from infill drilling that taps oil left between existing wells: tape out a half-size 'edge die' variant and a step map that fills the partial-field ring and narrows edge exclusion, using reticle blading and tighter bevel-etch and edge-bead control.
why: The edge ring wastes ~5-10% of gross 300 mm area; recovering a third of it adds ~2-3% bits per wafer at near-zero capex (cost per bit).

title: Reopen U.S. 200 mm fabs for Grade-1 automotive DRAM
idea: Magnify the node on purpose: run 65-90 nm DRAM with fat capacitors and long, low-leakage access transistors in idle U.S. 200 mm fabs, qualified to AEC-Q100 Grade 1 (125 C), with DUV only.
why: Cars need 2-16 GB each of hot-rated DRAM. Moving that volume off leading-edge lines frees EUV wafers for HBM and adds U.S. supply with no EUV and little helium.
note: Same shift of legacy/automotive DRAM to 200 mm lines as I-08505.

title: Center-tapped wordlines for chloride-precursor molybdenum fill
idea: Rearrange the wordline driver from the end to the middle: buried wordlines filled with Mo from MoO2Cl2 (replacing tungsten from WF6) are driven from a center tap, halving RC so far-end cells get a full restore within tRAS.
why: Under-restored far-end cells feed the retention tail; also removes WF6 and dependence on China-concentrated tungsten.

title: Dormant spare storage tiers swap in when a 3D tier wears out
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: in stacked-tier 3D DRAM, fabricate 2 unpowered spare tiers per ~32; on-die retention monitors detect a tier whose leakage tail has drifted, and a nonvolatile tier map swaps a spare in while data copy in the background.
why: Fact 2: makes 3D tiers field-repairable where laser fuses can't reach; ~6% area buys ~2-3x service life.
note: Standard redundancy extended to tiers; needs 3D DRAM to exist.

title: Sous-vide sealing: channel epi and gate oxide grown without air break
idea: Sous-vide food is sealed before cooking so nothing can contaminate it. Replace the HF-last pre-gate clean with a cluster tool that grows a fresh selective epitaxial silicon skin on the access-channel surface (SiH4/HCl/H2) and oxidizes it in situ by radical oxidation without breaking vacuum, so the gate interface is born clean and never touches hydrofluoric acid.
why: Pristine interfaces cut trap-assisted leakage and Vt variation (fact 3) and remove HF baths and their waste stream, easing U.S. fab permitting (U.S. manufacturability).

title: Reclaim end-of-life solar silicon as purified DRAM polysilicon feed
idea: Box [feedstock: retired PV cells | purification: hydrochlorination to trichlorosilane | deposition: US Siemens reactors | product: 11N poly for CZ]: delaminate retired modules, strip Ag/Al from the 5-6N cells, convert the silicon to trichlorosilane and re-deposit electronic-grade polysilicon.
why: Polysilicon concentration and energy: PV waste reaches millions of tonnes in the 2030s; recycled feed skips carbothermic reduction and diversifies a China-heavy supply chain.

title: Sputter-free fab: every liner, barrier and electrode by thermal ALD
idea: Box [ALD TiN/ZrO2 cap | Si | voltage SA | standard | Si | thermal ALD/CVD with N2 carriers + NH3/H2 reducers + remote NH3/NF3 pre-clean]: requalify every Ar-sputtered film (Ti/TiN contact liners, bitline metal, silicide seed, periphery gate metal) and every Ar sputter pre-clean as gas-phase thermal processes.
why: Removes argon from deposition entirely; the constraint also forces near-100% step coverage, which 3D DRAM tiers and high-AR contacts need anyway.

title: Po: contacts made of silicon itself — silicide-capped epi plugs
idea: Po: a contact with no tungsten. Fill periphery contacts with in-situ-doped selective epitaxial silicon capped by self-aligned TiSi2/NiSi, topped by a TiN/Al local layer, eliminating WF6 CVD tungsten plugs throughout the periphery.
why: Scarce resources: removes tungsten (China ~80%) from contacts using Si, Ti, Ni, N, Al; epi plugs also tighten contact-resistance spread.
note: Poly/epi plugs already common; contact tungsten volume negligible.

title: Fertilizer-plant fluorine: Florida phosphate byproduct replaces imported fluorspar
idea: Phosphate fertilizer plants scrub fluorosilicic acid from off-gas and mostly neutralize it; convert it via the bifluoride route to anhydrous HF and then to electronic-grade HF, NF3 and F2 at a Gulf Coast plant, recovering silica as a coproduct.
why: U.S. HF depends on imported fluorspar from Mexico and China; phosphate byproduct could supply all fab fluorine chemistry domestically while keeping it fluorocarbon-free.

title: Wafer-scale 180 nm DRAM with mesh self-routing around defects
idea: Ideal: 100% yield without a perfect fab. Closest: build an entire 200 mm wafer as one memory module of ~2,000 subarray tiles linked by a redundant mesh; a boot-time BIST disables bad tiles and soft-routes around them, so random defects only remove capacity and never kill the part.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: turns old 180 nm lines into high-capacity modules with no die sort, dicing or per-die packaging.
